api/EvoSim.ActContext.html.title: Class ActContext | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.ActContext.html.summary: Class ActContext Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll What an action may do in one tick (ACT-06): ask questions about what the animal could sense, and say where it wants to go (an intent) and what to do on arrival (an interaction). It can't move or change any animal itself. public sealed class ActContext Inheritance object ActContext Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples The grazing part of the reference EatAction: public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { var food = c.NearestResource(a); // within vision, diet-checked if (food == null) { c.Search(); return; } // nothing in sight: search (ACT-04) c.WalkTo(food.Value.Position, stopAt: 0f); // MOVE-04 c.OnArrival(Interaction.Graze(food.Value)); // applied after moving, within reach (ACT-10) } Remarks The act phase owns one context and reuses it for every animal. For each animal it calls Begin(Animal), then the chosen action's Act(Animal, ActContext), then reads Plan. Afterwards the species' Locomotion moves the animal, and the interaction applies only if the animal is within reach after moving (ACT-10). The queries (Nearest…, InCover(Animal), IsReady(Animal)) only return what the animal's senses could report: within its vision, never itself, never a killed animal, never an animal hidden from it in cover (ACT-05). In the sequential act orders they see the state left by the animals that acted before; in the simultaneous order, the state at the start of the act phase (ACT-31). The intent methods (WalkTo, RunTo, RunAwayFrom, WalkAwayFrom, Stay(), Wander(), Search()) replace each other: the last one called is the plan. The two OnArrival methods set the interaction the same way. Constructors ActContext(World) Creates a context for a world. The act phase makes one and reuses it for every animal; a test, or a student's own act phase, can make its own. public ActContext(World world) Parameters world World The world whose ground, queries and random streams the context uses. Properties GrazeReach Within this distance of a food item the animal grazes it, in meters (ACT-10; reference 0.5). The act phase copies its own graze reach here; an action reads it to tell that the animal already stands on its food. public float GrazeReach { get; set; } Property Value float Ground The world's ground (heights, walkable points, water), or null in a world without one. public Ground Ground { get; } Property Value Ground Intent The intent planned so far for the current animal: a stay until the action calls an intent method. public Intent Intent { get; } Property Value Intent Interaction The interaction planned so far for the current animal: none until the action calls OnArrival. public Interaction Interaction { get; } Property Value Interaction Plan What was planned for the current animal: its intent, interaction and target animal. public ActPlan Plan { get; } Property Value ActPlan TargetAnimal The animal the intent is about (followed, fled, chased), or null. The act phase records it as the animal's TargetId, for the inspector and for senses such as the sample ChasedSense. public Animal TargetAnimal { get; } Property Value Animal Tick The current tick of the world. public int Tick { get; } Property Value int World The world being simulated: its species, services, queries and random streams. public World World { get; } Property Value World Methods Begin(Animal) Starts planning for an animal: stay and no interaction until the action says otherwise. public void Begin(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The animal about to act. Remarks ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>) calls it before each Act(Animal, ActContext), and the act phase calls it for busy animals. Call it yourself only when you drive an action from your own code, such as a test. HeadingDirection(float) The unit direction of a heading in degrees (0 = +z, 90 = +x). public static Vector3 HeadingDirection(float degrees) Parameters degrees float A heading, in degrees clockwise from +z when seen from above. Returns Vector3 A unit vector on the horizontal plane. InCover(Animal) True when the animal stands in cover of any cover module (ENV-10). public bool InCover(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The animal to check, usually the one that acts. Returns bool True when its position is in cover; always false in a world without cover (ENV-12). IsReady(Animal) Whether another animal is ready to mate (REPRO-01), by its species' mating rule; never without one. public bool IsReady(Animal other) Parameters other Animal Any animal, usually one a query found. Returns bool True when it is ready to mate. NearestAnimal(Animal, AnimalSet, IReadOnlyList<Species>) The nearest visible animal of a set (threats, prey, kin, listed), within vision: never itself, never a killed animal, never one hidden from it in cover (ACT-05). public AnimalHit? NearestAnimal(Animal a, AnimalSet set, IReadOnlyList<Species> listed = null) Parameters a Animal The animal that looks. set AnimalSet Whom to look for: the species' threats, prey or kin, derived from the food web (SPEC-12), or the listed species. listed IReadOnlyList<Species> The species to look among when set is Listed; ignored otherwise. Returns AnimalHit? The animal found and its distance in meters, or null when none is in sight. Examples The reference FleeAction: var threat = c.NearestAnimal(a, AnimalSet.Threats); if (threat == null) { c.Search(); return; } c.RunAwayFrom(threat.Value.Animal); NearestCarcass(Animal) The nearest carcass this animal may eat from, within vision: its diet scavenges that species' carcasses, portions are left, it is not the killer and it has not eaten from it yet. public EntityHit<Carcass>? NearestCarcass(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The animal that looks for a carcass. Returns EntityHit<Carcass>? The carcass and its distance in meters, or null when none is in sight. NearestCover(Animal, float) The nearest cover within vision (or a given radius); distance 0 when the animal stands in cover (ENV-10). public CoverHit? NearestCover(Animal a, float radius = -1) Parameters a Animal The animal that looks for cover. radius float The search radius in meters; negative (the default) uses the animal's vision. Returns CoverHit? A point in cover and its distance, or null when none is in reach or the world has no cover module (ENV-12). NearestEgg(Animal, Species) The nearest egg (of a species, or any) the diet eats (REPRO-23), within vision. public EntityHit<Egg>? NearestEgg(Animal a, Species of = null) Parameters a Animal The animal that looks for eggs. of Species Only eggs of this species, or null for every species whose eggs the diet eats. Returns EntityHit<Egg>? The egg and its distance in meters, or null when none is in sight. NearestEntity<T>(Animal, Func<T, Animal, bool>) The nearest entity of a kind of your own (fruit, nests…) within the animal's vision, across every entity system of that type; used-up entities are skipped and ties go to the lower id (SPACE-07, SPACE-08). public EntityHit<T>? NearestEntity<T>(Animal a, Func<T, Animal, bool> filter = null) where T : Entity Parameters a Animal The animal that looks. filter Func<T, Animal, bool> Receives an entity and the looking animal and returns true to keep it; null keeps every entity. No diet is checked for you: check it here if the entity is food. Returns EntityHit<T>? The entity and its distance in meters, or null when none is in sight. Type Parameters T The entity class, a subclass of Entity. NearestReadyPartner(Animal) The nearest visible kin that is ready to mate (REPRO-01), within vision and within the partner range of the species' kin sense that reports readiness: the action never targets what the senses can't report (ACT-05). public AnimalHit? NearestReadyPartner(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The animal that looks for a partner. Returns AnimalHit? The partner and its distance in meters, or null when none is in sight. NearestResource(Animal, string) The nearest item of a layer the diet grazes, within vision; the diet and the layer's Edible are checked (SPEC-13). public ResourceItem? NearestResource(Animal a, string layerName = "") Parameters a Animal The animal that looks for food. layerName string A layer's name, or empty for every layer the diet grazes. Returns ResourceItem? The item (its layer, cell, position and distance), or null when none is in sight. OnArrival(IInteraction) Sets a custom interaction (22 §3). It applies after moving when the animal is within its Reach of the point the intent was heading to (Target). public void OnArrival(IInteraction custom) Parameters custom IInteraction The contact effect of your own. OnArrival(Interaction) Sets what to do on arrival: graze, strike, scavenge or eat an egg. It applies after moving, in the same tick, only when the animal is within reach and the diet allows it (ACT-10, SPEC-13). public void OnArrival(Interaction i) Parameters i Interaction An interaction built with Graze(ResourceItem), Strike(Animal), Scavenge(Carcass) or EatEgg(Egg). RunAwayFrom(Animal) Runs straight away from an animal (flee) and records it as the target animal. public void RunAwayFrom(Animal threat) Parameters threat Animal The animal to run from. RunAwayFrom(Vector3) Runs straight away from a point, as far as speed and stamina allow. Standing on the point itself, the animal runs along its heading. public void RunAwayFrom(Vector3 threat) Parameters threat Vector3 The point to run from. RunTo(Animal, float) Runs toward an animal (hunt), stopping at a distance, and records it as the target animal. public void RunTo(Animal target, float stopAt) Parameters target Animal The animal to reach; its position now is the point run to. stopAt float How far from it to stop, in meters. RunTo(Vector3, float) Runs toward a point at the species' running speed and stops at a distance from it (MOVE-04). Each meter costs the same stamina as walking (ANIM-21); running only covers more meters per tick. public void RunTo(Vector3 target, float stopAt = 0) Parameters target Vector3 The point to reach. stopAt float How far from the point to stop, in meters; 0 goes onto it. Search() Nothing to act on in sight: wander, counted as searching once per decision (ACT-04). public void Search() Remarks The first call after a decision sets the animal's Searching flag and adds one to its species' Invalid count (the prototype's "invalid"); the next decision clears the flag. Every action that can find nothing should call it rather than Wander(). Stay() Stays where it is this tick (rest, stay in cover, already on the food). public void Stay() Vision(Animal) The animal's vision, in meters (SENSE-22): its vision trait, or 20 m for a species without one. public float Vision(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The animal that looks. Returns float The radius within which the queries find things, in meters. WalkAwayFrom(Vector3) Walks straight away from a point, as far as speed and stamina allow. public void WalkAwayFrom(Vector3 threat) Parameters threat Vector3 The point to walk from. WalkTo(Animal, float) Walks toward an animal (follow, mate), stopping at a distance, and records it as the target animal. public void WalkTo(Animal target, float stopAt) Parameters target Animal The animal to reach; its position now is the point walked to. stopAt float How far from it to stop, in meters. WalkTo(Vector3, float) Walks toward a point and stops at a distance from it (MOVE-04): the locomotion never overshoots the stop distance. Already within it, the animal stays. public void WalkTo(Vector3 target, float stopAt = 0) Parameters target Vector3 The point to reach. stopAt float How far from the point to stop, in meters; 0 goes onto it. Wander() A persistent random walk (MOVE-05): keep the heading; with probability WanderTurnP turn by ±45° or ±90°; blocked, pick a new random heading. Walks. Draws from the species' actions stream. public void Wander() Remarks It turns the current animal's own heading. Without a locomotion it turns with probability 0.25. When the action has nothing to act on, call Search() instead, so that the search is counted (ACT-04).

FindObjectsInactive) Object.ToString() Object.name Object.hideFlags object.Equals(object, object) object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks Fourth phase of the reference tick, after Choose actions and before Breed. For each animal, in the act order: plan (its current action's ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>) gives an intent and maybe an interaction; busy animals and animals without an action stay), move (its species' MoveAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, IReadOnlyList<Intent>, MoveContext, Span<float>)), interact (the InteractionResolver applies graze, strike, scavenge, egg eating or a custom interaction within reach, diet-checked), settle (metabolism and stamina, then the busy countdown). An animal with an overlay (ACT-07) is planned twice: its action (the carrier) as above, then its overlay in the same context, of which only the interaction is kept. Both interactions apply after the move, the carrier's first; the overlay's countdown drops in settle, and the overlay ends when the animal becomes busy. The order (ACT-30): in SpeciesInTurn and AllMixed each animal does all four steps before the next one, on the state left by those before it (ACT-31); in Simultaneous every animal plans from the same state, all move, then interactions apply in a random order. Every shuffle comes from the act-order stream (ACT-32); strike rolls and sidesteps use each species' actions stream. A killed animal is only marked here; it acts no more this tick and dies in the death phase (ANIM-41). If a locomotion leaves an animal on non-walkable ground, the phase puts it back where it started, with a warning (MOVE-02). Properties GrazeReach Within this distance of a food item, in meters, an animal grazes it (ACT-10). public float GrazeReach { get; } Property Value float Order The act order (ACT-30); a scenario or test may change it before the World initialises. public ActOrder Order { get; set; } Property Value ActOrder ScavengeReach Within this distance of a carcass, in meters, an animal eats a portion (ACT-10). public float ScavengeReach { get; } Property Value float StrikeReach Within this distance of its prey, in meters, a hunter strikes (ACT-10). public float StrikeReach { get; } Property Value float Methods Initialize() Creates the contexts and the resolver with this phase's reaches, and makes room for as many animals as the caps allow. public override void Initialize() Remarks Look up what you need here, by role or name (Service<T>(), Phase<T>()), and reset your own state: the same object starts every run of the World. A service is initialised before the species' modules; a phase after them. Run(TickContext) Rebuilds the spatial index, clears last tick's per-animal flags, and lets every living animal act in the act order. public override void Run(TickContext t) Parameters t TickContext The current tick's context: the World, the tick number and the random streams. Remarks Called once per tick, after WaitsFor(TickContext)'s work is done. An exception stops the run. Validate(ValidationReport) Reports a species without exactly one locomotion (V-13), with a fix that adds a kinematic one when there is none. public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Only read: validation must not change the scene. Offer a change as a ValidationFix.

Modules read and write it through this record. public sealed class Animal Inheritance object Animal Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Examples Energy energy; public override void Initialize() => energy = Species.Module<Energy>(); public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) => a[energy.Value] < 30f ? 1 : 0; // a stat, by its id float vision = a.Trait(visionTrait); // a trait, fixed at birth Remarks An animal is no GameObject and has no Update: phases loop over the animals of each species (Animals), and a pooled view only shows it. Species modules keep their per-animal values here, as stats and traits they declared (ANIM-10, ANIM-15): read and write a stat with the indexer, a trait with Trait(TraitId) and SetTrait(TraitId, float). Animals are made by CreateAnimal(string, Vector3, float, Genome, int, int[], Action<Animal>) and join the living with Add(Animal). A dead animal is marked IsGone by RecordDeath(Animal, string); its record stays readable. Fields Action The current action: an index into Actions, or -1 before its first decision. reference FollowAction, without its relevance test: public class FollowAction : AnimalAction { protected override string DefaultDescription => "move toward the nearest other animal"; [SerializeField, Min(0f), Tooltip("Stop this far from the followed animal, in meters (reference 1).")] float stopAt = 1f; public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { var kin = c.NearestAnimal(a, AnimalSet.Kin); if (kin == null) { c.Search(); return; } c.WalkTo(kin.Value.Animal, stopAt); } } Remarks Derive from it, implement Act(Animal, ActContext) and DefaultDescription, and place the component on its own GameObject under a species. The GameObject's name is the action's name; the depth-first order of the species' actions is their order in the prompt and in the brain's answer (SPEC-03). A TextGene on the same GameObject, or on a child of it, is bound to it (GENE-05). Once the brain chose it, Act(Animal, ActContext) runs every tick until the next decision, or until the animal becomes busy or dies (ACT-02). An action done in passing (a call) is an Overlay: it runs beside a second, moving action (ACT-07). What Act(Animal, ActContext) must keep: Plan only through the ActContext: never set the position, stats or flags of any animal (ACT-06). Effects on others go through interactions, which check the reach and the diet. Target only what the context's queries return: what the animal's senses could report (ACT-05). With nothing to act on, call Search() (ACT-04). Never read gene sentences: genes reach an action only through traits (ACT-20). Draw random numbers only from the species' streams (World.Random.For(Species, "actions")), never from UnityEngine.Random, so that a seed repeats a run. Fields description The action's line in the prompt, after its name; empty uses DefaultDescription (PROMPT-01, PROMPT-07). [SerializeField] [TextArea(1, 4)] [Tooltip("The action's line in the prompt, after its name (PROMPT-01, PROMPT-07).")] protected string description Field Value string Properties DefaultDescription The reference prompt line of this action (08 §7), used when the Inspector field is empty. Every action should override it with a short phrase, such as "go to the nearest visible food and eat it". protected virtual string DefaultDescription { get; } Property Value string Description The prompt line: the Inspector's text, or DefaultDescription when it is empty. public string Description { get; } Property Value string Gene The text gene bound to this action (GENE-05), or null (V-05). The species binds it when it builds its action order. public TextGene Gene { get; } Property Value TextGene Hunts True for an action that chases and strikes animals: senses such as the sample ChasedSense read it. Override it to return true in a hunting action of your own. public virtual bool Hunts { get; } Property Value bool Index This action's index in the species' action order (SPEC-03): its place in the prompt and in the brain's probabilities, and the value of Action while it is chosen; -1 before the species is built. public int Index { get; } Property Value int Mates True for actions that seek a partner: the breed phase breeds animals that chose one (REPRO-02). public virtual bool Mates { get; } Property Value bool Name The action's name, unique in its species (ACT-01): its GameObject's name. public string Name { get; } Property Value string Overlay True for an action done in passing (a call, a scent mark): when the brain's draw picks it, the animal also does a second action, the carrier, drawn from the rest of the row; this one adds its interaction only (ACT-07). public virtual bool Overlay { get; } Property Value bool Examples A scent mark left in passing: public class MarkAction : AnimalAction { public override bool Overlay => true; protected override string DefaultDescription => "leave a scent mark; you also do your next choice"; public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) => c.OnArrival(new Mark()); // no intent: the carrier moves } Remarks The carrier is drawn from the same probabilities with every overlay set to 0, so it is what the animal would have done without the overlay (DEC-20). Each tick the carrier plans the intent and its interaction as usual; then the overlay's Act(Animal, ActContext) runs in the same context: its intent is ignored (the carrier moves the animal) and its interaction applies after the carrier's, measured from the point its own intent names (07 §3). It acts for OverlayTicks ticks, and ends when the animal becomes busy or dies. An overlay must not call Search() or Wander(): its intent is thrown away. It may not mate or hunt (V-27), and a species needs at least one action that is not an overlay (V-19). OverlayTicks How many ticks an overlay acts, counting the tick of its decision; 0 = until the next decision. Default 1: once. Ignored unless Overlay is true (ACT-07). public virtual int OverlayTicks { get; } Property Value int Rests True for actions that rest: the metabolism charges its rest cost, not its base cost, when the animal stays still (05 §4). public virtual bool Rests { get; } Property Value bool Methods Act(Animal, ActContext) Every tick while this action is chosen: say where to go, and what to do on arrival (ACT-02, ACT-03). public abstract void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) Parameters a Animal The animal that acts: alive and not busy. c ActContext The context to query and plan through; Begin(Animal) was already called for a. Remarks Called by the act phase, through ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>), once per tick for each animal that chose this action. Look the target up again each tick, so that a moving target is followed (ACT-02). The plan is the last intent and the last interaction the method set; doing nothing means stay. ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>) The batch entry point (20 §10, ARCH-12): the act phase plans every animal of the group (all chose this action) through it. The default calls Act for each; an override must give the plans Act would give. public virtual void ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal> group, ActContext c, Span<ActPlan> plans) Parameters group IReadOnlyList<Animal> The animals to plan, all of which chose this action: one animal in the sequential act orders, every such animal in the simultaneous one (ACT-30). c ActContext The shared context; call Begin(Animal) before planning each animal. plans Span<ActPlan> Where to write each animal's plan, at the same index as in group. Remarks Override it only to plan many animals at once (a job, a batched query). The single-animal Act(Animal, ActContext) stays the readable reference: the override must give the same plans, with the same random draws, and pass the same conformance tests. IsRelevant(ObservationView) Directed tests: is this observation relevant for this action (CTRL-10)? For eat, food in sight; for flee, a threat; for rest, any observation (the default). public virtual bool IsRelevant(ObservationView o) Parameters o ObservationView An observation of this species, read by sense label with Token(string). Returns bool True when the action would have something to act on in that situation. SetDescription(string) Sets the prompt line from code (WorldBuilder, tests). public void SetDescription(string text) Parameters text string The new line; empty uses DefaultDescription. WritePromptRules(PromptWriter) Adds the action's line to the prompt's action list: - name: description (PROMPT-01). public override void WritePromptRules(PromptWriter w) Parameters w PromptWriter The species' prompt writer: add a line with w.Rule("…"). Remarks Called while the species' prompt template is built, in module order. The lines go into the prompt's id, its cache keys and the species' results, so keep them stable.

MaterialPropertyBlock block; void Awake() => block = new MaterialPropertyBlock(); public override void OnShow(Animal a) { block.SetColor(ColorId, ActionColors.Of(a)); marker.SetPropertyBlock(block); } } Remarks It is the component on the root of a species' Body prefab. When an animal appears, the World takes a view from the species' ViewPool; when the animal is gone, it gives the view back. Each frame, in its LateUpdate, the World moves every view between its animal's previous and current tick positions, turns it toward where the animal goes, sets its height from the ground, then calls OnShow(Animal). Derive from it to show more of an animal (a colour per action, an animation by speed): override OnShow(Animal) and put your component on the root of the Body's prefab; a prefab without one gets a plain AnimalView. A view only reads: nothing the World computes may depend on it, so a run gives the same results with or without views (SPACE-12). ActionView is the reference. Properties AnimalId The animal shown, or -1 while the view waits in its pool (ids start at 0). public int AnimalId { get; } Property Value int Methods OnShow(Animal) Called each frame after the World placed the view: change colours or animations from the animal's state here. of the reference tick, after Sense (V-08) and before Choose actions, which waits for the answers. Each decision gets a source: memo (answered earlier in the run), same (another animal of this tick has the same key), cache (the answer cache on disk) or brain (sent now). HereSentence() => "I am at the water's edge."; public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) { if (s.Ground == null) return NoneToken; float vision = s.Vision(a); var water = s.Ground.NearestWater(a.Position, vision); return water == null ? NoneToken : TokenFor(water.Value.Distance, vision, here: water.Value.Distance <= 0.5f); } } Remarks Derive from it to sense the distance to anything: implement Read(Animal, SenseContext) with a SenseContext query and return TokenFor(float, float, bool) or NoneToken; override HasHere for a "here" token and HereSentence() for its V2 text. The base class declares the "vision" trait, builds the token list in Initialize(), writes both text styles and validates the bands. The texts state the vision trait's default (StatedVision), not each animal's own vision, so one token always gives one text (SENSE-10). Fields bandOf Per token: the band (0…k), -1 for none, -2 for here. protected readonly List<int> bandOf Field Value List<int> bands The band edges and the default vision, in meters, set in the Inspector (SENSE-20). api/EvoSim.Batch.html.summary: Class Batch Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll Headless runs (30 §6, 31 §1, 32 §4): Unity -batchmode -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] [-responsive]. In the open editor the same runs go through RunScenarioNamed (the unity CLI's eval). Worlds run in Freeze mode, outside Play mode: the World initialises itself (ARCH-04). public static class Batch Inheritance object Batch Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The command-line entry points, run from the project folder with the editor closed (or on a copy of the project), each exit Unity with 0 on success, 1 on a failure and, for RunScenario() and RunIntegrity(), 2 on an exception: Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] [-responsive]: one scenario (31 §1); each run's files go to Logs/EvoSim/runs/<scenario>-<variant>-s<seed>-<time>/. … -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunRegression: the EditMode tests of category T3 (pinned hashes, equivalences, scene checks); a report Logs/EvoSim/Reports/regression-<time>.txt. … -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarios -tier T2|T3|T4 [-ticks n]: every scenario variant of the tier, each seed twice (same hash); a report Logs/EvoSim/Reports/scenarios-<tier>-<time>.txt. … -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunIntegrity [-checks B-02,B-03] [-brain JEV] [-cpu] [-judge model]: the brain and mutator checks of 32 §2 (Integrity); one JSON and one Markdown report per check under Logs/EvoSim/Reports. From the open editor, the same code runs through RunScenarioNamed(string, string, int, int, bool) and RunTier(string, int?, out bool) (for instance with the unity CLI's eval), or the Scenario Runner window. A scene that is open in the editor cannot be run: WithScene(string, Func<World, string>) refuses it. Methods FindScenario(string) A scenario asset by asset name or by the start of its title ("S03"). public static ScenarioAsset FindScenario(string name) Parameters name string An asset name (S03_Lab1Small), the part before its first underscore, or the first word of its title. Returns ScenarioAsset The first matching asset under Assets/EvoSim/Scenarios, or null. HashOf(string, int, int, Action<World>) The events hash of a scene after a number of ticks with the random brain (R-01); configure may swap more (the mutator). public static string HashOf(string scenePath, int seed, int ticks, Action<World> configure = null) Parameters scenePath string The scene, relative to the project; it must not be open in the editor. seed int The world seed. ticks int The run length in ticks. configure Action<World> Called on the world before it initialises, after the random brain is made the default, or null. Returns string The full hash of the run's events. Remarks No run files are written. The regression tests pin these hashes. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The world doesn't validate, or the scene can't be run. Run(ScenarioAsset, string, int, int?, Action<World>, WaitMode) Runs one scenario variant and seed in Freeze mode; the recorder writes the run's files. public static string Run(ScenarioAsset scenario, string variant, int seed, int? ticks = null, Action<World> beforeInitialize = null, WaitMode mode = WaitMode.Freeze) Parameters scenario ScenarioAsset The scenario asset. variant string The variant's name; empty or unknown = the first variant. seed int The world seed. ticks int? The run length in ticks, or null for the scenario's. beforeInitialize Action<World> Called on the world after the scenario is applied and before it initialises (tests use it to swap a brain), or null. mode WaitMode Freeze (one call advances up to 100 ticks and blocks on the brains) or Responsive (one tick per call, yielding while the brains answer). Returns string A summary line: <scenario> <variant> seed <n> (<mode>): <ticks> ticks, hash <16 hex>, stopped: <reason>, <s> s, model calls …, folder <path>; or a line starting with FAILED: when the scenario can't be applied, the world doesn't validate or the scene is open. Remarks The scene is opened additively, the scenario applied (seed, length, brain, overrides, removals), the world initialised and advanced until it stops, then the scene is closed unsaved. The run folder (Logs/EvoSim/runs/<scenario>-<variant>-s<seed>-<time>/) holds run_info.json (with the scenario, variant and applied overrides), events.jsonl, stats.csv, alleles.jsonl, final_population.json and summary.json. RunIntegrity() -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunIntegrity: the brain and mutator checks (Integrity). public static void RunIntegrity() Remarks The same as -executeMethod EvoSim.Integrity.RunIntegrity, with the same options: see RunIntegrity(). RunRegression() -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunRegression: runs the EditMode tests of category T3 and exits with their result. public static void RunRegression() Remarks Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunRegression. Each failed test is logged as an error; the totals go to the log and to Logs/EvoSim/Reports/regression-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.txt. Exit code 1 when a test failed, else 0. In the open editor it runs the tests without exiting. RunScenario() Command-line entry point: runs one scenario (every seed of it unless -seed is given) and exits. public static void RunScenario() Remarks Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] [-responsive]. -scenario is an asset name or the id that starts its title (FindScenario(string)); without -variant the first variant runs; -responsive waits for the brains one tick at a time instead of freezing. Each run logs one summary line (EvoSim scenario: …) and writes its run folder under Logs/EvoSim/runs. Exit code: 0, 1 when a run failed, 2 on an exception. RunScenarioNamed(string, string, int, int, bool) The same run from the open editor (unity command eval): returns a one-line summary. public static string RunScenarioNamed(string name, string variant = "", int seed = -1, int ticks = -1, bool responsive = false) Parameters name string The scenario's asset name or id (S03). variant string The variant's name; empty = the first variant. seed int One seed, or -1 for every seed of the scenario. ticks int The run length in ticks, or -1 for the scenario's. responsive bool True to run in Responsive wait mode instead of Freeze. Returns string One summary line per seed (see Run(ScenarioAsset, string, int, int?, Action<World>, WaitMode)), or FAILED: no scenario …. Remarks For example unity command --timeout 900 --result-only eval --code 'return EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarioNamed("S03");'. Open another scene first: the scenario's own scene must not be open. RunScenarios() -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarios -tier T2: every variant of that tier (the variant's tier, else the scenario's), each seed run twice; a run fails when it doesn't finish or the two hashes differ (31: exact facts). public static void RunScenarios() Remarks Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarios -tier T2 [-ticks n] (the tier defaults to T2). The result lines go to the log and to Logs/EvoSim/Reports/scenarios-<tier>-<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>.txt; each run also writes its run folder under Logs/EvoSim/runs. Exit code 1 when a run failed, else 0. RunTier(string, int?, out bool) The same from the open editor: one line per run, and a report file. public static string RunTier(string tier, int? ticks, out bool failed) Parameters tier string The tier to run: T2 (fast), T3 (regression) or T4 (real models). ticks int? The run length in ticks, or null for each scenario's. failed bool Set to true when a run failed or its two hashes differed. Returns string One line per seed, PASS … or FAIL … | again: …, or a line saying the tier has no variant. WithScene(string, Func<World, string>) Opens a scene additively, runs the action on its World, then closes it unsaved. public static string WithScene(string scenePath, Func<World, string> action) Parameters scenePath string The scene, relative to the project (Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/….unity). action Func<World, string> What to do with the scene's first World; its string is returned. Returns string The action's result, or a line starting with FAILED: when the scene is open or has no World. Remarks A scene already open in the editor is refused: running on it would change it, then close it.

brain MemoryBrain: uniform rows, but not memoizable, so it sees every deciding animal's id. public class MemoryBrain : Brain { public readonly List<int> AnimalIds = new List<int>(); public override string Id => "memory"; public override bool Memoizable => false; public override BrainAnswer Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery> batch) { var rows = new float[batch.Count][]; for (int i = 0; i < batch.Count; i++) { AnimalIds.Add(batch[i].AnimalId); rows[i] = Uniform(batch[i].Species.Actions.Count); } return BrainAnswer.Now(rows); } } Remarks A brain is a world service: place the component under the World's services, then pick it as the World's default brain or as one species' brain (DEC-13). Derive from it, give it an Id and implement Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>); override the limits (MaxActions, MaxPromptTokens, AcceptsAttachments, CanMixSpecies), which validation checks against every species that uses the brain before the run (DEC-14, V-10, V-11, V-51). A brain behind a model server derives from HttpBrain instead, which adds retries, time-outs and parallel requests. Once per tick the ask-brains phase builds one DecisionQuery per deciding animal, answers what it can from the memo and the answer cache, and calls Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>) once with the rest (once per species when CanMixSpecies is false). The choose-actions phase waits for the BrainAnswer, checks each row, stores good rows in the memo and the cache, and draws the action. What a brain must keep: one row per query, in query order, one entry per action of the query's species in the species' action order, every entry ≥ 0, summing to 1 ± 1e-6 (DEC-11); the same query always gives the same row (DEC-12), unless Memoizable says otherwise; and it never moves an animal or changes the world (CORE-06). Fields strict The Inspector's strict setting: a failure after retries stops the run cleanly (DEC-40); off, the decision gets a uniform row and is counted as a failure. Off by default; on for HTTP brains. [SerializeField] [Tooltip("A failure after retries stops the run cleanly (DEC-40); off: uniform rows, counted.")] protected bool strict Field Value bool useCache The Inspector's cache setting: store and reuse answers in the answer cache across runs (DEC-33). Off by default; on for HTTP brains. [SerializeField] [Tooltip("Store and reuse answers in the answer cache across runs (DEC-33).")] protected bool useCache Field Value bool Properties AcceptsAttachments True when queries may carry attachments (SENSE-41); false by default, and then V-51 rejects senses that give them. public virtual bool AcceptsAttachments { get; } Property Value bool AnswerInstruction The answer instruction that ends the prompt, hard-coded per brain because its parsing depends on it (PROMPT-07); empty for brains that read no prompt. public virtual string AnswerInstruction { get; } Property Value string CanMixSpecies True when one batch may hold queries of several species (DEC-13); false gives one batch per species. public virtual bool CanMixSpecies { get; } Property Value bool Id A short name of the brain and its settings ("random", "tinynet-8"): part of memo and cache keys, and the name of its answer cache file (DEC-30, DEC-33). Two brains that may answer differently need different ids. public abstract string Id { get; } Property Value string MaxActions The most actions a species may have with this brain (DEC-14, V-11); no limit by default. public virtual int MaxActions { get; } Property Value int MaxPromptTokens The longest prompt this brain takes, in estimated tokens (DEC-14, V-11); 0 = no prompt or no limit. public virtual int MaxPromptTokens { get; } Property Value int Memoizable True (reference): equal queries get equal rows, so they are memoised and shared within a tick (DEC-30, DEC-32). A brain with memory, or one that learns, says false: every query then reaches it, with its animal's id. public virtual bool Memoizable { get; } Property Value bool Remarks False also turns the answer cache off for this brain's queries. Mode The brain's mode (points, choice…), part of cache keys (DEC-33); empty by default. public virtual string Mode { get; } Property Value string ModelIdentity The model and its pinned revision or digest, part of cache keys (DEC-33); the Id by default. public virtual string ModelIdentity { get; } Property Value string Strict True when a failure after retries stops the run cleanly (DEC-40); false when the decision gets a uniform row and is counted as a failure. Never cached either way (DEC-34). public bool Strict { get; set; } Property Value bool UsesCache True when the ask-brains phase looks answers up in the world's AnswerCache and stores new ones there (DEC-33). public bool UsesCache { get; set; } Property Value bool Methods Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>) Answers a batch of queries (DEC-11). Fast brains fill the answer at once; HTTP brains later. public abstract BrainAnswer Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery> batch) Parameters batch IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery> The queries the memo and the cache could not answer, at most one per memo key (DEC-32); never empty. Returns BrainAnswer One row or one failure per query, in query order: Now(float[][]) when every row is ready, or Later(int) filled from another thread, then completed. Remarks Called on the main thread by the ask-brains phase, once per tick and per batch. Read only the queries: a row must depend on the query alone (DEC-12), and the brain must not change the world (CORE-06). A query it can't answer is marked with Fail(int, string), never answered with a made-up row. EstimateTokens(string) Estimates a prompt's length in model tokens: one token per 4 characters, rounded up (PROMPT-06). public static int EstimateTokens(string prompt) Parameters prompt string The full prompt text; null or empty counts 0. Returns int The estimated token count, compared with MaxPromptTokens. Normalize(double[]) Makes a probability row from non-negative weights, as floats summing to 1 within 1e-6 (DEC-11). public static float[] Normalize(double[] weights) Parameters weights double[] One weight per action, in action order; negative and NaN weights count as 0. Returns float[] A new row; uniform when every weight is 0 or the sum is infinite. Uniform(int) Makes a uniform row over n actions (the random brain, and the non-strict failure answer). public static float[] Uniform(int n) Parameters n int The number of actions, at least 1. Returns float[] A new row of n entries, each 1/n.

api/EvoSim.BrainAnswer.html.summary: Class BrainAnswer Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll A brain's answer to a batch (DEC-11): one probability row per query, in query order, or a failure per query. Fast brains fill it at once; HTTP brains later, from another thread, then mark it done. public sealed class BrainAnswer Inheritance object BrainAnswer Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Answer now with Now(float[][]). Answer later with Later(int): fill each entry with SetRow(int, float[]) or Fail(int, string), from any thread, then call Complete() exactly once, also when everything failed: the choose-actions phase waits on Pending until then (TICK-03), and in the Freeze wait mode it blocks the main thread. The choose-actions phase reads each entry with Row(int) and Failed(int), checks it with Check(float[], int), and treats a bad row like a failure. Properties Count The number of queries in the batch, so of rows. public int Count { get; } Property Value int IsDone True once Complete() was called. public bool IsDone { get; } Property Value bool Milliseconds Wall-clock time from the batch's creation to its completion, in milliseconds (the summary's backend_s, 13 §5). public double Milliseconds { get; } Property Value double ModelCalls Model calls this batch made (cached answers excluded), for the summary. The brain sets it; 0 for brains without a model. public int ModelCalls { get; set; } Property Value int Pending What the Choose actions phase waits for (TICK-03). public Pending Pending { get; } Property Value Pending Methods Check(float[], int) Checks a row: one entry per action, all ≥ 0, summing to 1 ± 1e-6 (DEC-11). public static string Check(float[] row, int actions) Parameters row float[] The row to check, or null. actions int The number of actions of the query's species. Returns string What is wrong ("no row", "3 entries for 5 actions", "sums to 0.9"…), or null when the row is fine. Complete() Marks the answer done and records its time: call it once, after the last SetRow(int, float[]) or Fail(int, string). Now(float[][]) calls it for you. public void Complete() Error(int) Gives why a query has no row. public string Error(int i) Parameters i int The query's index in the batch. Returns string The failure message, "no answer" when the row was never set, or null when there is a row. Fail(int, string) The query failed (after retries): the row is not cached (DEC-34) and strict brains stop the run (DEC-40). public void Fail(int i, string error) Parameters i int The query's index in the batch. error string What went wrong, for the log; null gives "failed". Failed(int) Tells whether a query has no row: it failed, or the brain never answered it. public bool Failed(int i) Parameters i int The query's index in the batch. Returns bool True when there is no row. Later(int) Makes an answer that will be filled later; call Complete() when every row or failure is in. public static BrainAnswer Later(int count) Parameters count int The number of queries in the batch. Returns BrainAnswer An empty answer, not done yet. Later(int, Pending) Makes an answer filled later, done when the given pending is done (fakes that answer after N calls). public static BrainAnswer Later(int count, Pending wait) Parameters count int The number of queries in the batch. wait Pending What the choose-actions phase waits for instead of this answer's own pending. Returns BrainAnswer An empty answer, not done yet; Complete() is still needed. Now(float[][]) Makes an answer given at once, already complete. public static BrainAnswer Now(float[][] rows) Parameters rows float[][] One probability row per query, in query order; a null row counts as a failure. Returns BrainAnswer The complete answer. Row(int) Gives the row of one query. public float[] Row(int i) Parameters i int The query's index in the batch. Returns float[] The row, or null when the query failed or has no answer yet. SetRow(int, float[]) Sets the probability row of one query. public void SetRow(int i, float[] row) Parameters i int The query's index in the batch. row float[] One entry per action of the query's species, in action order, ≥ 0, summing to 1 (DEC-11).

of the reference tick, after Ask brains (V-08) and before Act. It is the phase the tick waits at while the brains think: in the Freeze wait mode the main thread blocks, in the Responsive mode the tick resumes here on a later frame (SPACE-14). Either way the result is the same. An animal that shares another's key (DEC-32) takes that animal's row. Every deciding animal gets a new action, its searching and bred-this-period flags are cleared (DEC-03), and its observation, situation and probabilities are kept for the inspector (DEC-21). When the draw picks an overlay (ACT-07), a second draw from the same stream picks the carrier among the other actions, in proportion to their probabilities (DEC-20). Species without overlays draw exactly once. Methods Initialize() Finds the World's answer cache, if any. public override void Initialize() Remarks Look up what you need here, by role or name (Service<T>(), Phase<T>()), and reset your own state: the same object starts every run of the World. A service is initialised before the species' modules; a phase after them. Run(TickContext) Stores the answers, then draws the action of every deciding animal. public override void Run(TickContext t) Parameters t TickContext The current tick's context: the World, the tick number and the random streams. Remarks A strict brain's failure stops the World before any action is drawn, so the tick changes nothing (RAND-20). Validate(ValidationReport) Reports this phase placed before Ask brains, or without it (V-08). public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Only read: validation must not change the scene. Offer a change as a ValidationFix. WaitsFor(TickContext) The brains' answers to this tick's batches that are not in yet, or null when all are in (or nothing was sent). public override Pending WaitsFor(TickContext t) Parameters t TickContext The current tick's context. Returns Pending What must be done before Run(TickContext), or null when nothing is awaited. A Pending already done lets the phase run at once. Remarks The World asks before every attempt to run the phase: in Responsive mode, again at every Advance call while the tick waits. Return the same work for the same tick, and don't change the world or draw random numbers here, so both wait modes give the same run (SPACE-14, RAND-11).

InCover(Vector3 p) => p.x >= MinX && p.x <= MaxX; public override bool NearestCover(Vector3 p, float radius, out Vector3 point, out float distance) { point = new Vector3(Mathf.Clamp(p.x, MinX, MaxX), reference, UniformCrossover: public class UniformCrossover : Crossover { public override Allele[] Cross(Genome a, Genome b, RandomStream rng) { CheckSpecies(a, b); var child = new Allele[a.Count]; for (int i = 0; i < child.Length; i++) child[i] = rng.NextBool() ? a[i] : b[i]; return child; } } Remarks One crossover per species, placed under it and found by type (Species.Module<Crossover>()). At each conception the breed phase calls Cross(Genome, Genome, RandomStream) once per baby of a two-parent litter, so siblings differ (GENE-32), and Copy(Genome) per baby of a one-parent litter. Mutations are drawn afterwards, on the result. Without a crossover, babies copy their first parent (V-26 warns). What an implementation must keep: call CheckSpecies(Genome, Genome) first; return a new array with one allele per locus, in locus order, taken from that same locus (loci are homologous, GENE-30); draw only from the stream it is given; never change the parents' genomes. Methods CheckSpecies(Genome, Genome) Throws unless both genomes belong to this species (SPEC-04, GENE-06). protected void CheckSpecies(Genome a, Genome b) Parameters a Genome The first parent's genome. b Genome The second parent's genome. Exceptions InvalidOperationException A genome belongs to another species. Copy(Genome) Asexual reproduction: the baby copies its parent (GENE-31). public virtual Allele[] Copy(Genome parent) Parameters parent Genome The only parent's genome. Returns Allele[] A new array with the parent's alleles. Cross(Genome, Genome, RandomStream) The baby's alleles from two parents (GENE-30), drawing from the mutation stream. public abstract Allele[] Cross(Genome a, Genome b, RandomStream rng) Parameters a Genome The first parent's genome: the animal that chose to mate. b Genome The partner's genome. rng RandomStream The species' mutation stream (RAND-03): draw only from it. Returns Allele[] A new array with one allele per locus, in locus order.

DiesOfThirst (22 §1): thirst grows in the death phase, and kills at a threshold. public class DiesOfThirst : DeathRule { static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> causes = System.Array.AsReadOnly(new[] { "thirst" }); Thirst thirst; public override IEnumerable<string> Causes => causes; public override void Initialize() => thirst = Species.Module<Thirst>(); public override string CauseOfDeath(Animal a) { if (thirst == null) return null; a[thirst.Value] += thirst.PerTick; // ages with the animal, in the death phase return a[thirst.Value] >= thirst.Deadly ? "thirst" : null; } } Remarks Derive from it, implement CauseOfDeath(Animal), list every cause it can give in Causes, and place the component under a species. Each tick the death phase first removes killed animals and ages every living animal by one tick (ANIM-35); then it asks the species' death rules, in module order, through CheckAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, string[]). The first rule that names a cause for an animal decides: later rules are not asked about it. The phase records the death and removes the animal; the rule only names the cause. A cause is a short lower-case name, such as starvation: it appears in death events and as the statistics column deaths_<cause>. Draw random numbers only from the species' streams. Properties Causes The causes this rule can give, for the statistics columns (deaths_<cause>). public virtual IEnumerable<string> Causes { get; } Property Value IEnumerable<string> Remarks Empty by default: list every name CauseOfDeath(Animal) may return. api/EvoSim.DecisionMemo.html.summary: Class DecisionMemo Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll Within a run, the answer for a key (species, brain, brain-visible genome key, observation) is computed once and reused (DEC-30). The entries are resolved by name in Declare(SpeciesBuilder) and Initialize(), and again when a species is added during a run (RebuildFoodWeb()). The World derives the food web from Striking(Species): the species a diet strikes are its prey, and it is their threat (SPEC-12). The interaction resolver asks Grazing(ResourceLayer), Striking(Species), Scavenging(Species) or EatingEggs(Species) before every meal, then EnergyFrom(Animal, EdibleTarget, float) for its energy and KillChanceAgainst(Animal, Animal) for a strike's odds. All six are virtual: derive from Diet to make meals depend on the eater or the prey. The species' modules find it with Species.Module<Diet>(), so keep one diet per species. Properties Entries The entries as written in the Inspector, in diet order. public IReadOnlyList<Diet.Entry> Entries { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Diet.Entry> KillChance The kill-chance trait, kill.chance, declared when the diet strikes (or may strike) a species; invalid otherwise. public TraitId KillChance { get; } Property Value TraitId Resolved The entries resolved at initialisation (ARCH-08), in diet order. public IReadOnlyList<EdibleTarget> Resolved { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<EdibleTarget> Strikes True when an entry resolved to a species: this diet strikes animals. public bool Strikes { get; } Property Value bool Methods Declare(SpeciesBuilder) Resolves the entries and declares the kill.chance trait (from 0 to 1) when the diet strikes, or may strike, a species. public override void Declare(SpeciesBuilder b) Parameters b SpeciesBuilder The species' declarations: call DeclareStat(string, StatStart, float, float, TraitId) and DeclareTrait(string, float, float, float, bool), and keep the ids they return. Remarks Called before any module's Initialize: don't look up other modules here. Two modules may declare the same name: they get the same id, and the first declaration counts (V-38 if they differ). EatingEggs(Species) The entry for eating eggs of this species, if listed and the egg kind is edible (REPRO-23); else null. public virtual EdibleTarget EatingEggs(Species s) Parameters s Species The species that laid the egg; species cloned from a listed one count too. Returns EdibleTarget The resolved entry, or null when the diet doesn't eat those eggs or the egg system has no Edible. EnergyFrom(Animal, EdibleTarget, float) The energy a meal gives this eater: the entry's energy by default (ACT-11); override it to depend on the eater. public virtual float EnergyFrom(Animal eater, EdibleTarget entry, float energy) Parameters eater Animal The animal that eats. entry EdibleTarget The diet entry the meal comes from. energy float The meal's energy before this hook, in points: the edible's energy (per item, kill or carcass portion) times the entry's scale. Returns float The energy gained, in points; the energy stat then stays at or below its maximum (ANIM-22). Remarks Called by the interaction resolver for every graze, kill, carcass portion and egg. Grazing(ResourceLayer) The entry for grazing this layer, if the diet lists it and it is edible (SPEC-13); else null. public virtual EdibleTarget Grazing(ResourceLayer layer) Parameters layer ResourceLayer The resource layer of the item to graze. Returns EdibleTarget The resolved entry, or null when the diet doesn't graze that layer or the layer has no Edible. Has(EdibleTargetKind) Whether the diet has an edible entry of this kind. public bool Has(EdibleTargetKind kind) Parameters kind EdibleTargetKind Layer, species, carcass or egg. Returns bool True when an entry of that kind resolved and its target has an Edible. Initialize() Resolves the entries again, once every module of every species has declared. public override void Initialize() Remarks Find things by role or name (ARCH-08): Species.Module<Energy>(), World.Service<Ground>(), Species.Declarations.FindTrait("vision"). Reset your own state here: the same object starts every run. KillChanceAgainst(Animal, Animal) The chance that this hunter's strike kills that prey (ACT-11): the hunter's kill-chance trait by default. public virtual float KillChanceAgainst(Animal hunter, Animal prey) Parameters hunter Animal The animal that strikes. prey Animal The animal struck, within reach and edible for this diet. Returns float A probability from 0 to 1; 0 when no kill-chance trait was declared. Remarks Called by the interaction resolver at every strike. Override it for odds that depend on the prey. Resolve() Resolves the entries by name (ARCH-08); called again when species are added during a run. public void Resolve() Remarks Called by Declare(SpeciesBuilder), Initialize() and RebuildFoodWeb(). Names that match nothing are kept for validation (V-20). Scavenging(Species) The entry for scavenging carcasses of this species, if listed and edible; else null. public virtual EdibleTarget Scavenging(Species s) Parameters s Species The species of the killed animal; species cloned from a listed one count too (SPEC-31). Returns EdibleTarget The entry as it applies to that species, or null when the diet doesn't list its carcasses or they are not edible. Set(params Entry[]) Sets the entries from code (WorldBuilder, scenarios). public Diet Set(params Diet.Entry[] entries) Parameters entries Entry[] The new entries, in diet order; they replace the old ones. Returns Diet This diet, to chain calls. Remarks Call it before the world initializes, or call Resolve() afterwards. Set(params string[]) Sets the entries by name, scale 1. public Diet Set(params string[] targets) Parameters targets string[] The targets, in diet order, such as "Grass", "prey" or "carcass:prey". Returns Diet This diet, to chain calls. SetKillChance(float) Sets the kill-chance setting, the default of the kill.chance trait, before the species declares its traits. public void SetKillChance(float p) Parameters p float A probability; clamped to [0, 1]. Striking(Species) The entry for striking this species, if listed and edible (SPEC-13); else null. public virtual EdibleTarget Striking(Species s) Parameters s Species The species of the struck animal; species cloned from a listed one count too (SPEC-31). Returns EdibleTarget The entry as it applies to that species, or null when the diet doesn't strike it or its Edible is missing or disabled. Remarks The World also calls it to derive the food web: the species it returns an entry for are this species' prey (SPEC-12). Validate(ValidationReport) Reports entries that name nothing (V-20), targets without an Edible (V-24, with a fix) and a diet with no food source at all (V-22). public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Called after every Initialize and after the food web is derived; only read, never change the scene. WritePromptRules(PromptWriter) The carcass system's line for a diet that scavenges carcasses (08 §7). public override void WritePromptRules(PromptWriter w) Parameters w PromptWriter The species' prompt writer: add a line with w.Rule("…"). Remarks Called while the species' prompt template is built, in module order. The lines go into the prompt's id, its cache keys and the species' results, so keep them stable.

eat action of the prey, and teaching-path exercise 4. Each tick it: finds the nearest food item in sight that its diet grazes (NearestResource(Animal, string)), on every grazed layer, or only on the layer its target names; with none in sight, calls Search() and stops there; stays when the item is within GrazeReach, else walks to it with a stop distance of 0 (MOVE-04); in both cases asks to graze it on arrival (Graze(ResourceItem)), so the animal eats on the very tick it arrives (ACT-10). With a target of "egg:<species>" it eats eggs instead (22 §15): it walks to the nearest egg of that species its diet eats (NearestEgg(Animal, Species)) and eats it on arrival (EatEgg(Egg)). Properties DefaultDescription The reference prompt line of this action (08 §7), used when the Inspector field is empty. api/EvoSim.Editor.Exercises.html.summary: Class Exercises Namespace EvoSim.Editor Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll EvoSim ▸ Exercises (21 §6, 22 §0): Replace with stub writes the student stub of a reference module into Assets/Student and swaps the module for it in the open scenes, keeping its settings; Restore reference undoes it. public static class Exercises Inheritance object Exercises Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub ▸ 1 RestAction … 14 LlmMutation, in the order of the teaching path (Path). The first time, the menu copies Assets/EvoSim/Exercises/My<Reference>.cs.txt to Assets/Student/Exercises/My<Reference>.cs (with the student assemblies, if missing) and waits for Unity to compile it; after the reload, every instance of the reference module in the open scenes is swapped for the student's class, which is marked [ExerciseOf(typeof(Reference))]. The student then writes the stub, in their own way: nothing grades it, and the conformance suite of its kind (Test Runner, EditMode) only checks that it fits the system. EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Restore reference puts every reference module back in the open scenes; the student's files stay. Both swaps keep the inspector settings and the component's place, and can be undone (Edit ▸ Undo). Save the scene to keep a swap. Returns Type The student's compiled stub class (the first by full name when several match), or null. Swap(Component, Type) Replaces a component by one of another type on the same object, at the same place among its components (module order matters, SPEC-03), copying every serialized field the two share and the enabled flag. Undoable. public static Component Swap(Component from, Type to) Parameters from Component The component to replace; it is destroyed. to Type The new component's class. api/EvoSim.Editor.PromptPreview.html.summary: Class PromptPreview Namespace EvoSim.Editor Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll The species inspector's prompt preview (21 §3, PROMPT-06): built by the same code as the Ask brains phase, so it is exactly what the brain receives — for JEV, its whole input text (T-PROMPT-05). public static class PromptPreview Inheritance object PromptPreview Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The SpeciesInspector calls it (and the editor tests, which check that it matches what the brains are sent). Nothing here changes the world except FounderGenome(World, Species, int), which registers the founder alleles it uses in the world's allele registry. Methods For(Species, Genome, Observation, TextStyle, Brain) The text a brain receives for a genome and an observation of a species. public static string For(Species s, Genome genome, Observation o, TextStyle style, Brain brain) Parameters s Species The species whose prompt template, senses and genes are used. genome Genome The genome whose brain-visible sentences fill the genes block, or null for no genes. o Observation The situation: one token per sense. style TextStyle The situation text style (V1 tokens or V2 sentences). brain Brain The brain that would answer: an HTTP brain gives the text it would send (JEV writes its own input), any other brain the filled prompt with its answer instruction; null leaves the answer instruction empty. Returns string The full prompt text. FounderGenome(World, Species, int) A founder genome for the preview: the first founder of each gene (or the one at the given index). public static Genome FounderGenome(World w, Species s, int which = 0) Parameters w World The world whose allele registry records the founder alleles. s Species The species whose genes are read, in locus order. which int The index in each gene's founder pool; a gene with fewer founders takes its last one. Returns Genome A genome with one founder allele per locus. Query(Species, Genome, Observation, TextStyle) The query the Ask brains phase would build (DEC-10). public static DecisionQuery Query(Species s, Genome genome, Observation o, TextStyle style) Parameters s Species The species of the deciding animal. genome Genome The genome to read, or null: no genes, and the species id as the genome key. o Observation The situation: one token per sense. style TextStyle The situation text style (V1 or V2). Returns DecisionQuery A query as a brain receives it, with no animal id (-1). Tokens(string) The token estimate shown next to the preview (PROMPT-06). public static int Tokens(string text) Parameters text string A prompt text. Returns int About one token per four characters, as EstimateTokens(string) counts.

api/EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.html.title: Class RealTimeRuns | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.html.summary: Class RealTimeRuns Namespace EvoSim.Editor Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll The real-time visual test from the unity CLI (eval): a headless reference run, a scene set up for Play mode, and the run's status while it plays. Levels: L0 the random brain and no mutation (offline), L1 the scene's brain (JEV) and no mutation, L2 the scene's brain and mutator. Example: unity command eval --code 'return EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.Headless("HideVsFlee", 1234, 600, "L2", "RT-L2-headless");' public static class RealTimeRuns Inheritance object RealTimeRuns Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks A real-time test compares what a watcher sees in Play mode with a headless run of the same seed: Headless(string, int, int, string, string) (blocks until the end) or HeadlessStart(string, int, int, string, string) and HeadlessStatus() (stepped, for long runs with model calls): the reference run, with its files and hash. PreparePlay(string, int, int, float, string, string, bool, float, string), then Play (the unity CLI's editor_play), then Status() while it plays: the watched run, with the same settings as the Windows player. Behaviour(string, int, int, string): counts, tick by tick, what the watcher should see (hiding, kills, births). With the editor closed: Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.FromCommandLine -do headless|behaviour -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -level L2 [-run NAME] -quit (see FromCommandLine()). Headless runs write their run folder under Logs/EvoSim/runs. The scene must not be open in the editor. Methods Behaviour(string, int, int, string) What a watcher should see, counted tick by tick on a headless replay (step 5): hunting predators whose nearest prey in sight is hidden in cover (they lose it), hunters targeting a hidden prey (never), prey hiding in cover, kills, carcass portions, prey meals and food regrown, babies farther than 2 m from both parents. public static string Behaviour(string scene, int seed, int ticks, string level) Parameters scene string A reference scene name; it must not be open in the editor. seed int The world seed. ticks int The run length in ticks. level string L0, L1 or L2 (SetLevel(World, string)). Returns string One line of counts (in animal-ticks unless said), or a line starting with FAILED:. Remarks No run files are written. The scene needs species with the ids prey and predator (the Lab 1 scenes, HideVsFlee, Terrain_Locomotion). FromCommandLine() Batch entry point (the editor closed): -do headless|behaviour -scene S -seed n -ticks n -level L0|L1|L2 [-run name]; the result line goes to the log and to Logs/EvoSim/realtime-batch.txt (appended). public static void FromCommandLine() Remarks Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.FromCommandLine -do headless -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -level L2 [-run NAME] -quit. Defaults: -do headless, -scene HideVsFlee, -seed 1234, -ticks 600, -level L0, -run <scene>-<level>-s<seed>-<ticks>. It does not exit Unity by itself: pass -quit. HashIn(string) The events hash recorded in a run folder's summary.json. public static string HashIn(string runFolder) Parameters runFolder string A run folder, such as one under Logs/EvoSim/runs. Returns string The events_hash of its summary.json, or a sentence saying the file is missing. Headless(string, int, int, string, string) A headless Freeze run with files (step 2): returns the events hash, the run folder and the model calls. public static string Headless(string scene, int seed, int ticks, string level, string runName) Parameters scene string A reference scene name; it must not be open in the editor. seed int The world seed. ticks int The run length in ticks. level string L0, L1 or L2 (SetLevel(World, string)). runName string The run folder's name under Logs/EvoSim/runs. Returns string A summary line (ticks, full events hash, brain, brain and mutator calls, cache hits, mutations, seconds, run folder), or a line starting with FAILED:. Remarks It blocks the editor until the run ends; for a long run with model calls use HeadlessStart(string, int, int, string, string). HeadlessStart(string, int, int, string, string) The same headless run, advanced from the editor's update loop a few ticks at a time, so a long run with model calls never blocks a CLI call (the pipeline's timer); poll HeadlessStatus(). The result also goes to Logs/EvoSim/realtime-headless.txt. public static string HeadlessStart(string scene, int seed, int ticks, string level, string runName) Parameters scene string A reference scene name; it must not be open in the editor. seed int The world seed. ticks int The run length in ticks. level string L0, L1 or L2 (SetLevel(World, string)). runName string The run folder's name under Logs/EvoSim/runs. Returns string started … with the run folder, the status of the run already going, or a line starting with FAILED:. Remarks One stepped run at a time. A script reload during the run loses it (the static state is reset). HeadlessStatus() The stepped headless run's progress, or its result once it stopped. public static string HeadlessStatus() Returns string running … with the tick, calls and seconds; or the last result line; or no headless run. LevelArgs(string) The player's arguments of a level (PlayerArgs): L0 the random brain and no mutation, L1 no mutation, L2 the scene as it is. public static string LevelArgs(string level) Parameters level string L0, L1 or L2; anything else counts as L2. Returns string -brain Random -noMutation, -noMutation, or an empty string. PreparePlay(string, int, int, float, string, string, bool, float, string) Opens a scene for a watched Play-mode run (step 3) without changing it: the settings are kept as a player command line (PlayerArgs) and applied to the World when Play mode wakes it (World.Configuring), as the Windows player does. Enter Play mode afterwards (editor_play); leaving Play mode forgets them. public static string PreparePlay(string scene, int seed, int ticks, float ticksPerSecond, string level, string runName, bool responsive = true, float captureSeconds = 10, string extra = "") Parameters scene string A reference scene name. seed int The world seed (-seed). ticks int The run length in ticks (-ticks). ticksPerSecond float The pace of the watched run, in ticks per second (-speed). level string L0, L1 or L2 (LevelArgs(string)). runName string The run folder's name (-run). responsive bool True to wait for the brains while Unity keeps rendering; false to freeze (-wait). captureSeconds float Seconds between two screen captures (-capture; 0 = start and end only). extra string More player arguments, such as -stagger or -minutes 10; empty for none. Returns string <scene> open, unchanged; on Play: <arguments>, or why nothing was prepared. Remarks For example unity command --result-only eval --code 'return EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.PreparePlay("HideVsFlee", 1234, 600, 5f, "L2", "RUN");'. The scene replaces the open scenes, so they must have no unsaved change. ScenePath(string) The path of a reference scene from its name. public static string ScenePath(string scene) Parameters scene string A scene name of ScenesFolder, such as HideVsFlee. Returns string Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/<scene>.unity. SetLevel(World, string) Sets a level on a World: L0 random brain and no mutation; L1 the scene's own default brain, no mutation; L2 both on. public static string SetLevel(World w, string level) Parameters w World A World that has not initialised yet. level string L0, L1 or L2. Returns string Null when the level was set; otherwise the problem (an unknown level, or no random brain for L0). Status() The run in Play mode now: tick, state, pace, numbers, hash, folders (step 3, polled). public static string Status() Returns string One line about the first World found: tick, state and what it waits for, ticks per second and frames per second, brain and mutator calls, events hash, run and capture folders, memory (MB); or not playing / no World.

api/EvoSim.Editor.ReferenceScenes.html.summary: Class ReferenceScenes Namespace EvoSim.Editor Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll Builds the reference content (20 §2, §7; 09 §3): the allele pools from the prototype's pool files, the module prefabs (Modules/), placeholder bodies, and the scenes Lab1_Small, Lab1_Full, HideVsFlee, ThreeSpecies, Terrain_Locomotion and Sandbox. The scenes are then the configuration (ARCH-01): edit them, not this builder, unless the reference itself changes. Scenes are opened additively from an empty file, so the editor's own open scene is never touched. public static class ReferenceScenes Inheritance object ReferenceScenes Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Menus: EvoSim ▸ Build Reference Scenes (BuildAll()) rebuilds everything and overwrites the six scenes, the pools, the module prefabs and the scenario assets; EvoSim ▸ Reference ▸ Update Reference Scenes (UpdateReferenceScenes()) only brings the saved scenes to the current reference settings. The same builder makes the World of GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ New World (NewWorld(string, float)), so a new world and the reference worlds have the same tree. Fields BodiesFolder The placeholder bodies' folder (prefabs and materials): Assets/EvoSim/Modules/Bodies. public const string BodiesFolder = "Assets/EvoSim/Modules/Bodies" Field Value string ModulesFolder The module prefabs' folder: actions at its root, senses in Senses/, genes in Genes/. public const string ModulesFolder = "Assets/EvoSim/Modules" Field Value string PoolsFolder The allele pool assets' folder, one asset per locus: Assets/EvoSim/Data/AllelePools. public const string PoolsFolder = "Assets/EvoSim/Data/AllelePools" Field Value string ReferenceDecisionPeriod Ticks between two decisions in the reference worlds (DEC-01; owner 2026-10-11: back to 4 after trying 20 and 10). public const int ReferenceDecisionPeriod = 4 Field Value int Root The EvoSim package folder, relative to the project. public const string Root = "Assets/EvoSim" Field Value string ScenariosFolder The scenario assets' folder: Assets/EvoSim/Scenarios. public const string ScenariosFolder = "Assets/EvoSim/Scenarios" Field Value string ScenesFolder The reference scenes' folder: Assets/EvoSim/Scenes. public const string ScenesFolder = "Assets/EvoSim/Scenes" Field Value string Methods BuildAll() EvoSim ▸ Build Reference Scenes: rebuilds the allele pools, the module prefabs and bodies, the six reference scenes and the scenario assets, overwriting them, then saves the assets. [MenuItem("EvoSim/Build Reference Scenes")] public static void BuildAll() Remarks Course staff only, when the reference itself changes: the scenes are the configuration (ARCH-01), and a rebuild erases any edit made in them. Scenes open in the editor should be closed first. BuildPools() The allele pools of 09 §3, one asset per locus, from Data/Pools (the prototype's v2 pools) plus the Unity hide draft. public static Dictionary<string, AllelePool> BuildPools() Returns Dictionary<string, AllelePool> The pools by species.locus, such as prey.eat or predator.hunt. Remarks Each pool is written to PoolsFolder as <species>_<locus>.asset, its founders and contrast pair (pro, anti) overwritten. BuildScenarios() The scenario assets whose scenes exist (31 §2); more come with the samples (M11). public static void BuildScenarios() Remarks Each asset of ScenariosFolder is created if missing, and its title, scene, length, brain, tier, seeds (1234, 7, 42 unless set after), expected facts and variants overwritten. ControlSentences() The control sentences of GENE-23: 20 shuffled-word and 20 irrelevant ones (Data/Pools/control_alleles_v1.json). public static List<string> ControlSentences() Returns List<string> The shuffled-word sentences, then the irrelevant ones. UpdateReferenceScenes() Brings the saved reference scenes to the builder's reference without rebuilding them: the reference decision period (DEC-01, owner 2026-10-11) and a staggered DecisionSchedule in every species' Life group (DEC-04, owner 2026-10-10); a species that has a schedule keeps it. [MenuItem("EvoSim/Reference/Update Reference Scenes")] public static string UpdateReferenceScenes() Returns string One line per scene: what changed, nothing, or open in the editor, skipped. Remarks EvoSim ▸ Reference ▸ Update Reference Scenes. A scene open in the editor is skipped; the others are opened additively, changed, saved when something changed, and closed. The result is logged.
