Project and Player settings are left as they are. Batch: -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.VisualPlayerBuild.BuildFromCommandLine [-scenes HideVsFlee,Lab1_Full] [-out folder]. Run it: EvoSim.exe -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -speed 5 -brain JEV -capture 10 -quitAtEnd -screen-fullscreen 0 -logFile player.log (PlayerArgs). public static class VisualPlayerBuild Inheritance object VisualPlayerBuild Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks From the menu: EvoSim ▸ Build ▸ Visual Player (a dialog shows the result). Batch, editor closed: Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.VisualPlayerBuild.BuildFromCommandLine [-scenes HideVsFlee,Lab1_Full] [-out Builds/EvoSim/2026-10-11]. From the open editor with the unity CLI: BuildLater(string, string), or CompilePlayerScriptsLater() to check that the player scripts compile. The Standalone scripting backend must be Mono: the build refuses otherwise rather than change Player settings (RAND-12 compares Mono runs). The player writes its run files and captures next to the exe, under Logs/EvoSim/, and keeps its answer cache in Library/EvoSim/AnswerCache. Returns string The build result with the exe's full path, scene count, size (MB), time (s), errors and warnings; or Failed: … when a scene is missing or the scripting backend isn't Mono. The result line is logged as EvoSim visual player: …; exit code 1 on failure. BuildFromMenu() EvoSim ▸ Build ▸ Visual Player: builds the player with the six default scenes into today's folder, Builds/EvoSim/<yyyy-MM-dd>/EvoSim.exe, and shows the result in a dialog. [MenuItem("EvoSim/Build/Visual Player")] public static void BuildFromMenu() BuildLater(string, string) For the unity CLI's eval in the open editor: starts the build after the call returns (a long synchronous call outlives the pipeline's timer) and writes the result to Logs/EvoSim/visual-player-build.txt. public static string BuildLater(string sceneList = null, string folder = null) Parameters sceneList string Comma-separated scene names, or null for DefaultScenes. folder string The output folder, or null for DefaultFolder(). Validate runs the validation (ValidationPanel); in Play mode the button shows the report of the world's initialisation. A fix button applies its fix and validates again. A student who wants an inspector for a module of their own writes the same kind of class: [CustomEditor(typeof(MyModule))] on a class deriving from UnityEditor.Editor, in an Editor folder or editor assembly. Methods OnInspectorGUI() Draws the state, the run controls (Play mode), the World's fields, the phases, the services and the validation. public override void OnInspectorGUI() RequiresConstantRepaint() True in Play mode, so the tick and state stay current. public override bool RequiresConstantRepaint() Returns bool

api/EvoSim.Editor.html.title: Namespace EvoSim.Editor | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.Editor.html.summary: Namespace EvoSim.Editor Classes AnimalInspectorWindow The selected animal (21 §4, lab C): stats, traits, genome sentences, last situation, last probabilities as bars, current action and target, busy reason, parents and offspring. Click an animal's view to select it. AskTheBrainWindow Ask the brain (21 §4, labs C and I): build a genome (founders, edited sentences, a gene's contrast pair, control sentences), pick a situation, and ask several brains side by side; a directed test asks with a gene's pro sentence, then with its anti one, so P(action) can be compared. Queries are built from texts only: nothing is registered in the world, so asking never changes a run. BrainHealthWindow Brain health (21 §4): every brain and mutator client of the current world with its host, a Test connection button (V-60, on demand), model and revision or digest, latency, failures, and the answer cache's size and hits. EcologyMonitorWindow The ecology monitor (21 §4, labs A and B): population per species over time, deaths by cause, births, action shares, memo hit rate, ticks per second — from LiveStatistics and the species counters. EditorWorlds What the windows look at (EDIT-05): the worlds of the open scenes, the selected world, the selected animal. EventLogWindow The event log (21 §4, lab D): the running world's events as they are recorded, filtered by kind, species and animal; following an animal shows its line and its descendants' births. EvoSimOverlay The scene-view overlay (21 §5): toggles for food, cover, carcasses, eggs and action letters, and species filters. Exercises EvoSim ▸ Exercises (21 §6, 22 §0): Replace with stub writes the student stub of a reference module into Assets/Student and swaps the module for it in the open scenes, keeping its settings; Restore reference undoes it. FoodWebWindow The food web (21 §4): species and layers as a graph with graze, strike, scavenge and egg edges, the derived threats, and the food-web warnings of validation. GenePoolWindow The gene pool (21 §4, labs D and E): per locus, the allele shares among the living over time (stacked), the current top alleles with their text and origin, and the lineage of a selected allele as a chain of texts; number genes as histograms of the living animals' values. PlayModeGate EDIT-01: before Play, every enabled World in the open scenes is validated with the same engine as World.Initialize; errors cancel Play and are logged with the object at fault (EDIT-02). PromptPreview The species inspector's prompt preview (21 §3, PROMPT-06): built by the same code as the Ask brains phase, so it is exactly what the brain receives — for JEV, its whole input text (T-PROMPT-05). RealTimeRuns The real-time visual test from the unity CLI (eval): a headless reference run, a scene set up for Play mode, and the run's status while it plays. Levels: L0 the random brain and no mutation (offline), L1 the scene's brain (JEV) and no mutation, L2 the scene's brain and mutator. Example: unity command eval --code 'return EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.Headless("HideVsFlee", 1234, 600, "L2", "RT-L2-headless");' ReferenceScenes Builds the reference content (20 §2, §7; 09 §3): the allele pools from the prototype's pool files, the module prefabs (Modules/), placeholder bodies, and the scenes Lab1_Small, Lab1_Full, HideVsFlee, ThreeSpecies, Terrain_Locomotion and Sandbox. The scenes are then the configuration (ARCH-01): edit them, not this builder, unless the reference itself changes. Scenes are opened additively from an empty file, so the editor's own open scene is never touched. RunViews Makes a scene watchable (20 §6): a "Run views" object with the ground, entity markers, overlay and capture, and a WorldCamera on the main camera; and the reference bodies (a capsule standing on the ground, a nose that shows where it goes, a marker in the colour of its action). All of them only read the World (SPACE-12). ScenarioRunnerWindow The scenario runner (21 §4, lab G): the scenario assets, a variant, seeds and length; runs them headless (Freeze, the same code as EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario) and lists the results; "twice" checks the reproducibility fact. SceneDrawing The scene view (21 §5): gizmos for the selected animal (vision, a line to its target, a 1 m circle coloured by action) and, as the overlay's toggles say, food items, cover, carcasses, eggs and a letter per action above each animal (stable colours from the action order). Drawing only reads the world (SPACE-12). ScriptTemplates Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim (21 §6): script templates for a new sense, action, gene kind, stat, phase, brain or mutation operator — each with the methods to override and a matching test — and a mutation deck. Scripts go to Assets/Student (with its assembly), tests to Assets/Student/Tests (with a test assembly that sees EvoSim.Testing). SpeciesInspector The Species inspector (21 §3, EDIT-04): read-only tables computed from the subtree (actions, senses, genes, stats and traits, food, population), the observation-space size, the signature, and a prompt preview built by the same code as the Ask brains phase (T-PROMPT-05). ValidationPanel The validation list of the inspectors (EDIT-01, EDIT-02): one line per message with its severity, a button that selects the object at fault, and the fix button when the validator offers one. VisualPlayerBuild Builds a Windows player that draws a run (07 real-time test): Windows 64-bit, Mono, the reference scenes (HideVsFlee first) given here, not in the Build Settings, into Builds/EvoSim/<date>/EvoSim.exe. Project and Player settings are left as they are. Batch: -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.VisualPlayerBuild.BuildFromCommandLine [-scenes HideVsFlee,Lab1_Full] [-out folder]. Run it: EvoSim.exe -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -speed 5 -brain JEV -capture 10 -quitAtEnd -screen-fullscreen 0 -logFile player.log (PlayerArgs). WorldFactory Creating things from the menus (21 §6): a new world with the default tree, a new species with the reference body modules, and actions, senses and genes from the module prefabs in Modules/. The static methods are what the menus call, so tests build worlds exactly as a student does. WorldInspector The World inspector (21 §3): state and tick, run controls in Play mode, the settings, the phases in order with their enable toggles, the services, and the validation panel.

one's own (from EvoSim's test probes): nothing moves or rots unless given a lifetime. public class Fruit : Entity { public override string Kind => "fruit"; } public class FruitSystem : EntitySystem<Fruit> { public override string Kind => "fruit"; } // From a phase: a fruit falls at p and rots in 50 ticks. World.Service<FruitSystem>().Add(new Fruit { Position = p, LifetimeLeft = 50 }); Remarks Derive from it with your entity type, give the kind a name (Kind), and place the component under the World (reference: under Environment). Entities enter through Add(T); actions and senses find them with Nearest(Vector3, float, Animal, Func<T, Animal, bool>, out T, out float) or NearestEntity<T>(Animal, float, Func<T, Animal, bool>). Once per tick the environment phase calls UpdateEntities(TickContext): Move(T, TickContext) each one, count lifetimes down, then remove the used-up and expired ones, calling OnRemoved(T, string, TickContext) for each. The list stays in creation (id) order, so every loop over it is deterministic (RAND-05). An override of Move(T, TickContext) draws random numbers only from a named stream of t. Put an Edible on the same GameObject to make the kind food; diets then name it "<kind>:<species>" (22 §15). Fields entities The living entities, in creation (id) order; derived systems read it, and change it only through the base methods. protected readonly List<T> entities Field Value List<T> Properties Entities Living entities, in creation (id) order. public IReadOnlyList<T> Entities { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<T> EntityCount How many entities the kind holds now, used-up ones not yet removed included. public override int EntityCount { get; } Property Value int Methods Add(T) Adds an entity: it gets an id and its creation tick. public T Add(T e) Parameters e T The new entity, its position and lifetime set. Returns T The same entity, for chaining. Clear() Removes everything (tests). public void Clear() EntityAt(int) The i-th living entity, in creation order (views read them; 0 ≤ i < EntityCount), or null if the kind keeps none. public override Entity EntityAt(int i) Parameters i int An index from 0 to EntityCount - 1. Returns Entity The entity, or null when the kind keeps no list. Initialize() Removes every entity: a new run starts empty. public override void Initialize() Remarks Look up what you need here, by role or name (Service<T>(), Phase<T>()), and reset your own state: the same object starts every run of the World. A service is initialised before the species' modules; a phase after them. Move(T, TickContext) Moves an entity (ENV-21); none by default. Only phases move entities, never the visuals. protected virtual void Move(T e, TickContext t) Parameters e T The entity to move; change its Position, keeping it on walkable ground. t TickContext This tick's context; draw random numbers only from its named streams (RAND-02). Remarks Called by UpdateEntities(TickContext) for every entity, used-up ones included, before lifetimes count down. Nearest(Vector3, float, Animal, Func<T, Animal, bool>, out T, out float) The nearest entity within radius that passes the filter (SPACE-07); ties by id (SPACE-08). The filter receives the viewer, so it needs no closure. public bool Nearest(Vector3 p, float radius, Animal viewer, Func<T, Animal, bool> filter, out T found, out float distance) Parameters p Vector3 The point searched from, usually the viewer's position. radius float The largest distance, in meters (inclusive). viewer Animal The animal that looks, passed to the filter; may be null. filter Func<T, Animal, bool> Keeps an entity when it returns true, e.g. (c, a) => c.CanBeEatenBy(a); null keeps all. found T The nearest entity, or null. distance float Its distance, in meters, or positive infinity when none is found. Returns bool True when an entity was found within the radius. Remarks Used-up entities are skipped. Distances are the world's (Distance(Vector3, Vector3)). OnRemoved(T, string, TickContext) Called when an entity is removed in the environment phase. protected virtual void OnRemoved(T e, string reason, TickContext t) Parameters e T The removed entity. reason string "used up" or "expired" (its lifetime ran out). t TickContext This tick's context. Remarks Record an event or recycle the object here (the carcass system pools them). Don't add or remove entities from here: the list is being compacted. UpdateEntities(TickContext) Moves, ages and removes entities; the environment phase calls it once per tick (ENV-22). public override void UpdateEntities(TickContext t) Parameters t TickContext This tick's context: the tick number and the named random streams. Remarks An entity whose lifetime reaches 0 here is removed in the same call ("expired"), as is a used-up one ("used up"). The others keep their order.

api/EvoSim.EventLog.html.title: Class EventLog | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.EventLog.html.summary: Class EventLog Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll The world's events and their running hash (RAND-10). The hash is chained: h0 = SHA-256 of the seeds, h(i) = SHA-256(h(i-1) ‖ UTF-8(line i)), so it can be read after any event. public sealed class EventLog Inheritance object EventLog Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The World creates one per run (Events). Code records an event with Record(SimEvent); every sink (the run recorder, the editor's event log, tests) then receives it with its canonical line. The final hash identifies the run: the same configuration, seeds and answer caches give the same hash (RAND-11). Record events only from the simulation (phases and modules), in a fixed order: an event recorded from the visuals or in a varying order would change the hash. Constructors EventLog(long, long) The chain starts from the hash of the seeds, so two seeds never share a hash, even for a world whose events happen to be equal (RAND-13). public EventLog(long seed = 0, long worldSeed = 0) Parameters seed long The run seed. worldSeed long The world seed (the map's), which may differ from the run seed (RAND-04). Properties Count How many events were recorded so far. public long Count { get; } Property Value long Hash The running hash, 64 hex digits. public string Hash { get; } Property Value string Lines Optional: keep every line in memory (tests). public List<string> Lines { get; set; } Property Value List<string> ShortHash The first 16 hex digits, as the summary prints it. public string ShortHash { get; } Property Value string Methods AddSink(IEventSink) Adds a receiver of every event from now on; adding it twice does nothing. public void AddSink(IEventSink sink) Parameters sink IEventSink The receiver, e.g. a RunRecorder. Record(SimEvent) Records an event: adds its canonical line to the hash, counts it, and passes it to every sink. public void Record(SimEvent e) Parameters e SimEvent The event; change it no more once recorded. Remarks Modules record their own event kinds the same way, e.g. World.Events.Record(new SimEvent("egg_lost", World.Tick, egg.Id, species.Id).With("reason", reason)). RemoveSink(IEventSink) Stops sending events to a receiver. public void RemoveSink(IEventSink sink) Parameters sink IEventSink The receiver to remove.

api/EvoSim.Expression.html.summary: Class Expression Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll What a gene expresses into (GENE-03/04): a trait of the animal being born, or a line of the prompt. Express(AlleleValue, Expression) receives one and calls SetTrait(string, float, bool) or PromptGene(string, string). public sealed class Expression Inheritance object Expression Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Every gene is expressed in two situations, each with one target only: at birth, by CreateAnimal(string, Vector3, float, Genome, int, int[], Action<Animal>): Animal is the newborn, traits are set, prompt lines are dropped; when the genes block of a decision is written, by BrainGenes(Species, Genome), for the genes the brain reads only: Animal is null, traits are dropped, prompt lines are collected. So a gene's Express(AlleleValue, Expression) must act only through this object. Constructors Expression(Animal, SpeciesBuilder, List<KeyValuePair<string, string>>) Prepares an expression for one target: an animal's traits, or the lines of a genes block. public Expression(Animal animal, SpeciesBuilder declarations, List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> promptGenes = null) Parameters animal Animal The animal being born, or null when only prompt lines are wanted. declarations SpeciesBuilder The species' declarations, where traits are found by name. promptGenes List<KeyValuePair<string, string>> The list that collects (label, text) lines for the genes block, or null when no prompt line is wanted. Properties Animal The animal whose traits are being set, or null when only prompt lines are wanted. public Animal Animal { get; } Property Value Animal Methods PromptGene(string, string) A sentence for the genes block of the prompt (PROMPT-02); dropped at birth. public void PromptGene(string label, string text) Parameters label string What the brain sees before the sentence: the gene's Label. text string The sentence, or a number written as text. SetTrait(string, float, bool) Sets a trait, or multiplies its default; the result is clamped to the trait's range (GENE-04, ANIM-18). public void SetTrait(string trait, float value, bool multiplyDefault) Parameters trait string The trait's name, as a module declared it, e.g. stamina.max. value float The value, in the trait's unit, or a factor when multiplyDefault is true. multiplyDefault bool False: the value replaces the trait. True: the trait becomes its default times the value. Remarks Does nothing when Animal is null, or when no module declares the trait (V-45 reports it before the run).

api/EvoSim.FieldPath.html.title: Class FieldPath | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.FieldPath.html.summary: Class FieldPath Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll Reads and overrides any serialized setting by path (CFG-02): "<GameObject path>/<Component>/<field>", relative to the World, e.g. "Prey/Litter/max", "World/decisionPeriod", "prey/Actions/flee/FleeAction/fleeIntoCover". Names are matched without case; a component is found by its class or a base class, on the GameObject or below it. public static class FieldPath Inheritance object FieldPath Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks How a path is read: the last part is the field, the one before it the component, the rest a GameObject path under the World. A GameObject matches by name, or a species by its id or display name. When the full GameObject path has no such component, shorter ones are tried, down to the World itself; the first component found below wins (depth-first). Failing a class name, the component part may be a GameObject's name: the first species module on that GameObject is taken. World/x is the World's own field. Only serialized fields count (public or [SerializeField], not read-only): what the inspector shows. Values convert from text in the invariant culture: string, int, long, float, double, bool, any enum (by name, any case) and float arrays ([8, 4]). Methods Format(object) A value as text (for run_info.json and the inspector). public static string Format(object v) Parameters v object The value. Returns string "" for null; floats and doubles in round-trip form; a Unity object by its name; a list as [a, b]; anything else as its invariant text. Get(World, string) The current value of the field at the path, as text. public static string Get(World world, string path) Parameters world World The World the path starts from. path string The setting's path, e.g. World/decisionPeriod. Returns string The value as Format(object) writes it, or null when the path leads nowhere. IsSerialized(FieldInfo) Public or [SerializeField], not [NonSerialized]: what the inspector shows. public static bool IsSerialized(FieldInfo f) Parameters f FieldInfo A field. Returns bool True when the field is public or marked [SerializeField], and neither [NonSerialized] nor read-only. Remove(World, string, out string) Deactivates the GameObject at a hierarchy path under the World (scenario "remove", S06). public static bool Remove(World world, string path, out string error) Parameters world World The World the path starts from. path string A GameObject path under the World, e.g. prey/Actions/hide. error string Why it failed (no such GameObject), or null. Returns bool True when the GameObject was found and switched off. Set(World, string, string, out string) Sets the field at the path from its text value; false with a reason if the path or value is wrong. public static bool Set(World world, string path, string value, out string error) Parameters world World The World the path starts from. path string The setting's path, e.g. Prey/Litter/max. value string The new value as text. error string Why it failed (no such GameObject, component or field; a value that doesn't convert), or null. Returns bool True when the field was set. Remarks Call it before the World initialises: modules read their settings then. It skips the inspector's limits. Snapshot(World) Every serialized setting of every component under the World, by path (CFG-03). public static SortedDictionary<string, object> Snapshot(World world) Parameters world World The World. Returns SortedDictionary<string, object> The settings, keys in ordinal order. Remarks Covers the World, its modules, species, species modules and Edibles that are active and enabled. Keys are <GameObject path>/<class>/<field>; values are numbers, strings, bools, enum names, Unity objects by name, lists, or dictionaries for serialized classes. RunInfo writes it as settings.

flee action of the prey, and teaching-path exercise 6. Each tick it: finds the nearest visible animal it flees from (NearestAnimal(Animal, AnimalSet, IReadOnlyList<Species>)): by default its species' threats, the species whose diet strikes it (SPEC-12); or the species listed by id or display name when from is Listed; with none in sight, calls Search(); with FleeIntoCover on: stays when already in cover, or runs into the nearest cover within coverSeek meters; otherwise runs straight away from the threat (RunAwayFrom(Animal)), as far as its running speed and stamina allow. Properties DefaultDescription The reference prompt line of this action (08 §7), used when the Inspector field is empty. Every action should override it with a short phrase, such as "go to the nearest visible food and eat it". protected override string DefaultDescription { get; } Property Value string FleeIntoCover True to flee like the prototype (scenario S06): stay when in cover, run into cover within coverSeek meters. Off in the reference, where hiding is its own action. public bool FleeIntoCover { get; set; } Property Value bool Methods Act(Animal, ActContext) Runs away from the nearest threat in sight, or into nearby cover when FleeIntoCover is on; searches when no threat is in sight (ACT-04). public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) Parameters a Animal The animal that acts: alive and not busy. c ActContext The context to query and plan through; Begin(Animal) was already called for a. Remarks Called by the act phase, through ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>), once per tick for each animal that chose this action. Look the target up again each tick, so that a moving target is followed (ACT-02). The plan is the last intent and the last interaction the method set; doing nothing means stay. Initialize() Resolves the listed species by id or display name (ARCH-08); names that match no species are skipped (V-20). public override void Initialize() Remarks Find things by role or name (ARCH-08): Species.Module<Energy>(), World.Service<Ground>(), Species.Declarations.FindTrait("vision"). Reset your own state here: the same object starts every run. IsRelevant(ObservationView) True when the threat sense (relevantSense, reference "Predator") reports a threat in sight (CTRL-10). public override bool IsRelevant(ObservationView o) Parameters o ObservationView An observation of this species, read by sense label with Token(string). Returns bool True when the action would have something to act on in that situation. Validate(ValidationReport) Warns when the species has nothing to flee from (V-21) and reports listed names that are no species (V-20). public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Called after every Initialize and after the food web is derived; only read, never change the scene.

under the World's Environment object with an Edible (reference: "Grass", grazed, 25 per item); diets and senses name it by its GameObject's name. Lifecycle: Initialize() lays the grid over the ground; Begin(), once cover exists, picks the cells that may hold food and the first items from the stream "world/<layer name>" (world seed, RAND-04); Regrow(RandomStream) runs once per tick in the environment phase with the layer's own stream (ENV-03). On a terrain, cells within nearWaterRadius of water regrow nearWaterBonus times faster. Properties Count How many items the layer holds (ENV-01). public override int Count { get; } Property Value int EligibleCount How many cells may hold food (known after Begin(); 0 before). public int EligibleCount { get; } Property Value int Grid The food cells' grid over the ground's rectangle. public CellGrid Grid { get; } Property Value CellGrid RegrowFactor A multiplier on regrowth set by other phases (seasons, 22 §9); 1 by default. public float RegrowFactor { get; set; } Property Value float RegrowP The probability that an empty eligible cell grows an item in one tick, before the factors. public float RegrowP { get; } Property Value float Methods Begin() After cover exists: which cells may hold food, then the first items (world stream, RAND-03/04). public override void Begin() Remarks Not called when the editor only validates. Draw random numbers from a named stream, e.g. World.Random.Get("world/" + ServiceName) for the map (RAND-04). Clear() Empties the layer (tests). public void Clear() Configure(float, float, bool) Sets the reference values from code (WorldBuilder, scenarios). public void Configure(float initial, float regrow, bool hungryCover = true) Parameters initial float Share of eligible cells holding an item at the start, from 0 to 1. regrow float Probability per empty eligible cell per tick of growing an item, from 0 to 1. hungryCover bool True to keep cover free of food (the reference). Remarks Call it before the World initialises: the items are placed in Begin(). Consume(ResourceItem) Removes the item at once; false if it was already gone (ENV-02). public override bool Consume(ResourceItem item) Parameters item ResourceItem An item this layer returned from Nearest(Vector3, float, out ResourceItem), this tick. Returns bool True when the item was there and is now eaten; false when it was gone or belongs to another layer. Remarks Called by the interaction resolver when an animal grazes; the act order decides who eats a contested item. HasItem(int) Checks whether a cell holds an item now. public bool HasItem(int cell) Parameters cell int A cell index of Grid. Returns bool True when the cell holds an item. Initialize() Lays an empty grid over the ground's rectangle and resets RegrowFactor to 1; no item yet. public override void Initialize() Remarks Look up what you need here, by role or name (Service<T>(), Phase<T>()), and reset your own state: the same object starts every run of the World. A service is initialised before the species' modules; a phase after them. IsEligible(int) Checks whether a cell may hold food (walkable, and outside cover when food is kept out of cover). public bool IsEligible(int cell) Parameters cell int A cell index of Grid. Returns bool True when the cell may hold food and regrows. Nearest(Vector3, float, out ResourceItem) The nearest cell holding an item, by the world distance to the cell centre; ties to the lower cell index. public override bool Nearest(Vector3 p, float radius, out ResourceItem item) Parameters p Vector3 The point searched from, usually an animal's position. radius float The largest distance, in meters (inclusive). item ResourceItem The nearest item, or default when none is found. Returns bool True when an item was found within the radius. Remarks Measure with the world's distance (Distance(Vector3, Vector3), SPACE-02), and break ties by a fixed key (SPACE-08). Regrow(RandomStream) Each empty eligible cell grows an item with probability regrowP (× the near-water bonus). public override void Regrow(RandomStream rng) Parameters rng RandomStream The layer's stream, named StreamName; draw only from it, in a fixed order. Remarks The probability is also multiplied by RegrowFactor; one draw per empty eligible cell, in cell order. SetItem(Vector3, bool) Puts or removes an item by hand (Place in tests); returns whether the cell is eligible. public bool SetItem(Vector3 p, bool value) Parameters p Vector3 A point in the cell to change. value bool True to put an item, false to remove it. Returns bool Whether the cell is eligible; false outside the grid. When the cell already was as asked, true for any cell of the grid. Remarks An item may be put on a cell that is not eligible: it can be eaten but never regrows there. Validate(ValidationReport) Reports a start fraction or regrowth probability outside [0, 1] (V-35), with a fix that clamps them. public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Only read: validation must not change the scene. Offer a change as a ValidationFix.

gene kind, as the Gene script template writes it (the trait must be declared by a module of the species): public class CourageGene : Gene { [SerializeField, Tooltip("The trait this gene sets.")] string trait = "courage"; [SerializeField, Tooltip("Founder values.")] List<float> founders = new List<float> { 1f }; public override AlleleKind Kind => AlleleKind.Number; public override IReadOnlyList<FounderAllele> FounderPool { get { var pool = new List<FounderAllele>(); foreach (var f in founders) pool.Add(new FounderAllele(AlleleValue.OfNumber(f), "founder")); return pool; } } public override void Express(AlleleValue value, Expression e) => e.SetTrait(trait, value.Number, false); } Remarks A gene is a component under a species. Its place among the species' genes (depth first in the hierarchy) is its locus, Locus: the index of its allele in every Genome of the species (GENE-06). A text gene on or under an action is bound to that action and takes its name as label (GENE-05). To add a gene kind, derive from it and implement Kind, FounderPool and Express(AlleleValue, Expression). Override Check(AlleleValue) to refuse some values, MayMutate(Allele) to protect some alleles, Decimals to compare numbers at another precision, and ReadByBrain when the brain should read it. A number gene kind should also implement INumberRange, so that GaussianMutation and the random-founders control (CTRL-01) work with it. What a gene kind must keep: it holds settings only, never per-animal state; FounderPool gives the same values in the same order in every run (GENE-21); Express(AlleleValue, Expression) acts only through the Expression it is given and draws no random number. Fields label The label set in the Inspector; empty = the bound action's name (GENE-05). Read Label. [SerializeField] [Tooltip("What the brain and the inspector show. Empty = the bound action's name (GENE-05).")] protected string label Field Value string Properties Action The action this gene is bound to (GENE-05), or null for a free gene. public AnimalAction Action { get; } Property Value AnimalAction Decimals Precision used to compare number alleles (GENE-10), in decimals; reference 4. Ignored for sentences. public virtual int Decimals { get; } Property Value int FounderPool The founder pool with its origins, neutral allele included (GENE-20). public abstract IReadOnlyList<FounderAllele> FounderPool { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<FounderAllele> Remarks A founder genome draws each locus uniformly from it, and newcomers below the floor too (POP-03). The World registers the whole pool first, in this order, so founder alleles get the same ids in every run (GENE-21): it must give the same values in the same order every time. The validator reports an empty pool (V-41). Kind Whether this gene's alleles are sentences or numbers (GENE-02). public abstract AlleleKind Kind { get; } Property Value AlleleKind Label What the brain and the Inspector show for this gene: the label field, else the bound action's name, else the GameObject's name (GENE-05). public string Label { get; } Property Value string Locus This gene's position in the species' locus order: the index of its allele in every genome of the species; -1 before the species is set up. public int Locus { get; } Property Value int LocusId The locus id, "<species id>.<label>", e.g. prey.eat; unique in the world (GENE-11). public string LocusId { get; } Property Value string ReadByBrain Whether the brain reads this gene (text genes; number genes only if configured, GENE-04). Only these genes enter the genes block of the prompt and the brain-visible genome key (DEC-31). public virtual bool ReadByBrain { get; } Property Value bool Methods Check(AlleleValue) Values allowed for this gene, e.g. the mutation guards for sentences (GENE-22). public virtual string Check(AlleleValue value) Parameters value AlleleValue A value: a founder, or a mutant about to be registered. Returns string Why the value is not allowed (e.g. "13 words (at most 12)"), or null when it is. Remarks The hatch phase checks every mutant with it, whatever operator made it: a refused mutant leaves the inherited allele and is counted as not allowed. Text genes also check their founders with it (V-40). Express(AlleleValue, Expression) Turn this gene's allele into what acts: a prompt line or a trait (GENE-03/04). public abstract void Express(AlleleValue value, Expression e) Parameters value AlleleValue The allele's value. e Expression The target: call SetTrait(string, float, bool) for a trait, PromptGene(string, string) for a line of the genes block. Remarks Called at birth with the newborn (prompt lines are then dropped), and each time a decision's genes block is written, with no animal (traits are then dropped), for the genes the brain reads. Act only through e. Returns bool True when it may mutate (the default); false keeps it unchanged. Remarks The breed phase asks at conception, after drawing the mutation rate, before starting a mutation. ground (FlatGround): the three questions every ground answers. public class FlatGround : Ground { [SerializeField, Min(1f)] float width = 192f; [SerializeField, Min(1f)] float depth = 192f; public override Rect Bounds => new Rect(0f, 0f, width, depth); public override float Height(Vector3 p) => 0f; public override bool IsWalkable(Vector3 p) => Inside(p); } // A flat ground with a round pond that animals can't enter (from EvoSim's test probes). public class PondGround : FlatGround { public Vector3 PondCenter = new Vector3(10f, 0f, 10f); public float PondRadius = 3f; public override bool IsWater(Vector3 p) => Flat(p, PondCenter) < PondRadius; public override bool IsWalkable(Vector3 p) => base.IsWalkable(p) && !IsWater(p); static float Flat(Vector3 a, Vector3 b) => new Vector2(a.x - b.x, a.z - b.z).magnitude; } Remarks One ground per World, under it (reference: the "Ground" GameObject). The World initialises it before every other service, since layers and cover are laid on it, and finds it as Ground. Derive from it and implement Bounds, Height(Vector3) and IsWalkable(Vector3); override IsWater(Vector3) and NearestWater(Vector3, float) for water, Distance(Vector3, Vector3) for path length. The answers must not change during a run, and IsWalkable(Vector3) is false outside Bounds. All walkable ground should be connected (SPACE-05). The movement helpers (SlideTo(Vector3, Vector3), SideStep(Vector3, float, RandomStream)) keep every animal on walkable ground (MOVE-02). Properties Bounds The world rectangle on the horizontal plane: x is world x, y is world z. Half-open [min, max). public abstract Rect Bounds { get; } Property Value Rect Methods Clamp(Vector3) The point clamped into the rectangle, its height set from the ground. public Vector3 Clamp(Vector3 p) Parameters p Vector3 A world point, maybe outside. Returns Vector3 The nearest point inside Bounds, on the ground; it may still be non-walkable. Clear(Vector3, Vector3) True if every sample of the straight segment is walkable (inside, not water, not an obstacle). public bool Clear(Vector3 from, Vector3 to) Parameters from Vector3 The start of the segment. to Vector3 The end of the segment, which must be walkable. Returns bool True when an animal can walk the segment in a straight line. Remarks Samples are EvoSim.Ground.SampleStep apart; the start point itself is not checked. Distance(Vector3, Vector3) The world distance: horizontal Euclidean in the reference. Override for path length (SPACE-02). public virtual float Distance(Vector3 a, Vector3 b) Parameters a Vector3 One point. b Vector3 The other point. Returns float The distance, in meters; height doesn't count in the reference (SPACE-06). Remarks Every module measures through Distance(Vector3, Vector3), which calls this. A replacement must never be shorter than the straight horizontal distance: Nearest(bool[], Vector3, float, Ground, out float) prunes its search with it. Height(Vector3) The ground's height under a point (SPACE-06). public abstract float Height(Vector3 p) Parameters p Vector3 A world point; only x and z count. Returns float The world height of the ground there, in meters. Inside(Vector3) Checks whether a point lies inside the rectangle (half-open: the far edges are outside). public bool Inside(Vector3 p) Parameters p Vector3 A world point; only x and z count. Returns bool True inside Bounds. IsWalkable(Vector3) Whether an animal may stand here; false outside the rectangle (SPACE-04). public abstract bool IsWalkable(Vector3 p) Parameters p Vector3 A world point; only x and z count. Returns bool True when the point is walkable: inside, and not water, too steep or an obstacle. IsWater(Vector3) Whether a point is water (terrain grounds; never on flat ground). public virtual bool IsWater(Vector3 p) Parameters p Vector3 A world point. Returns bool True when the point is water; false by default. NearestWater(Vector3, float) The nearest water within radius, with a walkable shore point next to it (22 §2); null if none. public virtual WaterHit? NearestWater(Vector3 p, float radius) Parameters p Vector3 The point searched from, usually an animal's position. radius float The largest distance, in meters. Returns WaterHit? The water point, its shore and its distance, or null when no water is within the radius (always, by default). Remarks The drink action walks to the shore point; the water sense reports the distance. OnGround(Vector3) The point with its height set from the ground (SPACE-06). public Vector3 OnGround(Vector3 p) Parameters p Vector3 A world point. Returns Vector3 The same x and z, with y = Height(Vector3). RandomWalkable(RandomStream) A uniformly random walkable point (founders, newcomers; POP-03, POP-04). public virtual Vector3 RandomWalkable(RandomStream rng) Parameters rng RandomStream The stream to draw from: the species' founders stream (RAND-03). Returns Vector3 A walkable point on the ground. Exceptions InvalidOperationException No walkable point was found in 10 000 tries. SideStep(Vector3, float, RandomStream) A random step of length d to walkable ground, for an animal that is stuck (MOVE-04). public virtual Vector3 SideStep(Vector3 from, float d, RandomStream rng) Parameters from Vector3 The stuck animal's position. d float The step length, in meters. rng RandomStream The stream to draw directions from: the species' actions stream (RAND-03). Returns Vector3 The new point, on the ground; from when all 8 tries are blocked. Remarks Tries up to 8 random directions and takes the first whose straight path is clear. SlideTo(Vector3, Vector3) Moves in a straight line toward to as far as walkable ground allows. Blocked by a border or an obstacle, it slides along it (MOVE-04): the best of the clamped point and the two one-axis moves, else the farthest walkable point of the straight segment. public virtual Vector3 SlideTo(Vector3 from, Vector3 to) Parameters from Vector3 The start, on walkable ground. to Vector3 The wanted end point. Returns Vector3 The point reached, on the ground and walkable; from when no move is possible. Remarks "Best" is the candidate that gets farthest along the wanted direction. The kinematic locomotion calls it once per move. SlopeDegrees(Vector3, Vector3) The slope in degrees between two points (0 on flat ground). public virtual float SlopeDegrees(Vector3 from, Vector3 to) Parameters from Vector3 The start point. to Vector3 The end point. Returns float The slope's steepness, from 0 to 90 degrees, up or down alike; 0 when the points are closer than Epsilon. Remarks Locomotions use it for slope costs or limits (22 §14).

OllamaPointsBrain: one chat call per request, the points turned into a row. public class OllamaPointsBrain : HttpBrain { public override string Id => "ollama-points"; public override string Mode => "points"; public override string AnswerInstruction => Instruction; protected override string HealthPath => "/api/tags"; protected override async Task AnswerAsync(HttpCaller c, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest> requests, BrainAnswer answer) { var calls = new List<Task>(requests.Count); foreach (var r in requests) calls.Add(One(c, r, answer)); await Task.WhenAll(calls).ConfigureAwait(false); } async Task One(HttpCaller c, BrainRequest r, BrainAnswer answer) { try { var response = await c.PostAsync("/api/chat", Body(r.Text, r.Actions)).ConfigureAwait(false); var row = PointsAnswer.ToRow((string)response["message"]?["content"], r.Actions, out var problem); if (row == null) answer.Fail(r.Index, problem); else answer.SetRow(r.Index, row); } catch (Exception e) { answer.Fail(r.Index, e.Message); } } } Remarks The Ask brains phase calls Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>) on the main thread with the queries that the memo and the answer cache could not answer (DEC-30, DEC-33). Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>) builds one BrainRequest per query, with the text from TextFor(DecisionQuery), returns an unfinished answer at once and runs AnswerAsync(HttpCaller, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest>, BrainAnswer) on the thread pool. Every await uses ConfigureAwait(false), so the answers never need the main thread: the Freeze wait mode can block it, and the Responsive mode keeps the editor drawing (SPACE-14). When AnswerAsync(HttpCaller, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest>, BrainAnswer) ends, or throws, every request left without a row fails and the answer is completed. Caller applies the time-out of each try, the tries with doubling waits and the cap on requests in flight (DEC-42). A request that still fails becomes a failed row. A strict brain (the default for HTTP brains) then stops the run cleanly; a non-strict one gets a uniform row, counted and never cached (DEC-40, DEC-34). The answers are stored in the answer cache by the decision phases, not here (DEC-33). To call another server, derive from it: implement AnswerAsync(HttpCaller, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest>, BrainAnswer) (post each body with PostAsync(string, JObject, CancellationToken), read the answer, then call SetRow(int, float[]) or Fail(int, string) for every request) and HealthPath, and override Id. Override ModelIdentity and Mode too, so that cache keys change with the model. AnswerAsync(HttpCaller, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest>, BrainAnswer) runs on another thread: it must not touch a Unity object. Place the component under the World, like any brain. An API key never goes in a field: apiKeyVariable names the environment variable that holds it (OUT-04). Constructors HttpBrain() Sets the defaults of a brain behind a language model: strict (DEC-40) and with the answer cache (DEC-33). protected HttpBrain() Fields apiKeyVariable The name of the environment variable that holds the API key, or empty when the server needs none. hunt action of the predator, and teaching-path exercise 12. Each tick it: finds the nearest visible prey (NearestAnimal(Animal, AnimalSet, IReadOnlyList<Species>) with Prey: not killed, not hidden in cover) and the nearest carcass it may eat (NearestCarcass(Animal)); if there is a carcass at least as near as the prey (or no prey), runs to it, stopping stopAt meters away, and scavenges it on arrival (Scavenge(Carcass)); else, if there is prey, runs to it and strikes it on arrival (Strike(Animal)); with neither in sight, searches (ACT-04). The strike kills with the hunter's kill chance (KillChanceAgainst(Animal, Animal)), at most once per tick (ACT-12); a kill or a portion makes the hunter busy digesting (Digestion). Properties DefaultDescription The reference prompt line of this action (08 §7), used when the Inspector field is empty. Every action should override it with a short phrase, such as "go to the nearest visible food and eat it". protected override string DefaultDescription { get; } Property Value string Hunts True: senses such as the sample ChasedSense see an animal that chose this action as hunting. public override bool Hunts { get; } Property Value bool Methods Act(Animal, ActContext) Runs to the nearer of the nearest prey and the nearest edible carcass (the carcass on a tie) and strikes or scavenges on arrival; searches when neither is in sight (ACT-04). public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) Parameters a Animal The animal that acts: alive and not busy. c ActContext The context to query and plan through; Begin(Animal) was already called for a. Remarks Called by the act phase, through ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>), once per tick for each animal that chose this action. Look the target up again each tick, so that a moving target is followed (ACT-02). The plan is the last intent and the last interaction the method set; doing nothing means stay. IsRelevant(ObservationView) True when the prey sense (relevantSense, reference "Prey") reports prey in sight (CTRL-10). public override bool IsRelevant(ObservationView o) Parameters o ObservationView An observation of this species, read by sense label with Token(string). Returns bool True when the action would have something to act on in that situation. Validate(ValidationReport) Warns when the species has no prey to strike and no carcass in its diet (V-21). public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Called after every Initialize and after the food web is derived; only read, never change the scene.

api/EvoSim.IHttpTransport.html.title: Interface IHttpTransport | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.IHttpTransport.html.summary: Interface IHttpTransport Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Http.dll Sends one HTTP request and returns the response body; throws HttpFailure for an error status. The real one is SystemHttpTransport; tests inject a fake (30 §2) so brains and mutators are tested without servers. public interface IHttpTransport Examples A test gives a JEV brain a fake server instead of a real one: var fake = FakeHttpTransport.Jev(); jev.Transport = fake; jev.ConfigureClient("http://jev.test", 5f, 3, 0f, 4); Remarks Set a transport through Transport or Transport; null gives back the component's own SystemHttpTransport. HttpCaller wraps it with the time-outs, tries and parallel cap, so a transport sends exactly one request per call. It is called from the thread pool, several calls at once: an implementation must be thread-safe and must not touch Unity objects. EvoSim.Testing.FakeHttpTransport (scripted answers, failures, hangs) and RecordingTransport (keeps every call) are the implementations to read. Methods SendAsync(string, string, string, string, CancellationToken) Sends one request and returns the response body. Task<string> SendAsync(string method, string url, string json, string apiKey, CancellationToken cancel) Parameters method string GET or POST. url string The full address: the host and the path. json string The request body, or null for a GET. apiKey string Sent as a bearer token when not empty; never logged (OUT-04). cancel CancellationToken Cancelled by the caller at its time-out; the caller doesn't rely on the transport honouring it. Returns Task<string> A task that gives the response body. Exceptions HttpFailure The server answered with an error status, with whether another try may succeed.

api/EvoSim.IInteraction.html.title: Interface IInteraction | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.IInteraction.html.summary: Interface IInteraction Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll A custom contact effect (22 §3, drink): applied after moving when the animal is within Reach of the point its action walked or ran to (ACT-10). public interface IInteraction Examples The sample DrinkAction (22 §3) walks to the shore of the nearest water and resets thirst there: public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { var water = c.Ground != null ? c.Ground.NearestWater(a.Position, c.Vision(a)) : null; if (water == null) { c.Search(); return; } c.WalkTo(water.Value.Shore, 0f); c.OnArrival(new Drink(thirst)); } sealed class Drink : IInteraction { readonly Thirst thirst; public Drink(Thirst t) { thirst = t; } public float Reach => 0.5f; public void Apply(Animal a, InteractionContext c) { if (thirst != null) a[thirst.Value] = 0f; } } Remarks An action asks for one with OnArrival(IInteraction), usually as a small private class inside the action. The act phase moves the animal, then the interaction resolver calls Apply(Animal, InteractionContext) once, in the same tick, if the animal ended within Reach of the point its intent was heading to (Target; its own position for a stay). What Apply(Animal, InteractionContext) must keep: it is the only place where an action's effect on animals happens (ACT-06); it draws random numbers only from Stream(Species, string); and nothing checks a diet for it, so check the Diet yourself when the effect is a meal. Properties Reach How close the animal must end, after moving, to the point its intent was heading to, in meters. PositiveInfinity applies the effect wherever the animal ends up. float Reach { get; } Property Value float Methods Apply(Animal, InteractionContext) Applies the effect (ACT-10). Called by the act phase's InteractionResolver, once, right after the actor moved, only when it is within Reach and was not killed earlier in the tick. void Apply(Animal actor, InteractionContext c) Parameters actor Animal The animal whose action asked for the interaction. c InteractionContext What the effect may use: the world, the ground, Feed(Animal, float, bool) and the random streams.

api/EvoSim.IStatsColumns.html.summary: Interface IStatsColumns Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll A module that adds columns to stats.csv (13 §4). A species module's columns get its species' prefix and hold that species' values; a world module's columns go at the end of the row, unprefixed. A new column during the run rewrites the header, with empty cells in the rows before it. public interface IStatsColumns Examples // A world service that counts every species' births and adds one column (from EvoSim's test probes). public class WorldHookProbe : WorldService, IStatsColumns { public int Born; static readonly string[] columns = { "world_born" }; public override void OnBorn(Animal a) => Born++; public IEnumerable<string> StatColumns => columns; public double StatValue(string column) => Born; } Remarks Implement it on a SpeciesModule (its columns follow the species' act_… columns) or on a WorldModule, a phase or a service (its columns end the row, phases first). The RunRecorder asks for the values when it writes a row, every statsEvery ticks, at the end of the record phase. A column whose name is already in the row is skipped. StatValue(string) only reads: it must not change the world or draw random numbers. Properties StatColumns The column names, without the species prefix, in a fixed order. IEnumerable<string> StatColumns { get; } Property Value IEnumerable<string> Methods StatValue(string) The value of one of the columns now (rounded to 4 decimals in the file). double StatValue(string column) Parameters column string One of the names of StatColumns, without the prefix. Returns double The value; a count, a mean or a rate.

api/EvoSim.Integrity.html.title: Class Integrity | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.Integrity.html.summary: Class Integrity Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll Brain and mutator integrity checks against the real servers (32 §2): B-01 smoke and B-11 blindness here, the gates B-02 to B-10 in IntegrityGates. Command line: -executeMethod EvoSim.Integrity.RunIntegrity [-checks B-01,B-11] [-scene path] [-brain JEV]; in the open editor: Integrity.RunNamed through the unity CLI's eval. public static class Integrity Inheritance object Integrity Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The checks need the model servers running (JEV for the brain; Ollama for B-07, B-10 and the mutator of B-11). Each check opens the scene additively (WithScene(string, Func<World, string>)), so the scene must not be open in the editor, and writes one JSON and one Markdown report under Logs/EvoSim/Reports (IntegrityReport). Only B-01 is blocking: the others are gates, tracked as trends (32 §2). Fields DefaultScene The scene the checks run on unless -scene says otherwise: Lab1_Small. public const string DefaultScene = "Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/Lab1_Small.unity" Field Value string Methods Blindness(string, int, int) B-11 blindness: the prompts the mutator model actually receives during a run (every text gene mutating, cache off) hold only the context line, one deck instruction, the sentence and the reply line (MUT-11, CORE-07). public static IntegrityReport Blindness(string scenePath, int requests = 12, int maxTicks = 400) Parameters scenePath string The scene, relative to the project; it needs an HTTP mutator client and a mutator service. requests int The number of mutator requests to check before stopping. maxTicks int The most ticks to run while waiting for those requests. Returns IntegrityReport The written report: one row per request, with its instruction, sentence, answer and verdict. Remarks The run uses the random brain and records every HTTP request of the mutator client; each request must hold only the allowed fields and one user message in the MUT-11 layout, with a deck instruction and a sentence of at most 12 words. RunIntegrity() Command-line entry point; exits 1 when a blocking check fails. public static void RunIntegrity() Remarks Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Integrity.RunIntegrity [-checks B-02,B-03] [-scene Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/Lab1_Small.unity] [-brain JEV] [-cpu] [-judge gemma4:12b]. Without -checks it runs B-01 to B-06, B-08, B-09 and B-11 (B-07 and B-10 only on request). -brain names the brain under test (GameObject name or id); -cpu runs the Ollama points brain on the CPU; -judge is the judge model of B-10. Each check logs one line, EvoSim integrity: …. Exit code: 0, 1 when a blocking check failed, 2 on an exception. RunNamed(string, string, string, bool) The same from the open editor: one line per check. public static string RunNamed(string checks = "B-01,B-11", string scene = "Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/Lab1_Small.unity", string brain = "JEV", bool cpuOnly = false) Parameters checks string Comma-separated check ids, B-01 to B-11. scene string The scene to run them on, relative to the project. brain string The brain under test: a GameObject name or a brain id. cpuOnly bool True to run the Ollama points brain on the CPU (B-01, B-07). Returns string One line per check: id, title, PASS or FAIL with the first problem, rows, report path. Remarks For example unity command --result-only eval --code 'return EvoSim.Integrity.RunNamed("B-01,B-02");'. Smoke(string, string, bool) B-01 smoke: one query per species with founder genes and three situations (every sense at its first, middle and last token), through the scene's real prompt and brain; every row valid; latency recorded. Blocking. public static IntegrityReport Smoke(string scenePath, string brainName, bool cpuOnly = false) Parameters scenePath string The scene, relative to the project; it must not be open in the editor. brainName string The brain under test: a GameObject name or a brain id. cpuOnly bool True to run an Ollama points brain on the CPU. Returns IntegrityReport The written report: one row per species and situation, with the probability row and its validity.

api/EvoSim.IntegrityGates.html.title: Class IntegrityGates | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.IntegrityGates.html.summary:
Class IntegrityGates Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Editor.dll The brain and mutator gates of 32 §2 (B-02…B-10), measured as the prototype measured them (e1_sensitivity): genomes from texts (founders, control sentences, the neutral genome, contrast pairs, single edits) × the reference situations (15 §2), through the scene's real prompt and brain. Queries are built from texts only: nothing is registered in the world. Each writes a report (IntegrityReport). public static class IntegrityGates Inheritance object IntegrityGates Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Each gate opens the scene additively, makes the named brain the default with no mutation, initialises the world (for its species, prompts and texts), asks the brain directly, and writes its report under Logs/EvoSim/Reports. None is blocking: a failed gate is a finding to track (32 §2). Run them through RunIntegrity() (-checks B-02,B-03…) or RunNamed(string, string, string, bool). The reference situations come from Data/Observations/prey_observations_v2.jsonl for prey and from ObservationSet.PredatorReference for a species that senses prey. Fields JudgePrompt The judge prompt of 32 §2 (the prototype's judge_sense_v1), used by B-10. public const string JudgePrompt = "Animals in a simulation act on short English rules called genes. Each gene sits in a slot. The slot "{slot}" is about {topic}.

The gene in the slot "{slot}" is: "{text}"

Does this gene still give the animal a usable rule about {topic}? A usable rule is understandable and could guide what the animal does, even if it is odd or unwise. Nonsense, or a sentence about something else, is not a usable rule.

Answer yes or no." api/EvoSim.InteractionResolver.html.summary: Class InteractionResolver Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll Applies the interactions of 07 §3 after moving (ACT-10, ACT-11): only within reach, only if the target is edible and the eater's diet lists it (SPEC-13). Hunters strike at most once per tick (ACT-12). public sealed class InteractionResolver Inheritance object InteractionResolver Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks The act phase makes one at initialization, with the reaches of its Inspector, and calls Apply(Animal, in Interaction, Vector3) for every animal that planned an interaction, right after that animal moved: in the act order for the sequential orders, in a fresh random order for the simultaneous one (ACT-30). brain. The server is vLLM on http://localhost:8000, serving the model autotrust/JEV-9B with its LoRA module under the name jev-decision. The decision head and the calibration come from two files of the pinned revision, given as TextAssets (Data/Models/JEV-9B); the model's GGUF files are the bare backbone, without that head. The text of a query follows the template bare-v1 (Text(string, string, IReadOnlyList<string>)): the species prompt without its answer instruction, a question line (Question(Species)) and the options A, B, C… Requests go by option count (the allowed tokens differ), with at most maxTextsPerRequest texts each. The model identity (repository, revision, served name) and the mode (template and questions) are part of the answer cache's keys (DEC-33). exercise 11. Move(Animal, Intent, float, MoveContext) works in five steps: a stay moves nothing and returns 0; the distance is the smallest of the speed trait (speed.run when running, speed.walk otherwise), the stamina budget and the intent's maximum distance; SlideTo(Vector3, Vector3) goes that far in a straight line, sliding along borders and obstacles; if that made no progress (less than 1 mm), SideStep(Vector3, float, RandomStream) takes a step of the same length in a random direction (up to 8 tries, else it stays), drawn from the species' actions stream; it sets the animal's position and returns the distance moved. Without a ground (some test worlds) it moves straight, with no check. of teaching-path exercise 2 (MyLevelSense, 22 §0). What it does: Tokens, in this order: "low" (0), "medium" (1), "high" (2). Initialize() finds the stat named in the Inspector once, with Species.Declarations.FindStat(stat). Read(Animal, SenseContext) reads the animal's value of that stat (a[value], 0 when the stat is missing) and returns "low" below the low threshold, "high" above the high threshold, else "medium": a value equal to a threshold is medium. Write(int, TextStyle) gives "Energy: low." in V1, and in V2 the Inspector's sentence for the token ("I am hungry and weak.", "I have some energy.", "I am well fed and strong."), or the V1 text when that sentence is missing or empty. The default label is the stat's name with a capital letter ("energy" gives "Energy"). Validate(ValidationReport) reports V-31 when the low threshold is above the high one, V-20 when no module declares the stat. One component per stat: the reference species have one for energy and one for stamina; recipe 22 §2 adds one for thirst with no code. Properties DefaultLabel The stat's name with a capital letter ("Energy"), or "Level" when no stat is set. protected override string DefaultLabel { get; } Property Value string High The high threshold, in the stat's points: above it the level is "high". public float High { get; } Property Value float Low The low threshold, in the stat's points: below it the level is "low". public float Low { get; } Property Value float Stat The name of the sensed stat ("energy", "stamina"…). public string Stat { get; } Property Value string Tokens Every token this sense can return, "none" included, in a fixed order: Read(Animal, SenseContext) returns an index into this list. Fixed before the run (SENSE-01); its length is the sense's factor in the observation space (SENSE-05). public override IReadOnlyList<string> Tokens { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> Remarks Build it in a field or in Initialize(), never during a run. A static list shared by every instance should be read-only. Methods Configure(string, float, float, string[]) Sets the sense from code (WorldBuilder, tests), as the Inspector fields do. public LevelSense Configure(string statName, float lowThreshold, float highThreshold, string[] v2Words = null) Parameters statName string The stat to sense, by name ("energy", "stamina"…). lowThreshold float Below this the level is low, in the stat's points. highThreshold float Above this the level is high, in the stat's points. v2Words string[] The V2 sentences for low, medium and high; null keeps the current ones. Returns LevelSense This sense, to chain calls. Initialize() Finds the sensed stat among the species' declarations, once, before the run. public override void Initialize() Remarks Find things by role or name (ARCH-08): Species.Module<Energy>(), World.Service<Ground>(), Species.Declarations.FindTrait("vision"). Reset your own state here: the same object starts every run. Read(Animal, SenseContext) "low" (0) when the animal's stat is below Low, "high" (2) when above High, else "medium" (1). A missing stat reads as 0. public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) Parameters a Animal The animal that decides. s SenseContext The world as it was at the start of the tick: nearest animals, food, cover, distances, rays. Returns int An index into Tokens. Remarks Called by the sense phase, through ReadAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, SenseContext, Span<int>), for every animal that decides this tick, and by tools (Observe(Animal, SenseContext)). It must give the same token for the same state, draw no random number, change nothing in the world, and learn about other animals only through s, which leaves out hidden and killed ones (SENSE-03, SENSE-06). Validate(ValidationReport) Reports V-31 when the low threshold is above the high one, and V-20 when no module declares the stat. public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Called after every Initialize and after the food web is derived; only read, never change the scene. Write(int, TextStyle) V1 "Energy: low."; V2 the Inspector's sentence for the token, or the V1 text when it has none (SENSE-11). public override string Write(int token, TextStyle style) Parameters token int An index into Tokens. style TextStyle The world's text style: V1 terse ("Energy: low."), or V2 first person ("I am hungry and weak.") (SENSE-11). Returns string A sentence ending with a period. The default writes "Label: token." in both styles. Remarks The species joins the fragments of its senses with spaces (Describe(Observation, TextStyle)). The text depends on the token only, never on the animal, so the same observation always gives the same text: the answer cache keys on it. Override it for V2 sentences or to state a range in meters (SENSE-12, SENSE-13).

parentEnergies) => 1; } Remarks The breed phase finds it by type (Species.Module<Litter>()), so a replacement derives from it. At each conception it calls Size(RandomStream, float[]); each parent then pays ChildEnergy / (number of parents) × k energy (REPRO-11), and each baby hatches with ChildEnergy. The Block cap rule may cut k further. Without a Litter, a conception makes one baby and costs nothing (V-26 warns). The reference Size(RandomStream, float[]), step by step (the exercise MyLitter rewrites it): k = rng.Range(Min, Max + 1): uniform in [Min, Max], one draw; share = ChildEnergy / number of parents; affordable = the smallest floor(energy / share) over the parents (no limit when share is 0); the result is max(Min, min(k, affordable)): what the poorest parent can pay, but never below Min, so a parent can end with zero or less energy. reference does, step by step (the exercise MyLlmMutation rewrites it): Initialize() reads the deck: one instruction per line, blank lines and lines starting with # skipped (Instructions(string), MUT-10). StartMutation(Gene, Allele, RandomStream) draws, for each of the tries tries in order, an instruction index (rng.Range(0, count)) and a seed (rng.NextUInt() & 0x7FFFFFFF): all of them at conception, even the tries a good first answer will make useless, so the stream never depends on the answers (MUT-30). It submits the parent sentence, these draws, the context line, the deck and the word limit (the smaller of its own and the gene's) to the World's MutatorService, which returns a running job. The service sends the first tries of the tick as one batch, cleans and checks each answer (Clean(string), Reject(string, string, int), MUT-12), and sends a rejected answer's next try in the next batch (MUT-13). When every try is rejected the job fails and the gene keeps its allele (MUT-04). Without a MutatorService, or with an empty deck, the job fails at once ("no mutator"), after the draws. The mutator is blind (CORE-07): its prompt holds the context line, the instruction and the sentence, nothing about the animal or the world. A mutant's operator detail is llm#n, n being the instruction's index in the deck. straight-line locomotion, the reference KinematicLocomotion without its random sidestep: public class StraightLocomotion : Locomotion { public override float Move(Animal a, Intent intent, float staminaBudget, MoveContext c) { if (intent.IsStay) return 0f; float speed = a.Trait(intent.Run ? RunSpeed : WalkSpeed); float d = Mathf.Min(speed, Mathf.Min(staminaBudget, intent.MaxDistance)); var from = a.Position; a.Position = c.Ground.SlideTo(from, from + intent.Direction * d); // never onto non-walkable ground return c.Distance(from, a.Position); } } Remarks Each species has exactly one locomotion (MOVE-01, V-13); place it anywhere under the species. In the act phase, after the animal's action planned its Intent, the phase calls MoveAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, IReadOnlyList<Intent>, MoveContext, Span<float>) for the animals whose intent moves; the default calls Move(Animal, Intent, float, MoveContext) for each one with its stamina budget. Then the metabolism charges the meters Move(Animal, Intent, float, MoveContext) reported, plus ExtraCost(Animal, Vector3, Vector3) (MOVE-06, ANIM-20). No other module assumes the intent was followed exactly. What an override must keep: change only the moved animal's Position; never end on non-walkable ground or outside the world (MOVE-02): use SlideTo(Vector3, Vector3) or Clear(Vector3, Vector3). The act phase moves an animal back, with a warning, if it does; never move more than the stamina budget (ANIM-21), and read speeds from the animal's traits, never from the settings (ANIM-16); return the meters actually moved, measured with Distance(Vector3, Vector3) (MOVE-06); draw random numbers only from Stream(Species, string). The sample SlopeLocomotion (22 §14) derives from KinematicLocomotion instead, to refuse steep ground and charge for climbing. Remarks Called before any module's Initialize: don't look up other modules here. Two modules may declare the same name: they get the same id, and the first declaration counts (V-38 if they differ). ExtraCost(Animal, Vector3, Vector3) Extra energy this movement costs (slopes, mud). None in the reference (MOVE-06). public virtual float ExtraCost(Animal a, Vector3 from, Vector3 to) Parameters a Animal The animal that moved. from Vector3 Where it was before moving. to Vector3 Where it is after moving. Returns float Energy points to pay, 0 or more; a negative value counts as 0. Remarks The act phase calls it after the animal moved more than 1 mm and passes it to Settle(Animal, float, float, bool), which pays it on top of the tick's cost (ANIM-20). The act phase only passes intents that move, but return 0 for a stay all the same. staminaBudget float The most it may move this tick, in meters (ANIM-21); infinity without a stamina module. c MoveContext The ground, the world distance and the random streams. Returns float The meters actually moved, measured with Distance(Vector3, Vector3); 0 when the animal didn't move. species; a species without it never breeds. The breed phase takes, by id, each animal whose current action mates, that IsReady(Animal) and hasn't bred this period, and pairs it with the nearest ready animal of its species within Reach that hasn't bred either (ties by id). When Sexual is false it breeds alone (REPRO-04). The litter, eggs and energy cost follow (Litter). Kin senses report readiness through the same IsReady(Animal). Overrides of IsAdult(Animal), IsReady(Animal) and Sexual must only read the animal: no change, no random draw. calls Settle(Animal, float, float, bool) for each living animal right after it moved and its interaction applied. The energy paid that tick is: moved (more than 1 mm): baseCost + moveCost × meters (reference 0.7 + 0.5 per meter); still and busy at the start of the tick: restCost (0.2); still, with an action that rests (Rests): restCost (0.2); still otherwise: baseCost (0.7); plus costPerUnit × the cost trait when one is set (09 §5), plus the locomotion's extra cost. Then the species' Stamina pays the meters or recovers (Settle(Animal, float, Energy)); recovering costs RegenEnergyCost more energy per tick (reference 0.3). Properties BaseCost Energy per tick when moving, or when still with an action that doesn't rest, in points (reference 0.7). public float BaseCost { get; } Property Value float CostPerUnit Extra energy per tick per unit of CostTrait, in points. public float CostPerUnit { get; } Property Value float CostTrait The trait the tick's cost grows with (09 §5), such as stamina.max; empty for none (reference). public string CostTrait { get; } Property Value string MoveCost Energy per meter moved, in points (reference 0.5). public float MoveCost { get; } Property Value float RestCost Energy per tick when still and busy, or still with a resting action, in points (reference 0.2). public float RestCost { get; } Property Value float Methods Configure(float, float, float) Sets the three costs from code (WorldBuilder, scenarios). public void Configure(float baseTick, float perMeter, float rest) Parameters baseTick float Energy per tick when moving or not resting, in points. perMeter float Energy per meter moved, in points. rest float Energy per tick when still and busy or resting, in points. Declare(SpeciesBuilder) Declares that a cost depends on CostTrait (09 §5), so that validation knows the number gene on it has a price (V-47). public override void Declare(SpeciesBuilder b) Parameters b SpeciesBuilder The species' declarations: call DeclareStat(string, StatStart, float, float, TraitId) and DeclareTrait(string, float, float, float, bool), and keep the ids they return. Remarks Called before any module's Initialize: don't look up other modules here. Two modules may declare the same name: they get the same id, and the first declaration counts (V-38 if they differ). Reset your own state here: the same object starts every run. SetTraitCost(string, float) A tick cost that grows with a trait (09 §5); an empty trait removes it. public void SetTraitCost(string trait, float perUnit) Parameters trait string A trait's name, such as stamina.max; empty or null removes the cost. perUnit float Extra energy per tick per unit of the trait, in points. Settle(Animal, float, float, bool) Charges the tick (ANIM-20): moved, busy, resting or standing still; stamina pays or recovers. public virtual void Settle(Animal a, float metersMoved, float extraCost, bool wasBusy) Parameters a Animal The animal that just acted. metersMoved float The meters its locomotion reported this tick (MOVE-06); less than 1 mm counts as still (ANIM-23). extraCost float The locomotion's extra cost for this move (ExtraCost(Animal, Vector3, Vector3)); a negative value counts as 0. wasBusy bool True when the animal was busy at the start of the tick. operator, as the MutationOperator script template writes it (values it pushes out of the gene's range are refused at hatching): public class Nudge : MutationOperator { public override bool Accepts(Gene g) => g.Kind == AlleleKind.Number; public override MutationJob StartMutation(Gene gene, Allele parent, RandomStream rng) => MutationJob.Done(parent.Number + (rng.Chance(0.5f) ? 1f : -1f), "nudge"); } Remarks Place operators as components under a species (the reference scenes keep them on a Mutation object). At each conception the breed phase picks, for each locus, the first operator that Accepts(Gene) the gene and lists it in OnlyThese, else the first that accepts it and lists no gene (OperatorFor(Species, Gene)). Then, in locus order and from the species' mutation stream, it draws whether the locus mutates with probability Rate (MUT-01), asks MayMutate(Allele), and calls StartMutation(Gene, Allele, RandomStream). To write an operator, derive from it and implement Accepts(Gene) and StartMutation(Gene, Allele, RandomStream). What it must keep: it sees only the gene and the parent allele, never the animal, its parents or the world (CORE-07); it draws random numbers only from the stream it is given, all of them inside StartMutation(Gene, Allele, RandomStream), as many whatever happens later (MUT-30): the same stream state gives the same job; its result must pass the gene's Check(AlleleValue) at hatching, and a result equal to the parent counts as a failure (MUT-04). The job may finish at once (Done(AlleleValue, string, string, long?), Failed(string)) or later (Running(Pending), or the MutatorService): the egg hatches only when it is done (MUT-32). See GaussianMutation, LlmMutation and the IntensityLadder sample (22 §8). FakeMutator.SentenceOf(requests[i].Prompt).TrimEnd('.') + " quickly."); reply.ModelCalls = requests.Count; reply.Complete(); return reply; } } Remarks A world service: place one under the World next The service calls Send(IReadOnlyList<MutatorRequest>) on the main thread, with at most one batch out at a time. What it does: Tokens (BuildTokens()): for each band in order, "close, ready" and "close, not ready" when readiness is on and part of the band lies within the partner range, then the plain "close" when readiness is off or part of the band lies beyond it; "none" last. Read(Animal, SenseContext): the animal's vision trait is the radius; the nearest visible animal of the set (NearestAnimal(Animal, AnimalSet, float, IReadOnlyList<Species>)) gives the band; within the partner range, IsReady(Animal) picks "ready" or "not ready"; nothing found gives "none".
