api/EvoSim.Testing.Stat.html.summary: Class Stat Namespace EvoSim.Testing Assembly EvoSim.Testing.dll Statistical asserts: a proportion or a mean within k standard errors, a χ² uniformity test (30 §2). public static class Stat Inheritance object Stat Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples T-ACT-06: 10 000 strikes with kill chance 0.5 kill half the time. Stat.Binomial(kills, n, 0.5, 4, "kills"); Remarks Random rules are tested by counting over many draws from a fixed seed: the test then passes or fails the same way on every run. k = 4 standard errors (the default) fails a correct rule about once in 16 000 seeds. Methods Binomial(long, long, double, double, string) Asserts that the observed proportion successes / trials is within k standard errors of p. public static void Binomial(long successes, long trials, double p, double k = 4, string what = "") Parameters successes long How many trials succeeded. trials long How many trials were made (above 0). p double The expected probability of success, 0 to 1. k double The tolerance, in standard errors. what string A name for the failure message. ChiSquareUpperTail(double, int) P(X ≥ x) for χ² with df degrees of freedom (Wilson–Hilferty normal approximation). public static double ChiSquareUpperTail(double x, int df) Parameters x double The χ² value. df int The degrees of freedom; 0 or less gives 1. Returns double The p-value, between 0 and 1. Count(long, long, double, double, string) Asserts that a count of events, each with probability p per trial, is within k standard errors; the same test as Binomial(long, long, double, double, string). public static void Count(long count, long trials, double p, double k = 4, string what = "") Parameters count long How many events happened. trials long How many trials were made (above 0). p double The expected probability per trial, 0 to 1. k double The tolerance, in standard errors. what string A name for the failure message. Mean(IReadOnlyList<double>, double, double, string) Asserts that the mean of the values is within k standard errors of the expected mean, the standard error taken from the values' own spread. public static void Mean(IReadOnlyList<double> values, double expected, double k = 4, string what = "") Parameters values IReadOnlyList<double> The measured values (at least 2 for a spread). expected double The expected mean. k double The tolerance, in standard errors. what string A name for the failure message. Uniform(IReadOnlyList<long>, double, string) χ² test that the counts are uniform; fails when p < alpha (Wilson–Hilferty approximation). public static void Uniform(IReadOnlyList<long> counts, double alpha = 0.001, string what = "") Parameters counts IReadOnlyList<long> How many times each outcome happened (e.g. each founder allele drawn). alpha double The significance level: the test fails when the p-value is below it. what string A name for the failure message.

api/EvoSim.Testing.WorldBuilder.html.summary: Class WorldBuilder Namespace EvoSim.Testing Assembly EvoSim.Testing.dll Builds a world in code, with no scene (30 §2): ground, food, cover, services, phases and species, each added by one chained call, then Build(). public sealed class WorldBuilder : IDisposable Inheritance object WorldBuilder Implements IDisposable Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Extension Methods Lab.CheckInvariants(WorldBuilder) Lab.Ecology(WorldBuilder, float, float, float, Action<SpeciesSetup>, Action<SpeciesSetup>, float) Lab.FakeMutation(WorldBuilder, Action<FakeMutator>) Lab.Lab1(WorldBuilder, int, int, float, ActOrder, bool, int, int, int) Lab.Recorder(WorldBuilder, bool, string, string, bool) Lab.ReferencePhases(WorldBuilder, ActOrder) Examples var w = New().Flat(20, 20).Food(0.1f, 0.01f) .Phase<SeasonsPhase>(p => p.Configure(10, 0.2f)).Phase<EnvironmentPhase>() .Species("prey", s => s.PreyBody().Action<RestAction>("rest")) .Build(); var grass = w.Service<FoodGrid>(); w.Advance(7); Assert.AreEqual(0.2f, grass.RegrowFactor, "winter"); Remarks The builder makes the same GameObject tree as a scene: a root with the World, then Environment (layers, entities), Brains (brains, caches, mutators), Phases and one object per species. The tree stays inactive until Build(), so no module runs before the World initialises it. A world has only what you add: no phase runs unless you add it (Phase<T>(Action<T>), or all of them with ReferencePhases(WorldBuilder, ActOrder)), and no species is populated unless you ask (Population(int), or Animal(Species, Vector3, Genome, float, string, Action<Animal>) after Build). The Lab extension methods add the reference species and the Lab 1 world in one call. In a test, start builders with New(int, WaitMode, string), which destroys the world afterwards; a builder made with new must be disposed. Constructors WorldBuilder(int, WaitMode, string) Starts an empty world: a root with its World and the Environment, Brains and Phases objects. public WorldBuilder(int seed = 1234, WaitMode waitMode = WaitMode.Freeze, string name = "Test World") Parameters seed int The world's seed: the same seed gives the same run (RAND-10). waitMode WaitMode How a tick waits for late answers; Freeze (the default) blocks, as tests need. name string The name of the root GameObject; give each world of a test its own. Remarks The World doesn't start on Play (StartOnPlay is off): the test drives it with Advance(int). Properties Root The root GameObject of the world being built (inactive until Build()). public GameObject Root { get; } Property Value GameObject World The World component on Root: set its options here or with Configure(Action<World>). public World World { get; } Property Value World Methods Build() Activates the tree and initialises the world: discovery, validation, founders. public World Build() Returns World The initialised World, ready for Advance(int). Exceptions InvalidOperationException The world failed validation; the message holds the validation report. BuildUninitialized() Activates the tree without initialising the world, to test validation or change the tree first. public World BuildUninitialized() Returns World The World, not initialised: call Initialize() or Prepare yourself. Carcasses(string) Adds the carcass system: killed animals leave carcasses that hunters can scavenge (ENV-20). public WorldBuilder Carcasses(string name = "Carcasses") Parameters name string The service's name. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Configure(Action<World>) Changes the World's settings now: text style, decision period, tick limit… public WorldBuilder Configure(Action<World> configure) Parameters configure Action<World> Called at once with the World, e.g. w => w.TextStyle = TextStyle.V2. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Cover(float, string) Adds a cover layer (a CoverLayer, thickets that hide animals from their hunters, ENV-11). public WorldBuilder Cover(float fraction = 0.2, string name = "Thickets") Parameters fraction float The share of walkable ground in cover, 0 to 1 (reference 0.2). name string The layer's name. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Remarks Put cover on an exact cell with Cover(CoverLayer, Vector3). DefaultBrain<T>(Action<T>, string) Adds a brain under Brains and makes it the World's default brain (DEC-13). public WorldBuilder DefaultBrain<T>(Action<T> configure = null, string name = null) where T : Brain Parameters configure Action<T> Called at once with the new brain, e.g. to set a Policy or keep a reference to it. name string The GameObject's name; null = the class name. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Type Parameters T The brain class: RandomBrain, ScriptedBrain, an HTTP brain, yours. Dispose() Destroys the world's GameObjects. WorldFixture calls it after each test. public void Dispose() Flat(float, float) Adds a flat ground, a rectangle starting at the origin (x from 0 to width, z from 0 to depth). public WorldBuilder Flat(float width, float depth) Parameters width float The size along x, in meters (at least 1). depth float The size along z, in meters (at least 1). Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Food(float, float, string, float, bool) Adds a food layer (a FoodGrid under Environment) whose items are grazed for energy points each. public WorldBuilder Food(float initialFraction = 0.1, float regrowP = 0.0015, string name = "Grass", float energy = 25, bool hungryCover = true) Parameters initialFraction float The share of eligible cells holding an item at the start, 0 to 1 (reference 0.1). regrowP float The chance per empty eligible cell per tick of growing an item (reference 0.0015); 0 = no regrowth. name string The layer's name, which diets and senses use (reference "Grass"). energy float The energy one item gives, in points (reference 25). hungryCover bool True: no item in cover, at the start or later (ENV-04). Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Remarks Food(0f, 0f) makes an empty layer that never regrows: place items with Food(FoodGrid, Vector3). Get<T>() Finds the first component of a type anywhere in the world being built, inactive objects included. public T Get<T>() where T : Component Returns T The first one in hierarchy order, or null. Type Parameters T The component class to find (a brain, a service, a module…). Ground<T>(float, float) Adds a flat ground of a subclass of your own: one that replaces the distance function, adds a pond or a ramp (DoubleDistanceGround, PondGround, RampGround). public WorldBuilder Ground<T>(float width, float depth) where T : FlatGround Parameters width float The size along x, in meters (at least 1). depth float The size along z, in meters (at least 1). Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Type Parameters T The ground class to add. Phase<T>(Action<T>) Adds a phase under Phases, after the phases added so far: phases run in hierarchy order (TICK-01). public WorldBuilder Phase<T>(Action<T> configure = null) where T : TickPhase Parameters configure Action<T> Called at once with the new phase, to set it up; null = defaults. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Type Parameters T The phase class to add. Service<T>(string, Action<T>) Adds a world service on its own GameObject: under Brains for brains, mutators and caches (by type name), under Environment for everything else (layers, entity systems, covers, recorders). public WorldBuilder Service<T>(string name = null, Action<T> configure = null) where T : WorldService Parameters name string The GameObject's name, which is also the service's name; null = the class name. configure Action<T> Called at once with the new component, to set it up; null = defaults. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Type Parameters T The service class to add. Species(string, Action<SpeciesSetup>, string) Adds a species, on its own GameObject under the root, with the modules configure adds. public WorldBuilder Species(string name, Action<SpeciesSetup> configure = null, string id = null) Parameters name string The species' display name, and its id unless id is given. configure Action<SpeciesSetup> Adds the species' modules through a SpeciesSetup; null = an empty species. id string The species' id when it differs from its name; null = the name. Returns WorldBuilder This builder, to chain more calls. Remarks The species starts with no founders: set some with Population(int).

api/EvoSim.Testing.html.summary: Namespace EvoSim.Testing Classes AdvancePending A wait that ends after a number of Advance(int) calls: how the test fakes answer late (30 §2). In the Freeze wait mode the World calls Wait(), which ends it at once. AllLayersObstacleSense A test batched sense that asks for its ray against every physics layer: even so, the views' layer is left out, so what is rendered never changes what animals sense (RAND-11). AllocationProbe A test phase placed just before and just after another phase: the pair measures the bytes the main thread allocated in between, every tick (R-07: no allocation per tick in the act phase after warm-up). BatchProbeAction A test-only action that wanders and records the group sizes the act phase plans through ActAll (ARCH-12, 20 §10). BatchProbeLocomotion A test-only locomotion that records the group sizes the act phase moves through MoveAll (ARCH-12, 20 §10). BatchProbeSense A test-only sense that records the group sizes the sense phase reads through ReadAll (ARCH-12, 20 §10). Blackboard Shared state for test phases that change "the world" and read it (T-TICK-02): one blackboard is given to several BlackboardPhases, to see which phases see a change. BlackboardPhase A test phase that reads the blackboard (logging what it sees), then optionally writes it: only the phases after a writer see the new value in the same tick (T-TICK-02). CallbackPhase A test-only phase that runs a callback at its place in the tick (to look at the state between two phases). CameraProbeSense A test sense that attaches an "image" (a byte array) to every query, with no cache key unless asked (T-SENSE-10, S24): such queries are never memoised or cached (SENSE-41), and a brain that takes no attachments fails validation (V-51). CountingCrossover A test-only uniform crossover that counts its calls (GENE-32: one cross per baby). DelayedPhase A test phase that waits, every Every ticks, for an answer that arrives DelayCalls Advance calls after it was asked (like a slow brain); in Freeze mode Wait() delivers it at once. DoubleDistanceGround A flat ground whose distance function is twice the Euclidean one: a replaced distance, which every sense and action must then use (T-SPACE-02, SPACE-06). ExerciseProbe A finished teaching-path exercise (22 §0) for the Exercises menu tests: a litter that keeps the reference's rule. Its name is not MyLitter, so the menu never takes it for a student's stub. FakeHttpTransport A fake server for HTTP brains and mutators (30 §2): answers each request with a scripted function, records every request, can fail, hang until the time-out, or answer late; counts requests in flight at once. FakeMutator A test mutator client (30 §2): answers mutation prompts with a scripted function (by default it appends "quickly" to the sentence), records every prompt and batch, and can answer N Advance calls late or fail. FeedAction A test-only action: stay, and eat a snack of Energy through a custom interaction that feeds the animal with Feed(Animal, float, bool) (a meal counted like any other). Fruit A test-only entity of a kind of one's own: a fruit. FruitSystem A test-only entity system for fruit: nothing moves or rots. Several systems of one kind can live in a world ("Apples", "Pears"), and actions find their entities with NearestEntity<Fruit>. GoToAction A test action that walks or runs toward a fixed point, stopping at a distance (T-SPACE-01, T-MOVE-01). Golden Golden files under Assets/EvoSim/Tests/Golden/ (30 §2): situation texts, prompts, hashes. A missing file is written from the current output (pinned from the first accepted run); an existing one must match exactly. Re-pinning is a deliberate commit that deletes or edits the file and says why. HookProbe A test-only species module that counts the births and deaths it hears and adds two statistics columns (probe_born, probe_died, written with the species' prefix in stats.csv). InvariantPhase A last phase for test worlds: fails the test on the first broken invariant (30 §5). Invariants The checks run after every tick in test worlds (30 §5): positions inside and walkable, no NaN, stats in range, unique ids, no dead or killed animal left, valid actions and rows, populations between floor and cap, carcass portions ≥ 0, genomes of the right length and species. Lab The Lab 1 reference species and world as ready-made recipes for tests (04 §5, 08 §7, 09 §3, 14 §2): prey (eat, flee, hide, follow, rest, mate) and predator (hunt, follow, rest, mate) with the prototype's values, founder pools, contrast pairs and prompt texts. MemoryBrain A test-only brain with memory: not memoizable, so every deciding animal's query reaches it with its id (even animals in the same situation), and it answers uniform rows. NeedsEnergyProbe A test-only module that names a companion it needs with RequiresModuleAttribute: a species without an Energy module gets the warning V-26, whose fix adds one. ObstacleSense A test batched sense: one ray along the heading; "blocked" if it hits a collider within 5 m (T-SENSE-09). OverlayProbeAction A test-only overlay (ACT-07): done in passing, it plans a walk that must be ignored and a custom interaction that counts the times it applied, per animal. Place Puts animals, food items, cover and carcasses at exact positions in a built world (30 §2), so a test sets up the very situation it checks. Records no event. PondGround A test ground: flat, with a round pond (not walkable) whose shore animals can reach (samples 22 §2–§3). It answers the water queries that the water sense and the drink action ask. ProbeAction A test-only action defined outside the runtime assembly (T-CORE-02): it counts its calls and stays. ProbeSense A test-only sense with two tokens; it returns the animal's id parity (T-CORE-02). RampGround A test ground: flat for x < RampStart, then a ramp rising at RampSlope (height per meter) (T-MOVE-07). RandomEventPhase A test phase that draws from a named stream every tick and records a "probe" event, so the hash depends on the draws. ScriptedBrain A test brain (30 §2): answers from a policy written in the test, or from given rows per (species, observation); counts calls and batches; can answer N Advance calls late, fail, or refuse to mix species. Test code only: the system ships no rule-based brain (owner decision). ShowProbeView A test-only view that remembers what OnShow told it. SideCover A test-only cover: every point with x in [MinX, MaxX] is in cover. Several covers in one world combine (ENV-11). SlopeLimitLocomotion A kinematic locomotion that refuses slopes steeper than a limit (T-MOVE-07, after 22 §14). SnapshotPhase A test phase that keeps every living animal's genome texts at the end of each tick (T-OUT-02). SourceScan Reads the EvoSim source files for static checks (T-RAND-01, T-CORE-08, T-ACT-09): comments removed, line numbers kept. SpeciesSetup Adds modules to one species of a world being built: what Species(string, Action<SpeciesSetup>, string) hands to its configure callback. Stat Statistical asserts: a proportion or a mean within k standard errors, a χ² uniformity test (30 §2). SureKillDiet A test-only diet: every strike kills, and every meal gives exactly Meal energy. ThrowingPhase A test phase that throws, for the RAND-20 test: the World stops the run cleanly ("exception in ThrowingPhase") and lets the exception through. TracePhase A test phase that writes "tick:name" to a log each time it runs (T-TICK-01). TraitProbe A test module declaring one trait (default 60, range [1, 120]) and one capped stat (T-ANIM-02, T-ANIM-03). TurningLocomotion A test locomotion that ignores the intent's direction: it turns it by 30° and halves the distance (T-MOVE-06). WorldBuilder Builds a world in code, with no scene (30 §2): ground, food, cover, services, phases and species, each added by one chained call, then Build(). WorldFixture The base class of tests that build worlds: every world started with New(int, WaitMode, string) is destroyed after each test, so tests leave nothing in the scene. WorldHookProbe A test-only world service that counts every species' births and deaths and adds one statistics column (world_born, after the species' columns in stats.csv).

§9, a phase placed before Environment that slows regrowth in winter: public class SeasonsPhase : TickPhase { [SerializeField] int yearLength = 2000; [SerializeField] float winterRegrowFactor = 0.2f; FoodGrid food; public override void Initialize() => food = World.Service<FoodGrid>("Grass"); public override void Run(TickContext t) { if (food != null) food.RegrowFactor = t.Tick % yearLength >= yearLength / 2 ? winterRegrowFactor : 1f; } } A phase that waits for the brains' answers (the Choose actions phase): public override Pending WaitsFor(TickContext t) => World.Decisions.Pending; Remarks Derive from it, implement Run(TickContext), and place the component among the World's phases (the children of its Phases object in the reference scenes): its place there is its place in every tick. Phases run in the same order every tick (TICK-07); a phase with nothing to do returns at once. A phase changes only what it is responsible for; what it changes is visible to the phases after it in the same tick (TICK-02). It draws random numbers only from named streams (Stream(string), RAND-02) and loops only over ordered lists (RAND-05), so a seed always gives the same run. A phase that needs answers from a service (brains, the mutator) returns them as a Pending from WaitsFor(TickContext): the World runs it only once they are in (TICK-03). Properties PhaseName A short name for logs and the profiler. public virtual string PhaseName { get; } Property Value string Remarks By default the class name; the profiler marker of the phase is EvoSim.<PhaseName>. Methods PlaceAfter(TickPhase) V-08's fix: move this phase just after another one, when both sit under the same GameObject. protected ValidationFix PlaceAfter(TickPhase other) Parameters other TickPhase The phase this one must follow, or null. Returns ValidationFix The fix, or null when other is null, is this phase, or has another parent. Examples report.Error("V-08", this, "Ask brains must come after the Sense phase.", PlaceAfter(World.Phase<SensePhase>())); PlaceBefore(TickPhase) V-08's fix: move this phase just before another one, when both sit under the same GameObject. protected ValidationFix PlaceBefore(TickPhase other) Parameters other TickPhase The phase this one must precede, or null. Returns ValidationFix The fix, or null when other is null, is this phase, or has another parent. Run(TickContext) Do this phase's work for the current tick. public abstract void Run(TickContext t) Parameters t TickContext The current tick's context: the World, the tick number and the random streams. Remarks Called once per tick, after WaitsFor(TickContext)'s work is done. An exception stops the run. WaitsFor(TickContext) Work this phase must wait for (brain answers, mutations); null = none (TICK-03). public virtual Pending WaitsFor(TickContext t) Parameters t TickContext The current tick's context. Returns Pending What must be done before Run(TickContext), or null when nothing is awaited. A Pending already done lets the phase run at once. Remarks The World asks before every attempt to run the phase: in Responsive mode, again at every Advance call while the tick waits. Return the same work for the same tick, and don't change the world or draw random numbers here, so both wait modes give the same run (SPACE-14, RAND-11).

api/EvoSim.ValueNoise.html.summary: Class ValueNoise Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll Value noise on a lattice: random values at lattice points, smoothly interpolated (the prototype's cover and terrain maps). World from code, as a test or a batch run does: world.Seed = 7; world.WaitMode = WaitMode.Freeze; if (!world.Initialize()) { Debug.LogError(world.LastReport); return; } world.Advance(500); world.Stop("done"); Debug.Log(world.Events.ShortHash); A module finds what it needs from its World in Initialize (ARCH-08): public override void Initialize() => food = World.Service<FoodGrid>("Grass"); Remarks Place one World at the root of a simulation. Everything below it belongs to it (ARCH-05): the species, the tick phases and the services. A World inside another World is an error (V-16). Modules never set themselves up in Awake, Start or OnEnable: the World calls them, always in the same order (ARCH-04). Initialize() (called by Play(), or in Awake when StartOnPlay is on) first runs Prepare(ValidationReport): random streams and event log from the seed, species found, world modules found and bound, services initialised (the ground first), each species' modules collected, genes bound, every Declare(SpeciesBuilder) then every Initialize(), phases initialised, founder pools registered, the food web derived, signatures and prompts built, then validation. When no error was found it makes the views, calls every Begin(), and spawns the founders (POP-04). A tick runs the phases in order (TICK-01). Before each phase the World asks its WaitsFor(TickContext); when the answer is not ready, Responsive returns from Advance(int) and resumes the same phase on a later call, and Freeze blocks on Wait(). Both give the same events hash (RAND-11). Stop conditions are checked only between ticks, so a stopped run's files are complete (RAND-20). The class is split in several files: World.Animals.cs (founders, newcomers, distance), World.Deaths.cs, World.FoodWeb.cs, World.Species.cs (species added during a run), World.Space.cs, World.Views.cs and World.Checks.cs. Fields ObservationSpaceError Sizes of a species' observation space (its number of possible observations) above which validation warns and fails (SENSE-05, V-50). public const double ObservationSpaceError = 10000000 Field Value double ObservationSpaceWarning Sizes of a species' observation space (its number of possible observations) above which validation warns and fails (SENSE-05, V-50). public const double ObservationSpaceWarning = 100000 Field Value double Properties AdvanceCalls Calls to Advance since Initialize. Test fakes count their delays in these calls (30 §2). public int AdvanceCalls { get; } Property Value int AllSpecies The enabled species of this World in hierarchy order, then those added during the run (SPEC-30). public IReadOnlyList<Species> AllSpecies { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<Species> Alleles Every allele seen in this run (GENE-10). public AlleleRegistry Alleles { get; } Property Value AlleleRegistry Asexual Control C7 ASEXUAL (CTRL-01, REPRO-04): true when each birth has one parent, copied and mutated. public bool Asexual { get; set; } Property Value bool Context The context every phase receives, the same object for the whole run. Tests use it to run one phase by hand. public TickContext Context { get; } Property Value TickContext ControlSentences The control sentences for C4 RANDOM-FOUNDERS and the brain tests (GENE-23). public IReadOnlyList<string> ControlSentences { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<string> DecisionPeriod Ticks between two decisions of one animal (DEC-01); at least 1. Reference 4. public int DecisionPeriod { get; set; } Property Value int Decisions The decisions of the current tick and the run's memo (08). public DecisionState Decisions { get; } Property Value DecisionState DefaultBrain The brain of the species that name none (DEC-13), or null. public Brain DefaultBrain { get; set; } Property Value Brain Events The run's event log and its running hash (RAND-10). New at each Initialize. public EventLog Events { get; } Property Value EventLog Ground The ground service (SPACE-04), or null in a world without one. public Ground Ground { get; } Property Value Ground InterpolateViews True to place each view between its animal's previous and current positions, for smooth motion between ticks. public bool InterpolateViews { get; set; } Property Value bool InterpolationFactor The fraction of the next tick already elapsed (0 just after a tick, 1 when the next is due): the FixedUpdate clock, or the RealTime carry. 1 while waiting or paused: the views rest where the last tick left them. public float InterpolationFactor { get; } Property Value float IsInitialized True once Initialize succeeded; false before it, and after a validation error. public bool IsInitialized { get; } Property Value bool LastReport The validation report of the last Initialize, or null before the first one. public ValidationReport LastReport { get; } Property Value ValidationReport MemoCapacity Most keys the decision memo keeps (DEC-30); 0 = no limit. A change takes effect at the next Initialize. public int MemoCapacity { get; set; } Property Value int Mutations Mutation statistics of the run (MUT-05). public MutationStats Mutations { get; } Property Value MutationStats NextPhaseIndex The index in Phases of the phase that runs next in the current tick (0 = between ticks). public int NextPhaseIndex { get; } Property Value int NoMutation Control C2 NO-MUT (CTRL-01): true when the mutation rate is 0 for every species. public bool NoMutation { get; set; } Property Value bool Phases The tick phases in the order they run every tick: their hierarchy order (TICK-01). public IReadOnlyList<TickPhase> Phases { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<TickPhase> Queries The queries senses and actions share (ACT-05, SENSE-06). public WorldQueries Queries { get; } Property Value WorldQueries Random The run's named random streams (RAND-02): every draw of the simulation comes from one. New at each Initialize. public RandomStreams Random { get; } Property Value RandomStreams RandomFounders Control C4 RANDOM-FOUNDERS (CTRL-01): true when founders get control sentences and random numbers in range. public bool RandomFounders { get; set; } Property Value bool RealTimeTicksPerSecond Ticks per second with the RealTime speed; at least 0.1. public float RealTimeTicksPerSecond { get; set; } Property Value float RunSpeed How fast a running World advances. Results never depend on it (SPACE-11). public RunSpeed RunSpeed { get; set; } Property Value RunSpeed SamplingTemperature The sampling temperature τ: each probability p becomes p^(1/τ), renormalised, before an action is drawn (DEC-20). 1 keeps the brain's probabilities; at least 0.01. public float SamplingTemperature { get; set; } Property Value float Seed The run seed: every random stream derives from it (RAND-02). A change takes effect at the next Initialize. public int Seed { get; set; } Property Value int Services The enabled services under the World, in hierarchy order. public IReadOnlyList<WorldService> Services { get; } Property Value IReadOnlyList<WorldService> ShowViews True to draw the animals. Views only read the run (SPACE-12), so this never changes it. public bool ShowViews { get; set; } Property Value bool ShuffledGenes Control C3 SHUFFLED (CTRL-01): true when each decision reads the genes of another living animal of the species, and number genes are expressed from another animal's genome at birth. public bool ShuffledGenes { get; set; } Property Value bool Space The spatial index of animals (SENSE-32), built on the ground's rectangle. public SpatialIndex Space { get; } Property Value SpatialIndex Remarks Made on first use. The sense and act phases rebuild it; the act phase updates it after each move. StartOnPlay True to initialise and run when Play mode starts. A launcher turns it off in Configuring. public bool StartOnPlay { get; set; } Property Value bool State The state of the run for the run controls and the editor: Idle before Initialize, Stopped, Blocked or Waiting when that holds, else what the controls asked (Running, Paused, Stepping). public RunState State { get; } Property Value RunState StopFile A file path: the run stops at the next tick boundary once this file exists. Empty = off; never null. public string StopFile { get; set; } Property Value string StopOnExtinction True to stop the run at the first tick boundary where a species has no animal left. public bool StopOnExtinction { get; set; } Property Value bool StopReason Why the run stopped ("tick limit", "stop file", "extinction of prey"…), or null while it runs. public string StopReason { get; } Property Value string TextStyle The style of the situation texts of every species (SENSE-11). public TextStyle TextStyle { get; set; } Property Value TextStyle Tick The current tick: the number of ticks completed since the run started (0 during the first tick). Simulation time is counted in ticks, never in seconds (SPACE-10). public int Tick { get; } Property Value int TickLimit Stops the run after this many ticks; 0 = no limit. public int TickLimit { get; set; } Property Value int TicksPerFixedUpdate Ticks per FixedUpdate with the PerFixedUpdate speed; at least 1. public int TicksPerFixedUpdate { get; set; } Property Value int ViewCount Views on screen now. public int ViewCount { get; } Property Value int ViewsOutsidePlayMode True to make views outside Play mode too (tests and batch runs leave it off). Read at Initialize. public bool ViewsOutsidePlayMode { get; set; } Property Value bool ViewsTick The tick the views last showed (-1 before the first sync), so checks compare like with like. public int ViewsTick { get; } Property Value int WaitCount Times a phase made a tick wait since Initialize, once per tick and phase (scenario S14's wait counter). public int WaitCount { get; } Property Value int WaitMode How a tick waits for brain answers and mutations: Freeze blocks the main thread, Responsive returns and resumes later (SPACE-14). Both give the same events hash (RAND-11). public WaitMode WaitMode { get; set; } Property Value WaitMode WaitingFor The phase the tick is waiting for, or null when it is not waiting. public TickPhase WaitingFor { get; } Property Value TickPhase WallClockMinutes Stops the run after this many minutes of wall-clock time since Initialize; 0 = no limit. public float WallClockMinutes { get; set; } Property Value float WorldSeed The seed of the map's streams (terrain, cover, initial food): its own seed when set, else the run seed (RAND-04). public int WorldSeed { get; } Property Value int Methods AddNewcomer(Species) A newcomer below the floor: founder genome, random walkable position, generation 0 (POP-03). public Animal AddNewcomer(Species s) Parameters s Species The species that gets the newcomer. Returns Animal The new animal, already among the living and recorded as an immigrant event. Remarks Called by the floor phase; a student's own phase may call it too. It draws from the species' founders stream. AddSpecies(Species, string, Species, int) A new species during a run (SPEC-30): a clone of the template under this World, with a new id (never reused, SPEC-32), its own population, streams and allele namespace. By default it inherits the parent's relations both ways (SPEC-31): it eats what the parent eats, and whoever hunted the parent hunts it. public Species AddSpecies(Species template, string name, Species parent = null, int founders = 0) Parameters template Species The species to clone, with all its modules; usually a species of this World. name string The wanted id and display name; name-2, name-3… when it is taken. parent Species The species it descends from (Parent); null = the template. founders int Founders to spawn at once, at random walkable positions. Returns Species The new species, set up, validated, and in AllSpecies. Remarks The new species goes through the same set-up and checks as at Initialize. Then the World records a species_created event and calls every world module's OnSpeciesAdded(Species) before the founders spawn. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The World is not initialised, or the new species fails validation (the clone is then destroyed). Advance(int) Runs up to maxTicks ticks and returns how many completed. In Responsive mode it returns early when a phase must wait, and the same tick continues at that phase on a later call; in Freeze mode it blocks. public int Advance(int maxTicks) Parameters maxTicks int The most ticks to run in this call. Returns int The ticks completed in this call: fewer than maxTicks when a phase waits (Responsive), when the run stops, or 0 once it stopped. Remarks Before running a phase it asks the phase's WaitsFor(TickContext). A Pending that is not done counts once in WaitCount; then Responsive returns, and Freeze calls Wait(). Stop conditions are checked between ticks only (RAND-20). An exception in a phase stops the run (its reason names the phase) and is thrown again. Exceptions InvalidOperationException The World is not initialised. Distance(Vector3, Vector3) The world distance between two points (SPACE-02): the ground's function, horizontal Euclidean by default. public float Distance(Vector3 a, Vector3 b) Parameters a Vector3 One point. b Vector3 The other point. Returns float The distance in meters, measured on the horizontal plane by default. Remarks Every module measures through it, so a ground that measures path length changes every distance at once. FindSpecies(string) A species by id, or null. public Species FindSpecies(string id) Parameters id string The species' id (SPEC-01), as files and stream names use it. Returns Species The species with that id, or null when there is none. FindSpeciesByName(string) A species by id or display name, or null. public Species FindSpeciesByName(string idOrName) Parameters idOrName string An id, or a display name when no species has that id. Returns Species The species found, ids first, or null. FounderGenome(Species, RandomStream) A founder genome: each locus drawn uniformly from its pool (GENE-20), or the C4 control's alleles. public Genome FounderGenome(Species s, RandomStream rng) Parameters s Species The species whose genes make the genome. rng RandomStream The stream to draw from: the species' founders stream (RAND-03). Returns Genome A new genome with one registered allele per gene, in locus order. Exceptions InvalidOperationException A gene has an empty founder pool (V-41), or C4 is on and the World has no control sentence. GenomeIds(Genome) The allele ids of a genome, in locus order, for events (OUT-03). public static List<string> GenomeIds(Genome g) Parameters g Genome The genome, or null. Returns List<string> A new list of allele ids; empty for a null genome. Initialize() Discovery, set-up, validation, founders. Returns false and keeps the report when an error is found. public bool Initialize() Returns bool True when the World is ready to advance (paused); false when validation found an error, which is logged and kept in LastReport. Remarks Runs Prepare(ValidationReport) (steps 1–8 of 20 §4), then makes the views (step 9), calls every world module's Begin() in hierarchy order, and spawns the founders at tick 0 (step 10, POP-04). Calling it again starts a new run from the seed. IsThreat(Species, Species) Whether hunter is a threat of target. public bool IsThreat(Species hunter, Species target) Parameters hunter Species The species that may strike. target Species The species that may be struck. Returns bool True when the hunter's diet strikes the target (SPEC-12). NextAnimalId() The next animal id: unique in the run, increasing, never reused (ANIM-02). public int NextAnimalId() Returns int An id no animal of this run had. CreateAnimal(string, Vector3, float, Genome, int, int[], Action<Animal>) takes one for each animal. NextEntityId() The next entity id (carcasses, eggs): unique in the run, never reused. public int NextEntityId() Returns int An id no entity of this run had. Entity systems take one for each entity. Pause() Stops advancing until Resume, Play, Step or RunFor. A tick that is waiting stays where it is. public void Pause() Phase<T>() The first phase of that type, or null. public T Phase<T>() where T : TickPhase Returns T The first matching phase in tick order, or null when the World has none. Type Parameters T The kind of phase to find. Play() Starts or resumes the run, initialising the World first when needed; clears any RunFor limit. public void Play() Prepare(ValidationReport) Steps 1–8 of 20 §4: find species and modules, initialise services, collect and bind species modules, declare and initialise, derive the food web, validate. No animal is created. The editor validates with it. public bool Prepare(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Receives every validation message (errors, warnings, information). Returns bool True when the report holds no error. It stops early at the first step that found one. Remarks It resets the run state (tick 0, new random streams and event log from the seed) and leaves the World not initialised: Initialize() calls it and then starts the run. PreyOf(Species) The species this one strikes. public IReadOnlyList<Species> PreyOf(Species s) Parameters s Species The hunting species. Returns IReadOnlyList<Species> Its prey in species order; empty when none. RandomPosition(RandomStream) A random walkable position (POP-03, POP-04); the origin without a ground. public Vector3 RandomPosition(RandomStream rng) Parameters rng RandomStream The stream to draw from, e.g. the species' founders stream. Returns Vector3 A walkable point on the ground, or UnityEngine.Vector3.zero when the World has no ground. RebuildFoodWeb() Re-derives the food web after a species was added during a run (SPEC-30, SPEC-31). public void RebuildFoodWeb() Remarks It first resolves every diet again, so diets that name the new species find it. RecordDeath(Animal, string) Marks the animal gone and records its death once (ANIM-42): cause, age, generation, meals, offspring, and the killer for a kill. It leaves the species' list at the end of the phase. public void RecordDeath(Animal a, string cause) Parameters a Animal The animal that dies; nothing happens when it is already gone. cause string The cause, as events and the statistics name it: "killed", "starvation", "old_age", "migrated", or a cause of your own (it gets its deaths_<cause> column). Examples World.RecordDeath(a, "lightning"); // a death of your own, in your own phase a.Species.RemoveGone(); Remarks After the death event, it calls the species' OnDied(Animal, string), then each of its modules' OnDied(Animal, string), then each world module's OnDied(Animal, string). The animal stays in Animals until the phase that killed it calls RemoveGone(): a death phase of your own must call it too. RequestStop(string) Stops at the next tick boundary (a button, a stop file). public void RequestStop(string reason) Parameters reason string Why the run stops; StopReason and every OnRunStopped(string) receive it. Remarks Between ticks it stops at once; inside a tick (a phase is waiting) it stops when that tick ends. Resolve(Species, AnimalSet, IReadOnlyList<Species>) The species of an animal set for a species (SPEC-12); Listed uses the given list. public IReadOnlyList<Species> Resolve(Species s, AnimalSet set, IReadOnlyList<Species> listed = null) Parameters s Species The species whose point of view the set takes (its threats, its prey, its kin). set AnimalSet Which set: threats, prey, kin, or listed. listed IReadOnlyList<Species> The species of a Listed set; ignored for the others. Returns IReadOnlyList<Species> The species of the set, in species order; empty when none. Resume() Continues a paused run. public void Resume() RunFor(int) Runs that many more ticks, then pauses. Does nothing before Initialize. public void RunFor(int ticks) Parameters ticks int The ticks to run; a negative number counts as 0. Service<T>() The first enabled service of that type, in hierarchy order. public T Service<T>() where T : class Returns T The service, or null when the World has none of that type. Type Parameters T The kind of service to find: a service class or an interface services implement. Remarks Call it in a module's Initialize and keep the result: services are found by role, never by a scene reference (ARCH-08). Service<T>(string) The service of that type with this name (its GameObject's name), ARCH-08. public T Service<T>(string name) where T : class Parameters name string The ServiceName to match, e.g. "Grass" for a layer. Returns T The first matching service in hierarchy order, or null. Type Parameters T The kind of service to find. ServicesOf<T>() Every enabled service of that type, in hierarchy order. public IEnumerable<T> ServicesOf<T>() where T : class Returns IEnumerable<T> The matching services; empty when there is none. Type Parameters T The kind of service to find: a service class or an interface. SetControlSentences(IEnumerable<string>) Replaces the control sentences (GENE-23). public void SetControlSentences(IEnumerable<string> sentences) Parameters sentences IEnumerable<string> The new sentences; the list is copied. SetWorldSeed(int) Gives the map its own seed (RAND-04), so many runs can share one map while everything else varies. public void SetWorldSeed(int value) Parameters value int The map's seed; it takes effect at the next Initialize. Step() Runs one tick, then pauses. Does nothing before Initialize. public void Step() Stop(string) Stops now. Called at a tick boundary, or inside a tick before anything changed the world (a strict brain failure in the Choose actions phase), so the outputs stay consistent (RAND-20). public void Stop(string reason) Parameters reason string Why the run stops; StopReason and every OnRunStopped(string) receive it. Remarks Calls every world module's OnRunStopped(string) once, in hierarchy order; an exception there is logged and the other modules still hear the stop. Does nothing when the run already stopped or was never initialised. Use RequestStop(string) from anywhere else. ThreatsOf(Species) The species whose diet strikes this one (SPEC-12); a cannibal is among its own threats (SPEC-11). public IReadOnlyList<Species> ThreatsOf(Species s) Parameters s Species The species that is hunted. Returns IReadOnlyList<Species> Its threats in species order; empty when none, or before the food web is derived. ViewOf(Animal) The view that shows an animal now. public AnimalView ViewOf(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The animal, or null. Returns AnimalView Its view, or null when it has none (no Body, views off, or gone). Events Configuring Heard by every World in Awake, before it starts on Play: a launcher (a player's command line, a test) sets the seed, speed or brain here, or turns StartOnPlay off. It runs before anything of the run exists. public static event Action<World> Configuring Event Type Action<World> Remarks Raised in Play mode only. The event is static: whoever subscribes must unsubscribe when done. See PlayerLauncher for the player's command line.

scene's camera (it needs a Camera on the same GameObject). It orbits a focus point on the ground, at Distance meters, looking down at the Inspector's pitch. Controls, read only while the window has the focus, in real time, so they work while the run is paused or waits: W A S D or the arrow keys: pan, at panSpeed camera distances per second; stops following. Mouse wheel: zoom, from 3 to 2 000 m; not over the overlay's panels. Right mouse button held: orbit (mouse left and right) and tilt (mouse up and down, 10° to 89°). Q and E: orbit left and right, at orbitSpeed degrees per second. Middle mouse button held: drag the ground; stops following. F: frame the whole world again; stops following. Remarks It compares screen positions of the views (a little above their feet), so views need no collider.

that counts births and reports them when the run ends: public class BirthCounter : WorldService { public int Born { get; private set; } public override void Initialize() => Born = 0; public override void OnBorn(Animal a) => Born++; public override void OnRunStopped(string reason) => Debug.Log($"{Born} births ({reason})"); } Remarks Do not derive from it directly: derive from TickPhase for a step of every tick, or from WorldService for something phases and modules use. Place the component on a GameObject under the World and outside every species (one under a species is ignored, V-15). A disabled component or an inactive GameObject is absent (ARCH-06). The World calls the hooks in this order, and in hierarchy order among modules: Initialize(): services first (the ground before the others), before the species' modules exist; phases later, after every species module is initialised (20 §4). Validate(ValidationReport): after every Initialize, in the editor and at the start of a run; again when a species is added during the run. Begin(): once, when the run starts, before the founders. OnBorn(Animal), OnDied(Animal, string), OnSpeciesAdded(Species): during the run, founders included. OnRunStopped(string): once, at the end. Never set things up in Awake, Start or OnEnable: Unity doesn't guarantee their order (ARCH-04). Keep no static state (ARCH-07): several Worlds may run side by side. Properties World The World this module belongs to; null until the World found it (step 2 of 20 §4). public World World { get; } Property Value World Methods Begin() Called once after every module is initialised and validated, before founders spawn, in hierarchy order: place initial content here (the first food items), when it depends on other services (cover). public virtual void Begin() Remarks Not called when the editor only validates. Draw random numbers from a named stream, e.g. World.Random.Get("world/" + ServiceName) for the map (RAND-04). Initialize() Called by the World in a fixed order, before any animal exists (ARCH-04). public virtual void Initialize() Remarks Look up what you need here, by role or name (Service<T>(), Phase<T>()), and reset your own state: the same object starts every run of the World. A service is initialised before the species' modules; a phase after them. OnBorn(Animal) An animal of any species joined the living (a founder, a baby, an immigrant), after its species' modules heard it. public virtual void OnBorn(Animal a) Parameters a Animal The new animal, its stats set and already among its species' animals. OnDied(Animal, string) An animal of any species died, after its species' modules heard it (ANIM-42). public virtual void OnDied(Animal a, string cause) Parameters a Animal The animal, already marked gone; it leaves its species' list at the end of the phase. cause string The cause of death, e.g. "killed", "starvation", "migrated". OnRunStopped(string) Called once when the run stops, whatever the reason (RAND-20). public virtual void OnRunStopped(string reason) Parameters reason string Why it stopped, as StopReason says: "tick limit", "stop file", "world disabled"… Remarks Write and close your files here (the run recorder does). An exception is logged and the other modules still hear the stop. OnSpeciesAdded(Species) Called when a species is added during the run (SPEC-30), after it is set up and its event recorded. public virtual void OnSpeciesAdded(Species species) Parameters species Species The new species; its founders are not spawned yet. Validate(ValidationReport) Report configuration problems (editor, and at the start of a run). public virtual void Validate(ValidationReport report) Parameters report ValidationReport Add one message per problem, naming its validator id (V-…) and the object at fault. An error stops the run from starting. Remarks Only read: validation must not change the scene. Offer a change as a ValidationFix.

api/EvoSim.WorldQueries.html.summary: Class WorldQueries Namespace EvoSim Assembly EvoSim.Runtime.dll The queries senses and actions share (ACT-05, SENSE-06): within the animal's vision, never itself, never a killed animal, never an animal hidden from it in cover, diets checked. Ties by id (SPACE-08). public sealed class WorldQueries Inheritance object WorldQueries Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Examples var threat = World.Queries.NearestAnimal(a, AnimalSet.Threats); // within a's vision if (threat != null && threat.Value.Distance < 5f) { /* ... */ } Remarks Reach it with Queries; senses usually call it through their SenseContext and actions through their ActContext. Using the same queries is what keeps an action from targeting something its senses could not report (ACT-05). Every query only reads the world. Results are null when nothing is found. api/EvoSim.html.title: Namespace EvoSim | EvoSim
api/EvoSim.html.summary: Namespace EvoSim Classes ActContext What an action may do in one tick (ACT-06): ask questions about what the animal could sense, and say where it wants to go (an intent) and what to do on arrival (an interaction). It can't move or change any animal itself. ActPhase Every living animal acts, in the act order (ACT-30): its action plans an intent and an interaction, its species' locomotion moves it, interactions apply within reach, then its metabolism is paid and busy counters drop (TICK-04 #4, ANIM-20, ANIM-30). ActionColors One colour per action name, shared by the views and the overlay's legend. Actions it doesn't know get a colour from their name's characters (the same on every run; no random numbers, RAND-11). ActionView The reference body's view (20 §6): a marker above the head in the colour of the animal's action (ActionColors), and a body that darkens as its energy drops. It only reads the animal (SPACE-12). Copy it to show something else: override OnShow(Animal) and read what you need. AgeSense Young or adult (06 §4): adult from the maturity trait (ANIM-36), reference 150 ticks. Allele One registered allele with its lineage (GENE-11, GENE-12): one version of a gene, such as the sentence "Rest when you are tired." at the prey's rest gene, or the number 60 at a stamina gene. AllelePool Founder and contrast sentences shared by several text genes, as an asset (GENE-24, 20 §3.8). AlleleRegistry Every allele seen in a run, once per (locus, value) (GENE-10), with ids "<locus>:<n>" (GENE-11). Animal One animal: plain data owned by its species (ANIM-01, ARCH-03). Modules read and write it through this record. AnimalAction A behaviour the brain can choose (ACT-01). Each tick it gives an intent and maybe an interaction; it never moves anything itself. AnimalView One animal's view (20 §6): it holds only the animal's id and has no Update; the World places it in LateUpdate and never reads it back (SPACE-12). AnimalWords Common animal words, for the stale-name check V-23 (SPEC-21): a founder sentence naming one of them that is no species of the world was probably written for another world, or before a rename. AnswerCache A persistent store of brain and mutator answers (DEC-33, MUT-14): append-only JSON lines, one file per brain, loaded at the first lookup. Keys hash everything that can change an answer, so a repeated run replays without model calls (RAND-21). Rows are stored with round-trip precision, so a replay is bit-identical. AskBrainsPhase Builds each deciding animal's query (DEC-10), answers it from the memo (DEC-30) or the answer cache (DEC-33), sends the rest as one batch per brain — per species for brains that can't mix species — with identical keys sent once (DEC-13, DEC-15, DEC-32). Nothing in the world changes here (CORE-06). BandedSense A sense that reports how far the nearest something is, in bands (06 §3): "here" (optional), the bands, "none". Wording (SENSE-10…13): V1 "Food: 1-4 meters away." / V2 "The nearest food is 1-4 meters away.". Bands Distance bands (06 §3, SENSE-20): increasing edges e1 < … < ek and a vision v > ek. A distance falls in the first band with d ≤ ei, in "far" if ek < d ≤ v, and is "none" beyond v. Reference: 1, 4, 10 m and 20 m. Batch Headless runs (30 §6, 31 §1, 32 §4): Unity -batchmode -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] [-responsive]. In the open editor the same runs go through RunScenarioNamed (the unity CLI's eval). Worlds run in Freeze mode, outside Play mode: the World initialises itself (ARCH-04). BatchedSense A sense that casts rays (line of sight, terrain ahead): it asks for its rays first; the sense phase casts the rays of all deciding animals in one batch, then each sense reads its results (SENSE-30). It must give the same tokens as evaluating it one animal at a time (SENSE-31). Body What a species' animals look like (20 §6): a view prefab, or a placeholder capsule of a colour. Views only read the simulation (SPACE-12); a species without a Body runs unseen. Brain Maps a batch of queries to probability rows over the species' actions (DEC-11). BrainAnswer A brain's answer to a batch (DEC-11): one probability row per query, in query order, or a failure per query. Fast brains fill it at once; HTTP brains later, from another thread, then mark it done. BrainRequest One decision query as an HTTP brain sends it: its place in the batch, the text for the model and the species' action names. Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>) builds it on the main thread; AnswerAsync(HttpCaller, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest>, BrainAnswer) reads it on the thread pool, so it holds plain values only, no Unity object. BreedPhase After all animals acted (TICK-06): each ready animal that chose mate and hasn't bred this period breeds with the nearest ready partner within reach that hasn't bred either — one partner's choice is enough (REPRO-02, REPRO-03). A litter is conceived (REPRO-10, REPRO-11): one egg per baby with its own crossover and its mutations drawn now (GENE-32, MUT-30); the LLM mutations are sent as one batch at the end (MUT-31). CanonicalJson Writes JSON with sorted keys and fixed number formatting, so equal data gives equal text (RAND-10). Separators follow Python's json.dumps defaults (", " and ": "), the prototype's format. CapRule The maximum population of a species (POP-01). Migrate (reference): births go on, and above the cap random older animals leave the world. Block: no conception at the cap, litters cut to the places left. Carcass What a kill leaves (03 §3): a few portions that other eaters may eat, one portion each, never the killer. It rots away when its lifetime runs out, eaten or not, and goes as soon as its last portion is eaten (ENV-22). CarcassSystem Carcasses, as each species' edible component describes them: portions, energy, lifetime (03 §3). A carcass of a species is edible when that species' Edible leaves one; diets name it "carcass:<species>". CellGrid A grid of square cells over the world rectangle, used inside layers (food cells, cover cells) — never to place animals (02 intro). Finds the nearest marked cell by expanding rings (20 §9). ChooseActionsPhase Waits for the brains (TICK-03), stores fresh answers in the memo and the cache (never a failure, DEC-34), and draws each deciding animal's action with its species' sampling stream after the temperature (DEC-20, RAND-03). A failed answer stops a strict run cleanly; otherwise it becomes a uniform row and is counted (DEC-40). ContactSheet A grid of a folder's PNG captures, scaled down on the GPU, saved as contact_sheet.png. Cover Places where an animal is hidden from the species that hunt it (03 §2). Optional: a world without one behaves as if no point were in cover (ENV-12). CoverLayer Cover in clustered patches (thickets): the top EvoSim.CoverLayer.fraction of walkable cells of a value-noise map, drawn from the world stream (03 §2 reference: 20 %, octaves 8 and 4 m). Crossover Builds a baby's genome from its parents', locus by locus (09 §4). Genomes never cross species (SPEC-04). DeathPhase Removes killed animals; every living animal ages by one tick (babies of this tick included); then each species' death rules (starvation, old age…) in module order. Every death is recorded once (TICK-04 #7, ANIM-35, ANIM-40…43). DeathRule A cause of death checked in the death phase (ANIM-40): return the cause's name, or null to live on. Decision One animal deciding this tick: what it sensed, what its brain was asked and answered (08 §1–§5). DecisionMemo Within a run, the answer for a key (species, brain, brain-visible genome key, observation) is computed once and reused (DEC-30). A hit gives exactly what the brain answered. Failed answers are never stored (DEC-34). Keys are kept as 128-bit hashes and identical rows are shared, so a long run's memo stays small (R-06). DecisionQuery What a brain receives for one deciding animal (DEC-10): its species, the genes its brain reads (label and sentence, in locus order), its observation, its situation text in the world's style, and any attachments. DecisionSchedule A species' own decision period, and staggering (DEC-04, MAY): an animal decides when (tick + id) % period == 0. Both change behaviour. In the reference scenes every species has one, staggered, with the World's period (owner 2026-10-10); a species without one decides all together, every World period, as the Python prototype does. DecisionState The decisions of the current tick, the brain answers they wait for, and the run's memo (08 §1–§4). Diet What a species eats (SPEC-15): layers, species, "carcass:<species>", "egg:<species>". Each target must carry an Edible (SPEC-10, V-24). A species with no diet eats nothing. Diet.Entry One line of the diet: what is eaten, and how much its energy is scaled (SPEC-15). Digestion After a kill or a carcass portion the eater is busy digesting for round(digestTicks × gain / killGain) ticks: 50 after a kill (+60), 25 after a portion (+30). Grazing never makes an animal busy (05 §5). EatAction Go to the nearest visible food and eat it (07 §4). Nothing in sight: search (ACT-04). Edible Makes what it sits on edible (SPEC-10): a species' animals, a resource layer's items, an entity kind. Without it nothing can eat that thing, whatever the diets say (ENV-23). EdibleTarget One resolved diet entry: what is eaten, how (its Edible), and the energy scale (SPEC-15). Egg A conceived baby waiting to hatch (REPRO-20): its parents, generation, genome after crossover, the mutations still running, and when it hatches. Not an animal: it doesn't sense, decide, move or count toward caps (REPRO-22). EggMutation One pending mutation of an egg: the locus, the inherited allele, the operator and its job (MUT-30). EggSystem Eggs as entities (REPRO-20). In the reference they have no Edible, so nothing eats them (owner decision); an Edible on this GameObject and a diet entry "egg:<species>" make them food (22 §15). Energy The energy stat (05 §4): founders and newcomers start at 60, the maximum is 100. Gains are clamped (ANIM-22). Entity A world object with a position that is not an animal: a carcass, an egg, a water hole (ENV-20). EntityKind A kind of entity and its system (ENV-20): carcasses, eggs. Diets name it "<kind>:<species>". EntityMarkers Small markers for the World's entities (ENV-20): a dark red disc per carcass, an ivory ball per egg, a grey cube for any other kind. Pooled primitives, placed each frame from the entity systems; they only read the World (SPACE-12): no collider, the Ignore Raycast layer. EntitySystem<T> The entities of one kind, found through spatial queries like animals (ENV-20). EnvironmentPhase Resource layers regrow, each with its own stream; entities move, rot or vanish (TICK-04 #9, ENV-03, ENV-22). EventLog The world's events and their running hash (RAND-10). The hash is chained: h0 = SHA-256 of the seeds, h(i) = SHA-256(h(i-1) ‖ UTF-8(line i)), so it can be read after any event. ExerciseOfAttribute Marks a student class as the exercise version of a reference module (22 §0, the teaching path): EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub swaps the reference for it, keeping the settings; Restore reference undoes it. Expression What a gene expresses into (GENE-03/04): a trait of the animal being born, or a line of the prompt. Express(AlleleValue, Expression) receives one and calls SetTrait(string, float, bool) or PromptGene(string, string). FieldPath Reads and overrides any serialized setting by path (CFG-02): "<GameObject path>/<Component>/<field>", relative to the World, e.g. "Prey/Litter/max", "World/decisionPeriod", "prey/Actions/flee/FleeAction/fleeIntoCover". Names are matched without case; a component is found by its class or a base class, on the GameObject or below it. FlatGround The Lab 1 ground: a flat rectangle at height 0, walkable everywhere inside (02 §1). FleeAction Run away from the nearest threat (07 §4). The prototype's "flee into cover" is an option, off in the reference: already in cover, stay; cover within coverSeek, run into it. FloorPhase While a species has fewer animals than its floor, a newcomer arrives (POP-03); it decides at the next tick (TICK-05). FloorRule The minimum population (POP-03): below it, newcomers with founder genomes arrive at random walkable places in the floor phase. A world that needs them is reported (POP-05): they restart that species' evolution. FollowAction Walk toward the nearest other animal of the species, stopping at 1 m (07 §4). FoodGrid The Lab 1 food layer (03 §1): at most one item per cell, at the cell centre; a share of walkable cells starts with an item; empty cells regrow at random, uniformly; no food in cover ("hungry cover", ENV-04). GaussianMutation The reference operator for number genes (MUT-20): v' = clamp(v + N(0, σ)) to the gene's range. Gene A gene (locus) of a species: a sentence for the brain or a number for a trait (GENE-01…04). Each animal carries one allele (one value) of every gene of its species. Genome One allele per locus of a species, in the species' locus order (GENE-06): the genes of one animal. Ground Answers, for any point, its height and whether it is walkable (SPACE-04), inside a bounded rectangle with hard borders (SPACE-03). It also owns the world's distance function (SPACE-02): every module measures through it. GroundView Draws a flat world's ground (02 §1) with its cover cells and food items (03 §1–2): one quad the size of the ground and a texture of one pixel per cell, repainted when a tick changed a cell. It only reads the World (SPACE-12): no collider, the Ignore Raycast layer, no random numbers. Hashing SHA-256 helpers for keys, signatures and prompt ids. Pure functions, no state. HatchPhase Eggs due this tick hatch, in conception order (REPRO-22), once their genome is complete: the tick waits for the mutator if its answers aren't in (MUT-32, REPRO-24). Each baby starts with the child energy, full stamina, age 0, at its first parent's position (REPRO-12), and a birth event records its litter and mutations (MUT-03). HideAction Go to the nearest cover and stay in it (07 §4, ENV-13). No cover in sight, or no cover module: search. HttpBrain The base of the brains that ask a model server over HTTP (08 §6): it turns a batch of queries into requests, sends them off the main thread and fills the BrainAnswer when the answers come back. HttpCaller JSON calls to one server with the reference client behaviour (DEC-42): a time-out per try, tries with doubling waits between them, a cap on requests in flight. The API key is read from its environment variable at each call and only sent, never stored or logged (OUT-04). HttpChecks Checks shared by HTTP brains and mutator clients (the key checks, V-61, are CheckFields(ValidationReport, MonoBehaviour)). HttpFailure An HTTP call that failed: an error status, or every try used (DEC-40, DEC-42). Messages never hold keys (OUT-04). HttpMutatorClient A mutator model behind a server (10 §2): one chat call per request with the prompt alone (CORE-07, MUT-11), the request's seed and temperature, thinking off. Calls run on the thread pool and fill the reply; the MutatorService caches answers and batches rounds (MUT-14, MUT-31). HttpStats What a brain's or mutator's HTTP calls did: tries, retries, failures, latencies (B-01, brain health window). HuntAction Chase the nearer of the nearest huntable animal and the nearest carcass it may eat (a carcass wins a tie, being a sure meal); strike the animal or eat from the carcass on arrival (07 §4). Incubation Ticks between conception and hatching (REPRO-20, REPRO-21): 0 in the reference (babies hatch the same tick); a few ticks hide the mutator's latency (MUT-33). Integrity Brain and mutator integrity checks against the real servers (32 §2): B-01 smoke and B-11 blindness here, the gates B-02 to B-10 in IntegrityGates. Command line: -executeMethod EvoSim.Integrity.RunIntegrity [-checks B-01,B-11] [-scene path] [-brain JEV]; in the open editor: Integrity.RunNamed through the unity CLI's eval. IntegrityGates The brain and mutator gates of 32 §2 (B-02…B-10), measured as the prototype measured them (e1_sensitivity): genomes from texts (founders, control sentences, the neutral genome, contrast pairs, single edits) × the reference situations (15 §2), through the scene's real prompt and brain. Queries are built from texts only: nothing is registered in the world. Each writes a report (IntegrityReport). IntegrityReport The result of one brain or mutator integrity check (32 §2): pass or fail, facts (models, digests or revisions, prompt ids, date), rows, written as JSON and Markdown under Logs/EvoSim/Reports so results compare over time. InteractionContext What a custom interaction may use when it applies: the world, the ground, the actor's streams. InteractionResolver Applies the interactions of 07 §3 after moving (ACT-10, ACT-11): only within reach, only if the target is edible and the eater's diet lists it (SPEC-13). Hunters strike at most once per tick (ACT-12). JevBrain JEV choice (08 §6): a distilled decision model behind vLLM. One /v1/completions request per batch with the list of texts, max_tokens 1, the option letters as the only allowed tokens and their log-probabilities; each row is softmax((log-prob + head bias) / T) with the head and T of the pinned revision. Options always in the species' action order; at most 16 (DEC-14); inputs above the training length are counted, not cut. JevBrain.SpeciesQuestion The question asked for one species (the prototype asked predators "Which action does this predator take now?"). JevHead JEV's decision head and calibration at a pinned revision (08 §6): the option letters' token ids, a bias per slot, the temperature of the "choice" kind. Row = softmax((log-prob + bias) / T) over the options. KinematicLocomotion The reference locomotion (MOVE-04): straight lines, no physics. Moves by the smallest of speed, stamina and the intent's maximum distance; slides along borders and obstacles; if stuck, takes a random sidestep. LevelSense A stat as low, medium or high (ANIM-12): low < low threshold ≤ medium ≤ high threshold < high. Reference: energy 30 / 70, stamina prey 20 / 40, predators 10 / 20. Litter Litter size and the energy babies cost (REPRO-10, REPRO-11): k uniform in [min, max], cut so that no parent pays more than it has, never below min; each baby starts with childEnergy, paid by the parents in equal shares. LiveStatistics Time series for the editor's ecology monitor (21 §4, OUT-06): population, mean energy and stamina, births, deaths and memo hit rate per species, sampled every few ticks into fixed-size buffers. LlmMutation The reference operator for text genes (10 §2): one instruction drawn from a deck, sent to the mutator with the sentence after one fixed context line, and nothing else (CORE-07, MUT-11). Every try's instruction and seed are drawn now (MUT-30); rejected answers are drawn again, up to tries (MUT-13). Locomotion How a species moves (MOVE-01): it turns each animal's intent into movement, and whatever it does is the tick's result. Inherit it for terrain, NavMesh or physics movement (MOVE-07). Speeds are traits (MOVE-03). ManualPending A pending completed by code: Wait() runs the given completion if it isn't done yet. MateAction Walk to the nearest ready partner in sight, stopping at 1 m (07 §4). Breeding itself happens in the breed phase, never here (ACT-13). MatingRule Who may breed and with whom (11 §1): an adult with enough energy is ready (REPRO-01); an animal that chose mate breeds with a ready partner within reach, whatever the partner chose (REPRO-02), once per decision period (REPRO-03). Metabolism What a tick costs, once per living animal after it acted (ANIM-20), from the meters its locomotion reported, its action and whether it was busy (05 §4 reference table). MigrationPhase Above its cap, a species loses animals chosen uniformly at random with its migration stream, ignoring genes, stats and position (POP-01, POP-02); animals born this tick are spared unless too few older ones remain. MoveContext What a locomotion gets to move animals: the ground, the distance function, the streams, stamina budgets. MutationJob One mutation of one gene of one baby (10 §1): its choices are drawn at conception (MUT-30); the result may come later, from the mutator (MUT-32). Succeeded → a new value; failed → the inherited allele stays (MUT-04). MutationOperator A rule that changes one allele, blind to everything but the gene and the allele (CORE-07, 10 §1). Exactly one operator applies to a locus: the one configured for the gene, else the species' default for its kind (MUT-02). MutationStats Mutation statistics of a run (MUT-05): attempts, successes, model calls, rejections by reason. MutationText The LLM mutation's prompt, cleaning and guards (MUT-10…12), as the prototype does them (prototype/promptevo/evolution/mutation.py). Pure functions. MutatorClient Sends prompts to the mutator model: Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server in EvoSim.Http, a fake in tests. It never sees anything but the prompts (CORE-07). MutatorReply The answers to a batch of mutator requests, filled later: an answer or an error per request. MutatorService Runs LLM mutations (10 §2, §4): every try's instruction and seed are drawn at conception (MUT-30); requests are batched by round — all first tries together, then the redraws of the rejected ones (MUT-31); answers are cached by model, prompt, seed and temperature (MUT-14). It advances only when pumped on the main thread, so the Freeze and Responsive wait modes give the same results. NearestAnimalSense The nearest animal of a set (threats, prey, kin, listed species), in bands (06 §4). With readiness on, a kin sense also says whether that animal is ready to mate, when it is within the partner range; beyond it readiness is unknown and not written. Hidden and killed animals are never reported (SENSE-06). NearestCoverSense The nearest cover (06 §4): "here" when standing in cover, else the bands or none. Without a cover module it always says none (ENV-12). Reference label "Cover". NearestEntitySense The nearest entity this animal may eat (06 §4): a carcass with portions left, not its own kill, not eaten from by it yet; or an egg its diet eats. Reference: the predator's "Carcass" sense. NearestResourceSense The nearest item of a layer the species grazes (06 §4): here, the bands, none. Reference label "Food". NumberGene A number expressed into one trait (GENE-04), e.g. a stamina gene setting stamina.max. Observation The tuple of an animal's sense tokens at one decision, in sense order (SENSE-02). ObservationSet A fixed list of situations, written by sense label and token (15 §2, "the 48 situations"): the prototype's rows ({"energy": "low", "food": "close", "animal": "adjacent", "animal_ready": true, …}) are matched to a species' senses by label; a sense the row doesn't name takes a default token. ObservationSet.Row One situation: tokens by sense label, plus its source and tags. ObservationView An observation read through its species' senses: the token of a sense by label (CTRL-10). OldAge Death of old age: age above the maximum (reference 1 500 ticks; ANIM-40). OllamaMutatorClient The reference mutator (10 §2): a model in Ollama on the CPU (gemma4:26b, owner 2026-10-10; num_gpu 0, num_ctx 1 024), thinking off, so the GPU stays JEV's. OllamaPointsBrain LLM, points mode (08 §6): one Ollama chat call per distinct query; the prompt ends with the points instruction, the answer is constrained by a JSON schema, temperature 0, a fixed seed, a fixed context length, thinking off; points become a row by DEC-41. OllamaTags Reads a model's digest from Ollama's /api/tags (first 12 characters), for cache keys and run info (DEC-33, GENE-12). OpenAIMutatorClient A mutator behind an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, docker profile gpu-mutator): /v1/chat/completions with the seed and temperature, thinking off through chat_template_kwargs. Ownership Who owns which module (ARCH-05, ARCH-06): the nearest owner above it; disabled means absent. Pending Work a phase waits for: brain answers, mutations (TICK-03, SPACE-13). PlayerArgs A watched run's settings from a command line (the Windows player): -scene name, -seed n, -ticks n, -minutes m (wall clock), -speed (ticks per second | fast | fixed), -wait (responsive | freeze), -brain (a brain's GameObject name or id), -capture seconds (0 = start and end only, off = none), -cache folder, -run folder name, -noMutation, -quitAtEnd, -window WIDTHxHEIGHT (a window of that many pixels), -stagger (every species decides staggered, DEC-04). Parsing and applying are separate, so tests check both without a player. PlayerLauncher In a player (not the editor), reads the command line (PlayerArgs) and sets each World before it starts (Configuring). With -scene, a World of another scene doesn't start and that scene loads instead. With -quitAtEnd, the player quits once the run stopped and its captures are written. Run files, captures and the answer cache land next to the build (paths are relative to its folder). PointsAnswer Points answers to rows (DEC-41): a missing action counts 0, negative points count 0, every action gets +0.01, then the row is normalised, so an all-zero answer becomes uniform. An answer that isn't a JSON object, or points that aren't numbers, are failures (as the prototype's int() raised). PromptTemplate A species' prompt with three holes: {genes}, {situation}, {ask} (PROMPT-01, PROMPT-04). Its id is a hash of this text, so any change to a header, an action line or a rule changes the id and the cache key (PROMPT-05). PromptWriter Collects the action lines and rule lines that modules contribute to a species' prompt (PROMPT-01). Numbers in rule lines come from placeholders filled from module settings (PROMPT-03): {field} on the writing module, {Module.field} on another module of the species, {species.Module.field} on a module of another species; {name} and {species.name} are display names. A placeholder reads a field or a property; {{ and }} write a brace. A module is named by its class, a base class, or its GameObject. PrototypeFormat The Python prototype's file conventions, for the recorder's compatibility mode (OUT-05): its two species were "the agents" and the predators, it logged kills as "predator" and prefixed predator statistics with "pred_". QuitWhenStopped Quits the player once its World stopped and the captures are written (-quitAtEnd). RandomBrain Uniform over the species' actions, whatever the genes and the situation: the null model (08 §6). RandomStream One named random stream: a PCG32 generator seeded from SHA-256 of the seed and the name (RAND-02). RandomStreams The named random streams of one world (RAND-02…04). Asking twice for a name returns the same stream. Map layers use "world/<layer name>", so adding a layer never changes another layer's map. RayBatch The rays of all deciding animals of a sense phase, cast in one batch (SENSE-30) with RaycastCommand, or one at a time with Physics.Raycast (Immediate, for comparison: SENSE-31). Version-specific physics code lives here (ARCH-10). RecordPhase A statistics row every statsEvery ticks and the periodic flushes (TICK-04 #11, RAND-22); live statistics for the editor. RecordingTransport Wraps a transport and keeps every request body and answer, for integrity checks that inspect what a model received (B-11). The API key is passed through and never kept (OUT-04). RequiresModuleAttribute Names a module this one needs beside it (a drink needs thirst): a species module on the same species, or a world module (a service or a phase) under the World.
