Validation reports a missing one (V-26) with a fix that adds it, and the conformance suites add it before testing the module. ResourceLayer Edible items spread over the ground, e.g. grass (03 §1). The layer's Edible says how it is eaten; diets name the layer by its GameObject's name. RestAction Stay still to catch your breath and save energy (07 §4). Never searches; the metabolism charges its rest cost. RunCapture Saves what the screen shows (overlay included): a PNG when the run starts, every few seconds of real time, and when it stops, into <folder>/<run>/ (the run recorder's folder name), then a contact sheet of them. PNGs are encoded off the main thread. It only reads the World and draws no random numbers (RAND-11). RunInfo What ran (13 §2, CFG-03): the scene, the full effective configuration by path, git commit, Unity version, brains and mutator (models, hosts), seeds, wait mode, act order and controls. Never any secret (OUT-04). RunNumbers What the overlay shows of a run, read from the World's own counters (13 §4–5) and nothing else: tick, state, population, births, deaths, kills, mutations, model calls. Read only; a test compares it with the event log. RunOverlay The run's numbers on screen, in the editor and in a build (immediate-mode GUI): tick, state and what the tick waits for, ticks per second achieved against the target, frames per second, each species' population, births and deaths, mutations, model calls; and the followed animal's action, stats and genes (WorldCamera). It only reads the World (RunNumbers). Tab hides it. RunRecorder Writes a run into its own folder (13): events.jsonl, stats.csv, alleles.jsonl, final_population.json, summary.json, run_info.json. Events and stats are flushed every 500 ticks, alleles every 5 000 (RAND-22), and every file is written when the run stops, whatever the reason (RAND-20). The compatibility mode writes a two-species world exactly as the prototype does (OUT-05). Sampling Sampling temperature (DEC-20): p^(1/τ), renormalised; τ < 1 sharpens, τ > 1 flattens. Pure functions. ScenarioAsset A scenario (31 §1, CFG-02): a scene plus overrides by path, variants, seeds, a length, a brain and the expected facts. The scenario runner window and EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario read it. ScenarioAsset.Override One setting to override: a path and its new value, as text. ScenarioAsset.Variant A variant of the scenario: its own brain, tier, overrides and removed GameObjects, on top of the scenario's. SearchRule The prompt's search rule (PROMPT-01): what an animal does when its action has nothing to act on (ACT-04). Put it on the species' own GameObject so it comes first among the rule lines. Secrets What a key, token or password looks like (OUT-04): one rule for validation (V-61, every serialized string of the World), the HTTP checks and the command line written to run_info.json. Sense Reads one animal and the world and returns one token from a fixed list (SENSE-01): what the brain is told about one aspect of the situation, such as the nearest food or the energy level. SenseContext What a sense may read at a decision: the world state at the start of the tick (SENSE-04), through the same queries as actions, so hidden and killed animals are never reported (SENSE-06). SensePhase Picks who decides (DEC-01): every living, not busy animal on the decision ticks, and animals without an action on the others; rebuilds the spatial index; casts the rays of batched senses in one batch; reads every sense of every deciding animal from the state at the start of the tick (TICK-04 #1, SENSE-04, TICK-05). SentenceGuards The checks a gene sentence must pass, founder or mutant (MUT-12, GENE-22). Pure functions. SimEvent One logged fact (OUT-02): kind, tick, animal id, species, and more fields. Keys are written sorted. SpatialIndex Animals by species in a uniform hash grid (20 §3.11, SENSE-32): rebuilt by the sense and act phases, updated as animals move in a sequential act order. Nearest queries search expanding rings and break ties by id (SPACE-07, SPACE-08). The ring bound assumes the world distance is at least the horizontal Euclidean one. Species A kind of animal (SPEC-01, SPEC-02). Configure it with child components; subclass it only for hooks. SpeciesBuilder Collects the stats and traits a species' modules declare before any animal exists (ANIM-10, ANIM-15). SpeciesBuilder.StatDeclaration One declared stat, with the module that declared it (for the species inspector). SpeciesBuilder.TraitDeclaration One declared trait, with the module that declared it. SpeciesCounters Cumulative counts of one species for the statistics rows and the summary (13 §4, §5). SpeciesModule A component under a species: a gene, a sense, an action, a stat, a rule... Stamina Stamina: the meters an animal can move before it must stop (05 §4). Each meter moved costs one point; standing still brings it back, which costs some energy until it is full (ANIM-21). Starvation Death by starvation: energy ≤ 0 at the death check (ANIM-40). SystemHttpTransport The real transport: an HttpClient owned by one brain or mutator client (ARCH-07: nothing shared between worlds), every await with ConfigureAwait(false) so answers never need the main thread (the Freeze mode blocks it, SPACE-14). Time-outs come from the caller (DEC-42). TerrainGround A Unity Terrain as ground (02 §1): heights from the heightmap; walkable above the water level, below a maximum steepness, outside tree footprints; only the largest connected walkable region is kept (SPACE-05). Walkability is computed once, on a grid of cells. TextGene A sentence the brain reads in the genes block of the prompt (GENE-03, PROMPT-02). TickContext What a phase gets each tick: the world, the tick number and the named streams. TickPhase One step of a tick. The World runs its phases in hierarchy order (TICK-01). UniformCrossover For each locus independently, the allele of one parent or the other with probability ½ (GENE-30). Units Units of the simulation: meters on the horizontal plane, ticks for time (README, Units). ValidationFix A fix button for a validation message (EDIT-02). ValidationMessage One problem, naming the object at fault (EDIT-02). ValidationReport The messages of one validation pass. The same engine runs in the editor, at Initialize and in CI (EDIT-01). ValueNoise Value noise on a lattice: random values at lattice points, smoothly interpolated (the prototype's cover and terrain maps). A noise map is built once from a stream; sampling it is a pure function. ViewPool Inactive views of one species, reused (20 §6): a new animal takes one, a dead one gives it back. Views have no active collider and sit on the "Ignore Raycast" layer, which every sense ray leaves out, so what the animals sense never depends on rendering (SPACE-12, RAND-11). World The root of a simulation (01 §3): finds its species, phases and services in its subtree, initialises them in a fixed order (ARCH-04, 20 §4) and runs ticks. FixedUpdate only drives the loop; time is Tick (SPACE-10). WorldCamera A camera for watching a run: it frames the world at the start; WASD or the arrows pan, the wheel zooms, the right mouse button (or Q and E) orbits, the middle button drags, F frames the world again. A left click on an animal follows it (Esc stops). Picking is done on screen, from the views' positions: views have no colliders (SPACE-12), and the camera only reads the World. WorldModule A component under the World (not under a species): a phase or a service. WorldQueries The queries senses and actions share (ACT-05, SENSE-06): within the animal's vision, never itself, never a killed animal, never an animal hidden from it in cover, diets checked. Ties by id (SPACE-08). WorldService Something phases and modules use: ground, layers, brains, recorder. Found with World.Service<T>(). Structs ActPlan One animal's plan for a tick (Plan): what ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>) writes for each animal of its group, and what the act phase then moves and applies. AlleleValue One allele value: a sentence or a number. AnimalHit An animal found by a spatial query, with its distance from the asker (SPACE-07). CoverHit The nearest cover found by a query: a point in cover and its distance (ENV-10). EntityHit<T> An entity found by a spatial query, with its distance (ENV-20). FounderAllele One value of a founder pool and its origin (founder, neutral, control…) (GENE-20). Intent What an action wants this tick (ACT-03): a direction (or none: stay), walk or run, and the farthest it should go (to stop at a target). The locomotion decides what actually happens (MOVE-01). Interaction The contact an action asks for on arrival (ACT-03, ACT-10): graze an item, strike an animal, eat a carcass portion or an egg, or a custom one. A small value, so planning allocates nothing. LiveStatistics.Point One sample of one species. MutatorRequest One prompt for the mutator model, with its seed and temperature (MUT-11, MUT-14). ResourceItem One item of a resource layer found by a query: its layer, cell, position and distance (ENV-01). RunNumbers.SpeciesLine One species' line of the overlay. SpeciesBuilder.Problem A declaration problem, reported by validation: V-36 (a default outside its range), V-38 (declared twice differently). StatId A handle to a declared stat (ANIM-10): its slot in the animal record, its name and its range. StatStart The value a stat takes when an animal is created (ANIM-10). TraitId A handle to a declared trait (ANIM-15): a per-animal number fixed at birth, with a default and a range. WaterHit The nearest water found by a ground: the water point, a walkable shore point next to it, the distance. Interfaces IEventSink Receives every recorded event with its canonical line (OUT-06): the run recorder, live graphs, tests. IHttpTransport Sends one HTTP request and returns the response body; throws HttpFailure for an error status. The real one is SystemHttpTransport; tests inject a fake (30 §2) so brains and mutators are tested without servers. IInteraction A custom contact effect (22 §3, drink): applied after moving when the animal is within Reach of the point its action walked or ran to (ACT-10). INumberRange A gene whose values are numbers within a range: what number operators (Gaussian, MUT-20) and the random-founders control (CTRL-01) need, so a student's own number gene kind works with them. IStatsColumns A module that adds columns to stats.csv (13 §4). A species module's columns get its species' prefix and hold that species' values; a world module's columns go at the end of the row, unprefixed. A new column during the run rewrites the header, with empty cells in the rows before it. Enums ActOrder The order in which animals act within a tick (ACT-30). AlleleKind What kind of value a gene holds (GENE-02): a sentence or a number. AnimalSet A set of species resolved from the food web (SPEC-12): whom an animal flees, hunts or follows. CapRule.Mode How the cap is kept (POP-01). EatMethod How something edible is eaten (SPEC-10). EdibleTargetKind What a diet entry points at (SPEC-15). InteractionKind The contact effects of 07 §3 (ACT-11), plus custom ones. RunSpeed How fast a running world advances (02 §4, run controls). Results never depend on it (SPACE-11). RunState The World's run loop states (brief, chapter B §13). Severity How serious a validation message is (21 §2): an error (E) blocks Play and the run; a warning (W) and an information (I) don't. TextStyle The style of situation texts (SENSE-11): V1 terse ("Energy: low."), V2 first person ("I am hungry and weak."). WaitMode How a tick waits for brain answers and mutations (SPACE-14). Both give the same events hash.

api/index.html.title: API reference | EvoSim
api/index.html.summary: API reference Generated by Docs/Site/tools/DocAudit --api-toc from the code and its documentation comments. Every public type of EvoSim, grouped by the folder of Assets/EvoSim it lives in. Each page lists the type's members with their documentation, and links to its source on GitHub. Where to start: World, Species, SpeciesModule, and the extension points. Core: world, species, animals, ticks Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Core Type Summary Animal class One animal: plain data owned by its species (ANIM-01, ARCH-03). Modules read and write it through this record. AnimalHit struct An animal found by a spatial query, with its distance from the asker (SPACE-07). CoverHit struct The nearest cover found by a query: a point in cover and its distance (ENV-10). EntityHit<T> struct An entity found by a spatial query, with its distance (ENV-20). ExerciseOfAttribute attribute Marks a student class as the exercise version of a reference module (22 §0, the teaching path): EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub swaps the reference for it, keeping the settings; Restore reference undoes it. Hashing static class SHA-256 helpers for keys, signatures and prompt ids. ManualPending class A pending completed by code: Wait() runs the given completion if it isn't done yet. Ownership static class Who owns which module (ARCH-05, ARCH-06): the nearest owner above it; disabled means absent. Pending abstract class Work a phase waits for: brain answers, mutations (TICK-03, SPACE-13). RandomStream class One named random stream: a PCG32 generator seeded from SHA-256 of the seed and the name (RAND-02). RandomStreams class The named random streams of one world (RAND-02…04). RequiresModuleAttribute attribute Names a module this one needs beside it (a drink needs thirst): a species module on the same species, or a world module (a service or a phase) under the World. Validation reports a missing one (V-26) with a fix that adds it, and the conformance suites add it before testing the module. RunSpeed enum How fast a running world advances (02 §4, run controls). RunState enum The World's run loop states (brief, chapter B §13). Secrets static class What a key, token or password looks like (OUT-04): one rule for validation (V-61, every serialized string of the World), the HTTP checks and the command line written to run_info.json. Severity enum How serious a validation message is (21 §2): an error (E) blocks Play and the run; a warning (W) and an information (I) don't. SpatialIndex class Animals by species in a uniform hash grid (20 §3.11, SENSE-32): rebuilt by the sense and act phases, updated as animals move in a sequential act order. Nearest queries search expanding rings and break ties by id (SPACE-07, SPACE-08). The ring bound assumes the world distance is at least the horizontal Euclidean one. Species class A kind of animal (SPEC-01, SPEC-02). SpeciesBuilder class Collects the stats and traits a species' modules declare before any animal exists (ANIM-10, ANIM-15). SpeciesBuilder.Problem struct A declaration problem, reported by validation: V-36 (a default outside its range), V-38 (declared twice differently). SpeciesBuilder.StatDeclaration class One declared stat, with the module that declared it (for the species inspector). SpeciesBuilder.TraitDeclaration class One declared trait, with the module that declared it. SpeciesCounters class Cumulative counts of one species for the statistics rows and the summary (13 §4, §5). SpeciesModule abstract class A component under a species: a gene, a sense, an action, a stat, a rule... StatId struct A handle to a declared stat (ANIM-10): its slot in the animal record, its name and its range. StatStart struct The value a stat takes when an animal is created (ANIM-10). TextStyle enum The style of situation texts (SENSE-11): V1 terse ("Energy: low."), V2 first person ("I am hungry and weak."). TickContext class What a phase gets each tick: the world, the tick number and the named streams. TickPhase abstract class One step of a tick. TraitId struct A handle to a declared trait (ANIM-15): a per-animal number fixed at birth, with a default and a range. Units static class Units of the simulation: meters on the horizontal plane, ticks for time (README, Units). ValidationFix class A fix button for a validation message (EDIT-02). ValidationMessage class One problem, naming the object at fault (EDIT-02). ValidationReport class The messages of one validation pass. WaitMode enum How a tick waits for brain answers and mutations (SPACE-14). World class The root of a simulation (01 §3): finds its species, phases and services in its subtree, initialises them in a fixed order (ARCH-04, 20 §4) and runs ticks. FixedUpdate only drives the loop; time is Tick (SPACE-10). WorldModule abstract class A component under the World (not under a species): a phase or a service. WorldQueries class The queries senses and actions share (ACT-05, SENSE-06): within the animal's vision, never itself, never a killed animal, never an animal hidden from it in cover, diets checked. Ties by id (SPACE-08). WorldService abstract class Something phases and modules use: ground, layers, brains, recorder. Found with World.Service<T>(). Tick phases Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Phases Type Summary ActOrder enum The order in which animals act within a tick (ACT-30). ActPhase class Every living animal acts, in the act order (ACT-30): its action plans an intent and an interaction, its species' locomotion moves it, interactions apply within reach, then its metabolism is paid and busy counters drop (TICK-04 #4, ANIM-20, ANIM-30). AskBrainsPhase class Builds each deciding animal's query (DEC-10), answers it from the memo (DEC-30) or the answer cache (DEC-33), sends the rest as one batch per brain — per species for brains that can't mix species — with identical keys sent once (DEC-13, DEC-15, DEC-32). BreedPhase class After all animals acted (TICK-06): each ready animal that chose mate and hasn't bred this period breeds with the nearest ready partner within reach that hasn't bred either — one partner's choice is enough (REPRO-02, REPRO-03). A litter is conceived (REPRO-10, REPRO-11): one egg per baby with its own crossover and its mutations drawn now (GENE-32, MUT-30); the LLM mutations are sent as one batch at the end (MUT-31). ChooseActionsPhase class Waits for the brains (TICK-03), stores fresh answers in the memo and the cache (never a failure, DEC-34), and draws each deciding animal's action with its species' sampling stream after the temperature (DEC-20, RAND-03). DeathPhase class Removes killed animals; every living animal ages by one tick (babies of this tick included); then each species' death rules (starvation, old age…) in module order. EnvironmentPhase class Resource layers regrow, each with its own stream; entities move, rot or vanish (TICK-04 #9, ENV-03, ENV-22). FloorPhase class While a species has fewer animals than its floor, a newcomer arrives (POP-03); it decides at the next tick (TICK-05). HatchPhase class Eggs due this tick hatch, in conception order (REPRO-22), once their genome is complete: the tick waits for the mutator if its answers aren't in (MUT-32, REPRO-24). Each baby starts with the child energy, full stamina, age 0, at its first parent's position (REPRO-12), and a birth event records its litter and mutations (MUT-03). MigrationPhase class Above its cap, a species loses animals chosen uniformly at random with its migration stream, ignoring genes, stats and position (POP-01, POP-02); animals born this tick are spared unless too few older ones remain. RecordPhase class A statistics row every statsEvery ticks and the periodic flushes (TICK-04 #11, RAND-22); live statistics for the editor. SensePhase class Picks who decides (DEC-01): every living, not busy animal on the decision ticks, and animals without an action on the others; rebuilds the spatial index; casts the rays of batched senses in one batch; reads every sense of every deciding animal from the state at the start of the tick (TICK-04 #1, SENSE-04, TICK-05). Senses Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Senses Type Summary AgeSense class Young or adult (06 §4): adult from the maturity trait (ANIM-36), reference 150 ticks. BandedSense abstract class A sense that reports how far the nearest something is, in bands (06 §3): "here" (optional), the bands, "none". Wording (SENSE-10…13): V1 "Food: 1-4 meters away." / V2 "The nearest food is 1-4 meters away.". Bands class Distance bands (06 §3, SENSE-20): increasing edges e1 < … < ek and a vision v > ek. A distance falls in the first band with d ≤ ei, in "far" if ek < d ≤ v, and is "none" beyond v. Reference: 1, 4, 10 m and 20 m. BatchedSense abstract class A sense that casts rays (line of sight, terrain ahead): it asks for its rays first; the sense phase casts the rays of all deciding animals in one batch, then each sense reads its results (SENSE-30). It must give the same tokens as evaluating it one animal at a time (SENSE-31). LevelSense class A stat as low, medium or high (ANIM-12): low < low threshold ≤ medium ≤ high threshold < high. Reference: energy 30 / 70, stamina prey 20 / 40, predators 10 / 20. NearestAnimalSense class The nearest animal of a set (threats, prey, kin, listed species), in bands (06 §4). NearestCoverSense class The nearest cover (06 §4): "here" when standing in cover, else the bands or none. Without a cover module it always says none (ENV-12). Reference label "Cover". NearestEntitySense class The nearest entity this animal may eat (06 §4): a carcass with portions left, not its own kill, not eaten from by it yet; or an egg its diet eats. Reference: the predator's "Carcass" sense. NearestResourceSense class The nearest item of a layer the species grazes (06 §4): here, the bands, none. Reference label "Food". Observation class The tuple of an animal's sense tokens at one decision, in sense order (SENSE-02). ObservationSet class A fixed list of situations, written by sense label and token (15 §2, "the 48 situations"): the prototype's rows ({"energy": "low", "food": "close", "animal": "adjacent", "animal_ready": true, …}) are matched to a species' senses by label; a sense the row doesn't name takes a default token. ObservationSet.Row class One situation: tokens by sense label, plus its source and tags. ObservationView class An observation read through its species' senses: the token of a sense by label (CTRL-10). RayBatch class The rays of all deciding animals of a sense phase, cast in one batch (SENSE-30) with RaycastCommand, or one at a time with Physics.Raycast (Immediate, for comparison: SENSE-31). Version-specific physics code lives here (ARCH-10). Sense abstract class Reads one animal and the world and returns one token from a fixed list (SENSE-01): what the brain is told about one aspect of the situation, such as the nearest food or the energy level. SenseContext class What a sense may read at a decision: the world state at the start of the tick (SENSE-04), through the same queries as actions, so hidden and killed animals are never reported (SENSE-06). Decisions and brains Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Brains Type Summary AnswerCache class A persistent store of brain and mutator answers (DEC-33, MUT-14): append-only JSON lines, one file per brain, loaded at the first lookup. Keys hash everything that can change an answer, so a repeated run replays without model calls (RAND-21). Rows are stored with round-trip precision, so a replay is bit-identical. Brain abstract class Maps a batch of queries to probability rows over the species' actions (DEC-11). BrainAnswer class A brain's answer to a batch (DEC-11): one probability row per query, in query order, or a failure per query. Fast brains fill it at once; HTTP brains later, from another thread, then mark it done. Decision class One animal deciding this tick: what it sensed, what its brain was asked and answered (08 §1–§5). DecisionMemo class Within a run, the answer for a key (species, brain, brain-visible genome key, observation) is computed once and reused (DEC-30). DecisionQuery class What a brain receives for one deciding animal (DEC-10): its species, the genes its brain reads (label and sentence, in locus order), its observation, its situation text in the world's style, and any attachments. DecisionSchedule class A species' own decision period, and staggering (DEC-04, MAY): an animal decides when (tick + id) % period == 0. Both change behaviour. In the reference scenes every species has one, staggered, with the World's period (owner 2026-10-10); a species without one decides all together, every World period, as the Python prototype does. DecisionState class The decisions of the current tick, the brain answers they wait for, and the run's memo (08 §1–§4). PromptTemplate class A species' prompt with three holes: {genes}, {situation}, {ask} (PROMPT-01, PROMPT-04). Its id is a hash of this text, so any change to a header, an action line or a rule changes the id and the cache key (PROMPT-05). PromptWriter class Collects the action lines and rule lines that modules contribute to a species' prompt (PROMPT-01). RandomBrain class Uniform over the species' actions, whatever the genes and the situation: the null model (08 §6). Sampling static class Sampling temperature (DEC-20): p^(1/τ), renormalised; τ < 1 sharpens, τ > 1 flattens. Pure functions. HTTP brains and the mutator client Assets/EvoSim/Http Type Summary BrainRequest class One decision query as an HTTP brain sends it: its place in the batch, the text for the model and the species' action names. builds it on the main thread; reads it on the thread pool, so it holds plain values only, no Unity object. HttpBrain abstract class The base of the brains that ask a model server over HTTP (08 §6): it turns a batch of queries into requests, sends them off the main thread and fills the when the answers come back. HttpCaller class JSON calls to one server with the reference client behaviour (DEC-42): a time-out per try, tries with doubling waits between them, a cap on requests in flight. The API key is read from its environment variable at each call and only sent, never stored or logged (OUT-04). HttpChecks static class Checks shared by HTTP brains and mutator clients (the key checks, V-61, are ). HttpFailure class An HTTP call that failed: an error status, or every try used (DEC-40, DEC-42). Messages never hold keys (OUT-04). HttpMutatorClient abstract class A mutator model behind a server (10 §2): one chat call per request with the prompt alone (CORE-07, MUT-11), the request's seed and temperature, thinking off. Calls run on the thread pool and fill the reply; the MutatorService caches answers and batches rounds (MUT-14, MUT-31). HttpStats class What a brain's or mutator's HTTP calls did: tries, retries, failures, latencies (B-01, brain health window). IHttpTransport interface Sends one HTTP request and returns the response body; throws HttpFailure for an error status. JevBrain class JEV choice (08 §6): a distilled decision model behind vLLM. One /v1/completions request per batch with the list of texts, max_tokens 1, the option letters as the only allowed tokens and their log-probabilities; each row is softmax((log-prob + head bias) / T) with the head and T of the pinned revision. Options always in the species' action order; at most 16 (DEC-14); inputs above the training length are counted, not cut. JevBrain.SpeciesQuestion class The question asked for one species (the prototype asked predators "Which action does this predator take now?"). JevHead class JEV's decision head and calibration at a pinned revision (08 §6): the option letters' token ids, a bias per slot, the temperature of the "choice" kind. Row = softmax((log-prob + bias) / T) over the options. OllamaMutatorClient class The reference mutator (10 §2): a model in Ollama on the CPU (gemma4:26b, owner 2026-10-10; num_gpu 0, num_ctx 1 024), thinking off, so the GPU stays JEV's. OllamaPointsBrain class LLM, points mode (08 §6): one Ollama chat call per distinct query; the prompt ends with the points instruction, the answer is constrained by a JSON schema, temperature 0, a fixed seed, a fixed context length, thinking off; points become a row by DEC-41. OllamaTags static class Reads a model's digest from Ollama's /api/tags (first 12 characters), for cache keys and run info (DEC-33, GENE-12). OpenAIMutatorClient class A mutator behind an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, docker profile gpu-mutator): /v1/chat/completions with the seed and temperature, thinking off through chat_template_kwargs. PointsAnswer static class Points answers to rows (DEC-41): a missing action counts 0, negative points count 0, every action gets +0.01, then the row is normalised, so an all-zero answer becomes uniform. An answer that isn't a JSON object, or points that aren't numbers, are failures (as the prototype's int() raised). RecordingTransport class Wraps a transport and keeps every request body and answer, for integrity checks that inspect what a model received (B-11). SystemHttpTransport class The real transport: an HttpClient owned by one brain or mutator client (ARCH-07: nothing shared between worlds), every await with ConfigureAwait(false) so answers never need the main thread (the Freeze mode blocks it, SPACE-14). Time-outs come from the caller (DEC-42). Actions and interactions Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Actions Type Summary ActContext class What an action may do in one tick (ACT-06): ask questions about what the animal could sense, and say where it wants to go (an intent) and what to do on arrival (an interaction). It can't move or change any animal itself. ActPlan struct One animal's plan for a tick (): what writes for each animal of its group, and what the act phase then moves and applies. AnimalAction abstract class A behaviour the brain can choose (ACT-01). EatAction class Go to the nearest visible food and eat it (07 §4). FleeAction class Run away from the nearest threat (07 §4). FollowAction class Walk toward the nearest other animal of the species, stopping at 1 m (07 §4). HideAction class Go to the nearest cover and stay in it (07 §4, ENV-13). HuntAction class Chase the nearer of the nearest huntable animal and the nearest carcass it may eat (a carcass wins a tie, being a sure meal); strike the animal or eat from the carcass on arrival (07 §4). IInteraction interface A custom contact effect (22 §3, drink): applied after moving when the animal is within of the point its action walked or ran to (ACT-10). Interaction struct The contact an action asks for on arrival (ACT-03, ACT-10): graze an item, strike an animal, eat a carcass portion or an egg, or a custom one. A small value, so planning allocates nothing. InteractionContext class What a custom interaction may use when it applies: the world, the ground, the actor's streams. InteractionKind enum The contact effects of 07 §3 (ACT-11), plus custom ones. InteractionResolver class Applies the interactions of 07 §3 after moving (ACT-10, ACT-11): only within reach, only if the target is edible and the eater's diet lists it (SPEC-13). Hunters strike at most once per tick (ACT-12). MateAction class Walk to the nearest ready partner in sight, stopping at 1 m (07 §4). RestAction class Stay still to catch your breath and save energy (07 §4). SearchRule class The prompt's search rule (PROMPT-01): what an animal does when its action has nothing to act on (ACT-04). Put it on the species' own GameObject so it comes first among the rule lines. Locomotion Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Locomotion Type Summary Intent struct What an action wants this tick (ACT-03): a direction (or none: stay), walk or run, and the farthest it should go (to stop at a target). The locomotion decides what actually happens (MOVE-01). KinematicLocomotion class The reference locomotion (MOVE-04): straight lines, no physics. Moves by the smallest of speed, stamina and the intent's maximum distance; slides along borders and obstacles; if stuck, takes a random sidestep. Locomotion abstract class How a species moves (MOVE-01): it turns each animal's intent into movement, and whatever it does is the tick's result. Inherit it for terrain, NavMesh or physics movement (MOVE-07). Speeds are traits (MOVE-03). MoveContext class What a locomotion gets to move animals: the ground, the distance function, the streams, stamina budgets. Food web Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Food Type Summary AnimalSet enum A set of species resolved from the food web (SPEC-12): whom an animal flees, hunts or follows. Diet class What a species eats (SPEC-15): layers, species, "carcass:<species>", "egg:<species>". Each target must carry an Edible (SPEC-10, V-24). A species with no diet eats nothing. Diet.Entry class One line of the diet: what is eaten, and how much its energy is scaled (SPEC-15). EdibleTarget class One resolved diet entry: what is eaten, how (its Edible), and the energy scale (SPEC-15). EdibleTargetKind enum What a diet entry points at (SPEC-15). Stats, metabolism and death Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Stats Type Summary DeathRule abstract class A cause of death checked in the death phase (ANIM-40): return the cause's name, or null to live on. Digestion class After a kill or a carcass portion the eater is busy digesting for round(digestTicks × gain / killGain) ticks: 50 after a kill (+60), 25 after a portion (+30). Grazing never makes an animal busy (05 §5). Energy class The energy stat (05 §4): founders and newcomers start at 60, the maximum is 100. Gains are clamped (ANIM-22). Metabolism class What a tick costs, once per living animal after it acted (ANIM-20), from the meters its locomotion reported, its action and whether it was busy (05 §4 reference table). OldAge class Death of old age: age above the maximum (reference 1 500 ticks; ANIM-40). Stamina class Stamina: the meters an animal can move before it must stop (05 §4). Each meter moved costs one point; standing still brings it back, which costs some energy until it is full (ANIM-21). Starvation class Death by starvation: energy ≤ 0 at the death check (ANIM-40). Genes and alleles Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Genes Type Summary Allele class One registered allele with its lineage (GENE-11, GENE-12): one version of a gene, such as the sentence "Rest when you are tired." at the prey's rest gene, or the number 60 at a stamina gene. AlleleKind enum What kind of value a gene holds (GENE-02): a sentence or a number. AllelePool class Founder and contrast sentences shared by several text genes, as an asset (GENE-24, 20 §3.8). AlleleRegistry class Every allele seen in a run, once per (locus, value) (GENE-10), with ids "<locus>:<n>" (GENE-11). AlleleValue struct One allele value: a sentence or a number. AnimalWords static class Common animal words, for the stale-name check V-23 (SPEC-21): a founder sentence naming one of them that is no species of the world was probably written for another world, or before a rename. Expression class What a gene expresses into (GENE-03/04): a trait of the animal being born, or a line of the prompt. receives one and calls or . FounderAllele struct One value of a founder pool and its origin (founder, neutral, control…) (GENE-20). Gene abstract class A gene (locus) of a species: a sentence for the brain or a number for a trait (GENE-01…04). Each animal carries one allele (one value) of every gene of its species. Genome class One allele per locus of a species, in the species' locus order (GENE-06): the genes of one animal. INumberRange interface A gene whose values are numbers within a range: what number operators (Gaussian, MUT-20) and the random-founders control (CTRL-01) need, so a student's own number gene kind works with them. NumberGene class A number expressed into one trait (GENE-04), e.g. a stamina gene setting stamina.max. SentenceGuards static class The checks a gene sentence must pass, founder or mutant (MUT-12, GENE-22). TextGene class A sentence the brain reads in the genes block of the prompt (GENE-03, PROMPT-02). Mutation Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Mutation Type Summary GaussianMutation class The reference operator for number genes (MUT-20): v' = clamp(v + N(0, σ)) to the gene's range. LlmMutation class The reference operator for text genes (10 §2): one instruction drawn from a deck, sent to the mutator with the sentence after one fixed context line, and nothing else (CORE-07, MUT-11). Every try's instruction and seed are drawn now (MUT-30); rejected answers are drawn again, up to tries (MUT-13). MutationJob class One mutation of one gene of one baby (10 §1): its choices are drawn at conception (MUT-30); the result may come later, from the mutator (MUT-32). Succeeded → a new value; failed → the inherited allele stays (MUT-04). MutationOperator abstract class A rule that changes one allele, blind to everything but the gene and the allele (CORE-07, 10 §1). MutationStats class Mutation statistics of a run (MUT-05): attempts, successes, model calls, rejections by reason. MutationText static class The LLM mutation's prompt, cleaning and guards (MUT-10…12), as the prototype does them (prototype/promptevo/evolution/mutation.py). MutatorClient abstract class Sends prompts to the mutator model: Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible server in EvoSim.Http, a fake in tests. It never sees anything but the prompts (CORE-07). MutatorReply class The answers to a batch of mutator requests, filled later: an answer or an error per request. MutatorRequest struct One prompt for the mutator model, with its seed and temperature (MUT-11, MUT-14). MutatorService class Runs LLM mutations (10 §2, §4): every try's instruction and seed are drawn at conception (MUT-30); requests are batched by round — all first tries together, then the redraws of the rejected ones (MUT-31); answers are cached by model, prompt, seed and temperature (MUT-14). It advances only when pumped on the main thread, so the Freeze and Responsive wait modes give the same results. Reproduction Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Reproduction Type Summary Crossover abstract class Builds a baby's genome from its parents', locus by locus (09 §4). Egg class A conceived baby waiting to hatch (REPRO-20): its parents, generation, genome after crossover, the mutations still running, and when it hatches. Not an animal: it doesn't sense, decide, move or count toward caps (REPRO-22). EggMutation class One pending mutation of an egg: the locus, the inherited allele, the operator and its job (MUT-30). EggSystem class Eggs as entities (REPRO-20). Incubation class Ticks between conception and hatching (REPRO-20, REPRO-21): 0 in the reference (babies hatch the same tick); a few ticks hide the mutator's latency (MUT-33). Litter class Litter size and the energy babies cost (REPRO-10, REPRO-11): k uniform in [min, max], cut so that no parent pays more than it has, never below min; each baby starts with childEnergy, paid by the parents in equal shares. MatingRule class Who may breed and with whom (11 §1): an adult with enough energy is ready (REPRO-01); an animal that chose mate breeds with a ready partner within reach, whatever the partner chose (REPRO-02), once per decision period (REPRO-03). UniformCrossover class For each locus independently, the allele of one parent or the other with probability ½ (GENE-30). Population Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Population Type Summary CapRule class The maximum population of a species (POP-01). CapRule.Mode enum How the cap is kept (POP-01). FloorRule class The minimum population (POP-03): below it, newcomers with founder genomes arrive at random walkable places in the floor phase. A world that needs them is reported (POP-05): they restart that species' evolution. Environment: food, cover, entities Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Environment Type Summary Carcass class What a kill leaves (03 §3): a few portions that other eaters may eat, one portion each, never the killer. It rots away when its lifetime runs out, eaten or not, and goes as soon as its last portion is eaten (ENV-22). CarcassSystem class Carcasses, as each species' edible component describes them: portions, energy, lifetime (03 §3). A carcass of a species is edible when that species' Edible leaves one; diets name it "carcass:<species>". CellGrid class A grid of square cells over the world rectangle, used inside layers (food cells, cover cells) — never to place animals (02 intro). Cover abstract class Places where an animal is hidden from the species that hunt it (03 §2). CoverLayer class Cover in clustered patches (thickets): the top of walkable cells of a value-noise map, drawn from the world stream (03 §2 reference: 20 %, octaves 8 and 4 m). EatMethod enum How something edible is eaten (SPEC-10). Edible class Makes what it sits on edible (SPEC-10): a species' animals, a resource layer's items, an entity kind. Without it nothing can eat that thing, whatever the diets say (ENV-23). Entity abstract class A world object with a position that is not an animal: a carcass, an egg, a water hole (ENV-20). EntityKind abstract class A kind of entity and its system (ENV-20): carcasses, eggs. Diets name it "<kind>:<species>". EntitySystem<T> abstract class The entities of one kind, found through spatial queries like animals (ENV-20). FoodGrid class The Lab 1 food layer (03 §1): at most one item per cell, at the cell centre; a share of walkable cells starts with an item; empty cells regrow at random, uniformly; no food in cover ("hungry cover", ENV-04). ResourceItem struct One item of a resource layer found by a query: its layer, cell, position and distance (ENV-01). ResourceLayer abstract class Edible items spread over the ground, e.g. grass (03 §1). ValueNoise class Value noise on a lattice: random values at lattice points, smoothly interpolated (the prototype's cover and terrain maps). A noise map is built once from a stream; sampling it is a pure function. Ground Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Ground Type Summary FlatGround class The Lab 1 ground: a flat rectangle at height 0, walkable everywhere inside (02 §1). Ground abstract class Answers, for any point, its height and whether it is walkable (SPACE-04), inside a bounded rectangle with hard borders (SPACE-03). TerrainGround class A Unity Terrain as ground (02 §1): heights from the heightmap; walkable above the water level, below a maximum steepness, outside tree footprints; only the largest connected walkable region is kept (SPACE-05). Walkability is computed once, on a grid of cells. WaterHit struct The nearest water found by a ground: the water point, a walkable shore point next to it, the distance. Recording Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Recording Type Summary CanonicalJson static class Writes JSON with sorted keys and fixed number formatting, so equal data gives equal text (RAND-10). EventLog class The world's events and their running hash (RAND-10). IEventSink interface Receives every recorded event with its canonical line (OUT-06): the run recorder, live graphs, tests. IStatsColumns interface A module that adds columns to stats.csv (13 §4). LiveStatistics class Time series for the editor's ecology monitor (21 §4, OUT-06): population, mean energy and stamina, births, deaths and memo hit rate per species, sampled every few ticks into fixed-size buffers. LiveStatistics.Point struct One sample of one species. RunInfo static class What ran (13 §2, CFG-03): the scene, the full effective configuration by path, git commit, Unity version, brains and mutator (models, hosts), seeds, wait mode, act order and controls. Never any secret (OUT-04). RunRecorder class Writes a run into its own folder (13): events.jsonl, stats.csv, alleles.jsonl, final_population.json, summary.json, run_info.json. Events and stats are flushed every 500 ticks, alleles every 5 000 (RAND-22), and every file is written when the run stops, whatever the reason (RAND-20). The compatibility mode writes a two-species world exactly as the prototype does (OUT-05). SimEvent class One logged fact (OUT-02): kind, tick, animal id, species, and more fields. Keys are written sorted. Scenarios and configuration Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Config Type Summary FieldPath static class Reads and overrides any serialized setting by path (CFG-02): "<GameObject path>/<Component>/<field>", relative to the World, e.g. "Prey/Litter/max", "World/decisionPeriod", "prey/Actions/flee/FleeAction/fleeIntoCover". Names are matched without case; a component is found by its class or a base class, on the GameObject or below it. ScenarioAsset class A scenario (31 §1, CFG-02): a scene plus overrides by path, variants, seeds, a length, a brain and the expected facts. The scenario runner window and EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario read it. ScenarioAsset.Override class One setting to override: a path and its new value, as text. ScenarioAsset.Variant class A variant of the scenario: its own brain, tier, overrides and removed GameObjects, on top of the scenario's. Prototype formats Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Compatibility Type Summary PrototypeFormat static class The Python prototype's file conventions, for the recorder's compatibility mode (OUT-05): its two species were "the agents" and the predators, it logged kills as "predator" and prefixed predator statistics with "pred_". Views Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Views Type Summary ActionColors static class One colour per action name, shared by the views and the overlay's legend. ActionView class The reference body's view (20 §6): a marker above the head in the colour of the animal's action (), and a body that darkens as its energy drops. It only reads the animal (SPACE-12). Copy it to show something else: override and read what you need. AnimalView class One animal's view (20 §6): it holds only the animal's id and has no Update; the World places it in LateUpdate and never reads it back (SPACE-12). Body class What a species' animals look like (20 §6): a view prefab, or a placeholder capsule of a colour. Views only read the simulation (SPACE-12); a species without a Body runs unseen. ContactSheet static class A grid of a folder's PNG captures, scaled down on the GPU, saved as contact_sheet.png. EntityMarkers class Small markers for the World's entities (ENV-20): a dark red disc per carcass, an ivory ball per egg, a grey cube for any other kind. Pooled primitives, placed each frame from the entity systems; they only read the World (SPACE-12): no collider, the Ignore Raycast layer. GroundView class Draws a flat world's ground (02 §1) with its cover cells and food items (03 §1–2): one quad the size of the ground and a texture of one pixel per cell, repainted when a tick changed a cell. It only reads the World (SPACE-12): no collider, the Ignore Raycast layer, no random numbers. RunCapture class Saves what the screen shows (overlay included): a PNG when the run starts, every few seconds of real time, and when it stops, into <folder>/<run>/ (the run recorder's folder name), then a contact sheet of them. PNGs are encoded off the main thread. It only reads the World and draws no random numbers (RAND-11). RunNumbers class What the overlay shows of a run, read from the World's own counters (13 §4–5) and nothing else: tick, state, population, births, deaths, kills, mutations, model calls. Read only; a test compares it with the event log. RunNumbers.SpeciesLine struct One species' line of the overlay. RunOverlay class The run's numbers on screen, in the editor and in a build (immediate-mode GUI): tick, state and what the tick waits for, ticks per second achieved against the target, frames per second, each species' population, births and deaths, mutations, model calls; and the followed animal's action, stats and genes (). It only reads the World (). Tab hides it. ViewPool class Inactive views of one species, reused (20 §6): a new animal takes one, a dead one gives it back. Views have no active collider and sit on the "Ignore Raycast" layer, which every sense ray leaves out, so what the animals sense never depends on rendering (SPACE-12, RAND-11). WorldCamera class A camera for watching a run: it frames the world at the start; WASD or the arrows pan, the wheel zooms, the right mouse button (or Q and E) orbits, the middle button drags, F frames the world again. A left click on an animal follows it (Esc stops). Picking is done on screen, from the views' positions: views have no colliders (SPACE-12), and the camera only reads the World. Player builds Assets/EvoSim/Runtime/Player Type Summary PlayerArgs class A watched run's settings from a command line (the Windows player): -scene name, -seed n, -ticks n, -minutes m (wall clock), -speed (ticks per second | fast | fixed), -wait (responsive | freeze), -brain (a brain's GameObject name or id), -capture seconds (0 = start and end only, off = none), -cache folder, -run folder name, -noMutation, -quitAtEnd, -window WIDTHxHEIGHT (a window of that many pixels), -stagger (every species decides staggered, DEC-04). Parsing and applying are separate, so tests check both without a player. PlayerLauncher static class In a player (not the editor), reads the command line () and sets each World before it starts (). QuitWhenStopped class Quits the player once its World stopped and the captures are written (-quitAtEnd). Samples Assets/EvoSim/Samples Type Summary ChasedSense class Recipe 22 §13: whether the nearest threat is hunting this animal — its target at the start of the tick (SENSE-04). Lets a cannibal tell a hungry neighbour from a peaceful one. DiesOfThirst class Recipe 22 §1: thirst grows in the death phase, and an animal at the deadly level dies of "thirst". DragAction class Scenario S18 (ENV-21): walk to the nearest carcass in sight, then drag it 1 m per tick toward the nearest cover. The carcass moves in the act phase through an interaction, never from the visuals. DrinkAction class Recipe 22 §3: walk to the nearest visible water's shore and drink there, which resets thirst. IntensityLadder class Recipe 22 §8 (MUT-21): a rule-based text operator that moves the sentence's intensity word one step along never, rarely, sometimes, often, always — no model. It sees only the gene and its stream (MUT-30). NearestWaterSense class Recipe 22 §2: how far the nearest water is, in bands, with "here" at the shore (a query the ground offers). SeasonsPhase class Recipe 22 §9: a phase before Environment that slows the grass's regrowth in the second half of every year. SlopeLocomotion class Recipe 22 §14: the kinematic locomotion that refuses ground steeper than a limit and charges energy for every meter climbed (MOVE-02 still holds: it only moves the animal through Move). Thirst class Recipe 22 §1: a thirst stat that grows every tick (with DiesOfThirst) and kills at a threshold. Testing Assets/EvoSim/Testing Type Summary AdvancePending class A wait that ends after a number of calls: how the test fakes answer late (30 §2). In the Freeze wait mode the World calls , which ends it at once. FakeHttpTransport class A fake server for HTTP brains and mutators (30 §2): answers each request with a scripted function, records every request, can fail, hang until the time-out, or answer late; counts requests in flight at once. FakeMutator class A test mutator client (30 §2): answers mutation prompts with a scripted function (by default it appends "quickly" to the sentence), records every prompt and batch, and can answer N Advance calls late or fail. Golden static class Golden files under Assets/EvoSim/Tests/Golden/ (30 §2): situation texts, prompts, hashes. A missing file is written from the current output (pinned from the first accepted run); an existing one must match exactly. Re-pinning is a deliberate commit that deletes or edits the file and says why. Invariants static class The checks run after every tick in test worlds (30 §5): positions inside and walkable, no NaN, stats in range, unique ids, no dead or killed animal left, valid actions and rows, populations between floor and cap, carcass portions ≥ 0, genomes of the right length and species. Lab static class The Lab 1 reference species and world as ready-made recipes for tests (04 §5, 08 §7, 09 §3, 14 §2): prey (eat, flee, hide, follow, rest, mate) and predator (hunt, follow, rest, mate) with the prototype's values, founder pools, contrast pairs and prompt texts. Place static class Puts animals, food items, cover and carcasses at exact positions in a built world (30 §2), so a test sets up the very situation it checks. ScriptedBrain class A test brain (30 §2): answers from a policy written in the test, or from given rows per (species, observation); counts calls and batches; can answer N Advance calls late, fail, or refuse to mix species. Test code only: the system ships no rule-based brain (owner decision). SourceScan static class Reads the EvoSim source files for static checks (T-RAND-01, T-CORE-08, T-ACT-09): comments removed, line numbers kept. SpeciesSetup class Adds modules to one species of a world being built: what hands to its configure callback. Stat static class Statistical asserts: a proportion or a mean within k standard errors, a χ² uniformity test (30 §2). WorldBuilder class Builds a world in code, with no scene (30 §2): ground, food, cover, services, phases and species, each added by one chained call, then . WorldFixture abstract class The base class of tests that build worlds: every world started with is destroyed after each test, so tests leave nothing in the scene. Testing: probes Assets/EvoSim/Testing/Probes Type Summary AllLayersObstacleSense class A test batched sense that asks for its ray against every physics layer: even so, the views' layer is left out, so what is rendered never changes what animals sense (RAND-11). AllocationProbe class A test phase placed just before and just after another phase: the pair measures the bytes the main thread allocated in between, every tick (R-07: no allocation per tick in the act phase after warm-up). BatchProbeAction class A test-only action that wanders and records the group sizes the act phase plans through ActAll (ARCH-12, 20 §10). BatchProbeLocomotion class A test-only locomotion that records the group sizes the act phase moves through MoveAll (ARCH-12, 20 §10). BatchProbeSense class A test-only sense that records the group sizes the sense phase reads through ReadAll (ARCH-12, 20 §10). Blackboard class Shared state for test phases that change "the world" and read it (T-TICK-02): one blackboard is given to several s, to see which phases see a change. BlackboardPhase class A test phase that reads the blackboard (logging what it sees), then optionally writes it: only the phases after a writer see the new value in the same tick (T-TICK-02). CallbackPhase class A test-only phase that runs a callback at its place in the tick (to look at the state between two phases). CameraProbeSense class A test sense that attaches an "image" (a byte array) to every query, with no cache key unless asked (T-SENSE-10, S24): such queries are never memoised or cached (SENSE-41), and a brain that takes no attachments fails validation (V-51). CountingCrossover class A test-only uniform crossover that counts its calls (GENE-32: one cross per baby). DelayedPhase class A test phase that waits, every ticks, for an answer that arrives Advance calls after it was asked (like a slow brain); in Freeze mode Wait() delivers it at once. DoubleDistanceGround class A flat ground whose distance function is twice the Euclidean one: a replaced distance, which every sense and action must then use (T-SPACE-02, SPACE-06). ExerciseProbe class A finished teaching-path exercise (22 §0) for the Exercises menu tests: a litter that keeps the reference's rule. Its name is not MyLitter, so the menu never takes it for a student's stub. FeedAction class A test-only action: stay, and eat a snack of through a custom interaction that feeds the animal with (a meal counted like any other). Fruit class A test-only entity of a kind of one's own: a fruit. FruitSystem class A test-only entity system for fruit: nothing moves or rots. Several systems of one kind can live in a world ("Apples", "Pears"), and actions find their entities with NearestEntity<Fruit>. GoToAction class A test action that walks or runs toward a fixed point, stopping at a distance (T-SPACE-01, T-MOVE-01). HookProbe class A test-only species module that counts the births and deaths it hears and adds two statistics columns (probe_born, probe_died, written with the species' prefix in stats.csv). InvariantPhase class A last phase for test worlds: fails the test on the first broken invariant (30 §5). MemoryBrain class A test-only brain with memory: not memoizable, so every deciding animal's query reaches it with its id (even animals in the same situation), and it answers uniform rows. NeedsEnergyProbe class A test-only module that names a companion it needs with : a species without an module gets the warning V-26, whose fix adds one. ObstacleSense class A test batched sense: one ray along the heading; "blocked" if it hits a collider within 5 m (T-SENSE-09). OverlayProbeAction class A test-only overlay (ACT-07): done in passing, it plans a walk that must be ignored and a custom interaction that counts the times it applied, per animal. PondGround class A test ground: flat, with a round pond (not walkable) whose shore animals can reach (samples 22 §2–§3). It answers the water queries that the water sense and the drink action ask. ProbeAction class A test-only action defined outside the runtime assembly (T-CORE-02): it counts its calls and stays. ProbeSense class A test-only sense with two tokens; it returns the animal's id parity (T-CORE-02). RampGround class A test ground: flat for x < RampStart, then a ramp rising at RampSlope (height per meter) (T-MOVE-07). RandomEventPhase class A test phase that draws from a named stream every tick and records a "probe" event, so the hash depends on the draws. ShowProbeView class A test-only view that remembers what OnShow told it. SideCover class A test-only cover: every point with x in [MinX, MaxX] is in cover. Several covers in one world combine (ENV-11). SlopeLimitLocomotion class A kinematic locomotion that refuses slopes steeper than a limit (T-MOVE-07, after 22 §14). SnapshotPhase class A test phase that keeps every living animal's genome texts at the end of each tick (T-OUT-02). SureKillDiet class A test-only diet: every strike kills, and every meal gives exactly energy. ThrowingPhase class A test phase that throws, for the RAND-20 test: the World stops the run cleanly ("exception in ThrowingPhase") and lets the exception through. TracePhase class A test phase that writes "tick:name" to a log each time it runs (T-TICK-01). TraitProbe class A test module declaring one trait (default 60, range [1, 120]) and one capped stat (T-ANIM-02, T-ANIM-03). TurningLocomotion class A test locomotion that ignores the intent's direction: it turns it by 30° and halves the distance (T-MOVE-06). WorldHookProbe class A test-only world service that counts every species' births and deaths and adds one statistics column (world_born, after the species' columns in stats.csv). Editor Assets/EvoSim/Editor Type Summary AnimalInspectorWindow class The selected animal (21 §4, lab C): stats, traits, genome sentences, last situation, last probabilities as bars, current action and target, busy reason, parents and offspring. Click an animal's view to select it. AskTheBrainWindow class Ask the brain (21 §4, labs C and I): build a genome (founders, edited sentences, a gene's contrast pair, control sentences), pick a situation, and ask several brains side by side; a directed test asks with a gene's pro sentence, then with its anti one, so P(action) can be compared. Queries are built from texts only: nothing is registered in the world, so asking never changes a run. Batch static class Headless runs (30 §6, 31 §1, 32 §4): Unity -batchmode -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] [-responsive]. In the open editor the same runs go through RunScenarioNamed (the unity CLI's eval). Worlds run in Freeze mode, outside Play mode: the World initialises itself (ARCH-04). BrainHealthWindow class Brain health (21 §4): every brain and mutator client of the current world with its host, a Test connection button (V-60, on demand), model and revision or digest, latency, failures, and the answer cache's size and hits. EcologyMonitorWindow class The ecology monitor (21 §4, labs A and B): population per species over time, deaths by cause, births, action shares, memo hit rate, ticks per second — from LiveStatistics and the species counters. EditorWorlds static class What the windows look at (EDIT-05): the worlds of the open scenes, the selected world, the selected animal. EventLogWindow class The event log (21 §4, lab D): the running world's events as they are recorded, filtered by kind, species and animal; following an animal shows its line and its descendants' births. EvoSimOverlay class The scene-view overlay (21 §5): toggles for food, cover, carcasses, eggs and action letters, and species filters. Exercises static class EvoSim ▸ Exercises (21 §6, 22 §0): Replace with stub writes the student stub of a reference module into Assets/Student and swaps the module for it in the open scenes, keeping its settings; Restore reference undoes it. FoodWebWindow class The food web (21 §4): species and layers as a graph with graze, strike, scavenge and egg edges, the derived threats, and the food-web warnings of validation. GenePoolWindow class The gene pool (21 §4, labs D and E): per locus, the allele shares among the living over time (stacked), the current top alleles with their text and origin, and the lineage of a selected allele as a chain of texts; number genes as histograms of the living animals' values. Integrity static class Brain and mutator integrity checks against the real servers (32 §2): B-01 smoke and B-11 blindness here, the gates B-02 to B-10 in . Command line: -executeMethod EvoSim.Integrity.RunIntegrity [-checks B-01,B-11] [-scene path] [-brain JEV]; in the open editor: Integrity.RunNamed through the unity CLI's eval. IntegrityGates static class The brain and mutator gates of 32 §2 (B-02…B-10), measured as the prototype measured them (e1_sensitivity): genomes from texts (founders, control sentences, the neutral genome, contrast pairs, single edits) × the reference situations (15 §2), through the scene's real prompt and brain. Queries are built from texts only: nothing is registered in the world. Each writes a report (IntegrityReport). IntegrityReport class The result of one brain or mutator integrity check (32 §2): pass or fail, facts (models, digests or revisions, prompt ids, date), rows, written as JSON and Markdown under Logs/EvoSim/Reports so results compare over time. PlayModeGate static class EDIT-01: before Play, every enabled World in the open scenes is validated with the same engine as World.Initialize; errors cancel Play and are logged with the object at fault (EDIT-02). PromptPreview static class The species inspector's prompt preview (21 §3, PROMPT-06): built by the same code as the Ask brains phase, so it is exactly what the brain receives — for JEV, its whole input text (T-PROMPT-05). RealTimeRuns static class The real-time visual test from the unity CLI (eval): a headless reference run, a scene set up for Play mode, and the run's status while it plays. Levels: L0 the random brain and no mutation (offline), L1 the scene's brain (JEV) and no mutation, L2 the scene's brain and mutator. Example: unity command eval --code 'return EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.Headless("HideVsFlee", 1234, 600, "L2", "RT-L2-headless");' ReferenceScenes static class Builds the reference content (20 §2, §7; 09 §3): the allele pools from the prototype's pool files, the module prefabs (Modules/), placeholder bodies, and the scenes Lab1_Small, Lab1_Full, HideVsFlee, ThreeSpecies, Terrain_Locomotion and Sandbox. The scenes are then the configuration (ARCH-01): edit them, not this builder, unless the reference itself changes. Scenes are opened additively from an empty file, so the editor's own open scene is never touched. RunViews static class Makes a scene watchable (20 §6): a "Run views" object with the ground, entity markers, overlay and capture, and a on the main camera; and the reference bodies (a capsule standing on the ground, a nose that shows where it goes, a marker in the colour of its action). All of them only read the World (SPACE-12). ScenarioRunnerWindow class The scenario runner (21 §4, lab G): the scenario assets, a variant, seeds and length; runs them headless (Freeze, the same code as EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario) and lists the results; "twice" checks the reproducibility fact. SceneDrawing static class The scene view (21 §5): gizmos for the selected animal (vision, a line to its target, a 1 m circle coloured by action) and, as the overlay's toggles say, food items, cover, carcasses, eggs and a letter per action above each animal (stable colours from the action order). Drawing only reads the world (SPACE-12). ScriptTemplates static class Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim (21 §6): script templates for a new sense, action, gene kind, stat, phase, brain or mutation operator — each with the methods to override and a matching test — and a mutation deck. Scripts go to Assets/Student (with its assembly), tests to Assets/Student/Tests (with a test assembly that sees EvoSim.Testing). SpeciesInspector class The Species inspector (21 §3, EDIT-04): read-only tables computed from the subtree (actions, senses, genes, stats and traits, food, population), the observation-space size, the signature, and a prompt preview built by the same code as the Ask brains phase (T-PROMPT-05). ValidationPanel static class The validation list of the inspectors (EDIT-01, EDIT-02): one line per message with its severity, a button that selects the object at fault, and the fix button when the validator offers one. VisualPlayerBuild static class Builds a Windows player that draws a run (07 real-time test): Windows 64-bit, Mono, the reference scenes (HideVsFlee first) given here, not in the Build Settings, into Builds/EvoSim/<date>/EvoSim.exe. Project and Player settings are left as they are. Batch: -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.VisualPlayerBuild.BuildFromCommandLine [-scenes HideVsFlee,Lab1_Full] [-out folder]. Run it: EvoSim.exe -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -speed 5 -brain JEV -capture 10 -quitAtEnd -screen-fullscreen 0 -logFile player.log (PlayerArgs). WorldFactory static class Creating things from the menus (21 §6): a new world with the default tree, a new species with the reference body modules, and actions, senses and genes from the module prefabs in Modules/. The static methods are what the menus call, so tests build worlds exactly as a student does. WorldInspector class The World inspector (21 §3): state and tick, run controls in Play mode, the settings, the phases in order with their enable toggles, the services, and the validation panel.

extending/action.html.title: An action or an interaction | EvoSim
extending/action.html.summary: An action or an interaction An action is a behaviour the brain can choose: drink, dig, call for help. Write one when animals need to do something new. If the brain should only know something new, write a sense instead. If the new thing happens on contact (drink at the shore, drag a carcass), the action asks for an interaction, a small class that runs once the animal is within reach. How actions run is explained in Actions and movement. The base class Derive from AnimalAction, itself a species module. Member You What it does, when it is called Act must implement Plans one tick for an animal that chose this action, through the context. Called by the act phase every tick until the animal's next decision. DefaultDescription should override The action's line in the prompt, used when the Inspector's Description is empty. Initialize() may override Find the modules you need once, after every module has declared its stats. Declare(SpeciesBuilder), Validate(ValidationReport) may override Declare stats or traits; report configuration mistakes before Play. Rests may override True for a resting action: a still tick costs the rest cost, not the base cost. Mates may override True for an action that seeks a partner: the breed phase breeds animals that chose it. Hunts may override True for an action that chases and strikes; senses such as the sample ChasedSense read it. Overlay, OverlayTicks may override True for an action done in passing, beside a second action drawn from the rest of the row; for how many ticks. See Actions done in passing. IsRelevant may override Declares when a situation is relevant to this action, for the specification's directed tests (CTRL-10). The simulation never calls it. ActAll may override Plans a group of animals at once (20 §10). It must give exactly the plans Act gives. Name, Description, Gene, Index read The GameObject's name; the prompt line; the bound text gene; the place in the action order. The base class already writes the action's line in the prompt, - name: description (PROMPT-01). A complete example The sample DrinkAction (Assets/EvoSim/Samples/DrinkAction.cs, recipe 22 §3) walks to the nearest visible water and resets the animal's thirst there. Thirst is a stat declared by the sample Thirst module. Its relevance test and its validation are left out here. [RequiresModule(typeof(Thirst))] public class DrinkAction : AnimalAction { Thirst thirst; // the species' thirst module, found in Initialize protected override string DefaultDescription => "go to the nearest visible water and drink"; public override void Initialize() => thirst = Species.Module<Thirst>(); public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { var water = c.Ground != null ? c.Ground.NearestWater(a.Position, c.Vision(a)) : null; if (water == null) { c.Search(); return; } // nothing in sight: search (ACT-04) c.WalkTo(water.Value.Shore, 0f); c.OnArrival(new Drink(thirst)); // applied after moving, within reach } sealed class Drink : IInteraction { readonly Thirst thirst; // the module whose stat is reset public Drink(Thirst t) { thirst = t; } public float Reach => 0.5f; public void Apply(Animal a, InteractionContext c) { if (thirst != null) a[thirst.Value] = 0f; } } } [RequiresModule(typeof(Thirst))] makes validation warn when the species has no thirst module (V-26), and makes the conformance suite add one when it tests the action. Where to put it Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Action asks for a class name and writes Assets/Student/<Name>.cs, an action that only searches, with a test in Assets/Student/Tests/<Name>Tests.cs. In the scene, add a child GameObject under the species' Actions object and name it after the action, for example drink. That name is the action's name in the prompt; it must be unique in the species (V-03). Add your component to it, and a TextGene on the same GameObject with its founder sentences ("Drink whenever you pass water."). Without a gene the brain can't be steered for the action (V-05, with a fix). See Genes. The actions' depth-first order is their order in the prompt and in the brain's answer (SPEC-03). Adding an action changes the species' signature; accept it in the validation panel (V-12). The prompt then lists - drink: go to the nearest visible water and drink. Set the Description field to change that line for one scene. The act context Act receives an ActContext. The context is reset to stay, no interaction before each animal, and the last intent and the last OnArrival called are the plan. Queries. Each returns only what the animal's senses could report (ACT-05), or null when nothing is in sight. Method Returns Vision(a) the animal's vision radius, in meters (20 in the reference) NearestAnimal(a, set, listed) the nearest visible animal of a set (AnimalSet: threats, prey, kin, listed), with its distance NearestReadyPartner(a) the nearest kin in sight that is ready to mate NearestResource(a, layerName) the nearest food item its diet grazes, on one layer or all of them NearestCarcass(a) the nearest carcass it may eat from NearestEgg(a, of) the nearest egg its diet eats, of one species or any NearestEntity<T>(a, filter) the nearest entity of a kind of your own; no diet check NearestCover(a, radius) the nearest point in cover; distance 0 when already in cover InCover(a), IsReady(other) whether the animal stands in cover; whether another one is ready to mate World, Ground and Tick give the rest, for example c.Ground.NearestWater(...). Intents. Say where to go this tick (ACT-03). Method Intent WalkTo(point, stopAt), RunTo(point, stopAt) go toward a point and stop at a distance from it, never past it (MOVE-04) WalkTo(animal, stopAt), RunTo(animal, stopAt) the same toward an animal, recorded as the animal's target RunAwayFrom(animal), RunAwayFrom(point), WalkAwayFrom(point) go straight away, as far as speed and stamina allow Stay() stay where it is Wander() keep the heading, sometimes turn by ±45° or ±90°; walks (MOVE-05) Search() wander, and count the choice as searching once per decision (ACT-04) Arrival. OnArrival(Interaction.Graze(item)) asks for a reference interaction; the other builders of Interaction are Strike(animal), Scavenge(carcass) and EatEgg(egg). OnArrival(myInteraction) asks for one of your own. Interactions An interaction is the effect of contact. It is the only place where an action changes an animal (ACT-06). Implement IInteraction: Member What it does, when it is called Reach How close to the point its intent was heading to, in meters, the animal must end its move. For a Stay, that point is the animal's own position. Apply Called once, in the same tick, right after the animal moved, if it is within reach and was not killed earlier in the tick. Apply receives an InteractionContext: World, Ground, Tick, Feed and Stream. Feed(a, energy, digest) feeds an animal like a meal: energy gained up to the maximum, one meal counted, and, if digest is true, digestion afterwards for a species with a Digestion module. It checks no diet, so check the eater's Diet yourself when your food should depend on it. A complete action with an interaction that feeds: the test probe FeedAction (Assets/EvoSim/Testing/Probes/FeedAction.cs) stays where it is and eats a snack every tick. public class FeedAction : AnimalAction { public float Energy = 5f; protected override string DefaultDescription => "stay and eat a snack (a test probe)"; public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { c.Stay(); c.OnArrival(new Snack(Energy)); // reach is measured from where it stays: always in reach } sealed class Snack : IInteraction { readonly float energy; // the snack's energy, in points public Snack(float e) { energy = e; } public float Reach => 0.5f; public void Apply(Animal actor, InteractionContext c) => c.Feed(actor, energy); } } Reach may be float.PositiveInfinity: the sample DragAction uses it to move a carcass along with the animal, wherever it ends up. Actions done in passing An action normally runs every tick until the next decision (ACT-02), and decides the intent: where the animal goes. That doesn't suit something done in a moment, such as a call, a scent mark or a look around: an animal that stood still to call would stand still for a whole decision period, next to the predator it warns about. Such an action is an overlay (ACT-07): override Overlay to return true. When the brain's draw picks an overlay, the engine draws a second action, the carrier, from the same row with every overlay set to 0 (DEC-20). That is what the animal would have done had it not drawn the overlay: flee, hide, eat. A row with nothing else leaves no carrier, and the animal stays. Each tick the carrier plans as usual. Then the overlay's Act runs in the same context: its intent is ignored, its interaction applies after the carrier's, measured from the point its own intent names (none: where the animal stood). Use float.PositiveInfinity as the reach for an effect that happens wherever the carrier took the animal. It acts for OverlayTicks ticks (1 by default: once, on the tick of the decision; 0: until the next decision), and ends early when the animal becomes busy or dies. The brain is asked nothing more; a species without overlays draws exactly as before. The prompt keeps the action's line, and the engine adds one rule: Some actions are done in passing (mark): the animal also does its next most likely choice. A species needs at least one action that is not an overlay (V-19), and an overlay may not mate or hunt (V-27). The inspector shows both, "flee + mark"; the decision counts count the overlay and its carrier. public class MarkAction : AnimalAction { public override bool Overlay => true; // done in passing (ACT-07) protected override string DefaultDescription => "leave a scent mark"; public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) => c.OnArrival(new Mark()); // no intent: the carrier moves it sealed class Mark : IInteraction { public float Reach => float.PositiveInfinity; // wherever the carrier took the animal public void Apply(Animal actor, InteractionContext c) => actor.Species.Module<Energy>()?.Pay(actor, 0.2f); // a mark costs a little energy } } The worked example Alarm calls builds a complete overlay, with a world service that keeps the calls and a sense that hears them. Rules Search when there is nothing to act on (ACT-04). Call c.Search(), not c.Wander(), so the choice is counted. Target only what the context returns (ACT-05): within vision, not hidden, not killed, not itself. Never change an animal in Act (ACT-06): no positions, stats or flags, yours included. Effects go through interactions, and the act phase moves the animal. Never read gene sentences or decision records (ACT-20). Genes reach an action only through traits. Draw random numbers only from the species' streams (RAND-03): World.Random.For(Species, "actions") in Act, c.Stream(actor.Species, "actions") in Apply. Never UnityEngine.Random. Keep settings in the module, state in the animal. One action object serves every animal of its species; a per-animal memory goes in a stat you declare. Set up in Initialize, not in Awake or Start. Test it The conformance suite runs every action class in the project: Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode, ConformanceTests ▸ ActionConformance, one case per class (the T-ACT template). It puts your action, with a text gene and the modules it requires, under the prey of a small world and checks that: the action has a description and a bound gene; calling Act on every prey changes no animal anywhere (ACT-06); alone in an empty world, the action searches or stays (ACT-04); resting actions are exempt; an overlay plans no move and must not search (ACT-07), and gets a rest action beside it as its carrier. A test to copy, from Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Samples/SampleTests.cs (its class derives from WorldFixture, which provides New()): [Test] public void DrinkResetsThirst() { var w = New().Ground<PondGround>(20, 20).Food(0f, 0f).Phase<ActPhase>() .Species("prey", s => s.PreyBody().Action<DrinkAction>("drink").Module<Thirst>()).Build(); var sp = w.FindSpecies("prey"); var a = Place.Animal(sp, Place.At(10f, 15f)); var thirst = sp.Module<Thirst>().Value; a[thirst] = 50f; a.Choose("drink"); w.Advance(3); Assert.AreEqual(0f, a[thirst], "drank"); } See Testing your module for the world builder and the other suites. Read next The reference actions, smallest first: RestAction, FollowAction, EatAction, FleeAction, HideAction, HuntAction, MateAction. Rewrite one from its stub: the teaching path. The samples DrinkAction and DragAction: the samples. A locomotion, to change how animals move; Genes, for the gene on your action.

extending/brain.html.title: A brain | EvoSim
extending/brain.html.summary: A brain A brain turns each deciding animal's query into one probability per action. Derive from Brain to decide in C#: with rules, a small network, or a model you run yourself. For a model behind a web API, derive from HttpBrain instead: see An HTTP brain or mutator server. To change when animals decide, you need no brain: see Decision timing. How decisions, the memo and the cache work is in Decisions and brains.
