The base class Member What it does, and when it is called Id must implement a short name ("random", "keyword-v1"), part of memo and cache keys and the name of its cache file Ask must implement answers a batch of queries with a BrainAnswer; called by the ask-brains phase once per tick and batch, on the main thread Memoizable may override false for a brain with memory: every query then reaches it (below) MaxActions may override the most actions a species may have with this brain (DEC-14, V-11); no limit by default MaxPromptTokens may override the longest prompt it takes, in estimated tokens (V-11); 0 = no limit AcceptsAttachments may override true if it reads attachments such as images (V-51); false by default CanMixSpecies may override false to get one batch per species (DEC-13); true by default AnswerInstruction may override the line that ends the prompt, {ask} (PROMPT-07); empty by default ModelIdentity, Mode may override the model with its revision, and the brain's mode: parts of the cache key (DEC-33) Initialize, Validate may override set up before the run; report configuration problems Two helpers make rows: Uniform and Normalize, which turns non-negative weights into a valid row. What a query holds is listed in Decisions and brains. A complete example A small rule-based brain, in the spirit of the prototype's keyword brain (08 §6). Each action starts with weight 1; its gene's wording pushes it up or down, and fleeing gets more likely when a predator is in sight. using System.Collections.Generic; using EvoSim; public class KeywordBrain : Brain { public override string Id => "keyword-v1"; public override BrainAnswer Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery> batch) { var rows = new float[batch.Count][]; for (int i = 0; i < batch.Count; i++) { var q = batch[i]; string threat = new ObservationView(q.Species, q.Observation).Token("Predator"); var weights = new double[q.Species.Actions.Count]; for (int k = 0; k < weights.Length; k++) { string action = q.Species.Actions[k].Name; weights[k] = Push(SentenceOf(q, action)); if (action == "flee" && threat != null && threat != "none") weights[k] *= 4.0; } rows[i] = Normalize(weights); // weights ≥ 0 → a row that sums to 1 } return BrainAnswer.Now(rows); // answered at once: nothing to wait for } // An action's gene is labelled with the action's name (PROMPT-02). static string SentenceOf(DecisionQuery q, string label) { foreach (var g in q.Genes) if (g.Key == label) return g.Value.ToLowerInvariant(); return ""; } static double Push(string gene) => gene.Contains("never") || gene.Contains("avoid") ? 0.2 : gene.Contains("always") || gene.Contains("whenever") ? 3.0 : 1.0; } Where to put it. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Brain writes Assets/Student/<Name>.cs (a uniform brain) and its test. Add the component on a child of the World's Brains object: a world service, enabled, not under a species (V-10). Select it as the World's Default Brain, or as one species' Brain. Validation checks your limits against every species that uses it. Answering now or later BrainAnswer has two forms. Now takes every row at once. Later returns an empty answer that you fill from another thread with SetRow or Fail, then close with Complete. The choose-actions phase waits until then. This is the pattern HttpBrain follows: public override BrainAnswer Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery> batch) { var answer = BrainAnswer.Later(batch.Count); var prompts = new string[batch.Count]; var actions = new int[batch.Count]; for (int i = 0; i < batch.Count; i++) // main thread: read what you need now { prompts[i] = batch[i].Prompt(this); actions[i] = batch[i].Species.Actions.Count; } Task.Run(() => { try { for (int i = 0; i < prompts.Length; i++) answer.SetRow(i, Score(prompts[i], actions[i])); } catch (Exception e) { for (int i = 0; i < prompts.Length; i++) if (answer.Row(i) == null) answer.Fail(i, e.Message); } finally { answer.Complete(); } // always, exactly once }); return answer; } static float[] Score(string prompt, int actions) => Uniform(actions); // your model here Read every Unity object (species, action names, prompts) in Ask, on the main thread; the background code touches only plain data. Brains with memory The memo assumes that the same query always gets the same row (DEC-12). A brain that remembers or learns breaks that assumption: override Memoizable to return false. Its queries are then never memoised, shared within a tick or cached, and each carries the animal's id in AnimalId. The test brain MemoryBrain does this: public override string Id => "memory"; public override bool Memoizable => false; // every deciding animal's query reaches Ask, with its AnimalId Strict mode and the cache Strict stops the run cleanly when a query fails or a row is malformed; off, the animal draws from a uniform row and the failure is counted (DEC-40). Use Cache stores good rows in the World's AnswerCache for later runs (DEC-33). Both are off by default, and on for HTTP brains. The cache trusts your keys: change Id (keyword-v2) whenever the answers change, and put every setting that changes an answer in ModelIdentity or Mode. Otherwise a later run replays old answers. Rules your brain keeps One valid row per query (DEC-11): in query order; one entry per action of that query's species, in the species' action order; every entry ≥ 0; the sum 1 ± 10⁻⁶. Normalize and Uniform make such rows. The same query gives the same row (DEC-12): no random draws, no clock, no state, unless Memoizable is false. Read only the queries. A brain never moves an animal or changes the world (CORE-06). Fail rather than invent: mark a query you can't answer with Fail. A failure is never stored (DEC-34). Complete a later answer exactly once, also when everything failed. The tick waits for it. State your limits (DEC-14): if a species can't fit, validation says so before the run instead of a failure during it. Test it The brain conformance suite, DecisionTests.BrainConformance, asks each brain of the EvoSim assemblies 20 queries twice, and checks every row and that both answers are equal. A brain in Assets/Student is not in its list: add the same two checks to the test written with your script. [Test] public void RowsAreValidAndRepeat() { var w = New().Ecology(prey: s => s.Population(0), predator: s => s.Population(0)) .ReferencePhases().DefaultBrain<KeywordBrain>().Build(); var prey = w.FindSpecies("prey"); var a = Place.Animal(prey, Place.At(10, 10)); w.Space.Rebuild(); var o = prey.Observe(a, new SenseContext(w)); var q = new DecisionQuery(prey, DecisionQuery.BrainGenes(prey, a.Genome), o, prey.Describe(o, TextStyle.V1), TextStyle.V1, a.Genome.BrainKey); var first = w.DefaultBrain.Ask(new[] { q }); first.Pending.Wait(); var again = w.DefaultBrain.Ask(new[] { q }); again.Pending.Wait(); Assert.IsNull(BrainAnswer.Check(first.Row(0), prey.Actions.Count), "a valid row"); CollectionAssert.AreEqual(first.Row(0), again.Row(0), "the same query, the same row"); } The test class derives from WorldFixture. To test a phase or an action against chosen answers, use the test brain ScriptedBrain. More in Testing your module. Decision timing When animals decide is set per species by a DecisionSchedule, with no code. Add one under the species (the reference species have one in their Life group): Field Reference Effect Period 0 ticks between two decisions of this species; 0 = the World's Decision Period (4) Staggered on an animal decides when (tick + id) % period == 0, so the decisions spread over the period Without a schedule, a species decides all together every World period. Both settings change behaviour (DEC-04). Whatever the schedule says, a busy animal never decides (DEC-02), and an animal without an action decides on the next tick (DEC-01). For other timing, derive from DecisionSchedule and override IsDue. The sense phase calls it at the start of every tick for each living, not busy animal. It must depend only on the tick and the animal's state, and draw no random number, so a seed still repeats the run. Keep one schedule per species: replace the reference one rather than adding a second. [RequiresModule(typeof(Energy))] public class HungryDecideOften : DecisionSchedule { Energy energy; public override void Initialize() => energy = Species.Module<Energy>(); // Hungry animals decide every 2 ticks; the others follow the usual schedule. public override bool IsDue(Animal a, int tick, World w) => a[energy.Value] < 30f ? tick % 2 == 0 : base.IsDue(a, tick, w); } Read next Prompt hooks: a text brain adds only its AnswerInstruction; rule lines come from WritePromptRules on species modules and world services (How the prompt is written). RandomBrain, the null model; rewrite it from its stub (exercise 13): the teaching path. MemoryBrain and ScriptedBrain, the test brains. HttpBrain, JevBrain, OllamaPointsBrain: An HTTP brain or mutator server. Decisions and brains and Senses and prompts. Specification: 08 — Decisions, brains and prompts.

extending/documenting-your-code.html.title: Writing documentation comments | EvoSim
extending/documenting-your-code.html.summary: Writing documentation comments Every type and every member in EvoSim carries a /// documentation comment. Your editor shows it when you hover over a name, and the API reference of this site is built from it. Document your own modules the same way: the next reader may be you, three weeks later. This page is the house style. A checker, the doc audit, enforces the parts a program can check. What gets a comment Element Needs Every type (class, struct, interface, enum, delegate), public or not a Every member (method, property, constructor, event, operator, indexer, enum member, constant), public or not a Every public or protected method, constructor, delegate or indexer a for each parameter, a for a returned value, a for each type parameter A public or protected field a A private field a , or a [Tooltip] (the Inspector shows it), or a // comment at the end of its line or on the line just above, or nothing when it only backs a property of the same name (animals behind Animals) An override whose base text fits /// An override that does something particular its own plus /// , which keeps the base's parameters and returns A test method its [Test, Description("…")] (no /// needed); the test class and its helpers get a A partial type (World) a in its main file only; each other part starts with a // line saying what that file holds Inside method bodies, write a // comment where a step is not obvious from the code: why it is done, which rule it keeps, what would break without it. Don't narrate code that reads well by itself. How to write a summary One or two sentences that say what the thing is for, in the words of the simulation, not of the code. Types and properties: a noun phrase. The species' brain, or the World's default (DEC-13). Methods: a verb in the third person. Reads one animal at a decision and returns one of its tokens (SENSE-03). Booleans: True when …; say what false means if it is not the plain opposite. Say what null, empty, -1 or 0 mean: … or null when nothing is in sight. Give the unit of every quantity: meters, ticks, points (energy, stamina), seconds, per tick. Say when it is called and by whom for hooks and lifecycle methods: Called by the World once per run, after every module declared its stats and before founders spawn. For something a student overrides, say what it must keep: the same tokens for the same animal, random draws only from the stream it is given, no change to the world from inside Act… Avoid: This method…, Gets or sets…, Helper, repeating the name (The species. for Species), the history of the code (fixed in M13.4 belongs to the implementation log), and we. Write plain English for second-year students: short sentences, common words, one idea per sentence. The first time a page uses a term of the glossary (allele, locus, tick, phase…), link it or explain it. Rule ids and spec references The specification numbers its rules. Name the rule a piece of code keeps, in parentheses: (SENSE-01), (DEC-30, DEC-33). Sections of a spec document are written (07 §4), validation messages V-08, tests T-ACT-09. The site turns rule ids into links to the specification. Tags Tag Use it for always; one or two sentences what the argument is and what values it takes: The animal that decides. what comes back, including the "nothing" case: The nearest prey within vision, or null. what the type parameter stands for: The kind of module to find. anything longer: lifecycle, rules to keep, how to extend, performance. Use for paragraphs and … for lists + on base classes students derive from and on the most used methods: a short, real example, taken from EvoSim or its samples a link to a type or member the reader may want to open next: , a parameter named in the text … a literal value, a file name, an Inspector field or code inline: "none", stats.csv null, true, false when they are values (plain "null" is fine in a sentence) take the base type's or interface's text an exception the caller should expect and handle XML rules: write < as <, > as > and & as &, also inside . Generic types in a cref take braces: . The compiler checks every cref: a wrong one is reported by the audit. Keep lines under 140 characters; wrap long comments on several /// lines. Examples A base class students derive from: /// /// Reads one animal and the world and returns one token from a fixed list (SENSE-01): what the brain is told about one /// aspect of the situation, such as the nearest food or the energy level. /// /// /// Derive from it, declare every token in , implement , and place the component /// under a species: its depth-first place among the species' senses is its place in the situation text. /// A sense only reads. It sees the world as it was at the start of the tick (SENSE-04) and draws no random number. /// /// /// /// public class HungerSense : Sense /// { /// static readonly string[] tokens = { "fed", "hungry" }; /// Energy energy; /// public override IReadOnlyList<string> Tokens => tokens; /// public override void Initialize() => energy = Species.Module<Energy>(); /// public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) => a[energy.Value] < 30f ? 1 : 0; /// } /// /// public abstract class Sense : SpeciesModule A method with parameters: /// Reads one animal at a decision (SENSE-03). /// The animal that decides. /// The world as it was at the start of the tick: nearest animals, food, cover, distances. /// An index into . public abstract int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s); An override that does something particular, keeping the base's parameters: /// Walks to the nearest visible food the diet allows and grazes it on arrival; searches when none is in sight (ACT-04). /// public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) An override that changes nothing in the contract: /// public override bool IsRelevant(ObservationView o) => Seen(o.Token(relevantSense)); Private state: [SerializeField, Tooltip("A layer name; empty = every layer the diet grazes.")] string target = ""; // the Tooltip documents it Species eggsOf; // whose eggs this action eats, when its target is "egg:" readonly List animals = new List(); // backs Animals: nothing more to say Check your comments The doc audit compiles the EvoSim assemblies with Unity's own compiler and lists what is missing or malformed: powershell -File Docs\Site\tools\audit.ps1 # everything powershell -File Docs\Site\tools\audit.ps1 --only Runtime/Senses --max 50 # one folder (relative to Assets/EvoSim) Code Meaning CS1591 a public or protected type or member has no doc comment DOC01 a non-public type or member has no doc comment (fields: see the table above) DOC02 a public or protected member's comment lacks a , or CS1570 the comment is not well-formed XML (an unescaped < or &?) CS1572, CS1573 a names no parameter, or a parameter has none CS1574, CS1580, CS1584 a cref points to nothing, or is badly written CS1587 a /// comment sits on nothing (use // there) --same-code GITREF checks that only comments and spaces changed since a git revision: use it after a pass that should not touch the code. The site itself is built by Docs/Site/build.ps1 (see Docs/Site/README.md).

extending/editor.html.title: The editor | EvoSim
extending/editor.html.summary: The editor Your module can come with its own editor tools: a window that shows what it does in a running world, an inspector that shows computed facts next to its fields, validation messages with fix buttons, a menu item that adds it to a species. Choose a validation message to catch a configuration mistake before Play; it works in the editor, in batch runs and in tests. Choose a window or inspector to look at a running world; it exists only in the editor. The hooks Hook Where What it does, when it runs Validate(ValidationReport) on a SpeciesModule or a WorldModule your module, in Assets/Student reports configuration problems; called by Prepare(ValidationReport) in the inspectors, before Play, and when a run starts ValidationFix inside Validate a button next to the message: a label and the change it makes Unity's EditorWindow an editor-only assembly a window, opened from a menu item Unity's UnityEditor.Editor with [CustomEditor(typeof(…))] an editor-only assembly replaces the inspector of your component Unity's [MenuItem("…")] an editor-only assembly a menu item, such as your own Add Action entry Where editor code lives Editor code uses UnityEditor, which players lack, so it lives in an editor-only assembly (EDIT-03); in the runtime Student assembly it would break the player build. Create Assets/Student/Editor/Student.Editor.asmdef: { "name": "Student.Editor", "references": ["Student", "EvoSim.Runtime", "EvoSim.Samples", "EvoSim.Editor"], "includePlatforms": ["Editor"] } Put your windows, inspectors and menus in that folder: they see your modules, EvoSim and its editor helpers. A window This window lists the living animals of each species with their energy. It uses EditorWorlds to find the world the other EvoSim windows show: the one of the selection, else the first running one. using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Editor; using UnityEditor; using UnityEngine; public class EnergyListWindow : EditorWindow { Vector2 scroll; [MenuItem("Window/EvoSim/Student/Energy List")] static void Open() => GetWindow<EnergyListWindow>("Energy").Show(); void OnInspectorUpdate() { if (Application.isPlaying) Repaint(); } // about ten times a second void OnGUI() { var w = EditorWorlds.Current(); if (w == null || !w.IsInitialized) { EditorGUILayout.HelpBox("Enter Play mode in a scene with a World.", MessageType.Info); return; } scroll = EditorGUILayout.BeginScrollView(scroll); foreach (var s in w.AllSpecies) { var energy = s.Module<Energy>(); if (energy == null) continue; EditorGUILayout.LabelField($"{s.DisplayName}: {s.Animals.Count} living", EditorStyles.boldLabel); foreach (var a in s.Animals) if (!a.IsGone) EditorGUILayout.LabelField($"#{a.Id}", $"{a[energy.Value]:0} energy"); } EditorGUILayout.EndScrollView(); } } Open it with Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Student ▸ Energy List, then press Play. Other helpers: EditorWorlds.SelectedAnimal gives the animal whose body is selected, and EditorWorlds.ActionColor the colour every EvoSim window uses for an action. An inspector An inspector of your own can show what the fields mean, not only what they are (EDIT-04). Write a class FearInspector : UnityEditor.Editor with [CustomEditor(typeof(Fear))] (Fear is the module of the next section). In OnInspectorGUI, call DrawDefaultInspector() to keep the fields, then draw facts computed from (Fear)target: in Play mode, for example, the mean of a[fear.Value] over fear.Species.Animals. Override RequiresConstantRepaint to return Application.isPlaying so the numbers follow the run. Write UnityEditor.Editor in full, as EvoSim's own inspectors do: inside a namespace under EvoSim, Editor alone means the EvoSim.Editor namespace. Validation messages with fixes A module checks its own settings in Validate. Each problem is one message: an id, the object at fault, a sentence that names the rule, and a fix when there is an obvious one. This stat module reports a start above its maximum, with a Clamp button, and notes when no sense lets the brain read it: using System.Linq; using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; /// <summary>A fear stat on every animal of the species, from <c>start</c> at birth up to <c>max</c>.</summary> public class Fear : SpeciesModule { [SerializeField, Min(0f), Tooltip("Fear at birth.")] float start = 0f; [SerializeField, Min(1f), Tooltip("The most fear an animal can feel.")] float max = 100f; public StatId Value { get; private set; } public float Start => start; public override void Declare(SpeciesBuilder b) => Value = b.DeclareStat("fear", StatStart.Fixed(start), 0f, max); public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) { if (start > max) report.Warning("V-36", this, $"Fear starts at {start}, above its maximum {max}.", new ValidationFix("Clamp", () => start = max)); if (!Species.ModulesOf<LevelSense>().Any(s => s.Stat == "fear")) report.Info("Fear-01", this, "No LevelSense reads the stat 'fear': the brain never hears about it."); } public void Configure(float startFear, float maxFear) { start = startFear; max = maxFear; } } Select the World and press Validate: the message reads V-36 Fear starts at 150, above its maximum 100., with Select and Clamp next to it. Clamp runs the fix on your component, marks it changed and validates again. An error (report.Error) also stops Play (Editor tooling). Rules for Validate: Only read. It runs in the editor and at the start of every run. Only the fix changes the scene, when clicked. Name the object at fault, usually this: Select and the Console use it (EDIT-02). Error when the run cannot be right (it blocks Play), Warning when it probably runs not as meant, Info for a fact worth knowing. The id is any short string. Reuse a catalogue id (21 §2) when your check is one of its kinds. A fix captures what it needs in local variables, not loop variables. A fix that changes the component's own fields, as above, is saved with the scene. More in Species modules; to require another module, [RequiresModule] checks it for you (dependencies). Your own Add menu item GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Action and Add Sense list fixed items. Each one copies a prefab from Assets/EvoSim/Modules with AddModule(GameObject, string, string). To offer your own module the same way: Make the prefab. Create an empty GameObject, add your action component and a TextGene, and fill the gene's Founders (or set its Pool). For a sense, name the GameObject after its label and add the sense. Save it by dragging it into Assets/EvoSim/Modules (an action: Drink.prefab), Assets/EvoSim/Modules/Senses or Assets/EvoSim/Modules/Genes. Delete the scene object. Add a menu item in your editor assembly (with the using lines of the window above): static class MyAddMenus { const string Item = "GameObject/EvoSim/Add Action/Drink (mine)"; [MenuItem(Item, false, 20)] static void AddDrink() { var species = Selection.activeGameObject.GetComponentInParent<Species>(true); var go = WorldFactory.AddModule(species.gameObject, "Actions", "Drink"); // under the species' Actions group Undo.RegisterCreatedObjectUndo(go, "Add Drink"); Selection.activeObject = go; } [MenuItem(Item, true)] // enabled only when a species, or an object under it, is selected static bool CanAddDrink() => Selection.activeGameObject != null && Selection.activeGameObject.GetComponentInParent<Species>(true) != null; } The kind is "Actions", "Senses" or "Genes"; the module is the prefab's file name without .prefab. An action is renamed in lower case (drink): its GameObject's name is its name in the prompt. You can also skip the menu and drag your prefab onto the species' Actions or Senses object. Test it Test validation with a world built in code, in a WorldFixture class with using System.Linq; (Testing your module): [Test, Description("A start above the maximum is reported (V-36), and Clamp fixes it")] public void StartAboveMaximum() { var w = New().Flat(20, 20) .Species("prey", s => s.Population(0).Action<RestAction>("rest").Module<Fear>(f => f.Configure(150f, 100f))) .BuildUninitialized(); var report = new ValidationReport(); w.Prepare(report); report.Messages.First(m => m.Id == "V-36").Fix.Apply(); Assert.AreEqual(100f, w.FindSpecies("prey").Module<Fear>().Start); } Windows and inspectors have no test suite: open them in Play mode and look. The API for tools Your editor code can call EvoSim's own tools, all static classes of the EvoSim.Editor assembly. Running and building shows Batch and RealTimeRuns at work, in the editor and in batch mode. extending/environment.html.title: Food, cover, entities and ground | EvoSim
extending/environment.html.summary: Food, cover, entities and ground Four kinds of world services make up the environment, and each is a base class you can derive from. Add a resource layer for food that sits on cells and grows back (berries, mushrooms), a cover for hiding places, an entity system for objects that appear, move or rot (fruit, nests), or a ground for a different world shape. Making something edible needs no code at all: see Who eats what. For how the reference modules behave, read The environment first. All four go under the World, outside any species: a layer, a cover or an entity system on its own GameObject under Environment, the ground on the World's Ground GameObject. There is no script template for them: create a C# file in Assets/Student and derive from the base class. A resource layer ResourceLayer holds edible items. Senses and actions find items through the eater's diet, and the act phase consumes them when an animal grazes. Member What it does, when it is called Count must implement how many items the layer holds now (ENV-01) Nearest must implement the nearest item within a radius, as a ResourceItem; called by senses and actions Consume must implement removes the item at once; false if it is gone already (ENV-02); called when an animal grazes Regrow may override once per tick, in the environment phase, with the layer's own stream (ENV-03); nothing by default StreamName may override the name of that stream; the layer's name by default WithinReach may override the nearest item within reach; Nearest by default Initialize may override build empty storage: the ground is ready, the cover may not be yet Begin may override place the first items: every module is ready, cover included LayerName is the GameObject's name, and Edible the Edible on the same GameObject. Example: berry bushes Bushes grow in some cells of a 4 m grid, each with one berry that grows back. It reuses CellGrid, the cell grid of the reference FoodGrid, which finds the nearest marked cell for you. using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; public class BerryBushes : ResourceLayer { [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f), Tooltip("Share of walkable cells with a bush.")] float bushShare = 0.2f; [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f), Tooltip("Chance per tick that a bush regrows its berry.")] float regrowP = 0.01f; CellGrid grid; bool[] bush, berry; // per cell: a bush grows here; its berry is ripe int count; public override int Count => count; public override void Initialize() { grid = new CellGrid(World.Ground.Bounds, 4f); bush = new bool[grid.Count]; berry = new bool[grid.Count]; count = 0; } public override void Begin() // the map: from the world seed (RAND-04) { var rng = World.Random.Get("world/" + ServiceName); for (int c = 0; c < grid.Count; c++) if (World.Ground.IsWalkable(grid.Center(c)) && rng.NextDouble() < bushShare) { bush[c] = berry[c] = true; count++; } } public override bool Nearest(Vector3 p, float radius, out ResourceItem item) { int c = grid.Nearest(berry, p, radius, World.Ground, out float d); // world distance, ties by cell index item = c >= 0 ? new ResourceItem(this, c, World.Ground.OnGround(grid.Center(c)), d) : default; return c >= 0; } public override bool Consume(ResourceItem item) { if (item.Layer != this || item.Cell < 0 || !berry[item.Cell]) return false; // gone already (ENV-02) berry[item.Cell] = false; count--; return true; } public override void Regrow(RandomStream rng) // the layer's own stream, in cell order { for (int c = 0; c < grid.Count; c++) if (bush[c] && !berry[c] && rng.NextDouble() < regrowP) { berry[c] = true; count++; } } } To use it: Add a GameObject Berries under the World's Environment, with BerryBushes and an Edible (Energy: the energy points of one berry). On each species that eats berries, add a diet entry Berries. Point the eater's actions and senses at it: an EatAction with Target Berries (or empty for every layer the diet grazes), a NearestResourceSense with Layer Name Berries if the brain should know. Rules Consume once (ENV-02): Consume removes the item before it returns true, and returns false for an item already eaten. The act order decides who gets a contested item. Change only in your phase (ENV-03): the items change only in Regrow and Consume. Regrow draws only from the stream it is given, in a fixed order: loop over cells, never over a Dictionary (RAND-05). The map from the world seed (RAND-04): draw the first items in Begin from World.Random.Get("world/" + ServiceName), so runs that share a world seed share the map. Nearest by the world distance (SPACE-02), ties broken by a fixed key such as the cell index (SPACE-08). CellGrid's Nearest does both. Items on walkable ground, so animals can reach them. A unique name: diets, senses and the stream use the GameObject's name. It must differ from the other layers and must not be world, act-order or contain / (V-18). A cover Cover answers where animals can hide. The World combines every cover: an animal is hidden when any cover hides it, and the hide action runs to the nearest cover point of all of them. Member What it does InCover must implement whether a point is in cover (ENV-10) NearestCover must implement the nearest point in cover within a radius, and its distance; the point itself, at 0, when already in cover Hides may override whether species hidden is hidden from species from: from its threats by default, limited by Hiding Species IsHiddenFrom may override Hides and InCover at the animal's position A complete cover, from EvoSim's test probes, where a band of the world is in cover: using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; public class SideCover : Cover { public float MinX = float.NegativeInfinity, MaxX = float.PositiveInfinity; public override bool InCover(Vector3 p) => p.x >= MinX && p.x <= MaxX; public override bool NearestCover(Vector3 p, float radius, out Vector3 point, out float distance) { point = new Vector3(Mathf.Clamp(p.x, MinX, MaxX), p.y, p.z); distance = Mathf.Abs(point.x - p.x); return distance <= radius; } } To hide every species from every other one, not only from its threats: public override bool Hides(Species hidden, Species from) => from != hidden; Rules. The same point gets the same answer for the whole run, or the answer changes only in a phase. Build a map in Initialize from World.Random.Get("world/" + ServiceName) and draw nothing afterwards (RAND-04). Return a walkable point from NearestCover, measured with the world distance. Hides gives the same answer for the same two species all run long, since senses, actions and strikes all ask it (ENV-11). An entity kind An Entity is an object with a position that is not an animal. Its EntitySystem<T> keeps the entities of one kind in creation order and finds them like animals (ENV-20). Member What it does, when it is called Entity.Kind, EntitySystem<T>.Kind must implement the kind's name, e.g. "apple" Add(e) call adds an entity: it gets its id and creation tick Nearest(p, radius, viewer, filter, out found, out distance) call the nearest entity passing the filter, ties by id; used-up ones are skipped Move(e, t) may override moves one entity, each tick in the environment phase (ENV-21); nothing by default OnRemoved(e, reason, t) may override after an entity is removed, "used up" or "expired" UpdateEntities(t) may override, call base the environment phase's call: Move each entity, count lifetimes down, remove used-up and expired ones (ENV-22) Initialize may override, call base empties the list for a new run An entity's LifetimeLeft counts down once per tick (-1 = never), and setting UsedUp removes it in this tick's environment phase. Example: apples that fall and rot using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; public class Apple : Entity { public override string Kind => "apple"; } public class AppleSystem : EntitySystem<Apple> { [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f), Tooltip("Chance per tick that an apple falls.")] float fallP = 0.2f; [SerializeField, Min(1), Tooltip("Ticks before an apple rots.")] int rotTicks = 200; public override string Kind => "apple"; public override void UpdateEntities(TickContext t) { base.UpdateEntities(t); // the old ones age and go first (ENV-22) var rng = t.Stream(ServiceName); // its own stream (RAND-02) if (rng.Chance(fallP)) Add(new Apple { Position = World.Ground.RandomWalkable(rng), LifetimeLeft = rotTicks }); } } Put AppleSystem on a GameObject Apples under Environment. Senses find apples with s.NearestEntity<Apple>(a, vision) on the SenseContext, actions with c.NearestEntity<Apple>(a) on the ActContext (within the animal's vision). The run views show one grey cube per apple: the EntityMarkers read every entity kind through EntityAt, which EntitySystem<T> provides. An apple is eaten through an action with an interaction of your own (An action). The interaction marks the apple used up first, so a second animal reaching it in the same tick gets nothing: using EvoSim; public class EatAppleAction : AnimalAction { protected override string DefaultDescription => "go to the nearest visible apple and eat it"; public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { var apple = c.NearestEntity<Apple>(a); // within the animal's vision if (apple == null) { c.Search(); return; } c.WalkTo(apple.Value.Position, 0f); c.OnArrival(new EatApple(apple.Value.Entity)); } sealed class EatApple : IInteraction { readonly Apple apple; public EatApple(Apple a) { apple = a; } public float Reach => 0.5f; public void Apply(Animal a, InteractionContext c) { if (apple.UsedUp) return; // eaten by an animal that acted earlier (ENV-02) apple.UsedUp = true; // removed in this tick's environment phase c.Feed(a, 20f); } } } Rules. Entities change only in phases and interactions, never from the views (ENV-21, SPACE-12). Keep them on walkable ground. Draw random numbers only from a named stream of t (RAND-02). Don't add or remove entities from OnRemoved: the list is being compacted. A ground Ground gives every point its height and walkability, and owns the world's distance (SPACE-02, SPACE-04). Member What it does, when it is called Bounds must implement the world rectangle (x, z), half-open; layers and covers lay their grids over it Height must implement the ground's height; animals and items follow it (SPACE-06) IsWalkable must implement whether an animal may stand there; checked after every move Distance may override the world distance; every query uses it through World.Distance IsWater, NearestWater may override water, for the food bonus, water senses and drinking SlopeDegrees may override the slope between two points, for locomotions SlideTo, SideStep may override how a straight move is blocked, and how a stuck animal is freed RandomWalkable may override where founders and newcomers appear The easiest start is a subclass of FlatGround. This flat ground with a pond comes from EvoSim's test probes: using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; public class PondGround : FlatGround { public Vector3 PondCenter = new Vector3(10f, 0f, 10f); public float PondRadius = 3f; public override bool IsWater(Vector3 p) => Flat(p, PondCenter) < PondRadius; public override bool IsWalkable(Vector3 p) => base.IsWalkable(p) && !IsWater(p); public override WaterHit? NearestWater(Vector3 p, float radius) { float d = Mathf.Max(0f, Flat(p, PondCenter) - PondRadius); if (d > radius) return null; var dir = new Vector3(p.x - PondCenter.x, 0f, p.z - PondCenter.z); if (dir.sqrMagnitude < 1e-6f) dir = Vector3.right; dir.Normalize(); return new WaterHit(PondCenter + dir * (PondRadius - 0.01f), PondCenter + dir * (PondRadius + 0.01f), d); } static float Flat(Vector3 a, Vector3 b) => new Vector2(a.x - b.x, a.z - b.z).magnitude; } Replace the FlatGround on the World's Ground GameObject with it: a World uses one ground. Rules. IsWalkable is false outside Bounds: nothing ever leaves the rectangle (SPACE-03). The answers don't change during a run: layers and covers read them once, at initialisation. All walkable ground is connected, or animals get trapped in pockets (SPACE-05). Distance is never shorter than the straight horizontal distance: the cell grids' nearest-cell search relies on it. SideStep and RandomWalkable draw only from the stream they are given (RAND-02). The ground is initialised before every other service: don't look up layers or covers in its Initialize. Who eats what Whether something is eaten is decided on both sides (SPEC-10, SPEC-13): the eaten thing carries an enabled Edible, which says how much energy it gives, and the eater's Diet lists it. The form of the diet entry decides how it is eaten: Diet entry Eaten The Edible goes on Energy per meal a layer's name: Grass grazed, an item within Graze Reach (0.5 m) the layer's GameObject Energy per item a species' id or display name: prey struck within Strike Reach (1 m), killing with the hunter's kill.chance the GameObject that holds the Species Energy per kill carcass:<species>: carcass:prey scavenged within Scavenge Reach (1 m), one portion per eater, never by the killer the killed species' GameObject, with Carcass Portions above 0; the world needs a CarcassSystem Carcass Energy per portion egg:<species>: egg:prey eaten whole within Graze Reach the EggSystem's GameObject Energy per egg The energy is multiplied by the entry's Energy Scale, then passed through Diet.EnergyFrom, which a subclass of Diet can override. Reaches are settings of the act phase. The Edible's Method field is only a label that the species inspector shows. Validation reports an entry that names nothing (V-20) and a target without an Edible (V-24, with a fix). Your own entity kinds, such as the apples above, are eaten through an interaction instead. Recipe: make eggs edible No code (22 §15): Give the laying species an Incubation with Ticks above 0, for example 20. With 0, eggs hatch in the tick they are laid and nothing can reach them. Add an Edible to the World's Eggs GameObject, the one with the EggSystem, with Energy 15. On the egg eater, add the diet entry egg:prey. Give it a way to find eggs: an EatAction whose Target is egg:prey, and, if its brain should know, a NearestEntitySense with Kind egg, Of Species prey and the label Eggs. An eaten egg never hatches and is recorded as egg_lost with the reason eaten (REPRO-23). Carcasses What a kill leaves is set on the killed species' Edible: Carcass Portions (reference 2, 0 = no carcass), Carcass Energy per portion (30) and Carcass Ticks before it rots (100). The hunter's diet lists carcass:prey. The carcass system's Prompt Rule is the line its prompt gets, {portions} replaced by the number of portions. On every kill, the act phase calls CarcassSystem.Create on the World's first carcass system. It is virtual: override it to change what a kill leaves, and keep the base call, which fills the carcass in and adds it. The system reuses removed carcasses, so an override of OnRemoved must call the base too. public class LeanCarcasses : CarcassSystem { public override Carcass Create(Animal killed, int killerId) { var c = base.Create(killed, killerId); if (c != null && killed.Age < 100) c.PortionsLeft = 1; // a young animal feeds one eater return c; } } Test it Every ResourceLayer class in the project, yours included, runs through the T-ENV layer template of the conformance suite (Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode, ConformanceTests ▸ LayerConformance). It puts your layer on a 30 × 30 m world as Grass, with an Edible, and checks that it starts with items, that Nearest finds one within the radius, and that an item is consumed once. A layer that starts empty fails it. For your own checks, build a small world in code (Testing your module): using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; public class BerryBushesTests : WorldFixture { [Test] public void BerriesAreEatenOnceAndGrowBack() { var w = New().Flat(40, 40).Phase<EnvironmentPhase>().Service<BerryBushes>("Berries").Build(); var bushes = w.Service<ResourceLayer>("Berries"); int start = bushes.Count; Assert.IsTrue(bushes.Nearest(Place.At(20, 20), 100f, out var berry)); Assert.IsTrue(bushes.Consume(berry)); Assert.IsFalse(bushes.Consume(berry), "eaten once (ENV-02)"); w.Advance(1000); Assert.AreEqual(start, bushes.Count, "the berry grew back"); } } WorldBuilder.Ground<T>(width, depth) builds a world on a FlatGround subclass of yours. The tests in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Environment/EnvironmentTests.cs check covers, carcasses and a replaced distance against brute-force searches: copy the one closest to your module. Read next Reference modules: FoodGrid, CoverLayer, CarcassSystem, EggSystem, TerrainGround. The samples: seasons that slow the grass, water senses and drinking on a ground with water. A sense and An action or an interaction: let animals see and use what you added. Phases, services and world hooks: services, Initialize and Begin. Specification: 03 — Environment.

extending/exercises.html.title: The teaching path | EvoSim
extending/exercises.html.summary: The teaching path The teaching path is a way in: rewrite a reference module yourself, from an empty class, and watch the world run with your version. Fourteen reference modules have a stub, from the smallest (stay still to rest) to the largest (a gene rewritten by a language model), in the order of 22 §0. Nothing grades your version and nothing has to match the reference: write it your own way, or change what it does. The conformance suite of its kind only checks that it fits the system. When you are done, invent modules of your own: Extending EvoSim. Replace with stub, Restore reference Open a scene, for example Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/Lab1_Small.unity. Work on a copy (File ▸ Save As) if you want to keep the reference scene as it is. Choose EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub ▸ 1 RestAction (or any of the 14). It writes Assets/Student/Exercises/MyRestAction.cs from the template Assets/EvoSim/Exercises/MyRestAction.cs.txt. If the file already exists, it is kept: your work is never overwritten. The first time, the menu also creates the Student and Student.Tests assemblies. Once Unity has compiled the stub, every component of exactly the reference type in the open scenes is replaced by the stub: on the same GameObject, at the same place among its components, with the same settings (every field of the same name) and the same enabled state. Subclasses of the reference are left alone. The swap can be undone (Edit ▸ Undo) and marks the scene as modified: save the scene to keep it. If the stub doesn't compile, the Console says so: fix the errors, then choose the menu item again. Write the methods that throw. Until you do, each one throws a NotImplementedException that names it ("Exercise: write MyRestAction.Act your own way…"), so the run stops when the World first calls it. Press Play and watch. Run the conformance suite of the module's kind (see Tips). EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Restore reference puts the reference module back wherever an exercise class stands in the open scenes, with its settings. Your files stay in Assets/Student/Exercises. What a stub gives you /// <summary>Exercise 1: stay still to rest (ACT-02, ANIM-21). Reference: <see cref="RestAction"/>.</summary> [ExerciseOf(typeof(RestAction))] public class MyRestAction : AnimalAction { /// <summary>The action's line in the prompt (08 §7), used when the Inspector's description is empty.</summary> protected override string DefaultDescription => "stay still to catch your breath and save energy"; public override bool Rests => true; /// <summary>… The reference gives the intent of staying, <c>c.Stay()</c>, and nothing else …</summary> public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) => throw new NotImplementedException(ExerciseOfAttribute.Todo("MyRestAction", "Act")); } A stub has the reference's base class, its Inspector settings under the same names (so the swap keeps them), and the small members that are not the exercise (the prompt line, the tokens, IsRelevant). The methods to write throw. Each one's documentation comment says what the reference does, step by step, with the calls it uses. [ExerciseOf] (ExerciseOfAttribute) ties the stub to its reference, for the two menu items. The fourteen exercises # Stub Base class Reference Write Look at 1 MyRestAction AnimalAction RestAction Act Stay; Rests makes the metabolism charge the rest cost 2 MyLevelSense Sense LevelSense Read, Write find the stat once in Initialize with FindStat; low below 30, high above 70 3 MyStarvation DeathRule Starvation CauseOfDeath find the Energy module in Initialize; energy ≤ 0 gives "starvation" 4 MyEatAction AnimalAction EatAction Act NearestResource, GrazeReach, Interaction.Graze; search when nothing is in sight (ACT-04) 5 MyNearestAnimalSense BandedSense NearestAnimalSense BuildTokens, Read the base's bands, Add and NoneToken; NearestAnimal, IsReady 6 MyFleeAction AnimalAction FleeAction Act NearestAnimal, RunAwayFrom; the Flee Into Cover option 7 MyHideAction AnimalAction HideAction Act InCover, NearestCover; no cover in sight: search (ENV-12) 8 MyStamina Stamina Stamina Budget, Settle the stat Value, the traits Max and Regen, RegenEnergyCost, Energy.Pay 9 MyLitter Litter Litter Size Min, Max, ChildEnergy; draw k with rng.Range(Min, Max + 1) (REPRO-10) 10 MyUniformCrossover Crossover UniformCrossover Cross CheckSpecies, one rng.NextBool() per locus (GENE-30) 11 MyKinematicLocomotion Locomotion KinematicLocomotion Move the speed traits WalkSpeed and RunSpeed, SlideTo, SideStep (MOVE-02, MOVE-04) 12 MyHuntAction AnimalAction HuntAction Act NearestCarcass, Interaction.Strike, Interaction.Scavenge 13 MyRandomBrain Brain RandomBrain Ask Uniform, BrainAnswer.Now (DEC-11) 14 MyLlmMutation MutationOperator LlmMutation StartMutation MutationText.Instructions, MutatorService.Submit; draw every try first (MUT-30) Why MyStamina and MyLitter derive from the reference Twelve stubs derive from the reference's base class, as a module of your own would. MyStamina and MyLitter derive from the reference itself, because other parts of the system look these two modules up by their type: the act phase and the metabolism ask the species for its Stamina, and the breed phase asks for its Litter. A stub of another type would not be found. Deriving also keeps what the reference declares. MyStamina inherits the stamina stat and the stamina.max and stamina.regen traits, so the stamina sense and number genes still work; you override only Budget and Settle. MyLitter inherits the Min, Max and Child Energy settings; you override only Size. What the stubs leave out A stub holds what you must write. Some references do a little more, which you may want to add yourself: Stub The reference also Why it matters MyHuntAction overrides Hunts to return true senses such as the sample ChasedSense read it to know an animal is hunting MyLlmMutation overrides UsesMutatorService to return true, and reads its deck in Initialize it tells the mutator client that an operator sends it work; the Ollama client then fetches the model's digest, recorded with the alleles (GENE-12) MyNearestAnimalSense overrides Write to add ", ready to mate." or ", not ready to mate.", and names its label after the species when the set holds one without it the readiness tokens are written like the plain band, and renaming a species doesn't change the label (SPEC-20) Several references also set themselves up in Initialize (the level sense finds its stat, starvation finds the energy module, eat, flee and the animal sense resolve species names) and check their settings in Validate. Each stub's class comment says which. Tips Read the reference's API page (the links in the table) and the stub's comments before you write: they say what the reference does and when the World calls each method. The extension page of the kind lists the rules a module of that kind keeps. Draw from the streams you are given. Size, Cross and StartMutation receive a RandomStream; a locomotion asks the move context for one (c.Stream(Species, "actions")). Never use UnityEngine.Random: a seed must replay the run (RAND-01). If your version does what the reference does, with the same draws in the same order, the run even gives the same events hash. Run the conformance suite of the kind in the Test Runner: the stub is in the Student assembly, so the suite finds it at once, and fails until the methods are written. Crossovers, litters and death rules have no suite of their own. See Testing your module. The reference's unit tests keep testing the reference. To hold your version to the same checks, copy a reference test into Assets/Student/Tests and put your class in the builder call (Action<MyRestAction>("rest")), with the helpers of Testing. Restore the reference before the regression tests. They run the reference scenes and compare pinned hashes. Read next Extending EvoSim: the base class for each kind of module, once you invent your own. The samples: complete extensions (thirst, water, seasons, slopes) to read and combine. 22 — Extending: recipes: the teaching path and the recipes in the specification.

extending/extension-points.html.title: Every extension point | EvoSim
extending/extension-points.html.summary: Every extension point Generated by Docs/Site/tools/DocAudit --inventory from the code: do not edit by hand. Every public type you can derive from or plug into, with the members you implement (abstract) or may replace (virtual), its events, and the EvoSim classes that already do it: read those first. The extension guide explains when to use which. EvoSim.Runtime AlleleRegistry AlleleRegistry — class. Every allele seen in a run, once per (locus, value) (GENE-10), with ids "<locus>:<n>" (GENE-11). Member What it does Registered event Raised once for each new allele, just after it is registered; not raised when a known value is registered again. AnimalAction AnimalAction — abstract class. A behaviour the brain can choose (ACT-01). Member What it does Act(Animal, ActContext) abstract method Every tick while this action is chosen: say where to go, and what to do on arrival (ACT-02, ACT-03). ActAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, ActContext, Span<ActPlan>) virtual method The batch entry point (20 §10, ARCH-12): the act phase plans every animal of the group (all chose this action) through it. The default calls Act for each; an override must give the plans Act would give. DefaultDescription virtual property The reference prompt line of this action (08 §7), used when the Inspector field is empty. Hunts virtual property True for an action that chases and strikes animals: senses such as the sample ChasedSense read it. Override it to return true in a hunting action of your own. IsRelevant(ObservationView) virtual method Directed tests: is this observation relevant for this action (CTRL-10)? For eat, food in sight; for flee, a threat; for rest, any observation (the default). Mates virtual property True for actions that seek a partner: the breed phase breeds animals that chose one (REPRO-02). Overlay virtual property True for an action done in passing (a call, a scent mark): when the brain's draw picks it, the animal also does a second action, the carrier, drawn from the rest of the row; this one adds its interaction only (ACT-07). OverlayTicks virtual property How many ticks an overlay acts, counting the tick of its decision; 0 = until the next decision. Rests virtual property True for actions that rest: the metabolism charges its rest cost, not its base cost, when the animal stays still (05 §4). In EvoSim: BatchProbeAction, DragAction, DrinkAction, EatAction, FeedAction, FleeAction, FollowAction, GoToAction, HideAction, HuntAction, MateAction, OverlayProbeAction, ProbeAction, RestAction. AnimalView AnimalView — class. One animal's view (20 §6): it holds only the animal's id and has no Update; the World places it in LateUpdate and never reads it back (SPACE-12). Member What it does OnShow(Animal) virtual method Called each frame after the World placed the view: change colours or animations from the animal's state here. Read the animal only; a view never writes to the run (SPACE-12). In EvoSim: ActionView, ShowProbeView. BandedSense BandedSense — abstract class. A sense that reports how far the nearest something is, in bands (06 §3): "here" (optional), the bands, "none". Wording (SENSE-10…13): V1 "Food: 1-4 meters away." / V2 "The nearest food is 1-4 meters away.". Member What it does BuildTokens() virtual method Fills and : "here" (optional), one token per band, then "none". Subclasses may add more tokens per band, as does for readiness. HasHere virtual property True when this sense has a "here" token (resources, cover); false by default. HereSentence() virtual method Writes the V2 text of "here". Noun virtual property The noun of V2 texts ("The nearest food is…", "No predator within…"): the Inspector's noun, or the label in lower case. In EvoSim: NearestAnimalSense, NearestCoverSense, NearestEntitySense, NearestResourceSense, NearestWaterSense. BatchedSense BatchedSense — abstract class. A sense that casts rays (line of sight, terrain ahead): it asks for its rays first; the sense phase casts the rays of all deciding animals in one batch, then each sense reads its results (SENSE-30). It must give the same tokens as evaluating it one animal at a time (SENSE-31). Member What it does RequestRays(Animal, RayBatch) abstract method Asks for this animal's rays with ; read their results in Read through . In EvoSim: AllLayersObstacleSense, ObstacleSense. Brain Brain — abstract class. Maps a batch of queries to probability rows over the species' actions (DEC-11). Member What it does Ask(IReadOnlyList<DecisionQuery>) abstract method Answers a batch of queries (DEC-11). Id abstract property A short name of the brain and its settings ("random", "tinynet-8"): part of memo and cache keys, and the name of its answer cache file (DEC-30, DEC-33). Two brains that may answer differently need different ids. AcceptsAttachments virtual property True when queries may carry attachments (SENSE-41); false by default, and then V-51 rejects senses that give them. AnswerInstruction virtual property The answer instruction that ends the prompt, hard-coded per brain because its parsing depends on it (PROMPT-07); empty for brains that read no prompt. CanMixSpecies virtual property True when one batch may hold queries of several species (DEC-13); false gives one batch per species. MaxActions virtual property The most actions a species may have with this brain (DEC-14, V-11); no limit by default. MaxPromptTokens virtual property The longest prompt this brain takes, in estimated tokens (DEC-14, V-11); 0 = no prompt or no limit. Memoizable virtual property True (reference): equal queries get equal rows, so they are memoised and shared within a tick (DEC-30, DEC-32). A brain with memory, or one that learns, says false: every query then reaches it, with its animal's id. Mode virtual property The brain's mode (points, choice…), part of cache keys (DEC-33); empty by default. ModelIdentity virtual property The model and its pinned revision or digest, part of cache keys (DEC-33); the by default. In EvoSim: HttpBrain, JevBrain, MemoryBrain, OllamaPointsBrain, RandomBrain, ScriptedBrain. CapRule CapRule — class. The maximum population of a species (POP-01). Member What it does Cap virtual property The maximum population, in animals (reference prey 270, predators 68; small scenes 40 and 6). CarcassSystem CarcassSystem — class. Carcasses, as each species' edible component describes them: portions, energy, lifetime (03 §3). A carcass of a species is edible when that species' Edible leaves one; diets name it "carcass:<species>". Member What it does Create(Animal, int) virtual method Leaves a carcass at the killed animal's position, if its species' Edible leaves one (ACT-11): portions, energy per portion and lifetime (at least 1 tick) come from that Edible. Cover Cover — abstract class. Places where an animal is hidden from the species that hunt it (03 §2). Member What it does InCover(Vector3) abstract method Checks whether a point is in cover (ENV-10). NearestCover(Vector3, float, Vector3, float) abstract method Finds the nearest point of cover within a radius (ENV-10): the hide action runs to it, the cover sense reports it. Hides(Species, Species) virtual method Whether an animal of hidden standing in cover is hidden from from: the reference hides a species from its threats; kin and its own prey still see it (ENV-11). IsHiddenFrom(Animal, Species) virtual method Whether this animal is hidden from that species right now: its species hides from them and it stands in cover. In EvoSim: CoverLayer, SideCover. Crossover Crossover — abstract class. Builds a baby's genome from its parents', locus by locus (09 §4). Member What it does Cross(Genome, Genome, RandomStream) abstract method The baby's alleles from two parents (GENE-30), drawing from the mutation stream. Copy(Genome) virtual method Asexual reproduction: the baby copies its parent (GENE-31). In EvoSim: CountingCrossover, UniformCrossover. DeathRule DeathRule — abstract class. A cause of death checked in the death phase (ANIM-40): return the cause's name, or null to live on. Member What it does CauseOfDeath(Animal) abstract method The cause of death for this animal now, or null. Causes virtual property The causes this rule can give, for the statistics columns (deaths_<cause>). CheckAll(IReadOnlyList<Animal>, string[]) virtual method The batch entry point (20 §10): writes each animal's cause, or null, into causes. In EvoSim: DiesOfThirst, OldAge, Starvation. DecisionSchedule DecisionSchedule — class. A species' own decision period, and staggering (DEC-04, MAY): an animal decides when (tick + id) % period == 0. Both change behaviour. In the reference scenes every species has one, staggered, with the World's period (owner 2026-10-10); a species without one decides all together, every World period, as the Python prototype does. Member What it does IsDue(Animal, int, World) virtual method Tells whether this animal's periodic decision falls on this tick. Diet Diet — class. What a species eats (SPEC-15): layers, species, "carcass:<species>", "egg:<species>". Each target must carry an Edible (SPEC-10, V-24). A species with no diet eats nothing. Member What it does EatingEggs(Species) virtual method The entry for eating eggs of this species, if listed and the egg kind is edible (REPRO-23); else null. EnergyFrom(Animal, EdibleTarget, float) virtual method The energy a meal gives this eater: the entry's energy by default (ACT-11); override it to depend on the eater. Grazing(ResourceLayer) virtual method The entry for grazing this layer, if the diet lists it and it is edible (SPEC-13); else null. KillChanceAgainst(Animal, Animal) virtual method The chance that this hunter's strike kills that prey (ACT-11): the hunter's kill-chance trait by default. Scavenging(Species) virtual method The entry for scavenging carcasses of this species, if listed and edible; else null. Striking(Species) virtual method The entry for striking this species, if listed and edible (SPEC-13); else null. In EvoSim: SureKillDiet. Digestion Digestion — class. After a kill or a carcass portion the eater is busy digesting for round(digestTicks × gain / killGain) ticks: 50 after a kill (+60), 25 after a portion (+30). Grazing never makes an animal busy (05 §5). Member What it does AfterMeal(Animal, float) virtual method Makes the animal busy for a meal of this energy (ANIM-30, ANIM-31). Energy Energy — class. The energy stat (05 §4): founders and newcomers start at 60, the maximum is 100. Gains are clamped (ANIM-22). Member What it does Gain(Animal, float) virtual method Adds energy from a meal, clamped to the maximum (ANIM-22). Pay(Animal, float) virtual method Removes energy (costs, paying for a litter); it may fall below zero. Entity Entity — abstract class. A world object with a position that is not an animal: a carcass, an egg, a water hole (ENV-20). Member What it does Kind abstract property The entity kind's name, e.g. "carcass". In EvoSim: Carcass, Egg, Fruit. EntityKind EntityKind — abstract class. A kind of entity and its system (ENV-20): carcasses, eggs. Diets name it "<kind>:<species>". Member What it does EntityCount abstract property How many entities the kind holds now, used-up ones not yet removed included. Kind abstract property The kind's name in diet entries, e.g. "carcass" or "egg". UpdateEntities(TickContext) abstract method The environment phase: entities move, rot, and the used-up ones are removed (ENV-21, ENV-22). EntityAt(int) virtual method The i-th living entity, in creation order (views read them; 0 ≤ i < EntityCount), or null if the kind keeps none. In EvoSim: CarcassSystem, EggSystem, EntitySystem<T>, FruitSystem. EntitySystem<T> EntitySystem<T> — abstract class. The entities of one kind, found through spatial queries like animals (ENV-20). Member What it does Move(T, TickContext) virtual method Moves an entity (ENV-21); none by default. OnRemoved(T, string, TickContext) virtual method Called when an entity is removed in the environment phase. In EvoSim: CarcassSystem, EggSystem, FruitSystem. ExerciseOfAttribute ExerciseOfAttribute — attribute. Marks a student class as the exercise version of a reference module (22 §0, the teaching path): EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub swaps the reference for it, keeping the settings; Restore reference undoes it. Gene Gene — abstract class. A gene (locus) of a species: a sentence for the brain or a number for a trait (GENE-01…04). Each animal carries one allele (one value) of every gene of its species. Member What it does Express(AlleleValue, Expression) abstract method Turn this gene's allele into what acts: a prompt line or a trait (GENE-03/04). FounderPool abstract property The founder pool with its origins, neutral allele included (GENE-20). Kind abstract property Whether this gene's alleles are sentences or numbers (GENE-02). Check(AlleleValue) virtual method Values allowed for this gene, e.g. the mutation guards for sentences (GENE-22). Decimals virtual property Precision used to compare number alleles (GENE-10), in decimals; reference 4. MayMutate(Allele) virtual method Whether this allele may mutate (the neutral allele's setting, MUT-22). ReadByBrain virtual property Whether the brain reads this gene (text genes; number genes only if configured, GENE-04). In EvoSim: NumberGene, TextGene. Ground Ground — abstract class. Answers, for any point, its height and whether it is walkable (SPACE-04), inside a bounded rectangle with hard borders (SPACE-03). Member What it does Bounds abstract property The world rectangle on the horizontal plane: x is world x, y is world z. Half-open [min, max). Height(Vector3) abstract method The ground's height under a point (SPACE-06). IsWalkable(Vector3) abstract method Whether an animal may stand here; false outside the rectangle (SPACE-04). Distance(Vector3, Vector3) virtual method The world distance: horizontal Euclidean in the reference. Override for path length (SPACE-02). IsWater(Vector3) virtual method Whether a point is water (terrain grounds; never on flat ground). NearestWater(Vector3, float) virtual method The nearest water within radius, with a walkable shore point next to it (22 §2); null if none. RandomWalkable(RandomStream) virtual method A uniformly random walkable point (founders, newcomers; POP-03, POP-04). extending/genes.html.title: Genes | EvoSim
extending/genes.html.summary: Genes Three changes need no code: a free text gene (a temperament the brain reads), a number gene that lets evolution tune a trait, and a shared allele pool of founder sentences. Write a gene kind only when a value must be stored or expressed in a new way: a number the brain reads as words, a choice among a few options, the weights of a small network (GENE-07). How genes work is explained in Genes and mutation. A free text gene A free gene belongs to no action; it appears in the genes block under its own label. Under the species, outside its Actions group (a Genes group is a good place), create an object named temperament and add a Text Gene. Tick Free. Leave Label empty to use the object's name. Leave Pool empty and fill Founders: "Be bold.", "Be careful.". Keep Has Neutral: the pool also gets "No preference.". Press Play. The species inspector's Genes foldout lists prey.temperament, and its Prompt preview shows the line - temperament: "Be bold." in the genes block. The species' LlmMutation (with an empty Only These) mutates it like any other text gene. A text gene that is neither under an action nor free is treated as free, with a warning (V-06). Adding a gene changes the species' signature (SPEC-03): accept the new one with the fix V-12 offers. A number gene A NumberGene sets one trait at birth, and a GaussianMutation moves it a little at each mutation. Select the species and choose GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Gene ▸ Stamina gene. You get a StaminaGene object in the species' Genes group, with a Number Gene labelled stamina (Trait stamina.max, Min 20, Max 120, Founders 45, 60, 75) and a Gaussian Mutation (Sigma 5). For another trait, change Trait to a name a module of the species declares: the inspector's Stats and traits foldout lists them (stamina.max, stamina.regen, speed.walk, speed.run, vision, maturity…). Tick Multiply Default to scale the trait's default instead of replacing it: a speed.run gene with range 0.8 to 1.2 and founders 0.9, 1, 1.1 makes some animals 10 % faster. Set Sigma in the gene's own unit. A Gaussian Mutation with an empty Only These is the species' default for every number gene; for a gene on another scale, add a second Gaussian Mutation and list the gene in its Only These (MUT-02). Give the trait a cost, or the gene drifts to whichever end helps (09 §5, V-47): on the species' Metabolism, set Cost Trait to stamina.max and Cost Per Unit to 0.005, so that 60 stamina costs 0.3 energy a tick. GaussianMutation accepts any number gene that implements INumberRange (Min and Max), so your own number gene kinds work with it too. An allele pool An AllelePool is an asset of founder and contrast sentences that several text genes share, for example the same follow sentences in two species. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Allele Pool. Fill Founders (at most 12 words each, plain words, no numbers), and Contrast Pro and Contrast Anti, the two sentences brain tests use (GENE-23). Drag the asset into the Pool field of each text gene. Its founders replace the gene's own list; its contrast sentences do too, when not empty. The neutral allele stays a setting of each gene. The reference pools are in Assets/EvoSim/Data/AllelePools (prey_eat.asset…). Founder pools are frozen for an experiment (GENE-21): changing one starts a new experiment, and its new sentences make new prompts that the brain and mutator caches have never seen. A new gene kind Derive from Gene. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Gene kind writes a number gene template into Assets/Student, with a test in Assets/Student/Tests. Member What it does, and when it is called Kind must implement Text or Number. It decides which operators accept the gene: LlmMutation takes text, GaussianMutation takes numbers with a range. FounderPool must implement The values founders draw from, each with its origin (founder, neutral). Read at the start of the run, registered before anything else. Express must implement Turns a value into a trait (e.SetTrait) or a genes-block line (e.PromptGene). Called at birth, and each time a decision's prompt is written. ReadByBrain may override True: the gene enters the genes block and the brain key. Default: text genes only. Check may override Why a value is not allowed, or null. Every mutant is checked at hatching, whatever made it. Decimals may override The precision at which two numbers are the same allele (default 4). MayMutate may override False keeps an allele from mutating, as TextGene does for the neutral allele (MUT-22). Initialize, Validate may override Reset caches; report bad settings before the run. A complete example: a number in [0, 1] that the brain reads as a word. using System.Collections.Generic; using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; /// <summary>A boldness in [0, 1] that the brain reads as "Be careful.", "Be balanced." or "Be bold.".</summary> public class BoldnessGene : Gene, INumberRange { [SerializeField, Tooltip("Founder values, in [0, 1].")] List<float> founders = new List<float> { 0.2f, 0.5f, 0.8f }; public float Min => 0f; public float Max => 1f; public override AlleleKind Kind => AlleleKind.Number; public override bool ReadByBrain => true; // it enters the genes block public override int Decimals => 2; // 0.501 and 0.502 are one allele public override IReadOnlyList<FounderAllele> FounderPool { get { var pool = new List<FounderAllele>(); foreach (var f in founders) pool.Add(new FounderAllele(AlleleValue.OfNumber(f), "founder")); return pool; } } public override void Express(AlleleValue value, Expression e) => e.PromptGene(Label, value.Number < 0.33f ? "Be careful." : value.Number < 0.67f ? "Be balanced." : "Be bold."); public override string Check(AlleleValue value) => value.Number < Min || value.Number > Max ? $"{value.Number} outside [0, 1]" : null; } Add the component under the species, on an object named boldness: its label, and so its locus id prey.boldness, comes from the object's name unless you set Label. A Gaussian Mutation with Sigma 5 would throw the value to 0 or 1 at every mutation, so add a Gaussian Mutation with Sigma 0.1 and list this gene in its Only These. Only TextGene and its subclasses are bound to actions. To make a text gene kind that binds, derive from TextGene; a text kind derived from Gene should return SentenceGuards.Check(value.Text) from Check. Rules your gene kind keeps Settings only. One component serves every animal of the species: nothing per animal in its fields. A frozen pool (GENE-21). FounderPool returns the same values in the same order in every run, built from the settings alone. It is never empty: the reference kinds report an empty pool as V-41 in Validate; do the same. Express through the expression only (GENE-03, GENE-04). It runs at birth with an animal, and for prompts without one: change nothing else, draw no random number, give the same output for the same value. Check is the contract with every operator. A mutant it refuses leaves the inherited allele (MUT-04). Text founders and mutants pass the sentence guards (GENE-22). A label unique in the species, so the locus id is unique in the world (GENE-11). Test it There is no conformance suite for gene kinds, but the operators' suite (T-MUT) mutates a number gene and a text gene and checks the results against the gene's Check. Test your expression the way T-GENE-01 does: using System.Collections.Generic; using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; public class BoldnessGeneTests : WorldFixture { [Test] public void BoldValuesSayBeBold() { var w = New().Flat(20, 20).Species("prey", s => s.Population(2).Action<RestAction>("rest").Module<BoldnessGene>()).Build(); var sp = w.FindSpecies("prey"); var lines = new List<KeyValuePair<string, string>>(); sp.Module<BoldnessGene>().Express(AlleleValue.OfNumber(0.9f), new Expression(null, sp.Declarations, lines)); Assert.AreEqual("Be bold.", lines[0].Value); } } See Testing your module for the test assembly and the runner. Read next The reference kinds: TextGene and NumberGene; the API: Expression, AlleleValue, SentenceGuards. How your gene's values change: Mutation. The contract: 09 — Genes, alleles and genomes.

extending/http-brains.html.title: An HTTP brain or mutator server | EvoSim
extending/http-brains.html.summary: An HTTP brain or mutator server Derive from HttpBrain to decide with a model behind a web API: a chat server, a classifier, a service of your own. The base class sends the requests off the main thread, with time-outs, retries and a cap on parallel requests; you only build each request and read each answer. A brain that needs no server is a plain Brain (A brain). To mutate genes with another server, derive from HttpMutatorClient; for a mutator without a server, from MutatorClient. The reference servers Component Server Default Host Calls Reference settings JevBrain vLLM serving JEV-9B with its LoRA module jev-decision http://localhost:8000 POST /v1/completions, GET /v1/models time-out 60 s, 4 in flight, 64 texts per request OllamaPointsBrain Ollama http://localhost:11434 POST /api/chat, GET /api/tags gemma4:12b, context 4 096 tokens, seed 0, 2 in flight OllamaMutatorClient Ollama, the model on the CPU http://localhost:11434 POST /api/chat, GET /api/tags the mutator service's model (gemma4:26b, temperature 1.2), context 1 024 tokens, 2 in flight OpenAIMutatorClient an OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM) http://localhost:8001 POST /v1/chat/completions, GET /v1/models answers of at most 64 tokens, thinking off The GET path is the connection test: Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Brain Health has a Test connection button for each brain and mutator client (V-60), and shows their tries, failures and latencies during a run. Client settings Every HTTP brain and mutator client has these Inspector fields; HttpCaller applies them to each request. Field What it does HTTP brains Mutator clients Host the server's address see above see above Api Key Variable the name of the environment variable that holds the API key; empty for none empty empty Timeout Seconds the time-out of one try, in seconds 120 (JEV 60) 60 Tries tries per request, 1 to 10 3 3 Backoff Seconds the wait before the second try; the waits between tries are Backoff × 1, 2, 4… 1 1 Max Parallel requests in flight at once; the others wait their turn 4 (Ollama brain 2) 2 A try that times out, gets no answer, or gets the status 408, 429 or 5xx is tried again after its wait: with the reference values, 1 s then 2 s. Any other error status fails at once. A request that still fails after its last try fails its query (DEC-42). An HTTP brain Step Thread Done by The Ask brains phase sends the queries the memo and the cache can't answer, one batch per brain (DEC-15) main the World Each query becomes a BrainRequest: index, text, action names main Ask, your TextFor The requests are posted, the answers read, each row set or failed thread pool your AnswerAsync The answer is completed; a request left without a row fails thread pool HttpBrain The tick waits (Freeze blocks the main thread, Responsive keeps Unity drawing, SPACE-14), stores the rows in the memo and the cache, draws the actions main the Choose actions phase What you write and what you use: Member You What it does, when it is called AnswerAsync must implement Once per batch, on the thread pool. Post with c.PostAsync, then call answer.SetRow(r.Index, row) or answer.Fail(r.Index, reason) for every request. Don't call Complete HealthPath must implement the path the connection test reads Id must implement the brain's name in memo and cache keys ModelIdentity, Mode should override the model and how you use it: part of the cache key (below) AnswerInstruction may override the prompt's last line, fixed by the brain because its parsing depends on it (PROMPT-07) TextFor may override the text sent for a query, built on the main thread; by default the full prompt MaxActions, MaxPromptTokens, CanMixSpecies; Initialize, Begin, Validate may override (call the base for the last three) limits checked before the run (DEC-13, DEC-14); the base drops its client at Initialize and checks Host (V-20) and keys (V-61) Caller, Stats, Transport, ConfigureClient use the client, its counts, a fake server for tests, the settings from code To make a row, use PointsAnswer for points answers (DEC-41), or Brain.Normalize for any non-negative weights. Example: points from an OpenAI-compatible server A brain modelled on OllamaPointsBrain, for a server such as llama.cpp (port 8080) or vLLM: using System; using System.Collections.Generic; using System.Threading.Tasks; using EvoSim; using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq; using UnityEngine; /// <summary>Points mode on an OpenAI-compatible server: one chat call per query.</summary> public class ChatPointsBrain : HttpBrain { [SerializeField, Tooltip("The model's name on the server.")] string model = "my-model"; public ChatPointsBrain() { host = "http://localhost:8080"; maxParallel = 2; } public override string Id => "chat-points"; public override string Mode => "points-v1"; public override string ModelIdentity => model; public override string AnswerInstruction => OllamaPointsBrain.Instruction; protected override string HealthPath => "/v1/models"; protected override async Task AnswerAsync(HttpCaller c, IReadOnlyList<BrainRequest> requests, BrainAnswer answer) { var calls = new List<Task>(requests.Count); foreach (var r in requests) calls.Add(One(c, r, answer)); await Task.WhenAll(calls).ConfigureAwait(false); } async Task One(HttpCaller c, BrainRequest r, BrainAnswer answer) { try { var body = new JObject { ["model"] = model, ["temperature"] = 0, ["seed"] = 0, ["messages"] = new JArray(new JObject { ["role"] = "user", ["content"] = r.Text }), ["response_format"] = new JObject { ["type"] = "json_object" }, }; var response = await c.PostAsync("/v1/chat/completions", body).ConfigureAwait(false); var row = PointsAnswer.ToRow((string)response["choices"]?[0]?["message"]?["content"], r.Actions, out var problem); if (row == null) answer.Fail(r.Index, problem); else answer.SetRow(r.Index, row); } catch (Exception e) { answer.Fail(r.Index, e.Message); } } } Put the file in Assets/Student: Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Brain writes a plain brain and its test there; change its base class to HttpBrain. Add the component to a GameObject under the World's Brains object, then pick it in a species' Brain field or the World's Default Brain. The cache key The answer cache replays rows without calling the model (DEC-33). Its key (AnswerCache.KeyFor) joins the brain's Id, ModelIdentity and Mode with the prompt's id, the text style, the genes and the situation. So ModelIdentity must change with the model: give its name and its revision or digest when the server tells them (JEV: autotrust/JEV-9B@b63f651ce8ed:jev-decision; Ollama: gemma4:12b@<digest>). Mode must change when you change how a prompt becomes a request or an answer a row: put a version in it (points-v1). Anything that changes answers and is missing from the key makes a replay return old answers. Strict by default, keys from the environment An HTTP brain starts with Strict and Use Cache on. When a query still fails after its tries, a strict brain stops the run cleanly: every file is written and the run can be resumed (DEC-40). With Strict off, the query gets a uniform row instead, counted as a failure and never cached (DEC-34). Never type an API key in the Inspector. Put it in an environment variable of the environment Unity (or the player) starts from, and write the variable's name in Api Key Variable, for example OLLAMA_API_KEY. The key is read at each call and sent as a bearer token; it is never stored, logged or written (OUT-04). Validation reports any serialized field that looks like a key (V-61). A mutator client The MutatorService sends each round of mutation prompts that its cache can't answer to the World's mutator client, then checks and caches the answers (MUT-14).
