An HttpMutatorClient posts one chat call per prompt from the thread pool; Body and Content run there. Member You What it does ChatPath, HealthPath must implement the chat path and the connection test's path Body must implement the request body for one MutatorRequest: its Prompt, Model, Seed, Temperature Content must implement the answer text in a response, or null: the request then fails ModelIdentity should override the model, recorded with every mutant allele (GENE-12) UserMessage use the messages array: the prompt as the only user message The body carries the prompt and nothing else (CORE-07, MUT-11): one user message, no system message, nothing about the animal. Send the request's own seed and temperature: the cache's key holds them (MUT-14). The integrity check B-11 reads the bodies a real run sends and accepts only model, messages, seed, temperature, max_tokens, options, stream, think and chat_template_kwargs. using EvoSim; using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq; /// <summary>A mutator behind a llama.cpp server (OpenAI-style chat).</summary> public class LlamaCppMutatorClient : HttpMutatorClient { public LlamaCppMutatorClient() { host = "http://localhost:8080"; } public override string ModelIdentity => World != null && World.Service<MutatorService>() != null ? World.Service<MutatorService>().Model : ""; protected override string ChatPath => "/v1/chat/completions"; protected override string HealthPath => "/health"; public override JObject Body(MutatorRequest r) => new JObject { ["model"] = r.Model, ["messages"] = UserMessage(r.Prompt), ["max_tokens"] = 64, ["seed"] = r.Seed, ["temperature"] = HttpCaller.Number(r.Temperature), }; protected override string Content(JToken response) => (string)response["choices"]?[0]?["message"]?["content"]; } In the reference scenes the client sits on the Mutator client GameObject under the World's Brains object, next to the Mutator service: put yours there in place of OllamaMutatorClient. The model's name and the temperature are the service's fields. A mutator without a server derives from MutatorClient: its Send returns a MutatorReply filled with SetAnswer or Fail, then Complete. Read FakeMutator. Rules your brain or client must keep No Unity object off the main thread: read Unity objects in TextFor or Initialize, keep plain values. Await with ConfigureAwait(false): in Freeze mode an await that needs the main thread never resumes. A row or a failure for every request (DEC-11): one entry per action, in action order, each ≥ 0, summing to 1. The same query gives the same row (DEC-12): temperature 0 and a fixed seed. Keys only from the environment (OUT-04), a complete cache key (DEC-33), a blind mutator (CORE-07). Test it Tests never call a model: they give the brain a FakeHttpTransport through Transport. Its Respond function answers each request; FailWith, Hang and DelayMs make it fail, time out or answer late; Requests and MaxInFlight show what it received. using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Testing; using Newtonsoft.Json.Linq; using NUnit.Framework; public class ChatPointsBrainTests : WorldFixture { [Test] public void AnswersFromAFakeServer() { var choice = new JObject { ["message"] = new JObject { ["content"] = "{\"eat\": 80, \"flee\": 20}" } }; var fake = new FakeHttpTransport { Respond = (method, path, body) => new JObject { ["choices"] = new JArray(choice) } }; var w = New().Lab1(prey: 6, predators: 2, randomBrain: false) .DefaultBrain<ChatPointsBrain>(b => { b.Transport = fake; b.ConfigureClient("http://fake.test", 5f, 1, 0f, 2); }) .Build(); w.Advance(8); Assert.AreEqual(8, w.Tick, "no failure stopped the strict brain"); Assert.Greater(fake.Count, 0, "the brain called its server"); } } The test uses Newtonsoft's JObject: add Newtonsoft.Json.dll to the Assembly References of Assets/Student/Tests/Student.Tests.asmdef. More in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Http: HttpBrainTests.cs (formats, retries, time-outs, strict stops, the cache, both wait modes) and HttpMutatorTests.cs. Read next OllamaPointsBrain, then JevBrain (batched requests, log-probabilities); OllamaMutatorClient, OpenAIMutatorClient; A brain, Mutation, Decisions and brains; the specification's 08 — Decisions, brains and prompts and 10 — Mutation.

extending/index.html.title: Extending EvoSim | EvoSim
extending/index.html.summary: Extending EvoSim Everything in EvoSim is a component you can add, remove, replace or subclass: senses, actions, genes, stats, death rules, mutation operators, brains, tick phases, food layers, cover, ground. The reference modules are written exactly like yours: they derive from the same public base classes and use no hidden shortcut. Any of them is a working example of its kind, and any of them can be replaced by your own. The workflow Write a class. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ writes a template for a Sense, an Action, a Gene kind, a Stat, a Phase, a Brain or a Mutation operator into Assets/Student, together with a test in Assets/Student/Tests. For other kinds, derive from the base class named in the table below. Place the component. A module under a species belongs to that species. A phase or a service sits under the World, outside any species. Order matters only among modules of the same kind: the n-th action found, depth first, is action n. See Species modules and Phases, services and world hooks. Press Play. The World discovers your component, sets it up in its fixed order, and validates the tree. If something is missing, a message names the object to fix. Test it. Your sense, action, stat, layer, mutation operator, phase or locomotion runs through the conformance suite of its kind: Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode. A brain gets a test to copy instead. See Testing your module. I want to… I want to… Use Code? Page tell the brain something new about the situation a Sense (distance bands: BandedSense; raycasts: BatchedSense) yes A sense give animals a new behaviour to choose an AnimalAction, with a text gene to steer it yes An action make something happen when an animal reaches its target an IInteraction yes An action change how a species moves (slopes, mud, paths) a Locomotion subclass yes A locomotion add a stat (thirst, fear, temperature) a SpeciesModule that declares it yes Stats, costs and death rules change what living costs per tick Metabolism (settings, or a subclass) maybe Stats, costs and death rules add a cause of death a DeathRule yes Stats, costs and death rules give a species a temperament that is not tied to one action a free TextGene no Genes let evolution tune a number (stamina, speed, vision) a NumberGene and a GaussianMutation no Genes invent a new kind of gene a Gene subclass yes Genes change how gene sentences mutate a mutation deck, or a MutationOperator maybe Mutation change how parents' genes mix, litter sizes, who mates Crossover, Litter, MatingRule maybe Reproduction and population lay eggs that hatch later, cap or prop up a population Incubation, CapRule, FloorRule no Reproduction and population decide at other moments, or stagger decisions a DecisionSchedule on the species no A brain decide with rules, a small network or another model a Brain yes A brain use a model behind a web API, or another mutator server an HttpBrain, a MutatorClient yes An HTTP brain or mutator server run something every tick (seasons, weather, events) a TickPhase yes Phases, services and world hooks share state or a query between modules a WorldService yes Phases, services and world hooks react to every birth and death OnBorn and OnDied on any module yes Phases, services and world hooks set worlds up from code before they start the Configuring event yes Phases, services and world hooks add a food source (berries, water) a ResourceLayer yes Food, cover, entities and ground add hiding places a Cover yes Food, cover, entities and ground add objects that live in the world (fruit, nests) an EntitySystem<T> of your Entity yes Food, cover, entities and ground make something edible, or change who eats whom Edible and Diet no Food, cover, entities and ground change what the ground allows a Ground yes Food, cover, entities and ground add a species duplicate one and change it; subclass Species only for hooks no Species modules record more numbers or events IStatsColumns, IEventSink, World.RecordDeath yes Recording and statistics colour or animate the animals an AnimalView on a body prefab yes Views say that your module needs another one [RequiresModule(typeof(…))] yes Species modules catch configuration mistakes before Play Validate(ValidationReport) and a ValidationFix yes Species modules add your own editor window or inspector Unity's editor API, reading the World yes The editor Every abstract and virtual member of every public type is listed in Every extension point, generated from the code. Five rules every module keeps Draw random numbers only from the stream you are given (a RandomStream), never from UnityEngine.Random, System.Random or the clock. Otherwise a seed no longer replays the run (RAND-01). Never decide by iterating a Dictionary or a HashSet: their order is not fixed. Iterate lists (RAND-05). Keep settings in the module and state in the animal. One module serves every animal of its species. What belongs to one animal goes in its stats, through the ids your module declared. Each kind of module does its own job. Senses only read. Actions only say where to go and what to do on arrival; the act phase moves the animal. Phases change the world. Views only display (SPACE-12). Set up in Initialize, not in Awake or Start. The World calls its modules in a fixed order (ARCH-04). Tip The fastest way in is to rewrite a reference module from its stub: the teaching path. The samples (thirst, water, seasons, slopes…) show complete extensions working together. Worked example: alarm calls follows one student change, a sense, an action, a gene and a world service, from the idea to a tested scene.

extending/locomotion.html.title: A locomotion | EvoSim
extending/locomotion.html.summary: A locomotion A locomotion decides how a species moves: an action only says where the animal wants to go (an Intent), and the locomotion turns that into a movement over the ground (MOVE-01). Write one to make movement depend on the terrain (slopes, mud, water), to follow paths around obstacles, or to charge extra energy for some moves. To change where animals may stand at all, change the ground instead. How movement fits in the tick is explained in Actions and movement. The base class Derive from Locomotion, or from the reference KinematicLocomotion to keep its straight lines, sliding and side steps and change only part of them. Member You What it does, when it is called Move must implement Moves one animal for this tick, sets its Position and returns the meters actually moved (MOVE-06). Called in the act phase, after the action planned, for animals whose intent moves. ExtraCost may override Extra energy for a move from one point to another (slopes, mud). Called after the animal moved more than 1 mm; the metabolism adds it to the tick's cost. 0 in the reference. MoveAll may override Moves a group of animals at once (20 §10). The default calls Move for each with its stamina budget. Declare(SpeciesBuilder) inherited Declares the traits speed.walk and speed.run. If you override it, call base.Declare(b). WritePromptRules, Validate inherited Write the Prompt Rule line; check Wander Turn P (V-35). WalkSpeed, RunSpeed read The speed traits, in meters per tick: read them with a.Trait(WalkSpeed). walkSpeed, runSpeed, wanderTurnP, promptRule protected The Inspector settings: Walk Speed, Run Speed, Wander Turn P, Prompt Rule. What Move receives The intent says what the action wants: Member Meaning Direction a unit vector on the horizontal plane; zero for a stay Run true to run (RunSpeed), false to walk (WalkSpeed) MaxDistance the farthest to go this tick, in meters, so a stop distance is never overshot; infinity for "as far as you can" Target the point the action is heading to (or running away from) Wandering true for a wandering intent IsStay, Stay() whether it moves at all; the same intent turned into a stay, to refuse a move The stamina budget is the most the animal may move this tick, in meters: its stamina, or infinity for a species without a stamina module (ANIM-21). The move context (MoveContext) gives Ground (heights, walkable points, SlideTo, SideStep, SlopeDegrees), Distance(a, b) (the world distance, SPACE-02), Stream(species, purpose) (a random stream), StaminaBudget(a), World and Tick. A complete example The sample SlopeLocomotion (Assets/EvoSim/Samples/SlopeLocomotion.cs, recipe 22 §14) refuses ground steeper than a limit and charges energy for every meter climbed. It changes the intent, then lets the kinematic locomotion do the moving. public class SlopeLocomotion : KinematicLocomotion { [SerializeField, Range(0f, 90f), Tooltip("Steeper ground is refused, in degrees (reference 35).")] float maxSlopeDegrees = 35f; [SerializeField, Min(0f), Tooltip("Energy per meter climbed (reference 0.3).")] float energyPerMeterClimbed = 0.3f; public override float Move(Animal a, Intent intent, float staminaBudget, MoveContext c) { if (!intent.IsStay && c.Ground != null) { Vector3 ahead = a.Position + intent.Direction; if (c.Ground.SlopeDegrees(a.Position, ahead) > maxSlopeDegrees) intent = intent.Stay(); // too steep: don't go } return base.Move(a, intent, staminaBudget, c); } public override float ExtraCost(Animal a, Vector3 from, Vector3 to) => Mathf.Max(0f, to.y - from.y) * energyPerMeterClimbed; // downhill is free } The reference KinematicLocomotion itself moves by the smallest of speed, stamina budget and MaxDistance; Ground.SlideTo slides along borders and obstacles; with no progress, Ground.SideStep takes a random step drawn from c.Stream(Species, "actions"). Where to put it Write the class in Assets/Student. There is no script template for a locomotion: start from the example above, or from the stub of exercise 11 (EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub ▸ 11 KinematicLocomotion). On the species' Locomotion child, replace the KinematicLocomotion component by yours and set its speeds. A species has exactly one locomotion (V-13); with none, validation offers to add a kinematic one. Each species can have its own: give the predator a slope locomotion and leave the prey kinematic, and they move differently over the same terrain. Slopes only matter on a ground with heights, such as the terrain ground. Rules Whatever Move does is the tick's result (MOVE-01). Change only the moved animal's Position; the act phase sets its heading afterwards. Never end on non-walkable ground or outside the world (MOVE-02). Use Ground.SlideTo, or check Ground.Clear and Ground.IsWalkable. If you don't, the act phase moves the animal back and logs a warning. Never move more than the stamina budget (ANIM-21), nor more than MaxDistance (MOVE-04). Read speeds from the animal's traits, a.Trait(WalkSpeed), never from the settings (MOVE-03, ANIM-16), so a number gene can change them. Return the meters actually moved, measured with c.Distance (MOVE-06). The metabolism and the stamina charge exactly that. ExtraCost returns 0 or more. Draw random numbers only from c.Stream(Species, ...) (RAND-03), so a seed replays the run. An override of MoveAll must give the same result as calling Move for each animal in order. Test it The conformance suite runs every locomotion class in the project: Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode, ConformanceTests ▸ LocomotionConformance, one case per class (the T-MOVE template). Eight walkers on a 20 × 20 m ground start on a circle of 8 m around a pond of radius 3 m and walk toward its centre for 30 ticks. The suite checks that: no walker ever ends a tick on water or outside the world (MOVE-02); the meters reported are the distance actually moved (MOVE-06); no walker stays stuck for more than 3 ticks away from the shore (MOVE-04); ExtraCost is never negative. A test to copy: SlopeLocomotion in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Samples/SampleTests.cs, which walks an animal up a ramp and checks where it stops and what climbing costs. See Testing your module. Read next KinematicLocomotion (exercise 11 of the teaching path) and the sample SlopeLocomotion. Ground: what is walkable, SlideTo, SideStep, SlopeDegrees; see Food, cover, entities and ground. Stats, costs and death rules: how the meters you report are charged. Specification: 07 §2, in 07 — Actions and locomotion.

extending/mutation.html.title: Mutation | EvoSim
extending/mutation.html.summary: Mutation There are three ways to change how genes mutate: a mutation deck, to change what the mutator model is asked to do with a sentence (no code); a mutation operator, to change how values change: a rule without a model, a new number rule, your own model; a mutator client, to send the same prompts to another server: see An HTTP brain or mutator server. How mutation works from conception to hatching is explained in Genes and mutation. A mutation deck The deck is the list of instructions the LlmMutation draws from. Each mutation draws one per try and sends it to the mutator with the sentence. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Mutation Deck asks where to save a .txt file and writes a copy of the reference deck mutate_v4.txt into it. Edit it: one instruction per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored (MUT-10). Short instructions about the rule work best, such as "Change when this rule applies.". Drag the file into the Deck field of the species' Llm Mutation (in the reference scenes, on the species' Mutation object). The same component has three more fields: Context Line, the one fixed line before the instruction (no line break, no {: V-49); Tries, 5 instructions and seeds per mutation before the gene stays unchanged; Max Words, 12, the longest mutant (a text gene's own Max Words wins when smaller). Note A mutant records its instruction's index in the deck (llm#3, and "prompt": 3 in the birth event). Reordering the lines changes what those numbers mean. New instructions make new prompts, which the answer cache has never seen. A mutation operator Derive from MutationOperator. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Mutation operator writes a template into Assets/Student (a number operator that adds ±1), with a test in Assets/Student/Tests. Member What it does, and when it is called Accepts must implement Whether it can change this gene, usually by its Kind. Asked for each locus at each conception (MUT-02), and by the validator (V-48). StartMutation must implement Draws every random choice from rng, then returns a job. Called in the breed phase, once per mutating locus of each baby. UsesMutatorService may override True when the work goes to the MutatorService (see below). Validate may override Call base.Validate(report) first: it checks the rate (V-35). Rate, Only These Inspector The probability per gene per baby (reference 0.03); the genes it is configured for. StartMutation returns a MutationJob: Factory Use it when MutationJob.Done(text, op), Done(number, op) the new value is ready at once; op is the short detail recorded with the allele, e.g. ladder+1 MutationJob.Failed(reason) there is nothing to change: the gene keeps its allele (MUT-04) MutationJob.Running(pending) the work goes on in the background (see below) A complete example, the sample Assets/EvoSim/Samples/IntensityLadder.cs (IntensityLadder): it moves the sentence's intensity word one step along a ladder, without any model (MUT-21). using System; using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; public class IntensityLadder : MutationOperator { static readonly string[] Ladder = { "never", "rarely", "sometimes", "often", "always" }; public override bool Accepts(Gene g) => g.Kind == AlleleKind.Text; public override MutationJob StartMutation(Gene g, Allele parent, RandomStream rng) { var words = parent.Text.Split(' '); int i = -1, k = -1; for (int w = 0; w < words.Length && i < 0; w++) { k = Array.IndexOf(Ladder, words[w].ToLowerInvariant().Trim('.', ',', '!', '?', ';', ':')); if (k >= 0) i = w; } if (i < 0) return MutationJob.Failed("no intensity word"); int step = rng.NextBool() ? 1 : -1; string next = Ladder[Mathf.Clamp(k + step, 0, Ladder.Length - 1)]; string original = words[i]; string trail = original.Substring(original.TrimEnd('.', ',', '!', '?', ';', ':').Length); if (char.IsUpper(original[0])) next = char.ToUpperInvariant(next[0]) + next.Substring(1); words[i] = next + trail; return MutationJob.Done(string.Join(" ", words), step > 0 ? "ladder+1" : "ladder-1"); } } Put the component under the species, for example on its Mutation object, and list the genes it should mutate in its Only These. Exactly one operator applies to a locus (MUT-02): the first that accepts the gene and lists it, else the first that accepts it and lists no gene. With an empty Only These next to the reference LlmMutation, the one found first in the hierarchy would be the default for every text gene. Rules your operator keeps Blind (CORE-07). It reads the gene's settings and the parent allele, nothing else: no animal, no other gene, no world state, no clock. Selection alone decides what is good. Draw now, from the given stream (MUT-30). Every random choice comes from rng, inside StartMutation, as many draws whatever happens later. The same stream state gives the same job, so a seed replays the run. Guards hold. At hatching the gene's Check judges every result: a refused value (a 13-word sentence, a number outside the range) leaves the inherited allele and counts as not allowed. A result equal to the parent counts as unchanged (MUT-04). A stable operator detail. The op string is recorded with every mutant (GENE-12): keep it short and meaningful. An asynchronous operator A model takes time to answer. A job may finish after StartMutation returns: the egg then waits until its genome is complete (MUT-32). Through the mutator service. The World's MutatorService sends prompts to the mutator server in batches, caches the answers, cleans and checks them (MUT-12) and redraws rejected ones (MUT-13). Draw each try's instruction and seed, then Submit them. Return true from UsesMutatorService, so the client records the model's identity in the run info. using System.Collections.Generic; using EvoSim; public class OppositeMutation : MutationOperator { static readonly List<string> Deck = new List<string> { "Make this rule say the opposite." }; public override bool Accepts(Gene g) => g.Kind == AlleleKind.Text; public override bool UsesMutatorService => true; public override MutationJob StartMutation(Gene gene, Allele parent, RandomStream rng) { var instruction = new int[3]; // every try uses instruction 0 var seeds = new long[3]; for (int i = 0; i < 3; i++) seeds[i] = rng.NextUInt() & 0x7FFFFFFF; // drawn now, used or not (MUT-30) var service = World.Service<MutatorService>(); if (service == null) return MutationJob.Failed("no mutator"); return service.Submit(parent.Text, instruction, seeds, "The sentence below is a rule that a wild animal follows.", Deck, 12); } } With your own background work. Return MutationJob.Running with a Pending that tells when the work is done, and complete or fail the job as the work's last step: public override MutationJob StartMutation(Gene gene, Allele parent, RandomStream rng) { bool up = rng.NextBool(); // every draw now, on the main thread (MUT-30) string text = parent.Text; // copy what the work needs: no Unity object in the task var job = MutationJob.Running(null); job.Pending = Pending.Of(System.Threading.Tasks.Task.Run(() => { string mutant = text.Replace("often", up ? "always" : "rarely"); // stands for slow work if (mutant == text) job.Fail("no often"); else job.Complete(AlleleValue.OfText(mutant), up ? "often+1" : "often-1"); })); return job; } The result must depend only on the parent and the draws, never on timing: then the Freeze and Responsive wait modes, and a replay, give the same genes. Never touch Unity objects or the world from the background thread. Test it Your operator enters the T-MUT conformance suite by itself (Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode, ConformanceTests ▸ MutationOperatorConformance). It mutates a text gene and a number gene twice with the same seed and checks that the operator accepts at least one of them, that both jobs finish with the same outcome and the same value, and that the value passes the gene's Check. For a test of your own, copy IntensityLadderSteps in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Samples/SampleTests.cs; see Testing your module. Read next The reference operators: LlmMutation, GaussianMutation; rewrite LlmMutation from its stub in the teaching path. The prompt, cleaning and guards as pure functions: MutationText, SentenceGuards. New kinds of values to mutate: Genes. Another server: An HTTP brain or mutator server. The contract: 10 — Mutation.

extending/recording.html.title: Recording and statistics | EvoSim
extending/recording.html.summary: Recording and statistics Your module can leave four kinds of trace in a run's files (Recording and outputs): statistics columns, numbers over time in stats.csv: implement IStatsColumns; causes of death, each with its own deaths_<cause> column: World.RecordDeath, or a DeathRule; events of your own in events.jsonl, one per occurrence, part of the run's history and of its hash: a SimEvent; listeners that see every event as it is recorded, without changing anything: an IEventSink. Use a column for a quantity you want to plot, an event for something that happens and must be traceable later. Statistics columns IStatsColumns has two members: Member What it does, when it is called StatColumns the column names, without the species prefix, always in the same order StatValue one column's value now; called by the RunRecorder for every row, at the end of the record phase, every Stats Every ticks (100) Where the columns go depends on what implements it: Implemented on Columns Values a SpeciesModule in the species' block, after its act_<action> columns, prefixed: mean_age becomes prey_mean_age that species' a TickPhase or a WorldService at the end of the row, unprefixed (phases first) the world's Name columns in lower case with underscores, like the built-in ones. A name already in the row is skipped. Values are written with at most 4 decimals. A column that appears during the run rewrites the file's header, with empty cells in the rows before it. StatValue only reads: it must not change the world, record events or draw random numbers. A column never changes the run or its hash. Example: the mean age using System.Collections.Generic; using EvoSim; // Adds the column <species>_mean_age to stats.csv: the mean age of the living animals, in ticks. public class MeanAgeColumn : SpeciesModule, IStatsColumns { static readonly string[] columns = { "mean_age" }; public IEnumerable<string> StatColumns => columns; public double StatValue(string column) { int n = 0; double sum = 0; foreach (var a in Species.Animals) if (!a.IsGone) { n++; sum += a.Age; } return n > 0 ? sum / n : 0; } } Put it on any GameObject under the species, for example its Stats object. A world-level column works the same way on a WorldService under the World's Recording object. Causes of death Every death goes through World.RecordDeath: it marks the animal gone, records its death event with the cause, counts it, and calls every OnDied hook (ANIM-42). Any cause string you pass gets its column, <species>_deaths_<cause>, with no other step. There are two ways to kill an animal: A death rule, for a condition checked every tick on every animal (thirst, disease). The death phase asks it and records the death for you. List the causes it can give in Causes: their columns then exist from the first row. See Stats, costs and death rules. Your own phase, for an event that strikes from outside. Call RecordDeath, then remove the dead from the species' list with Species.RemoveGone() once your loop is over: using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; // Lightning: each tick, each animal dies with a small chance, whatever its genes. Place it among the Phases, after Deaths. public class LightningPhase : TickPhase { [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f), Tooltip("Chance per animal per tick.")] float chance = 0.0005f; public override void Run(TickContext t) { foreach (var s in World.AllSpecies) { var rng = t.Stream(s, "lightning"); // the species' own stream (RAND-03) foreach (var a in s.Animals) if (!a.IsGone && rng.Chance(chance)) World.RecordDeath(a, "lightning"); s.RemoveGone(); // after the loop: the dead leave the list } } } The column prey_deaths_lightning appears at the first such death; rows before it leave it empty. Events of your own Build a SimEvent with its kind, the tick, the animal's id (-1 for none) and the species id (null for a world event), add fields with With, and record it with World.Events.Record. The egg system records lost eggs this way: World.Events.Record(new SimEvent("egg_lost", World.Tick, egg.Id, egg.Species.Id) .With("parents", new List<int>(egg.Parents)) .With("reason", reason)); A world event, from a seasons phase: World.Events.Record(new SimEvent("season", t.Tick, -1, null).With("winter", winter)); Field values are numbers, strings, bools, lists and dictionaries of those. The line is written as canonical JSON: keys sorted, at most 6 decimals. Record from simulation code only, a phase or a module's hook, once per occurrence and in a fixed order: the event becomes part of the events hash. Never record from a view, an editor window or a sink. Listening to events An IEventSink receives every event, with its canonical line, right after it is hashed: OnEvent. The run recorder and the Event Log window are sinks. Register with AddSink. The World makes a new event log each time it initialises, so register in Begin, when the run's log exists, and unregister when the run stops. This world service counts the kills of the last 100 ticks and adds them as a column: using System.Collections.Generic; using EvoSim; public class RecentKills : WorldService, IEventSink, IStatsColumns { static readonly string[] columns = { "recent_kills" }; readonly Queue<int> killTicks = new Queue<int>(); // the tick of each kill, oldest first public override void Begin() // the run's event log exists from here on { killTicks.Clear(); World.Events.AddSink(this); } public override void OnRunStopped(string reason) => World.Events.RemoveSink(this); public void OnEvent(SimEvent e, string line) // read only: record nothing, change nothing { if (e.Kind == "death" && "killed".Equals(e["cause"])) killTicks.Enqueue(e.Tick); while (killTicks.Count > 0 && killTicks.Peek() <= e.Tick - 100) killTicks.Dequeue(); } public IEnumerable<string> StatColumns => columns; public double StatValue(string column) { int n = 0; foreach (int t in killTicks) if (t > World.Tick - 100) n++; return n; } } Put it on a GameObject under the World's Recording object. A sink only reads: it must not record events, change the world or draw random numbers. What changes the events hash The hash identifies a run (Determinism and replay). Two runs with the same hash recorded the same events in the same order. Changes the hash Leaves it unchanged the run seed or the world seed: the chain starts from them the wait mode, run speed, frame rate and ticks per frame (RAND-11) anything that changes what happens: a setting, a module, a phase or its place, a brain's answers the views, the editor windows, LiveStatistics an event added, removed, reordered or given another field, such as your own SimEvent statistics columns and event sinks that only read a value written differently in an event the compatibility mode, Write Files, the run's folder and run_info.json Draws from a stream of your own don't shift the numbers of other streams (RAND-02): only what your module then changes in the world shows in the hash. Compare hashes on one machine (RAND-12). Test it Build a world with a recorder that writes files, run it, and read stats.csv (Testing your module): using System.IO; using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; public class MeanAgeColumnTests : WorldFixture { [Test] public void AddsItsColumn() { var b = New(19, name: "mean-age").Lab1(prey: 20, predators: 3).Recorder(true, "Logs/EvoSim/test-runs", "mean-age"); b.Root.transform.Find("prey").gameObject.AddComponent<MeanAgeColumn>(); var w = b.Build(); w.Advance(200); w.Stop("test"); var header = File.ReadAllLines(Path.Combine(w.Service<RunRecorder>().RunFolder, "stats.csv"))[0].Split(','); CollectionAssert.Contains(header, "prey_mean_age"); } } OpenHooksTests.ModulesAddStatsColumns (in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Core) checks a species column, a world column and a cause of death recorded by a phase, row by row. To check that a module doesn't change a run, compare w.Events.Hash with and without it. Read next Probes that do this: HookProbe (a species module with columns) and WorldHookProbe (a world service with a column), in Assets/EvoSim/Testing/Probes. RunRecorder, EventLog, LiveStatistics, CanonicalJson. Phases, services and world hooks: phases, services, Begin, OnBorn and OnDied. Specification: 13 — Outputs and recording, 12 — Tick order and determinism.

extending/reproduction.html.title: Reproduction and population | EvoSim
extending/reproduction.html.summary: Reproduction and population Six modules in a species' Life group decide how it breeds and how many of its animals the world keeps: who mates, how many babies a mating makes, how the parents' genes mix, how long eggs incubate, and the population's cap and floor. Most changes are settings; override a member when the rule itself must change. How these modules work together is explained in Reproduction and population. The phases find each module by its type (s.Module<Litter>()), so a species has one of each, and a replacement derives from the reference class: MyLitter : Litter, MyRule : MatingRule. Crossovers derive from the abstract Crossover. Module Override Called Crossover Cross (must), Copy breed phase, once per baby of two parents (Cross) or one parent (Copy) Litter Size, ChildEnergy breed phase, once per conception; hatch phase, for each baby's energy MatingRule IsReady, IsAdult, Sexual breed phase, for seekers and partners; kin senses, to report readiness Incubation Ticks breed phase, once per conception CapRule Cap migration phase every tick; breed phase in Block mode FloorRule settings only (Floor) floor phase every tick A crossover The reference UniformCrossover takes each locus from either parent with probability ½ (GENE-30). This one cuts the genome once: loci before a random cut come from one parent, the others from the other. using EvoSim; public class OnePointCrossover : Crossover { public override Allele[] Cross(Genome a, Genome b, RandomStream rng) { CheckSpecies(a, b); // genomes never cross species (SPEC-04) bool aFirst = rng.NextBool(); // which parent gives the loci before the cut int cut = rng.Range(0, a.Count + 1); var first = aFirst ? a : b; var second = aFirst ? b : a; var child = new Allele[a.Count]; for (int i = 0; i < child.Length; i++) child[i] = i < cut ? first[i] : second[i]; return child; } } Replace the UniformCrossover component of the species' Life group with yours. Note Neighbouring loci now travel together, like linked genes on a chromosome. This leaves the contract's independent loci (GENE-30): fine for an experiment, but it is no longer the reference. A litter Override Size to change how many babies a mating makes. The reference draws k in [Min, Max] and cuts it to what the parents can pay, never below Min (REPRO-10). This one makes small litters unless both parents are rich: using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; public class CarefulLitter : Litter { [SerializeField, Min(0f), Tooltip("Energy every parent needs for a full litter, in points.")] float richEnergy = 80f; public override int Size(RandomStream rng, float[] parentEnergies) { int k = base.Size(rng, parentEnergies); // always draw: the stream stays the same foreach (var e in parentEnergies) if (e < richEnergy) return Min; return k; } } Each parent then pays Child Energy / (number of parents) × k (REPRO-11). The cap's Block mode may cut the litter further. Who mates Most changes to the MatingRule are settings: Mate Energy (50 points), Maturity (150 ticks, a trait a number gene can set), Reach (1 m), Sexual. Override a predicate to change who is ready: using EvoSim; public class AgeLimitedMating : MatingRule { public override bool IsReady(Animal a) => base.IsReady(a) && a.Age < 1200; // old animals stop breeding } The brain reads the rule in the prompt: when you change who mates, change Prompt Rule to say so. Incubation, caps and floors Incubation. Set Ticks above 0 and babies hatch later; the mutator's answers usually arrive meanwhile, so the world doesn't wait (MUT-33). Override Ticks to compute it, without random draws. Cap. Choose Mode Migrate (reference: random animals leave above the cap) or Block (no conception at the cap). Override Cap to compute it, without random draws. Floor. Floor 0 means no newcomers. To bring newcomers another way, replace the FloorPhase with your own tick phase. Eggs as food In the reference nothing eats eggs. Eggs exist only while they incubate, so: give the species that lays them an Incubation above 0, e.g. 20 ticks; add an Edible to the World's Environment ▸ Eggs object (method graze: an egg is taken whole); add a diet entry egg:prey to the egg eater's Diet, and give it a way to find eggs: an action pointed at eggs, and a sense if its brain should know about them. An eaten egg never hatches and is recorded as an egg_lost event with the reason eaten (REPRO-23). The details are in Food, cover, entities and ground. Rules your module keeps Draw only from the stream you are given (RAND-03): Size gets the species' litter stream, Cross its mutation stream. Draw the same number of times whatever the parents, as CarefulLitter does by calling base.Size first. A crossover returns a new array: one allele per locus, in locus order, each taken from that same locus of a parent (GENE-30), after CheckSpecies. It never changes the parents' genomes. It is called once per baby, so siblings differ (GENE-32). Readiness only reads. IsReady, IsAdult and Sexual change nothing and draw nothing: kin senses call IsReady too, while the world is being sensed. Computed settings are deterministic. Ticks, Cap and ChildEnergy depend only on the settings and the world state, never on the clock or UnityEngine.Random. Test it These modules have no conformance suite. Copy the tests in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Reproduction/ReproductionTests.cs: T-REPRO-05 checks litter sizes and the energy cut, T-GENE-08 runs 10 000 crossovers and checks that each locus comes from the first parent half the time. See Testing your module. Read next Rewrite the reference Litter and UniformCrossover from their stubs (EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub ▸ 9 Litter, 10 UniformCrossover): the teaching path. What a baby inherits and how it mutates: Genes, Mutation. The contract: 11 — Reproduction and population.

extending/samples.html.title: The samples | EvoSim
extending/samples.html.summary: The samples The samples are the recipes of 22 — Extending written out as working modules: thirst, water, drinking, seasons, slopes, a mutation operator without a model, a sense that tells a hunter from a neighbour, and a carcass that can be dragged away. Read them as complete examples of each mechanism, and add them to a scene to try them. They live in Assets/EvoSim/Samples, assembly EvoSim.Samples, namespace EvoSim.Samples. No reference scene uses them, so they change nothing until you put one in a world. Most are tested in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Samples/SampleTests.cs, and the senses, actions, stat, operator, phase and locomotion also go through the conformance suite of their kind. Sample Adds Mechanism Recipe Thirst a thirst stat and its prompt rule a stat module 22 §1 DiesOfThirst thirst that grows, and death by thirst a death rule 22 §1 NearestWaterSense "Water: 1-4 meters away." a banded sense 22 §2 DrinkAction an action that walks to the shore and drinks an action and an interaction 22 §3 IntensityLadder often becomes always or sometimes a mutation operator 22 §8 SeasonsPhase winters in which grass regrows slowly a tick phase 22 §9 ChasedSense "Something is chasing me." a plain sense 22 §13 SlopeLocomotion steep slopes refused, climbing paid in energy a locomotion subclass 22 §14 DragAction a carcass dragged into cover an interaction that moves an entity scenario S18 To add a sample, select the GameObject named below, choose Add Component in the Inspector and type the class name. To change a sample, copy its file into Assets/Student and rename the class: the Student assembly sees the samples, so your class can also derive from one. Thirst Thirst declares a stat, thirst, on every animal of the species: 0 at birth, kept between 0 and Deadly (100). It adds a rule line to the prompt: "Thirst grows every step; an animal dies of thirst at 100. Drinking resets it." It does not change the stat itself: DiesOfThirst makes it grow and DrinkAction resets it. Mechanism. A SpeciesModule that declares a stat in Declare and writes a rule in WritePromptRules. Other modules read it through Value: a[thirst.Value]. See Stats, costs and death rules. In a scene. On a child of the species, next to its other stats. Settings: Per Tick (0.5), Deadly (100). To let the brain feel thirst, add a LevelSense with Stat thirst: no code needed. DiesOfThirst DiesOfThirst runs in the death phase, once per animal per tick. It adds Per Tick to the animal's thirst, then returns the cause "thirst" when thirst has reached Deadly. At the reference values, an animal that never drinks dies after 200 ticks. The cause gets its own column in stats.csv (deaths_thirst, prefixed with the species id). Mechanism. A DeathRule: Causes names its causes and CauseOfDeath returns one, or null to live on. [RequiresModule(typeof(Thirst))] (RequiresModuleAttribute) names the module it needs. In a scene. On a child of the species (its Life object, beside Starvation). It needs a Thirst. NearestWaterSense NearestWaterSense tells the brain how far the nearest water is: here within 0.5 m (V2: "I am at the water's edge."), one token per distance band, or none. It asks the ground with NearestWater. Mechanism. A BandedSense: the base class builds the tokens and writes the texts; the sample turns on the here token (HasHere) and maps a distance to a token in Read. See A sense. In a scene. On a new child of the species' Senses object: its place among the senses is its place in the situation text. It needs a ground that knows water: the TerrainGround (ground below its Water Level is water). On a flat ground it always says none. It multiplies the species' number of possible observations by 6. DrinkAction DrinkAction gives the brain a new choice, drink: walk to the shore of the nearest water in sight, and reset thirst to 0 on arrival. With no water in sight the animal searches (ACT-04). Mechanism. An AnimalAction that only states an intent and an interaction: the act phase moves the animal, then applies a small IInteraction (reach 0.5 m) that sets thirst to 0. Its IsRelevant reads the Water sense. See An action or an interaction. In a scene. On a new GameObject under the species' Actions, named drink (the action's name in the prompt and its gene's label), with a TextGene on the same GameObject. It needs a Thirst on the species and a ground with water. IntensityLadder IntensityLadder mutates a text gene without a model: it finds the first of never, rarely, sometimes, often, always in the sentence and moves it one step up or down, keeping its capital and punctuation. "Rest often when tired." becomes "Rest always when tired." or "Rest sometimes when tired.". A sentence without such a word fails the job, and the gene stays as it was. Mechanism. A MutationOperator: Accepts takes text genes, and StartMutation draws its one coin from the stream it is given (MUT-30). It sees nothing but the gene (CORE-07). See Mutation. In a scene. On the species' Mutation object, beside the LlmMutation. Drag the genes it should handle into its Only These list. A gene goes to the operator that lists it; the other genes go to the first operator whose list is empty (MUT-02). SeasonsPhase SeasonsPhase splits time into years of Year Length ticks (2 000). In the second half of each year, winter, the food layer named in Layer ("Grass") regrows at Winter Regrow Factor (0.2) times its normal rate. Mechanism. A TickPhase: Initialize finds the layer, Run sets its regrowth factor every tick, and the environment phase, later in the same tick, uses it (TICK-02). Validate reports a missing layer (V-20) and a wrong place (V-08). See Phases, services and world hooks. In a scene. On a new GameObject under the World's Phases, above Environment: phases run in hierarchy order. ChasedSense ChasedSense answers yes when the nearest threat in sight is doing an action that hunts and its target is this animal, no otherwise. A cannibal, which flees its own kind, can then tell a hungry neighbour from a peaceful one. Mechanism. A plain Sense with two tokens. It reads the hunter's action through Hunts and its target through CurrentTarget, both as they were at the start of the tick (SENSE-04), and writes its own V2 sentences. In a scene. On a new child of the species' Senses. It only says yes in a species that has threats. It doubles the number of possible observations. SlopeLocomotion SlopeLocomotion moves like the kinematic locomotion, but refuses a step onto ground steeper than Max Slope Degrees (35) and charges Energy Per Meter Climbed (0.3 points) for every meter of height gained. Going down costs nothing extra. Mechanism. A subclass of a reference module (MOVE-07): it overrides Move to change the intent before calling the base, and ExtraCost, which the metabolism adds to the cost of the move. See A locomotion. In a scene. It replaces the species' KinematicLocomotion on its Locomotion object: a species has exactly one locomotion (V-13). Copy Walk Speed, Run Speed and Prompt Rule from the old one. It matters only on a ground with heights. DragAction DragAction walks to the nearest carcass in sight; within Grab Reach (1 m) it walks toward the nearest cover and drags the carcass along, at walking speed, until both are hidden. It is not a recipe of 22: it writes out scenario S18 of 31 — Scenarios, an entity that moves (ENV-21). Mechanism. An action whose interaction moves an entity: the carcass changes position in the act phase, never from the views. Its interaction's reach is unlimited, so it applies wherever the animal ends its move. In a scene. On a new GameObject drag under the actions of a species whose diet eats carcasses (the predator), with a TextGene. It needs a cover layer, and reads the Carcass sense. Worked example: thirst on the terrain The Terrain_Locomotion scene has a 96 m terrain whose lowest ground, about 15 %, is water. Four samples together make its prey thirsty. Do this in a copy of the scene. Open Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/Terrain_Locomotion.unity and save it as Assets/Student/ThirstyTerrain.unity. Select Terrain World. Unless the JEV server runs, set Default Brain to Brains/Random. Select Terrain World/Prey/Stats (it holds Energy, Stamina and Metabolism) and add a Thirst. Keep Per Tick 0.5 and Deadly 100. Select Prey/Life and add a Dies Of Thirst. Under Prey/Senses, create an empty child named Water, below Food, and add a Nearest Water Sense. Optionally, create a Thirst child below it with a Level Sense: Stat thirst, Low 30, High 70, and Words "I am not thirsty.", "I am thirsty.", "I am parched." (low thirst comes first). Under Prey/Actions, create a child named drink and add a Drink Action and a Text Gene. In the gene's Founders, write "Drink whenever you pass water." and "Drink only when very thirsty."; keep Has Neutral on. Contrast Pro and Contrast Anti ("Always drink, whatever happens." / "Never drink unless parched.") are optional: only brain tests use them. Press Play. The validation panel may warn that the prey's signature changed (V-12; Accept it) and that its observation space is large (V-50). Warnings don't stop the run. Open Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Event Log: deaths with the cause thirst appear from about tick 200, for prey that found no water. In the run's stats.csv the column prey_deaths_thirst counts them. To see what drinking is worth, disable the drink GameObject and run the same seed again, then compare the deaths by thirst. Scenario S16 makes the same comparison with a scripted brain. Then try the others on the same scene: a Seasons Phase above Phases/Environment, or a Slope Locomotion for the predator only, with a Max Slope Degrees below the ground's 35°, so the two species cross the hills differently. Test it The same combination, in a test world with a pond (PondGround): a thirsty prey 2 m from the shore drinks within three ticks. See Testing for the helpers. public class ThirstyPondTests : WorldFixture { [Test, Description("22 §3: drink walks to the shore and resets thirst on arrival")] public void DrinkResetsThirst() { var w = New().Ground<PondGround>(20, 20).Food(0f, 0f).Phase<ActPhase>() .Species("prey", s => s.PreyBody().Action<DrinkAction>("drink").Module<Thirst>()).Build(); var sp = w.FindSpecies("prey"); var a = Place.Animal(sp, Place.At(10f, 15f)); var thirst = sp.Module<Thirst>().Value; a[thirst] = 50f; a.Choose("drink"); w.Advance(3); Assert.AreEqual(0f, a[thirst], "drank"); Assert.IsFalse(w.Ground.IsWater(a.Position), "on the shore, not in the water"); } } Read next Extending EvoSim: every mechanism the samples use, and the others. The teaching path: rewrite the reference modules the samples build on. 31 — Scenarios: S16 (water and thirst), S17 (terrain and locomotion), S18 (moving carcasses).

extending/sense.html.title: A sense | EvoSim
extending/sense.html.summary: A sense A sense tells the brain one new thing about the situation: whether water is near, whether a threat is chasing the animal, what lies ahead. Derive from Sense for a few tokens of your own, from BandedSense for "how far is the nearest X", and from BatchedSense when you need raycasts. To sense a stat as low, medium or high (thirst, fear), you need no code: add a LevelSense and set its Stat and thresholds. How senses, observations and situation texts fit together is in Senses and prompts. The base class Member What it does, and when it is called Tokens must implement every token the sense can return, "none" included, fixed before the run Read must implement returns the animal's token, as an index into Tokens; called by the sense phase for each deciding animal Write may override the text of a token in V1 or V2; the default writes Label: token. in both DefaultLabel may override the label when the Inspector's Label is empty; by default the class name without "Sense" ReadAll may override reads all the deciding animals of the species at once; the default calls Read for each HasAttachments, Attachment, AttachmentKey may override an image or other object for the query (Attachments) Declare may override declares the traits the sense needs ("vision", "maturity"), before any animal exists Initialize may override finds stats and other modules, builds the token list Validate may override reports configuration problems before the run Read receives a SenseContext. It is the only way to look at the world: Vision, NearestAnimal, NearestResource, NearestCarcass, NearestEgg, NearestEntity<T>, NearestCover, InCover, IsReady, CurrentTarget, Ground and Rays. Its queries leave out animals hidden from the reader and animals killed this tick. A complete example The sample ChasedSense (Assets/EvoSim/Samples/ChasedSense.cs) says whether the nearest threat is hunting this animal. It lets a cannibal tell a hungry neighbour from a peaceful one. using System.Collections.Generic; namespace EvoSim.Samples { public class ChasedSense : Sense { static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> tokens = System.Array.AsReadOnly(new[] { "no", "yes" }); public override IReadOnlyList<string> Tokens => tokens; protected override string DefaultLabel => "Chased"; public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) { var threat = s.NearestAnimal(a, AnimalSet.Threats, s.Vision(a)); if (threat == null) return 0; var t = threat.Value.Animal; bool hunting = t.CurrentAction != null && t.CurrentAction.Hunts; return hunting && s.CurrentTarget(t) == a ? 1 : 0; // the hunter's target this tick } public override string Write(int token, TextStyle style) => style == TextStyle.V2 ? (token == 1 ? "Something is chasing me." : "Nothing is chasing me.") : $"{Label}: {tokens[token]}."; } } Where to put it. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Sense writes Assets/Student/<Name>.cs, a sense that compiles, and its test Assets/Student/Tests/<Name>Tests.cs. Add the component under the species, in its Senses group, on a child GameObject named after its label, as the reference species do. Any place under the species works. The order matters. The senses are taken depth-first: the n-th sense found gives the n-th token of the observation and the n-th fragment of the situation text. The species inspector lists them in situation-text order. Adding, removing or moving a sense changes the species' signature. Validation warns until you accept it (V-12), because results and cached answers change too. If your sense reads a module of your own (a Thirst stat), put [RequiresModule(typeof(Thirst))] on the class: validation then checks that the species has it (V-26), and the test suites add it for you. Distances: BandedSense A BandedSense does most of the work for "how far is the nearest X". It declares the "vision" trait, builds the tokens from its Bands (here, adjacent, close, medium, far, none), writes both styles with ranges in meters, and checks the bands (V-30). You write Read, and return TokenFor or NoneToken. The sample NearestWaterSense: public class NearestWaterSense : BandedSense { protected override bool HasHere => true; // a "here" token, at the shore protected override string DefaultLabel => "Water"; protected override string HereSentence() => "I am at the water's edge."; // V2 text of "here" public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) { if (s.Ground == null) return NoneToken; float vision = s.Vision(a); var water = s.Ground.NearestWater(a.Position, vision); return water == null ? NoneToken : TokenFor(water.Value.Distance, vision, here: water.Value.Distance <= 0.5f); } } Member Use Vision the "vision" trait: a.Trait(Vision) is the animal's vision in meters (or s.Vision(a)) HasHere, HereSentence add a "here" token, and its V2 sentence Noun the noun of V2 texts ("The nearest water is…"); the Noun field, or the label in lower case BuildTokens override to add tokens per band, as NearestAnimalSense does for readiness If you override Declare, Initialize or Validate, call the base method. Raycasts: BatchedSense A BatchedSense asks for its rays first, in RequestRays. The sense phase casts the rays of every deciding animal in one batch (SENSE-30); then Read gets the k-th ray back from SenseContext.Rays. The test sense ObstacleSense casts one ray along the heading: public override void RequestRays(Animal a, RayBatch rays) => rays.Add(a.Position + Vector3.up * 0.5f, ActContext.HeadingDirection(a.Heading), 5f); // ray 0 public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) => s.Rays.Hit(a, this, 0, out _) ? 1 : 0; Ask for the same rays in the same order for the same state: Read finds them by number. The tokens must equal those of rays cast one at a time (SENSE-31); Immediate casts them that way for a test. Attachments A sense can attach an object to the query, such as a small camera image (SENSE-40). Override HasAttachments to return true and Attachment to return the object; the ask-brains phase calls it for each query. A query with an attachment is memoised and cached only if AttachmentKey gives a key for it, such as a coarse summary of the image (SENSE-41). Only a brain whose AcceptsAttachments is true can serve the species (V-51); no reference brain is. The test sense CameraProbeSense shows the three members. Rules your sense keeps A fixed list of tokens (SENSE-01): build it in a field or in Initialize, never during the run. Include the "nothing" token. Keep it short: each token multiplies the species' observation space (SENSE-05, V-50). Same state, same token (SENSE-03): draw no random number and read no clock. Only the state at the start of the tick (SENSE-04): read the world through the SenseContext you receive. Keep settings in the module, nothing per animal. Hidden and killed things are never sensed (SENSE-06): find animals, food and cover with the context's queries, which leave them out. A sense only reads. It never changes an animal or the world. One text per token (SENSE-10): Write depends on the token and the style only, never on the animal. Every token has a non-empty text in both styles. Distances say "meters" (SENSE-12, SENSE-13). A label of its own within the species (V-17): the brain tells senses apart by label. The batch gives the same tokens: a ReadAll override, or a batched sense, gives exactly what Read would give for each animal alone (SENSE-31). Test it Your sense runs through the sense conformance suite, ConformanceTests.SenseConformance, as soon as it compiles. The suite finds every sense class of the EvoSim assemblies and of Assets/Student, puts it under the prey of a small ecology with the random brain, and checks that: the token list is not empty, and no token is empty; Write gives a non-empty text for every token and both styles, the same text each time; over 60 ticks, every observation holds a valid index for your sense. Run it from Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode tab: expand EvoSim.Tests.EditMode ▸ EvoSim.Tests ▸ ConformanceTests ▸ SenseConformance and run the case named after your class. The failure message names the rule. Then test what your sense means. The sample test of ChasedSense (Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Samples/SampleTests.cs, shortened here) places animals, runs a tick and reads the sense: [Test] public void ChasedSense() { var w = New().Ecology(40f, 0f, 0f, regrow: 0f, prey: s => s.Sense<ChasedSense>()).Phase<ActPhase>().Build(); var prey = Place.Animal(w.FindSpecies("prey"), Place.At(10, 10)); var hunter = Place.Animal(w.FindSpecies("predator"), Place.At(15, 10)); prey.Choose("rest"); hunter.Choose("hunt"); var sense = w.FindSpecies("prey").Module<ChasedSense>(); Assert.AreEqual("no", sense.Tokens[sense.Read(prey, new SenseContext(w))], "nobody hunted yet"); w.Advance(1); w.Space.Rebuild(); // animals moved: refresh the spatial index Assert.AreEqual("yes", sense.Tokens[sense.Read(prey, new SenseContext(w))]); Assert.AreEqual("Something is chasing me.", sense.Write(1, TextStyle.V2)); } The test class derives from WorldFixture. More in Testing your module. Read next The reference senses, written like yours: LevelSense, AgeSense, NearestResourceSense, NearestCoverSense, NearestEntitySense, NearestAnimalSense. Rewrite LevelSense (exercise 2) or NearestAnimalSense (exercise 5) from their stubs: the teaching path. The samples ChasedSense and NearestWaterSense: The samples. An action reads your tokens by label in IsRelevant: An action. Rule lines in the prompt for your module: Species modules. Specification: 06 — Senses and observations.

extending/species-modules.html.title: Species modules, the common base | EvoSim
extending/species-modules.html.summary: Species modules, the common base Everything under a species is a SpeciesModule: senses, actions, genes, stats, death rules, the diet, the locomotion, the mating rule. The specialised kinds have their own pages; this one covers what they all share: the lifecycle the World runs them through, declaring stats, depending on another module, and validation. Derive from SpeciesModule directly for a feature of one species that is none of those kinds: a stat, a setting other modules read, a rule line in the prompt. For something shared by every species, write a world module instead (Phases, services and world hooks). The lifecycle Member You When the World calls it Species, World read set before Declare: the owning species and its World Declare(b) may override once per set-up, before any module of the species initialises: declare your stats and traits, keep their ids Initialize() may override after every module of the species declared: look up other modules, services, traits; reset your own fields WritePromptRules(w) may override while the species' prompt template is built, in module order: add rule lines with w.Rule(…) Validate(report) may override after every Initialize, in the editor and at the start of a run: report configuration problems OnBorn(a) may override each time an animal of this species joins the living (founder, baby, newcomer), its stats set OnDied(a, cause) may override each death of an animal of this species, once recorded; the animal is marked gone Declare, Initialize, WritePromptRules and Validate also run in Edit mode, when the editor validates the scene. The whole set-up order is in The world and its modules. A complete example: a stat Recipe 22 §1, the sample Assets/EvoSim/Samples/Thirst.cs (Thirst): every animal gets a thirst stat, and the prompt explains it. /// <summary>A thirst stat that grows every tick (with DiesOfThirst) and kills at a threshold.</summary> public class Thirst : SpeciesModule { [SerializeField, Min(0f), Tooltip("Thirst added every tick (reference 0.5).")] float perTick = 0.5f; [SerializeField, Min(1f), Tooltip("Thirst at which an animal dies (reference 100).")] float deadly = 100f; public StatId Value { get; private set; } public float PerTick => perTick; public float Deadly => deadly; public override void Declare(SpeciesBuilder b) => Value = b.DeclareStat("thirst", StatStart.Fixed(0f), 0f, deadly); public override void WritePromptRules(PromptWriter w) => w.Rule($"Thirst grows every step; an animal dies of thirst at {Bands.Number(deadly)}. Drinking resets it."); } The module holds settings only. The value belongs to each animal: other modules read and write it with a[thirst.Value], clamped to its range. Here the sample death rule DiesOfThirst raises it every tick, and DrinkAction resets it. Where it goes. Put your class in Assets/Student: Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Stat writes a stat module there, with a test in Assets/Student/Tests. Add the component anywhere under the species, for example on its Stats object beside Energy and Stamina. (The examples on this page leave out the usual using EvoSim; and using UnityEngine; lines.) Stats, traits and their ids A stat changes during life (energy, stamina, thirst); a trait is fixed at birth (vision, stamina.max) and a number gene may set it. Declare both in Declare with the SpeciesBuilder: Call Returns b.DeclareStat(name, start, min, max, capTrait) a StatId; start is StatStart.Fixed(v) or StatStart.FullTrait(trait) b.DeclareTrait(name, default, min, max, changeable) a TraitId Species.Declarations.FindStat(name), FindTrait(name) the id another module declared, for Initialize Two modules that declare the same name share one value; the first declaration counts (V-38 if they differ). Read and write with a[statId] and a.Trait(traitId). Warning An id is only good once resolved. FindStat and FindTrait return an invalid id when no module declared the name. Resolve every id in Declare or Initialize, check IsValid, and report a missing one in Validate. Never read or write an animal with an id you have not checked. Rules your module keeps Settings in the module, state in the animal (CORE-05). One module serves every animal of its species: anything that belongs to one animal goes in a stat or a trait. A static check enforces it for the reference modules. Set up in Initialize, never in Awake, Start or OnEnable (ARCH-04), and reset your fields there: the same object starts every run. Change nothing in the scene in Declare, Initialize or Validate: they also run in Edit mode. Random numbers only from a named stream, such as World.Random.For(Species, "purpose") (RAND-01, RAND-03). Keep rule lines stable. They are part of the prompt, so changing one changes the prompt's id and the answers the cache can reuse. Species A new species is configuration, not code. Duplicate the prey in the Hierarchy and change, on its Species: Field What it is Id the stable id of files, streams, locus ids and statistics columns (deer); empty = the display name; no ., not world Display Name what the brain reads in prompts and situations Brain its own brain; empty = the World's Default Brain Initial Population founders at tick 0 Prompt Header, Genes Intro, Frozen Prompt the fixed parts of its prompt Ids and display names must be unique (V-07). Then change its modules and founder sentences, and give a hunter a diet entry for it (deer): the food web and the threats update by themselves. GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ New Species starts a species from scratch, and Add Action and Add Sense fill it. Adding, removing or moving an action, gene or sense changes the species' signature (SPEC-03). Once a signature has been accepted, validation warns when it changes (V-12), until you accept the new one. Subclass Species only for its two hooks, OnBorn and OnDied. They run before the modules' hooks. They are protected internal, so from your own assembly the override is protected: public class LoggedSpecies : Species { protected override void OnBorn(Animal a) => Debug.Log($"{a} joins ({a.Origin})"); protected override void OnDied(Animal a, string cause) => Debug.Log($"{a} died: {cause}"); } At run time, World.AddSpecies clones a species under the World with a new id (SPEC-30): World.AddSpecies(prey, "deer", parent: prey, founders: 6). The clone gets its own population, streams and allele ids, and inherits the parent's relations both ways: it eats what the parent eats, and whoever hunted the parent hunts it (SPEC-31). It is set up and validated like a species at Initialize; an error throws an InvalidOperationException and the clone is removed. An id is never reused: a second deer becomes deer-2 (SPEC-32). Call it between ticks, or from a phase outside any loop over World.AllSpecies. Dependencies A module that needs another one beside it says so with RequiresModuleAttribute. The sample death rule needs a thirst: [RequiresModule(typeof(Thirst))] public class DiesOfThirst : DeathRule { static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> causes = System.Array.AsReadOnly(new[] { "thirst" }); Thirst thirst; public override IEnumerable<string> Causes => causes; public override void Initialize() => thirst = Species.Module<Thirst>(); public override string CauseOfDeath(Animal a) { if (thirst == null) return null; // no Thirst: nothing to do a[thirst.Value] += thirst.PerTick; return a[thirst.Value] >= thirst.Deadly ? "thirst" : null; } // … (Validate) } Put it on a species module's class, once per module needed; subclasses inherit it, and a subclass of the named type counts. The named module is looked for on the same species, or under the World for a world module. When it is missing, validation warns (V-26: DiesOfThirst needs a Thirst on 'prey') with a fix that adds it on a new child named after it (no fix for an abstract type). It is only a warning, so the run still starts: look the companion up in Initialize and cope with null, as above. The conformance suites add the companions before they test your module. Validation Override Validate to catch configuration mistakes before Play. Add one message per problem to the ValidationReport, naming the object at fault (usually this), with a validator id from the catalogue of 21 §2 that fits (V-20 for a name that matches nothing, V-35 for a value out of range…): Method Effect Error(id, obj, text, fix) blocks Play and the run Warning(id, obj, text, fix) the run starts; something is probably wrong Info(id, obj, text, fix) worth knowing A ValidationFix is a button in the inspector's validation list: a label and the change to make; the editor records it for Undo, then validates again. Validation itself only reads: the change belongs in the fix. Write each message for a student who has never seen your code: what is wrong, and the rule it breaks. public class PreferredFood : SpeciesModule { [SerializeField, Tooltip("A food layer's name.")] string layer = "Grass"; [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f), Tooltip("How strongly it prefers that layer.")] float preference = 0.5f; // … public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) { if (World.Service<ResourceLayer>(layer) == null) { var first = World.Service<ResourceLayer>(); report.Error("V-20", this, $"No food layer is named '{layer}'.", first == null ? null : new ValidationFix($"Use {first.LayerName}", () => layer = first.LayerName)); } if (!(preference >= 0f && preference <= 1f)) // also catches NaN report.Error("V-35", this, $"The preference {preference} is outside [0, 1].", new ValidationFix("Clamp", () => preference = Mathf.Clamp01(preference))); } } Test it The stat suite (T-ANIM, ConformanceTests.StatConformance) runs every species module with a public StatId property: founders start as declared, and the stat stays in its range for 1 000 ticks. Your own tests derive from WorldFixture and build a world in code (Testing your module). To test validation, build it without initialising and prepare it: var w = New(name: "no layer").Flat(20, 20) .Species("prey", s => s.Population(0).Action<RestAction>("rest").Module<PreferredFood>()) .BuildUninitialized(); var report = new ValidationReport(); Assert.IsFalse(w.Prepare(report)); Assert.IsTrue(report.Has("V-20"), report.ToString()); Read next References: Energy, Stamina, Metabolism, DecisionSchedule; the samples Thirst, DiesOfThirst, DrinkAction. The specialised kinds: A sense, An action, Stats, costs and death rules, Genes, A locomotion. Phases, services and world hooks, for what all species share.

extending/stats-and-death.html.title: Stats, costs and death rules | EvoSim
extending/stats-and-death.html.summary: Stats, costs and death rules Four things can be added or changed here: a stat every animal of a species carries (thirst, fear, temperature), what living costs per tick, the reference energy, stamina and digestion modules, and a cause of death. Stats and traits, energy, stamina, metabolism and death are explained in Animals, stats and death. If the cost depends on how an animal moves (slopes, mud), a locomotion's ExtraCost is the simpler place. A stat module A stat is declared by a SpeciesModule, in Declare, before any animal exists. Keep the id you get back: it is how every module reads and writes the stat. Call on the SpeciesBuilder Parameters DeclareStat a name; a start, Fixed(float) or full at a trait's value (FullTrait(TraitId)); a minimum and a maximum (default: none); optionally a trait that caps it for each animal DeclareTrait a name; its default, your Inspector setting; a minimum and a maximum; whether it may change during life (default: no) The sample Thirst (Assets/EvoSim/Samples/Thirst.cs, recipe 22 §1) declares a stat and describes it in the prompt: public class Thirst : SpeciesModule { [SerializeField, Min(0f), Tooltip("Thirst added every tick (reference 0.5).")] float perTick = 0.5f; [SerializeField, Min(1f), Tooltip("Thirst at which an animal dies (reference 100).")] float deadly = 100f; public StatId Value { get; private set; } public float PerTick => perTick; public float Deadly => deadly; public override void Declare(SpeciesBuilder b) => Value = b.DeclareStat("thirst", StatStart.Fixed(0f), 0f, deadly); public override void WritePromptRules(PromptWriter w) => w.Rule($"Thirst grows every step; an animal dies of thirst at {Bands.Number(deadly)}. Drinking resets it."); } Other modules find it with Species.Module<Thirst>() in their Initialize, then read and write a[thirst.Value]. Every write is clamped to the stat's range (ANIM-22). A trait is read with a.Trait(id). To let the brain sense the stat, add a LevelSense with the stat thirst: no code (A sense). Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Stat writes such a module, with a start and a maximum, into Assets/Student. Put the component on a child GameObject of the species, next to its other stats (Stats in the reference scenes). Changing what a tick costs Metabolism charges each living animal once per tick, after it acted (ANIM-20). Its settings cover most changes: Field Reference Meaning Base Cost 0.7 energy per tick when moving, or when still with an action that doesn't rest Move Cost 0.5 energy per meter moved Rest Cost 0.2 energy per tick when still and busy, or still with a resting action Cost Trait empty a trait the tick's cost grows with, e.g. stamina.max (09 §5) Cost Per Unit 0.005 extra energy per tick per unit of that trait: 60 stamina costs 0.3 a tick A cost trait gives a number gene a price, so evolution can't push the trait up for free. Validation reports a cost trait that no module declares (V-45), and reminds you when a number gene's trait has no cost (V-47). For a rule the settings can't express, derive from Metabolism and override Settle. It receives the animal, the meters it moved, the locomotion's extra cost, and whether it was busy at the start of the tick. The reference does this: public virtual void Settle(Animal a, float metersMoved, float extraCost, bool wasBusy) { if (energy != null) { float cost; if (metersMoved > Units.Epsilon) cost = baseCost + moveCost * metersMoved; // less than 1 mm counts as still else if (wasBusy) cost = restCost; else cost = a.CurrentAction != null && a.CurrentAction.Rests ? restCost : baseCost; if (costId.IsValid) cost += costPerUnit * a.Trait(costId); // the cost trait (09 §5) energy.Pay(a, cost + Mathf.Max(0f, extraCost)); } stamina?.Settle(a, metersMoved, energy); // pays the meters or recovers } An override must still pay through Energy.Pay and let the stamina settle, or stamina never recovers. Replacing energy, stamina or digestion Other modules find these by type: Species.Module<Energy>(), Module<Stamina>(), Module<Digestion>(), Module<Metabolism>(). That call also returns a subclass, so a replacement must derive from the reference and take its place (one of each per species). Override the virtual members: Module Virtual members Called by Energy Gain(a, amount), Pay(a, amount) every meal; the metabolism, stamina recovery, litters Stamina Budget(a), Settle(a, metersMoved, energy) the act phase, before moving; the metabolism, after Digestion AfterMeal(a, gain) the interactions, after a kill or a carcass portion Metabolism Settle(a, metersMoved, extraCost, wasBusy) the act phase, once per animal per tick The stub of exercise 8, EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub ▸ 8 Stamina, is such a subclass: it keeps the reference's declarations and asks you to write Budget and Settle. A death rule Derive from DeathRule to add a cause of death. Member You What it does, when it is called CauseOfDeath must implement Returns the cause's name for this animal now, or null to live on. Called in the death phase, once per tick for every living animal, after it aged. Causes should override Lists every cause the rule can return, so its <species>_deaths_<cause> column is in stats.csv from the first row. CheckAll may override Checks all living animals at once (20 §10). The default calls CauseOfDeath for each animal that has no cause yet. The sample DiesOfThirst (Assets/EvoSim/Samples/DiesOfThirst.cs) makes thirst grow with the animal and kills at the deadly level: [RequiresModule(typeof(Thirst))] public class DiesOfThirst : DeathRule { static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> causes = System.Array.AsReadOnly(new[] { "thirst" }); Thirst thirst; public override IEnumerable<string> Causes => causes; public override void Initialize() => thirst = Species.Module<Thirst>(); public override string CauseOfDeath(Animal a) { if (thirst == null) return null; a[thirst.Value] += thirst.PerTick; // ages with the animal, in the death phase return a[thirst.Value] >= thirst.Deadly ? "thirst" : null; } } Place it under the species, next to the other death rules (Life in the reference scenes). The species' rules run in module order, and the first one that names a cause decides: later rules are not asked about that animal. The death phase records the death (cause, age, generation, meals, offspring) and removes the animal; the rule only names the cause. To remove animals at another moment, call World.RecordDeath from a phase of your own: see Phases, services and world hooks. Rules Settings in the module, state in the animal (ANIM-01). One module serves every animal of its species: what belongs to one animal goes in a stat it declared, never in a field of the module. Declare in Declare, look up in Initialize. Read and write only through the ids (ANIM-10). Read traits, not settings (ANIM-16): a number gene may have changed the animal's value. Stats stay in range (ANIM-22): writes are clamped, so a gain never passes the maximum. A death rule only names causes. It may update a stat that grows with age, as thirst does, but never removes an animal itself. Draw random numbers only from the species' streams (RAND-03), World.Random.For(Species, purpose). Test it The stat suite runs every species module with a public StatId property: Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode, ConformanceTests ▸ StatConformance (the T-ANIM stat template). It puts the module under the prey of a small world and checks that every founder starts as declared, and that the stat stays in its range for 1 000 ticks (ANIM-10, ANIM-22). There is no suite for death rules. A test to copy, from Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Samples/SampleTests.cs (its class derives from WorldFixture): [Test] public void ThirstKills() { var w = New().Flat(20, 20).Food(0f, 0f).Phase<DeathPhase>() .Species("prey", s => s.PreyBody().Action<RestAction>("rest").Module<Thirst>(t => t.Configure(10f, 30f)).Module<DiesOfThirst>()) .Build(); var sp = w.FindSpecies("prey"); var a = Place.Animal(sp, Place.At(5, 5)); a.Choose("rest"); w.Advance(3); Assert.IsTrue(a.IsGone, "dies at 30"); Assert.AreEqual(1, sp.Counters.Deaths["thirst"]); } See Testing your module. Read next The reference modules: Energy, Stamina, Metabolism, Digestion, Starvation (exercise 3) and OldAge. The samples Thirst, DiesOfThirst and the action that resets thirst, DrinkAction: An action or an interaction, the samples. Genes: number genes that set your traits. Specification: 05 — Animals, stats and life cycle.

extending/testing-your-module.html.title: Testing your module | EvoSim
extending/testing-your-module.html.summary: Testing your module Every module you write gets two kinds of test. The conformance suite of its kind finds your class on its own and checks that it fits the system: a sense returns declared tokens, an action only sets intents, a locomotion never ends a tick on water. Your unit tests check that it does what you meant: the drink action resets thirst, your sense says near at 3 m. A green suite means your module fits; only your own tests say it is right. All tests use the Unity Test Framework (NUnit) and run in Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, without any language model: brains and mutators are fakes. Their helpers live in the EvoSim.Testing assembly (Testing). Step by step Create the class with its test. In the Project window, Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Sense, Action, Gene kind, Stat, Phase, Brain or Mutation operator asks for a class name and writes two files: Assets/Student/<Name>.cs (assembly Student) and Assets/Student/Tests/<Name>Tests.cs (assembly Student.Tests, editor only, which sees EvoSim.Testing). The test class derives from WorldFixture and has one test, Works, that builds a small world with your class and runs it. For a kind with no template (a locomotion, a resource layer), derive from the base class yourself in Assets/Student. Write the module.
