If it needs another module to work, say so with [RequiresModule(typeof(…))] (see Species modules). Run the conformance suite of its kind. Open Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, tab EditMode, and expand EvoSim.Tests.EditMode ▸ EvoSim.Tests ▸ ConformanceTests. Each suite lists one case per class, named after it. Select the cases of your class and choose Run Selected. A failure message names the rule broken. Write your unit tests in the generated file: they appear under Student.Tests in the same tab. Start from the example below, or copy a test of a reference module of the same kind (see Tests to copy). Before you share your work, run every EditMode test (Run All), then the PlayMode tab. Before a merge into the main branch, also run the slow tests of category T3 (below). The conformance suites ConformanceTests (Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Conformance/ConformanceTests.cs) holds one parameterised test per kind of module. Each builds a small world, puts your module in it (under the prey species, or under the World for a phase or a layer), runs it and checks the rules every module of that kind must keep. Kind Base class The suite checks Test sense Sense tokens are declared and none is empty; Write gives the same non-empty text every time, for every token, in both text styles; over 60 ticks every observation holds a declared token (SENSE-01, SENSE-10) SenseConformance action AnimalAction it has a description for the prompt; a text gene placed beside it binds to it; Act changes no animal, it only sets an intent; alone in an empty world it searches or stays, unless it rests (ACT-04, ACT-06) ActionConformance stat a SpeciesModule with a public StatId property founders start at the declared value; the stat stays in its range for 1 000 ticks, with every other invariant (ANIM-10, ANIM-22) StatConformance food or other item layer ResourceLayer the layer starts with items; the nearest item is found within a radius (for grids, the same one as a brute-force search); an item can be consumed only once (ENV-01, ENV-02) LayerConformance mutation operator MutationOperator it accepts a text or a number gene; the same parent and seed give the same result; a result passes the gene's own checks (MUT-20, MUT-30) MutationOperatorConformance tick phase TickPhase it runs 20 ticks in a world without animals; disabling and re-enabling it leaves the events hash of a populated world unchanged (TICK-01) PhaseConformance locomotion Locomotion eight walkers head into a pond: none ever ends a tick on water or outside the world; the meters reported are the meters moved; the extra cost is never negative; none stands still more than 3 ticks away from the shore (MOVE-02, MOVE-03, SPACE-04, SPACE-05) LocomotionConformance How a class enters a suite You do nothing: no registration, no class to derive from. Each suite finds its classes by reflection, so a new class appears in the Test Runner as soon as Unity has compiled it: every class deriving from the suite's base class that is concrete, not generic and has a parameterless constructor (every MonoBehaviour without a constructor of its own has one); in the assemblies EvoSim.Runtime, EvoSim.Http and EvoSim.Samples, in Student (everything under Assets/Student), and in Assembly-CSharp (scripts outside any assembly). The test probes of EvoSim.Testing and the editor code are left out; the modules your class names with RequiresModuleAttribute are added beside it first: a species module on the species under test, a world module under the World. A drink action is tested with its thirst. Testing a brain The brain suite is DecisionTests.BrainConformance (Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode/Decisions/DecisionTests.cs). It checks DEC-11 and DEC-12: one valid row per query, of the species' length, in query order, and the same row for the same query. It only looks at brains of the EvoSim assemblies, so it does not run yours. Copy it into your test file with your class: [Test, Description("DEC-11, DEC-12: one valid row per query, in order; the same query twice gives the same row")] public void MyBrainConforms() { var w = New().Ecology(48f).ReferencePhases().DefaultBrain<MyBrain>().Build(); var rng = new RandomStream(3, "queries"); var queries = new List<DecisionQuery>(); for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) { var s = w.FindSpecies(i % 2 == 0 ? "prey" : "predator"); var a = Place.Animal(s, Place.At(rng.Range(0f, 48f), rng.Range(0f, 48f))); w.Space.Rebuild(); var o = s.Observe(a, new SenseContext(w)); queries.Add(new DecisionQuery(s, new List<KeyValuePair<string, string>>(), o, s.Describe(o, TextStyle.V1), TextStyle.V1, a.Genome.BrainKey)); } var answer = w.DefaultBrain.Ask(queries); answer.Pending.Wait(); var again = w.DefaultBrain.Ask(queries); again.Pending.Wait(); for (int i = 0; i < queries.Count; i++) { Assert.IsNull(BrainAnswer.Check(answer.Row(i), queries[i].Species.Actions.Count), $"row {i}"); CollectionAssert.AreEqual(answer.Row(i), again.Row(i), "deterministic"); } } It needs using System.Collections.Generic; beside the usings of the generated file. A brain that calls a server (an HttpBrain) is tested against a fake server: set its Transport to a FakeHttpTransport before Build() (see An HTTP brain or mutator server). A complete unit test This test checks the sample DrinkAction: an animal 2 m from a pond walks to the shore and drinks. Your own tests have the same shape: build a world in code, place animals, give them an action, advance, assert. using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Samples; using EvoSim.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; public class DrinkActionTests : WorldFixture { [Test, Description("ACT-10 (22 §3): drink walks to the shore and resets thirst on arrival")] public void DrinkResetsThirst() { var w = New().Ground<PondGround>(20, 20).Food(0f, 0f).Phase<ActPhase>() .Species("prey", s => s.PreyBody().Action<DrinkAction>("drink").Module<Thirst>()).Build(); var sp = w.FindSpecies("prey"); var a = Place.Animal(sp, Place.At(10f, 15f)); // 2 m from the pond's shore var thirst = sp.Module<Thirst>().Value; a[thirst] = 50f; a.Choose("drink"); // no decision phase: it keeps this action w.Advance(3); Assert.AreEqual(0f, a[thirst], "drank"); Assert.IsFalse(w.Ground.IsWater(a.Position), "on the shore, not in the water"); } } New starts a WorldBuilder with seed 1234, and the fixture destroys the world after the test. The world has only the phases the test adds: here the act phase, so no brain is asked and the animal keeps the action given by Choose. Place.Animal puts an animal exactly where the test needs it, and Advance runs ticks. The Description is the test's documentation: say what it checks and name the rules it keeps. The reference set-ups (PreyBody, Ecology, Lab1, ReferencePhases) are in Lab; see Testing. Fakes and helpers Helper Use it to ScriptedBrain decide without a model. Its Policy maps a query to a row; ScriptedBrain.Prefer(species, "flee") builds a row that prefers one action and ScriptedBrain.Token(query, "Predator") reads one sense. It counts Calls and Batches, keeps every query in Seen, can answer DelayCalls calls late and fail on demand (FailWhen). Without a policy it answers uniformly. FakeMutator mutate without a model. Add it with FakeMutation. By default it appends quickly to the sentence; set Answer for another rule. It records every prompt in Prompts and can answer late or fail. FakeHttpTransport play a server for an HTTP brain or mutator client: FakeHttpTransport.Jev(), FakeHttpTransport.OllamaPoints(), or your own Respond. It records every request (Requests) and can fail (FailWith), hang or answer slowly. Stat check a statistic over many draws with a fixed seed: Stat.Binomial(successes, trials, p) within 4 standard errors, Stat.Mean, Stat.Uniform (a χ² test). CheckInvariants called after the other phases, add a phase that fails the test at the first broken invariant of 30 §5: an animal outside or on water, a NaN, a stat out of range, a duplicate id, a dead animal still listed, a bad probability row… Invariants runs the same checks at any moment. Draw every random number in a test from a fixed seed, the world's (New(seed)) or a RandomStream of your own (new RandomStream(7, "my-test")), so that a failing test fails the same way every time. Tests to copy The tests of the reference modules are the best models. They are in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode: To test Copy from any module, in the simplest form Samples/SampleTests.cs: one short test per sample (thirst, water sense, drink, seasons, slopes) a sense Senses/SenseTests.cs (tokens one by one, distance bands, situation texts) an action or an interaction Actions/ActionTests.cs (intents, reach, contested items) a locomotion Actions/MovementTests.cs (speeds, stop distances, corners, slopes) a stat or a death rule Animals/AnimalTests.cs (the energy table, causes of death) a mutation operator Mutation/MutationTests.cs (rates, same seed same result, clamping) a phase Core/TickLoopTests.cs (order, what later phases see) a brain Decisions/DecisionTests.cs; over HTTP, Http/HttpBrainTests.cs a food layer or cover Environment/EnvironmentTests.cs (queries against brute force) The teaching path EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Replace with stub ▸ … writes Assets/Student/Exercises/My<Reference>.cs and swaps the reference module for it in the open scenes (The teaching path). The stub is in the Student assembly, so the conformance suite of its kind runs it at once; it fails until you write the methods that throw. The reference module's own unit tests do not grade your stub: they build their worlds with the reference class by type (Action<RestAction>("rest")). To hold your version to the same expectations, copy such a test into your test file and put your class in the builder call (Action<MyRestAction>("rest")). Golden files Some tests compare an output with a file pinned from an accepted run, in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/Golden (Golden): File Pinned by Holds hashes.json RegressionTests.PinnedHashes (R-01) the events hash of 12 runs: two reference scenes × seeds 1234, 7, 42 × the random brain or a scripted prey, 2 000 ticks prompts.txt PromptTests (T-PROMPT-03) the assembled prompts of both reference species situations.tsv SenseTests (T-SENSE-08) the situation texts of 48 situations per species jev_text.txt HttpBrainTests the text the JEV brain sends for the example of 08 §7 A missing file is written from the current run; an existing one must match exactly, and the failure shows the first line that differs. To re-pin, delete the file, run its test once, and commit the new file with a message that says why. Re-pin only when the change was meant: a rule changed, a reference value changed, a prompt text was rewritten. Do not re-pin after a change that should not alter any run (a refactoring, comments): find what changed the behaviour. Hashes are compared on one machine only (RAND-12). Your modules in Assets/Student change no golden file unless you put them in a reference scene or change a reference module: try them in a copy of a scene, and restore any exercise stub (EvoSim ▸ Exercises ▸ Restore reference) before you run the regression tests. The slow tests (T3) Eleven tests carry the NUnit category T3: the regression tests of 30 §6 (pinned hashes, equivalences, soak, performance, the prototype's analysis tools) and the long scenarios (S01, S06, S10, S16, S17, S23). They run whole scenes for thousands of ticks: minutes each, the soak up to 30 minutes. Run them before a merge, from the Test Runner with the category filter set to T3, or headless: Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunRegression RunRegression writes its totals to Logs/EvoSim/Reports/regression-<date-time>.txt and exits with code 1 when a test failed (Running and building). Warning Tests that use a reference scene open it beside the current one and close it unsaved (WithScene(string, Func<World, string>)). If that scene is open in the editor, the test fails with "… is open in the editor: open another scene first": do that and run it again. Read next Testing: the EvoSim.Testing assembly in depth: the builder, the fixture, the test probes. 30 — Tests: every test id, the tiers, the conformance suites and the regression tests. The teaching path and the samples: modules to rewrite, and tested extensions to read.

extending/views.html.title: Views | EvoSim
extending/views.html.summary: Views A view shows an animal; it never changes it. Write an AnimalView subclass to colour, scale or animate the animals from their state, put it on a body prefab, and give the prefab to the species' Body. This page also shows how to make your own entities visible and how to add a panel of your own. If what you want must change the run (an animal that reacts to something), it is not a view: write a module instead (Extending EvoSim). How the views work at run time is in Views and real time. The base class The World places every view in its LateUpdate, then calls OnShow. A view has nothing else to do. Member You What it does, when it is called OnShow(Animal) override Every frame the view is shown, on the main thread, right after the World placed it. Its argument is the view's animal, as the last tick left it. Also called while the run is paused, or waits for a brain in the Responsive mode. The base does nothing AnimalId read the id of the animal shown, or -1 while the view waits in its pool Awake may write Unity's, called once when the pool makes the view: create your MaterialPropertyBlock, find child renderers What a view usually reads from its animal (every member of Animal is readable): Read Gives a.CurrentAction, a.Searching the current action (.Name is its name, e.g. flee), or null; true while it searches a.Generation, a.Age its generation (founders are 0) and its age in ticks a[stat] a stat's value; the id comes from its module, e.g. a.Species.Module<Energy>().Value a.IsBusy, a.BusyReason true while it can't act, and why (digesting after a meal) a.LastProbabilities the probabilities of its last decision, in action order a.Species, a.Genome its species and its genes Example: colour by generation A view that paints the body blue for the founders, shading to red at generation 20 and later. using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; /// <summary>Colours the body by generation: founders blue, generation 20 and later red.</summary> public class GenerationView : AnimalView { static readonly int ColorId = Shader.PropertyToID("_Color"); [SerializeField, Tooltip("The body's renderer.")] Renderer body; [SerializeField, Min(1), Tooltip("The generation shown fully red.")] int reddest = 20; MaterialPropertyBlock block; // sets the colour without copying the material int shown = -1; // the generation the body shows now void Awake() => block = new MaterialPropertyBlock(); public override void OnShow(Animal a) { if (body == null || a.Generation == shown) return; // nothing changed: no update shown = a.Generation; block.SetColor(ColorId, Color.Lerp(Color.blue, Color.red, Mathf.Clamp01(a.Generation / (float)reddest))); body.SetPropertyBlock(block); } } Put the class in Assets/Student (there is no script template for views; a new C# script file will do). Compare with what is shown rather than remembering the animal: a pooled view is reused for another animal when its own dies. ActionView is the reference view to read next: it updates two renderers, each only when its colour changed. Make a body prefab Duplicate Assets/EvoSim/Modules/Bodies/PreyBody.prefab into Assets/Student, or build your own. The root's pivot is the animal's feet: the World sets the root at the ground's height. The reference body is 1 m high and looks along +z, with a dark nose at the front, because the World turns the view toward where the animal moves. Put your view on the root. A root holds one AnimalView only: remove the ActionView of the copy first. Fill your view's fields (the body's renderer above). Leave out colliders. The pool disables every collider and moves every part to layer 2 anyway. Select the species, and on its Body set Prefab to your prefab and Size in meters: the prefab's scale is multiplied by it (prey 0.6, predator 0.9). Prewarm is the number of views made when the run starts (0 = the initial population). With no prefab, the species shows capsules of the Color field. A prefab with no AnimalView on its root gets a plain one: it follows its animal and shows nothing more. Rules your view must keep Read only (SPACE-12). Never write a stat, an action, a position or a genome, and call nothing that changes the World. The run must give the same events hash with Show Views on or off (RAND-11). No simulation random streams (RAND-01). Drawing from the World's streams would shift every later draw of the run. A visual effect that needs chance (a wobble, a blink) uses Time or Unity's own Random, which the simulation never reads. Main thread, every frame, every animal. Keep OnShow cheap: find components in Awake, change a renderer only when its value changed, and use a MaterialPropertyBlock; renderer.material copies the material for each view. Layer 2 and no colliders. The pool puts the view on Ignore Raycast (IgnoreRaycastLayer), which every sense ray leaves out, and disables its colliders. Don't change a layer or enable a collider at run time: a sense could then hit your view. Don't move the root. The World sets its position and rotation every frame, and the pool scaled it by Size. Animate child objects instead. Make your entities visible EntityMarkers draws one marker per entity of every EntityKind under the World. It reads them through EntityCount and EntityAt. A system derived from EntitySystem<T> implements both: your entities appear with no code, as grey 0.3 m cubes (the Other colour of EntityMarkers). Carcasses and eggs have their own shapes. A class derived from EntityKind directly must override EntityAt. Its default returns null, and an entity it doesn't return is not drawn. For a look of your own, write a run view like EntityMarkers: a component outside the World that, in LateUpdate, reads World.Service<FruitSystem>().Entities and places pooled objects without colliders, on IgnoreRaycastLayer. A panel of your own RunNumbers reads everything the overlay shows from the World's counters. A panel of your own can read it too. Give the camera a Blocks test so that clicks on your panel don't pick an animal; keep the overlay's test in it. using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; /// <summary>A panel at the bottom left: living animals and highest generation per species.</summary> public class PopulationPanel : MonoBehaviour { readonly RunNumbers numbers = new RunNumbers(); World world; WorldCamera cam; RunOverlay overlay; Rect panel = new Rect(8f, 0f, 260f, 0f); // in GUI coordinates: origin at the top left void Update() { if (world == null) world = FindAnyObjectByType<World>(); if (overlay == null) overlay = FindAnyObjectByType<RunOverlay>(); if (cam == null && (cam = FindAnyObjectByType<WorldCamera>()) != null) cam.Blocks = Covers; if (world != null && world.IsInitialized) numbers.Read(world); } // Screen points have their origin at the bottom left. bool Covers(Vector2 p) => panel.Contains(new Vector2(p.x, Screen.height - p.y)) || (overlay != null && overlay.Covers(p)); void OnGUI() { if (world == null || !world.IsInitialized) return; panel.height = 10f + 22f * numbers.Species.Count; panel.y = Screen.height - panel.height - 8f; GUILayout.BeginArea(panel, GUI.skin.box); foreach (var s in numbers.Species) GUILayout.Label($"{s.Name}: {s.Living} living, generation {s.MaxGeneration}"); GUILayout.EndArea(); } } Put it on the scene's Run views object. It only reads, like every run view. Test it A view needs frames, so check it in Play mode: Run the scene with your body and note the events hash (see Determinism and replay). Run it again with the same seed and Show Views off on the World. The hash must be the same. EvoSim's own play-mode tests do this in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/PlayMode/ViewPlayTests.cs: ViewsNeverChangeTheRun (T-SPACE-06) compares hashes with views on, off and uninterpolated, and ViewsHearTheirAnimal checks that a view of one's own (ShowProbeView) hears OnShow with its own animal every frame. Read next ActionView: the reference view. ActionColors: the action colours, to reuse. EntityMarkers, GroundView, RunOverlay: the run views, all read-only. Food, cover, entities and ground: entity systems of your own. Specification: 02 — Space and time (SPACE-12).

extending/worked-example-alarm-calls.htm.title: Worked example: alarm calls | EvoSim
extending/worked-example-alarm-calls.htm.summary: Worked example: alarm calls This page follows one change from idea to tested scene, written the way you would write yours: in Assets/Student, without touching Assets/EvoSim. The idea: a prey can call in passing, as it runs away or hides, at a cost in energy; its kin nearby hear the call and can flee or hide before they see the danger themselves. Evolution decides whether calling pays. The change touches the four kinds of extension: Piece Class Kind Page the world remembers calls AlarmCalls and FadeAlarmCalls a WorldService and a TickPhase Phases, services and world hooks an animal calls AlarmCallAction an AnimalAction done in passing (an overlay) with an interaction An action evolution tunes calling a TextGene on the action a gene, no code Genes kin hear the call AlarmSense a Sense A sense The files are Assets/Student/AlarmCalls.cs, FadeAlarmCalls.cs, AlarmCallAction.cs, AlarmSense.cs, the tests in Assets/Student/Tests/AlarmCallsTests.cs, and the scene builder in Assets/Student/Editor/AlarmCallsScene.cs. The code below is that code, with its /// comments left out. 1. The world: a list of calls Several modules share the calls, so they live in a service under the World. A call is a small struct: who, where, when, how far. The calls are kept in a List, in the order they were made, so every query gives the same answer in every run (RAND-05). The service draws no random number. public readonly struct AlarmCall { public readonly Species Species; public readonly int CallerId; public readonly Vector3 Position; public readonly int Tick; public readonly float Range; public AlarmCall(Species s, int id, Vector3 p, int tick, float range) { Species = s; CallerId = id; Position = p; Tick = tick; Range = range; } } public class AlarmCalls : WorldService { [SerializeField, Min(1)] int memory = 4; // ticks a call stays audible: one decision period readonly List<AlarmCall> calls = new List<AlarmCall>(); public int CallsMade { get; private set; } public override void Initialize() { calls.Clear(); CallsMade = 0; } public void Register(Animal caller, int tick, float range) { calls.Add(new AlarmCall(caller.Species, caller.Id, caller.Position, tick, range)); CallsMade++; } public bool IsAudible(AlarmCall c, int now) => now - c.Tick <= memory; public float? NearestHeard(Animal listener, int now) { float? best = null; foreach (var c in calls) // a list: the same order in every run { if (c.Species != listener.Species || c.CallerId == listener.Id || !IsAudible(c, now)) continue; float d = new Vector2(c.Position.x - listener.Position.x, c.Position.z - listener.Position.z).magnitude; if (d <= c.Range && (best == null || d < best.Value)) best = d; } return best; } public int Forget(int now) => calls.RemoveAll(c => !IsAudible(c, now)); } Old calls are already ignored by NearestHeard. A phase forgets them so the list stays short. It does nothing in a world without the service (TICK-07): public class FadeAlarmCalls : TickPhase { AlarmCalls calls; public override void Initialize() => calls = World.Service<AlarmCalls>(); public override void Run(TickContext t) { if (calls != null) calls.Forget(t.Tick); } } 2. The action: a call done in passing A chosen action runs every tick until the next decision (ACT-02), up to a whole decision period. A first version stood still to call: next to a predator, for up to 4 ticks, the caller paid 4 times and was caught, and evolution would only have learnt to keep quiet. That was an artefact of timing, not a result. So the call is an overlay, an action done in passing (Actions done in passing, ACT-07): Overlay returns true. When the brain's draw picks alarm, the engine draws a second action, the carrier, from the rest of the row (flee, hide, eat…), which moves the animal; the call itself happens once, on the tick of the decision. Act only plans (ACT-06), and plans no move: it asks for an interaction, and the act phase ignores an overlay's intent. The interaction runs after the carrier's, once the animal moved. It is the only place that changes the caller (its energy, through Energy) and the world (a new call). Its reach is unlimited, as in the sample DragAction: the call happens wherever the carrier took the animal. Nothing stops a call with no predator in sight, a false alarm: the gene and the brain decide whether that pays. The [RequiresModule] attribute makes validation warn when the World has no AlarmCalls (V-26), and makes the conformance suite add one. [RequiresModule(typeof(AlarmCalls))] public class AlarmCallAction : AnimalAction { [SerializeField, Min(1f)] float range = 20f; // meters [SerializeField, Min(0f)] float cost = 0.5f; // energy per call AlarmCalls calls; Energy energy; public override bool Overlay => true; // call, and do the next most likely choice (flee, hide…) protected override string DefaultDescription => $"give an alarm call that kin within {Bands.Number(range)} meters hear"; public override void Initialize() { calls = World.Service<AlarmCalls>(); energy = Species.Module<Energy>(); } public override void Act(Animal a, ActContext c) { if (calls != null) c.OnArrival(new Call(this)); // no intent: the carrier moves the animal } sealed class Call : IInteraction { readonly AlarmCallAction action; public Call(AlarmCallAction owner) { action = owner; } public float Reach => float.PositiveInfinity; // wherever the carrier took the caller public void Apply(Animal a, InteractionContext c) { if (action.energy != null) action.energy.Pay(a, action.cost); action.calls.Register(a, c.Tick, action.range); } } } The real file also writes a prompt rule ("An alarm call costs 0.5 energy; kin within 20 meters hear it.") and declares the action relevant when the Predator sense sees one (CTRL-10). The engine adds its own rule for the species, "Some actions are done in passing (alarm): the animal also does its next most likely choice." The species needs another action beside the overlay to carry the animal (V-19), which the prey of HideVsFlee has six times over. 3. The gene: how often to call An action needs a TextGene on its GameObject (V-05). No code: set its Founders to "Call out whenever you see a predator.", "Stay silent, save your energy.", "Warn your kin when danger is near." and "Call only when you are safe in cover.", keep Has Neutral ("No preference."), and set Contrast Pro to "Always give an alarm call." and Contrast Anti to "Never give an alarm call." for the brain tests (GENE-23). The species' LlmMutation then rewrites these sentences, and selection keeps the ones that pay. 4. The sense: did kin call? Three tokens, a V2 sentence per token with the distance in meters (SENSE-12), and no change to the world (SENSE-03): [RequiresModule(typeof(AlarmCalls))] public class AlarmSense : Sense { static readonly IReadOnlyList<string> tokens = System.Array.AsReadOnly(new[] { "none", "close", "far" }); [SerializeField, Min(0.5f)] float closeDistance = 10f; AlarmCalls calls; public override IReadOnlyList<string> Tokens => tokens; protected override string DefaultLabel => "Alarm"; public override void Initialize() => calls = World.Service<AlarmCalls>(); public override int Read(Animal a, SenseContext s) { float? d = calls != null ? calls.NearestHeard(a, s.Tick) : null; return d == null ? 0 : d.Value <= closeDistance ? 1 : 2; } public override string Write(int token, TextStyle style) { if (style != TextStyle.V2) return $"{Label}: {tokens[token]}."; string near = Bands.Number(closeDistance); return token == 1 ? $"A kin gave an alarm call less than {near} meters away." : token == 2 ? $"A kin gave an alarm call {near} meters away or more." : "No kin is giving an alarm call."; } } 5. The scene Assets/Student/Scenes/AlarmCalls.unity is the reference HideVsFlee scene plus four objects: Under the World's Environment: Alarm calls, with AlarmCalls. Under the World's Phases, just after Act: Fade alarm calls, with FadeAlarmCalls. Under Prey ▸ Actions, last: alarm, with AlarmCallAction and its text gene. Under Prey ▸ Senses, last: Alarm, with AlarmSense. You can add them by hand. The example builds them with a short editor script instead, so the scene can be rebuilt identically: EvoSim ▸ Student ▸ Build Alarm Calls Scene, or from the command line with the editor closed: Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod AlarmCallsScene.BuildFromCommandLine. The script lives in Assets/Student/Editor with its own editor-only assembly, Student.Editor. 6. The tests AlarmCallsTests derives from WorldFixture. It checks that a call is heard close or far by kin within range, and not by the caller, kin out of range or another species; that a call fades after memory ticks; that the call is made once while the carrier, flee, runs the animal away, and costs once; that a false alarm is possible; the prompt lines; the sense's texts; that nothing breaks without the service; and that the same seed gives the same events hash. A test gives an animal a carrier and an overlay with Choose(carrier, overlay). How often the overlay and each carrier are drawn is the engine's business, tested in OverlayTests. The heart of the first test: public class AlarmHearingTests : WorldFixture { [Test] public void KinWithinRangeHearTheCall() { var w = New().Flat(60, 60).Food(0f, 0f).Carcasses().Phase<ActPhase>().Service<AlarmCalls>("Alarm calls") .Species("prey", s => s.PreyBody().Action<AlarmCallAction>("alarm").Action<FleeAction>("flee") .Action<RestAction>("rest").Sense<AlarmSense>()) .Species("predator", s => s.PredatorBody().Action<RestAction>("rest")).Build(); var prey = w.FindSpecies("prey"); Place.Animal(w.FindSpecies("predator"), Place.At(5, 10)).Choose("rest"); var caller = Place.Animal(prey, Place.At(10, 10)); // flees, and calls where the flight took it var near = Place.Animal(prey, Place.At(15, 10)); caller.Choose("flee", "alarm"); // the carrier, then the overlay near.Choose("rest"); w.Advance(1); var sense = prey.Module<AlarmSense>(); Assert.AreEqual("close", sense.Tokens[sense.Read(near, new SenseContext(w))]); } } The four classes also go through the conformance suites: in the Test Runner, ConformanceTests ▸ SenseConformance ▸ AlarmSense, ActionConformance ▸ AlarmCallAction and PhaseConformance ▸ FadeAlarmCalls. 7. A run EvoSim ▸ Student ▸ Run Alarm Calls Headless (L0) runs the scene for 400 ticks with the random brain, twice, and logs what the calls did. With seed 1234 the prey decided 3 204 times and drew alarm 438 times; 438 calls were made (one per draw, beside its carrier, predator in sight or not), and 2 333 decisions were taken while hearing a call, 800 of which fled or hid. The two runs give the same events hash. The random brain chooses alarm without looking; with a real brain (L1, L2) the gene and the sense start to matter, and you can compare how often the prey calls, and how many prey survive, with and without the alarm action. Read next The samples: thirst, water, seasons and slopes, written the same way. Testing your module and Determinism and replay. Documenting your code: the /// comments of the real files follow it.

extending/world-modules.html.title: Phases, services and world hooks | EvoSim
extending/world-modules.html.summary: Phases, services and world hooks A world module sits under the World, outside every species, and serves all species at once. Write a TickPhase to make something happen every tick (seasons, weather, an epidemic), and a WorldService to share state or a query between modules (a calendar, a water map). Both derive from WorldModule, whose hooks let any world module react to births, deaths, new species and the end of the run. For a feature of one species, write a species module instead. A tick phase Member You What it does, when Run(t) must implement the phase's work, once per tick, in its place among the phases WaitsFor(t) may override the work the phase must wait for before Run, or null (the default) PhaseName may override the name in logs, stop reasons and the profiler; the class name by default PlaceAfter(other), PlaceBefore(other) call in Validate a fix that moves this phase just after or before another one (V-08) Initialize, Validate and the hooks may override inherited from WorldModule; a phase initialises after every species module Recipe 22 §9, adapted from the sample SeasonsPhase: in the second half of every year the grass regrows more slowly. using EvoSim; using UnityEngine; /// <summary>Slows the grass's regrowth in the second half of every year; must run before Environment.</summary> public class WinterPhase : TickPhase { [SerializeField, Min(2), Tooltip("Ticks per year (reference 2 000).")] int yearLength = 2000; [SerializeField, Range(0f, 1f), Tooltip("Regrowth factor in winter (reference 0.2).")] float winterFactor = 0.2f; [SerializeField, Tooltip("The food layer's name.")] string layer = "Grass"; FoodGrid food; public bool IsWinter(int tick) => tick % yearLength >= yearLength / 2; public override void Initialize() => food = World.Service<FoodGrid>(layer); public override void Run(TickContext t) { if (food != null) food.RegrowFactor = IsWinter(t.Tick) ? winterFactor : 1f; } public override void Validate(ValidationReport report) { if (World.Service<FoodGrid>(layer) == null) report.Error("V-20", this, $"Winter acts on the food layer '{layer}', which doesn't exist."); var environment = World.Phase<EnvironmentPhase>(); if (environment != null && IndexOf(environment) < IndexOf(this)) report.Error("V-08", this, "Winter must come before the Environment phase.", PlaceBefore(environment)); } int IndexOf(TickPhase p) { for (int i = 0; i < World.Phases.Count; i++) if (World.Phases[i] == p) return i; return -1; } } Where it goes. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ Phase writes an empty phase into Assets/Student, with a test. Add the component on a new child of the World's Phases object: its place among the children is its place in every tick. Here it must come before Environment, which applies the factor; the World inspector's phase list shows the order and moves a phase with ▲. The reference phases check their own order (V-08): Ask brains after Sense, Choose actions after Ask brains, Hatch after Breed. Waiting for asynchronous work A phase that needs an answer from another thread or a server returns it from WaitsFor as a Pending. The World runs the phase only when the pending work is done: in Responsive mode it comes back on a later frame, in Freeze mode it blocks on Wait (A tick, phase by phase). Build it with Done when Pending.Done() at once Pending.Of(task) the Task completes (a null task: at once) Pending.All(parts) every part is done; returns null for an empty list a ManualPending your code calls SetDone; in Freeze mode its completion runs at once using System.Threading.Tasks; using EvoSim; /// <summary>Computes next tick's rain on another thread while the rest of the tick runs.</summary> public class RainPhase : TickPhase { Task<float> forecast; // started by the previous tick public float Rain { get; private set; } public override void Initialize() { forecast = null; Rain = 0f; } public override Pending WaitsFor(TickContext t) => Pending.Of(forecast); public override void Run(TickContext t) { Rain = forecast != null ? forecast.Result : 0f; int next = t.Tick + 1; forecast = Task.Run(() => RainAt(next)); // pure: no World, no Unity object } static float RainAt(int tick) => System.Math.Sin(tick * 0.01) > 0.5 ? 1f : 0f; } The work on the other thread reads nothing of the World and touches no Unity object, and its result doesn't depend on when it finishes: the run is the same in both wait modes (RAND-11). The reference does the same with the brains (ChooseActionsPhase waits for World.Decisions.Pending) and the mutator (HatchPhase). A world service Member You What it does, when ServiceName may override the name modules find it by; its GameObject's name by default WritePromptRules(species, w) may override rule lines for one species' prompt, after the species' own modules wrote theirs Initialize, Validate and the hooks may override a service initialises before the species' modules exist /// <summary>The year's seasons, shared by every module that asks.</summary> public class Calendar : WorldService { [SerializeField, Min(2), Tooltip("Ticks per year (reference 2 000).")] int yearLength = 2000; public bool IsWinter(int tick) => tick % yearLength >= yearLength / 2; public override void WritePromptRules(Species species, PromptWriter w) => w.Rule($"Every {yearLength} steps, a winter of {yearLength / 2} steps slows the grass."); } Put it anywhere under the World but outside the species, for example under Environment. Other modules find it in their Initialize, by role, never through a field pointing into the scene (ARCH-08): Call Finds World.Service<T>() the first enabled service of type T (a class or an interface), or null World.Service<T>(name) the one whose ServiceName is name, such as the layer "Grass" World.ServicesOf<T>() all of them, in hierarchy order Layers and brains are found by name, so two of them may not share one (V-18). A service initialises before the species' modules: look up species modules later, in Begin or when first needed. Hooks Every world module, phase or service, may override these. Each is called on the world modules in hierarchy order. A species module has its own OnBorn and OnDied, for its species' animals only (Species modules). Hook Called Begin() once per run, after every module initialised and validation passed, before the founders spawn; never during Edit-mode validation. Place initial content here (the first food items). OnSpeciesAdded(species) when World.AddSpecies adds a species during the run, after its set-up and its species_created event, before its founders OnBorn(a) each animal of any species that joins the living, founders included, after its species' modules heard it OnDied(a, cause) each death, after it was recorded and the species' modules heard it; the animal is marked gone OnRunStopped(reason) once, when the run stops, whatever the reason; write and close your files here /// <summary>Counts the births and deaths of every species and reports them when the run ends.</summary> public class LifeCounter : WorldService { int born, died; public override void Initialize() { born = 0; died = 0; } public override void OnBorn(Animal a) => born++; public override void OnDied(Animal a, string cause) => died++; public override void OnRunStopped(string reason) => Debug.Log($"{born} births, {died} deaths ({reason})"); } An exception in OnRunStopped is logged, and the other modules still hear the stop. World.Configuring The static event Configuring is raised by every World in Awake, in Play mode, before the run exists. A launcher sets the seed, speed or brain there, or turns Start On Play off to start the run itself. The player's command line works this way (PlayerLauncher). public static class FrozenRuns { static void SetUp(World w) { w.Seed = 7; w.WaitMode = WaitMode.Freeze; } public static void Install() { World.Configuring -= SetUp; World.Configuring += SetUp; } public static void Uninstall() => World.Configuring -= SetUp; } The event is static: a handler stays subscribed across scenes and, when domain reload is off, across Play sessions. Always unsubscribe when you are done, and unsubscribe before subscribing so a handler never runs twice. Rules your module keeps Change only what the phase is responsible for (TICK-02); with nothing to do, return at once (TICK-07). Random numbers only from named streams: t.Stream(species, "purpose") or t.Stream("name") in a phase, World.Random.Get("world/" + ServiceName) for a service's map content (RAND-01, RAND-03, RAND-04). WaitsFor only looks: no random draw and no change to the world, since it may be asked several times per tick. Set up in Initialize, create content in Begin: Initialize and Validate also run in Edit mode. No static state (ARCH-07): several Worlds may run side by side. Test it The phase suite (T-TICK, ConformanceTests.PhaseConformance) runs every phase class 20 ticks in a world without animals, and checks that switching it off and on leaves a populated world's events hash unchanged. The test written by the Phase template builds a small world with your phase and advances it 10 ticks. Add a test that runs twice with the same seed (Determinism and replay), and see Testing your module. Read next The reference phases, from SensePhase to RecordPhase, and the sample SeasonsPhase. Services with hooks: FoodGrid (Begin), RunRecorder (Begin, OnRunStopped); a test phase that waits: DelayedPhase. The world and its modules, A tick, phase by phase. Food, cover, entities and ground and Recording and statistics: the specialised services.

guides/actions-and-movement.html.title: Actions and movement | EvoSim
guides/actions-and-movement.html.summary: Actions and movement The brain only picks an action. The action then does the work, every tick until the animal's next decision: it looks for its target, says where the animal wants to go and what to do on arrival. The species' locomotion moves the animal, an interaction (graze, strike, scavenge) happens if the target is within reach, and the metabolism charges the tick. This split keeps actions short and readable, and lets each species move in its own way (07). One animal's act step The act phase (ActPhase) runs these steps for every living animal, in the act order: flowchart TD B{Busy, or no action?} -->|yes| ST[Stay, no interaction] B -->|no| P[The action plans: an intent and an interaction] P --> M[The locomotion moves it: speed, stamina, ground] M --> R{Within reach, and the diet allows it?} R -->|yes| I[The interaction applies] R -->|no| S I --> S[Metabolism and stamina settle the tick] ST --> S S --> C[Busy countdown] Plan. The animal's action receives an ActContext and calls its methods. Nothing moves yet. Move. The species' Locomotion turns the intent into a movement and reports the meters moved. Interact. The InteractionResolver applies the planned interaction if the target is within reach, still there, and allowed by the eater's diet. Settle. Metabolism charges energy for what the animal did, and Stamina pays the meters or recovers. A busy animal's countdown drops by one. Planning with the act context An action never moves an animal and never changes another one (ACT-06). It only asks questions and states a plan: Kind Methods What they do Queries NearestAnimal, NearestReadyPartner, NearestResource, NearestCarcass, NearestEgg, NearestEntity<T>, NearestCover, InCover, IsReady, Vision Return only what the animal's senses could report: within its vision (20 m in the reference), never itself, never a killed animal, never an animal hidden from it in cover (ACT-05). null means nothing in sight. Intents WalkTo, RunTo (a point or an animal, with a stop distance), RunAwayFrom, WalkAwayFrom, Stay, Wander, Search Say where to go this tick. Running uses the species' running speed. Arrival OnArrival(Interaction), OnArrival(IInteraction) Say what to do once within reach: graze, strike, scavenge, eat an egg, or a custom effect. Before each action runs, the context is reset to stay, no interaction. The intent methods replace each other: the last call wins. The same goes for OnArrival. An action that calls nothing makes the animal stay. WalkTo and RunTo stop at the given distance and never overshoot it (MOVE-04). An animal already within that distance stays. The action looks its target up again every tick, so it follows a moving target (ACT-02). The reference actions Action Class Target Intent On arrival Searches when eat EatAction nearest food item of a layer its diet grazes walk to it (stop 0); stay if already on it graze, on the tick of arrival too no food in sight flee FleeAction nearest threat run straight away from it — no threat in sight hide HideAction nearest cover walk (or run) into it; stay once inside — no cover in sight, or no cover module follow FollowAction nearest animal of its own species walk toward it, stop at 1 m — no kin in sight rest RestAction — stay — never mate MateAction nearest ready partner walk toward it, stop at 1 m — (the breed phase breeds it) no ready partner in sight hunt HuntAction the nearer of the nearest prey and the nearest carcass it may eat; a carcass wins a tie run toward it, stop at 1 m strike the prey, or scavenge the carcass neither in sight The prey has eat, flee, hide, follow, rest and mate; the predator has hunt, follow, rest and mate (04 §5). Flee has an option from the prototype, Flee Into Cover (off in the reference): an animal already in cover stays, and cover within Cover Seek meters (6) is run into instead of running away. Mating itself is not an interaction: the mate action only brings the animal next to a partner, and the breed phase does the rest (ACT-13). Searching When an action has nothing to act on, it calls Search() (ACT-04). The animal wanders: it keeps its heading, and each tick turns by ±45° or ±90° with probability Wander Turn P (0.25 on the locomotion). Blocked by a border or an obstacle, it picks a new random heading. It walks. The first search after a decision sets the animal's Searching flag and counts one invalid choice for its species (the prototype's name). The next decision clears the flag. The <species>_invalid column of stats.csv counts them. Busy animals A busy animal (BusyTicks above 0) doesn't decide and doesn't move: the act phase gives it a stay plan with no interaction. It pays the rest cost and recovers stamina. The counter drops by one at the end of each tick that started busy. When it reaches 0, the animal has no action and decides at the start of the next tick (ANIM-30). In the reference only digestion makes animals busy: see Animals, stats and death. Moving Each species has exactly one locomotion component (MOVE-01, V-13). The reference KinematicLocomotion moves in straight lines, without physics (MOVE-04): The distance is the smallest of the speed (the animal's speed.walk or speed.run trait), its stamina budget and the intent's maximum distance. A stop distance is therefore never overshot. SlideTo(Vector3, Vector3) moves along that line as far as walkable ground allows. Blocked by a border or an obstacle, the animal slides along it. If that made no progress, SideStep(Vector3, float, RandomStream) takes a step of the same length in a random direction, drawn from the species' actions stream. The locomotion sets the position and returns the meters moved (MOVE-06). The stamina budget is the animal's stamina in meters (ANIM-21): an exhausted animal can't move, whatever it chose. A species without a stamina module has no limit. Whatever the locomotion does is the tick's result (MOVE-01); after it, the act phase turns the animal toward where it moved (a wandering animal keeps its own heading). If a locomotion ever leaves an animal on non-walkable ground, the act phase puts it back and logs a warning (MOVE-02). Speeds are traits, so number genes can change them (MOVE-03). Reference: prey walk and run 1 m per tick, predators walk 1 and run 2. A predator outruns a prey over short chases; the prey has twice the stamina (07 §4). Interactions and reach After moving, in the same tick, the planned interaction applies if the target is within reach (ACT-10) and both sides allow it: the target has an Edible component and the eater's Diet lists it (SPEC-13). See The food web. Interaction Built with Reach (reference) Effect graze Interaction.Graze(item) 0.5 m from the item the item is consumed (an item goes to the first animal that reaches it); the eater gains its energy strike Interaction.Strike(animal) 1 m with the hunter's kill chance, the prey is killed; the hunter eats it and digests; a carcass may appear scavenge Interaction.Scavenge(carcass) 1 m one portion is eaten; the eater gains its energy and digests eat egg Interaction.EatEgg(egg) 0.5 m the egg is eaten and never hatches (REPRO-23) custom OnArrival(IInteraction) its own Reach, from the point the intent was heading to whatever its Apply does Kills. A hunter strikes at most once per tick (ACT-12); a miss uses that strike too. The chance that a strike kills is the hunter's kill.chance trait (Kill Chance on its diet, 0.5 in the reference), drawn from the hunter species' actions stream. An animal standing in cover that hides it from the hunter is never struck (ENV-11). A killed animal is marked at once: for the rest of the tick it is not sensed, not targeted, doesn't act and doesn't breed. It is removed in the death phase (ANIM-41). A prey that survives a strike can be struck again by another hunter in the same tick. Act order The act order is the Order setting of the act phase (ACT-30). The random orders come from the act-order stream, so a seed repeats them (ACT-32). Order How animals take turns Species In Turn (reference) species in the World's order; within a species, a fresh random order each tick. Each animal plans, moves, interacts and settles before the next one starts, so prey move before predators strike. All Mixed every animal of every species in one fresh random order each tick, one after another. Simultaneous every action plans from the state at the start of the phase; each locomotion moves its animals as a group; interactions apply in a fresh random order (a contested item goes to the first one drawn); then every animal that was not killed settles. In the two sequential orders an animal acts on the state left by those before it: positions, eaten items, kills (ACT-31). Reference numbers are measured with Species In Turn (ACT-33). After the move: the metabolism Each living animal then pays for its tick, once (ANIM-20): a base cost plus a cost per meter moved, or a lower rest cost when it stood still resting or busy, plus any extra cost its locomotion reports (slopes, mud). Then its stamina pays the meters moved, or recovers. The numbers are in Animals, stats and death. The main types Type Role AnimalAction A behaviour the brain can choose; plans one tick through the context ActContext What an action may ask and plan; reused for every animal Intent Where the animal wants to go: direction, walk or run, farthest distance Interaction What to do on arrival: graze, strike, scavenge, eat an egg, or custom Locomotion How a species moves; KinematicLocomotion is the reference MoveContext What a locomotion gets: ground, distance, random streams, stamina budget InteractionResolver Applies interactions after moving: reach, diet, kill chance ActPhase Runs the whole act step in the act order Settings Where Field Reference Meaning Act phase Order Species In Turn the act order Act phase Graze Reach, Strike Reach, Scavenge Reach 0.5, 1, 1 m how close an interaction needs the animal; eggs use the graze reach Locomotion Walk Speed, Run Speed prey 1 and 1, predator 1 and 2 m per tick defaults of the speed.walk and speed.run traits Locomotion Wander Turn P 0.25 chance per tick that a wandering animal turns Diet Kill Chance 0.5 default of the hunter's kill.chance trait Follow, Mate, Hunt Stop At 1 m stop this far from the target Eat Target empty a layer name, empty for every layer the diet grazes, or egg:<species> Flee From, Listed Threats whom to flee: the species' threats, or listed species by id or name Hide Run off run into cover instead of walking In the editor Scene view, in Play mode: select an animal to see its vision, a line to its target and a circle coloured by its action. The EvoSim overlay can write each animal's action letter above it. Animal Inspector (Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Animal Inspector): the selected animal's current action and target, its busy reason, its stats. Go further Add an action or an interaction, Add a locomotion. The food web: who may eat whom, and what a meal gives. A tick, phase by phase: where the act phase sits in the tick.
