guides/animals-and-stats.html.title: Animals, stats and death | EvoSim
guides/animals-and-stats.html.summary: Animals, stats and death An animal is plain data: an Animal record owned by its species, not a GameObject. It holds where the animal is, what it is doing, and its numbers: stats that change during its life (energy, stamina) and traits fixed at birth (speeds, maximum stamina). Modules declare the stats and traits they need, so a species without a stamina module has no stamina at all (ANIM-11). This page covers the record, the reference stats, what a tick costs, busy states and how animals die. The animal record Fields Meaning Written by Id, Species unique id in the run, never reused (ANIM-02); its species for life creation Origin, Generation, Parents, BornTick, Genome "founder", "immigrant" or "birth"; 0 for founders and newcomers, else one more than the larger of its parents' generations creation Age ticks since birth or hatching the death phase, +1 per tick Position, Heading where it stands; the direction it faces, in degrees the locomotion; the act phase and wandering Action, Searching, BredThisPeriod index of its current action (-1: none); whether it searches; whether it bred since its last decision the choose-actions phase; ActContext.Search; the breed phase BusyTicks, BusyReason ticks left busy, and why a module such as Digestion; the act phase counts down Killed, KilledBy struck dead this tick, and by whom the interaction resolver Meals, Offspring items grazed, kills and portions eaten; babies parented every meal; the breed phase IsGone dead or migrated; the record stays readable RecordDeath(Animal, string) MetersMoved, TargetId, TargetPoint this tick's movement, and what its action was about the act phase LastObservation, LastSituation, LastProbabilities its last decision, for the inspector the choose-actions phase a[stat], a.Trait(trait) the values of the declared stats and traits the modules that use them Modules may add stats and traits, never untyped fields (ANIM-01): what belongs to one animal goes in its stats. Stats and traits Stat Trait What a number that changes during life a number fixed at birth Examples energy, stamina, thirst speed.walk, speed.run, stamina.max, stamina.regen, kill.chance, maturity, vision Declared with DeclareStat(name, start, min, max) DeclareTrait(name, default, min, max) Id StatId TraitId Read a[id] a.Trait(id) Write a[id] = v, clamped to its range (ANIM-22) only at creation, unless declared changeable (ANIM-17) Each module declares what it needs in Declare, on the species' SpeciesBuilder, before any animal exists. The ids it gets back are how it reads and writes the values later. Declaring a name that already exists returns the first declaration (V-38 warns if they differ). Anyone can look a declaration up by name on Species.Declarations. A stat starts at a fixed value (Fixed(float)) or full, at a trait's value (FullTrait(TraitId)). Its maximum can be a trait: stamina is capped by each animal's own stamina.max. A trait starts at its default, the module's setting; a number gene may replace or scale it (ANIM-15). Modules always read the trait, never their own setting, so a gene changes behaviour with no extra code (ANIM-16). See Genes and mutation. Energy and stamina Energy declares the stat energy. Founders and newcomers start at 60, babies get the energy their parents pay for them (40, the litter's Child Energy), and the maximum is 100: a meal never raises it higher. It has no minimum. At 0 or below, the animal starves at the next death check. Stamina is the number of meters an animal can still move. It declares the traits stamina.max (prey 60, predators 30) and stamina.regen (2 per tick), and the stat stamina, which starts full. Each meter moved costs one point; the locomotion never moves an animal farther than its stamina (ANIM-21). A tick without movement (less than 1 mm, ANIM-23) brings back stamina.regen points, up to the maximum, and costs 0.3 energy while stamina is below full. Metabolism: what a tick costs Metabolism charges every living animal once per tick, right after it acted (ANIM-20), from what it did: the meters its locomotion reported, its action, and whether it was busy at the start of the tick. Situation (reference values, prey and predators) Energy Stamina moved d meters −0.7 − 0.5 × d −d still, with the rest action −0.2 +2, up to the maximum still, any other action −0.7 +2, up to the maximum still and busy (digesting) −0.2 +2, up to the maximum while stamina recovers (still, not full) −0.3 more — graze one food item +25 — a kill +60 — a carcass portion +30 — So walking 1 m costs 1.2 energy, a predator running 2 m costs 1.7, and a predator can run at full speed for 15 ticks from full stamina. A locomotion may add a cost of its own for the move (slopes, mud), and the metabolism may also charge a cost that grows with a trait (off in the reference; see Stats, costs and death rules). Busy states and digestion While an animal is busy it doesn't decide and doesn't move; it pays the busy cost and recovers stamina (ANIM-30). A module that makes an animal busy sets BusyTicks and gives a reason, shown in the inspector (ANIM-31). The act phase counts down at the end of each busy tick. At 0 the animal has no action, and it decides at the start of the next tick. In the reference only Digestion does it, on the predator. After a kill or a carcass portion the eater is busy for round(Digest Ticks × gain / Reference Gain) ticks: 50 after a kill (+60), 25 after a portion (+30), with the reason digesting. Grazing never makes an animal busy, and the prey has no digestion module. Age, maturity and generations Every living animal ages by one tick per tick, in the death phase, babies born that tick included (ANIM-35). An animal is an adult when its age reaches its maturity trait (150 ticks, declared by the MatingRule, ANIM-36); an adult with at least 50 energy is ready to mate. Founders and newcomers are generation 0; a baby is one generation more than the larger of its parents' generations. See Reproduction and population. Death The death phase (DeathPhase) runs once per tick: Animals killed this tick die, with the cause killed and the killer's id. Every living animal ages by one tick. Each DeathRule of the species is asked about every living animal, in module order. The first rule that names a cause decides; later rules are not asked about that animal. Each death is recorded once (ANIM-42), and the dead leave their species before the next tick's decisions (ANIM-43). Cause Rule When (reference) stats.csv column starvation Starvation energy ≤ 0 <species>_deaths_starve old_age OldAge age above Max Age (1 500 ticks) <species>_deaths_age killed a strike (ANIM-41) killed by a hunter <species>_deaths_pred migrated the cap rule (mode Migrate), in the migration phase the species is above its cap <species>_deaths_migrated Modules may add causes of their own, such as thirst; each gets a <species>_deaths_<cause> column (ANIM-40). The main types Type Role Animal One animal: plain data, read and written by every module SpeciesBuilder Collects the stats and traits a species' modules declare StatId, TraitId The ids to read and write a stat or a trait Energy, Stamina The reference stats Metabolism What a tick costs Digestion Makes an eater busy after a kill or a portion DeathRule A cause of death; Starvation and OldAge in the reference Settings In the reference scenes these modules sit on the species' Stats and Life children. Module Field Reference Energy Max, Start 100, 60 Stamina Max, Regen Per Tick, Regen Energy Cost prey 60, predators 30; 2; 0.3 Metabolism Base Cost, Move Cost, Rest Cost 0.7, 0.5 per meter, 0.2 Metabolism Cost Trait, Cost Per Unit empty (none), 0.005 Digestion (predators) Digest Ticks, Reference Gain 50, 60 Old Age Max Age 1 500 ticks Mating Rule Mate Energy, Maturity 50, 150 ticks Litter Child Energy 40 In the editor Animal Inspector (Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Animal Inspector): in Play mode, click an animal in the Scene view to read its stats, traits, genome, current action, busy reason, parents and offspring. Species inspector: select a species and press Show the computed tables to list every declared stat and trait, with its default, its range and the module that declared it. Ecology Monitor (Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Ecology Monitor): population and deaths by cause over time. Go further Add a stat, change costs, add a death rule. Actions and movement: where moving and resting come from. Reproduction and population: litters, caps and newcomers. Specification: 05 — Animals, stats and life cycle.

guides/brains-and-decisions.html.title: Decisions and brains | EvoSim
guides/brains-and-decisions.html.summary: Decisions and brains An animal does not choose every tick. Every few ticks it decides: its senses describe its situation, a brain reads that situation with the animal's genes and gives one probability per action, and the animal draws its next action from those probabilities. The brain is usually a language model, so it is the slow part of a run. Most of this page is about asking it as little as possible: answers are remembered, shared and cached, and the run still repeats exactly with its seed (08 — Decisions, brains and prompts). Who decides, and when Every Decision Period ticks (World setting, 4 in the reference) a living animal decides (DEC-01). The reference scenes stagger decisions: each species has a DecisionSchedule with Staggered on, so an animal decides when (tick + id) % 4 == 0. About a quarter of the animals decide on each tick, instead of all of them every fourth tick (DEC-04). A species without a schedule decides all together on ticks 0, 4, 8…, as the Python prototype did. An animal without an action decides on the next tick, whatever the schedule says: a baby, a newcomer, or an animal whose busy state ended on the previous tick. A busy animal never decides, for example one that is digesting a meal (DEC-02). At a decision, the animal's searching and bred this period flags are cleared (DEC-03). All the animals that decide in a tick sense the same state: the state at the start of the tick (SENSE-04). A decision's path Three phases at the start of every tick carry each decision. flowchart TD S[Sense phase: observation and situation text] --> Q[Ask brains: build the query] Q --> M{In the memo?} M -->|yes| R[Row] M -->|no| D{Same key earlier this tick?} D -->|yes| R D -->|no| C{In the answer cache?} C -->|yes| R C -->|no| B[One batch per brain: Brain.Ask] B --> W[Choose actions: wait, check the row] W --> R R --> T[Temper with τ, draw with the sampling stream] Sense (SensePhase) picks who decides, reads their senses and writes their situation texts (Senses and prompts). Each decision is a Decision in Decisions. Ask brains (AskBrainsPhase) builds each animal's query, answers what it can from the memo and the cache, and sends the rest to the brains. Nothing in the world changes here. Choose actions (ChooseActionsPhase) waits for the brains, checks each row, stores good rows, and draws each animal's action. The query A DecisionQuery is everything a brain receives for one animal (DEC-10): Member What it holds Species the species: its actions give the row's length and order Genes the genes the brain reads, as (label, sentence) pairs, in locus order Observation, Situation the tokens, and the text in the world's style GenomeKey a hash of the species id and the alleles the brain reads (DEC-31) Attachments images or other attachments from senses, usually none AnimalId the deciding animal, for brains with memory A text brain builds its prompt with Prompt. Number genes the brain doesn't read are not in the genome key, so they don't make the same situation look new. The memo Within a run, the answer for a key (species, brain, genome key, observation) is computed once and reused (DEC-30). A hit gives exactly what the brain answered. Since animals of one species share many genes and few situations, the memo answers 52–80 % of prey decisions in the reference runs. The World's Memo Capacity (262 144 keys, about 10 MB) bounds it: beyond it, new situations go to the brain and its cache again. A failed answer is never stored (DEC-34). Duplicates in a tick. When two animals of one tick have the same key, the query is sent once and the second animal shares the answer (DEC-32). The answer cache The memo forgets everything when the run stops. The AnswerCache keeps answers across runs (DEC-33). It is a service under the World's Brains object, and a brain uses it when its Use Cache is on (on for the HTTP brains). Answers go to Library/EvoSim/AnswerCache, one .jsonl file per brain id. A key covers everything that can change an answer: the brain and its model (with its revision or digest), the prompt id, the brain's mode, the text style, the genome key and the situation text. A run repeated with the same seed replays from the cache without any model call, bit for bit. Delete the folder to ask the models again. The mutator caches its answers in the same folder. Batches and brains Each species is decided by one brain: its own Brain field, or else the World's Default Brain (DEC-13). A brain is a component under the World's Brains object; validation refuses a species without one, or a brain that is disabled or under a species (V-10). It also checks each brain's limits against the species that use it: the number of actions and the prompt length (DEC-14, V-11). All the queries of a tick that go to one brain are sent in one call to Ask (DEC-15). A brain that can't mix species gets one batch per species. The brain returns a BrainAnswer: now, with every row filled, for brains that compute in C# (the random brain); later, for brains behind a server: requests leave from another thread and the rows arrive while the editor goes on drawing. Waiting for the brain The choose-actions phase waits until every answer of the tick is in (TICK-03). The World's Wait Mode says how: Wait Mode What happens Responsive the tick pauses at that phase and Unity keeps drawing; the panel says waiting for JEV: 6 queries. The editor default. Freeze the main thread blocks until the answers are in. Tests and batch runs use it. Both modes give the same run and the same events hash (SPACE-14). A decision never uses an old observation. Checking rows and failures Every row is checked (DEC-11): one entry per action of the species, in action order, each ≥ 0, summing to 1 ± 10⁻⁶. A query that failed after its retries, or a row that fails the check, is a failure: With the brain's Strict setting on (the reference for HTTP brains), the run stops cleanly, before anything in the world changed in that tick, and every output is written (DEC-40, RAND-20). Run it again: the answers already received come back from the answer cache. With Strict off, the animal draws from a uniform row, and the failure is counted (failures in summary.json). A failure is never stored in the memo or the cache (DEC-34), so the next run asks again. Retries, time-outs and connection tests are on An HTTP brain or mutator server. Drawing the action Before the draw, the row is tempered with the World's Sampling Temperature τ: each p becomes p^(1/τ), then the row is renormalised (DEC-20, Sampling). τ < 1 sharpens towards the likeliest action, τ > 1 flattens towards uniform. The reference is τ = 1, which changes nothing. Row τ = 0.5 τ = 1 τ = 2 eat 0.6, flee 0.3, rest 0.1 0.78, 0.20, 0.02 0.6, 0.3, 0.1 0.47, 0.33, 0.19 The draw uses the species' sampling random stream, so the seed decides it (RAND-03). The memo and the cache keep the brain's own rows, untempered. The animal keeps its last observation, situation text and row for the inspector (DEC-21). The reference brains Brain Class Needs How it answers Limits Random RandomBrain nothing at once: a uniform row, whatever the genes and the situation none JEV JevBrain vLLM on localhost:8000 serving autotrust/JEV-9B with its LoRA jev-decision, plus the decision head and calibration files in Assets/EvoSim/Data/Models/JEV-9B later: one forward pass per query; the actions are lettered options, and a probability comes from each letter's log-probability 16 actions; prompts of 1 024 tokens, its training length Ollama points OllamaPointsBrain Ollama on localhost:11434 with gemma4:12b later: one chat call per query; the model shares 100 points between the actions, and the points become a row (DEC-41) prompts up to the Context Length, 4 096 tokens Scripted ScriptedBrain tests only rows from a policy written in the test, or given rows per situation; can answer late, fail, or refuse to mix species set by the test The random brain is the null model: random hunters can't feed themselves, which shows that the brain matters. It is also the default brain of a new world, so a world runs without any server. The full reference scenes use JEV by default; their Brains object also holds a Random and an Ollama points brain to switch to. JEV and Ollama points are strict and use the answer cache by default. Settings Where Field Reference Effect World Decision Period 4 ticks ticks between two decisions World Sampling Temperature 1 τ, at least 0.01 World Memo Capacity 262 144 most keys the memo keeps; 0 = no limit World Default Brain JEV (Random in a new world) the brain of species that name none World Wait Mode Responsive how a tick waits for answers Species Brain empty this species' own brain Decision Schedule Period, Staggered 0 (the World's), on this species' own period, and staggering Any brain Strict, Use Cache off / on for HTTP brains stop on failure; use the answer cache Answer Cache Folder, Read, Write Library/EvoSim/AnswerCache, on, on where the cache lives; answer from it; store new answers In the editor Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Animal Inspector: in Play mode, pause and click an animal to see its last situation and the brain's probabilities as bars. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Ask the Brain: build a genome, pick a situation, and ask several brains side by side. Directed test asks with a gene's pro sentence, then with its anti sentence. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Brain Health: each brain's host, a Test connection button, its model, latency and failures, and the answer cache's size and hits. The species inspector's Prompt preview shows the exact text a brain receives (Senses and prompts). summary.json reports, per species, memo_hit_rate and backend_s (time spent waiting for the brain), and for the run llm_calls, cache_hits and failures (Recording and outputs). Go further A brain: write a brain, and change when animals decide (Decision timing). An HTTP brain or mutator server: JEV, Ollama, and brains behind your own server. A tick, phase by phase and Determinism and replay: waiting, streams and replay. API: Brain, BrainAnswer, DecisionQuery, DecisionMemo, AnswerCache, DecisionState, Sampling. Specification: 08 — Decisions, brains and prompts.

guides/determinism.html.title: Determinism and replay | EvoSim
guides/determinism.html.summary: Determinism and replay The same scene, seed and brain answers give the same run, event for event, on the same machine and build (RAND-11). It doesn't matter how the run is driven: Responsive or Freeze, one tick per frame or a thousand, views on or off, in the editor, headless or in a player build. That is what makes a comparison between two gene pools fair, lets a long run with a language model be replayed without calling the model again, and turns "it behaved oddly at tick 4 000" into a bug you can reproduce. This page explains the mechanisms and the rules your code keeps so that it stays true. Random streams Every random number of the simulation comes from a RandomStream: a PCG32 generator whose starting state is the SHA-256 of the text seed/name, for example 1234/prey/sampling. The World's RandomStreams hands out one stream per name. The same seed and name always give the same numbers, and draws from one stream never shift another stream's numbers (RAND-02). Streams are per purpose and, where a species is involved, per species (RAND-03): Stream Used for world, world/<layer> the map: terrain, cover patches, initial food; they use the world seed <layer> (e.g. Grass) the regrowth of one food layer act-order the order animals act in (ACT-32) <species>/founders founder and newcomer genomes and positions <species>/sampling drawing actions from the brain's probabilities <species>/actions wandering, sidesteps, strike rolls <species>/litter litter sizes, babies' headings <species>/mutation crossover and mutation choices, drawn at conception <species>/migration who leaves above the cap So adding a species doesn't change the draws of the others, and adding a food layer doesn't change another layer's map. A purpose of your own is just a new name: t.Stream(s, "lightning") makes prey/lightning on first use. The world seed is the run seed unless Separate World Seed is on: then many runs can share one map while everything else varies (RAND-04). The names world and act-order are reserved: no species id (V-07) or layer name (V-18) may take them. The events hash Every event (a founder, a birth, a death, an immigrant, an egg lost, a new species) is one line of canonical JSON, keys sorted (RAND-10). The World's EventLog chains them into a running SHA-256: it starts from the hash of the two seeds, and each event's hash covers the previous hash and the event's line. The final hash identifies the run: two runs with the same hash recorded the same events in the same order, and two seeds never share a hash (RAND-13). Where What World.Events.Hash, ShortHash 64 hex digits, and the first 16 summary.json in the run folder events_hash, events_sha, and events (the count) a headless run's result line, the player with -quitAtEnd the hash at the end What a replay needs Ingredient Where it lives the configuration the scene; run_info.json lists every serialized setting of the World's tree under settings the seed and the world seed the World's Seed and World Seed; run_info.json the brain's answers within a run, the decision memo; across runs, the answer cache, Library/EvoSim/AnswerCache by default, which also keeps the mutator's answers the same machine and build floating-point results may differ across machines and scripting backends; hashes are compared on one machine only (RAND-12) A language model may not answer the same question twice in the same way. The answer cache removes that doubt: a live run writes every answer to it, and running the same command again replays from it with no model call (RAND-21, test T-RAND-06). To replay in a player build, give it the cache folder with -cache. A brain with a memory of its own is neither memoised nor cached: its runs repeat only if the brain itself does. Replay a player run in the editor A run watched in the player can be replayed headless in batch mode, to check its hash or to probe it, without calling the models again. Two things make this go wrong silently: the player writes its answer cache next to the exe by default, and FromCommandLine has no -cache option and no replay-only mode. It reads the project's Library/EvoSim/AnswerCache, and any answer missing there becomes a real model call, with no warning. So: Run the player on the project's cache. Pass -cache with the absolute path of the project's cache (a relative path is taken from the build's folder), and the level's arguments (Run levels): EvoSim.exe -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -minutes 30 -run my-live -cache "C:\path\to\project\Library\EvoSim\AnswerCache" -quitAtEnd Read the run's length. Open Logs/EvoSim/runs/my-live/summary.json next to the exe and note ticks and events_hash. Close the editor, then replay exactly that many ticks, at the same level, from the repository root: & $U -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.FromCommandLine -do headless -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 9000 -level L2 -run my-live-replay -quit ($U is the Unity.exe path, as in Batch mode; 9000 stands for the ticks of step 2.) Read the result line, the last line of Logs/EvoSim/realtime-batch.txt. Its hash must equal the live run's events_hash, and it must say brain calls 0 and mutator calls 0: any other number means answers were missing from the cache and the models were asked again, so the replay is not a replay. Don't trust the exit code: FromCommandLine exits with 0 whatever happened, a failure included (the line then starts with FAILED). A model server that was down when the live run started records the model as @unknown; the replay then misses the cache. Start the servers and check them in Brain Health before a live run you want to replay. The same run everywhere The World makes the run independent of how it is driven: a decision always waits for its answers; it is never made on old observations (SPACE-13); every random draw happens in a phase, on the main thread, at a fixed point of the tick: mutation choices are drawn at conception, not when the mutator answers; the views, the camera and the overlays only read the simulation (SPACE-12); views have no collider and sit on a layer the sense rays ignore. The tests check it: Freeze and Responsive give the same hash with late answers (T-SPACE-07, R-04), one tick per call gives the same hash as ten (R-04), views shown or hidden give the same hash (T-SPACE-06), a late mutator changes nothing (T-MUT-10), the reference scenes keep their pinned hashes (R-01, Tests/Golden/hashes.json), and each scenario run twice gives one hash (EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarios). The rules that keep it No other randomness (RAND-01): no UnityEngine.Random, no System.Random, no Guid.NewGuid, no clock used as a seed. Draw from the stream you are given, or ask the World for one by name. One stream per purpose and species (RAND-02, RAND-03): a species' draws come from its own streams, so adding a species changes nothing for the others. Ordered loops only (RAND-05): loop over lists, in creation or id order. Never decide by iterating a Dictionary or a HashSet, whose order is not defined; looking a key up in one is fine. No time. Never read Time.deltaTime, Time.time, a frame count or the wall clock in simulation code: the tick is the only clock (SPACE-10). Views only read (SPACE-12). A view never writes to an animal or to the world. Asynchronous work doesn't leak its timing. Work on another thread never touches the World or a Unity object, and its result doesn't depend on when it finishes. The phase that needs it waits through WaitsFor (TICK-03). WaitsFor only looks. In Responsive mode it is asked again at every call while the tick waits: it must not draw random numbers or change the world. No statics (ARCH-07). Two Worlds may run side by side, and a World runs again after Initialize: keep state in your module's fields and reset it in Initialize. The static checks Tests/EditMode/Core/StaticChecks.cs (tier T0, Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, EditMode) reads the source code instead of running it: Test What it looks for NoGlobalRandomness (T-RAND-01) UnityEngine.Random, new System.Random(, Guid.NewGuid, DateTime.Now.Ticks and the like NoIterationOverHashCollections (T-RAND-04) a foreach over a Dictionary or a HashSet (or their Keys, Values) ModulesKeepNoAnimalState (T-CORE-05) a species module field that holds animals or maps animal ids CoreNamesNoSpecies (T-CORE-08) a species or action name written in the core code They scan Assets/EvoSim/Runtime, Http and Samples, not your folder: in your own code the rules are yours to keep. The conformance suites check behaviour instead. A phase, for example, must run without animals and leave a populated world's hash unchanged when it is switched off and on (T-TICK). Add a test of your own that runs twice. This one tests the LightningPhase of A tick, phase by phase: public class LightningTests : WorldFixture { [Test, Description("RAND-11: the same seed gives the same run")] public void SameSeedSameRun() { string Run(string name) { var w = New(7, name: name).Lab1(prey: 20, predators: 3).Phase<LightningPhase>().Build(); w.Advance(300); return w.Events.Hash; } Assert.AreEqual(Run("first"), Run("second")); } } When two runs disagree Compare the configurations. Diff the two run_info.json files: seed, world seed, wait mode, brain, controls and every serialized setting are there. A difference here is usually the whole story. Find the first differing event. Compare the two events.jsonl files line by line, for example with git diff --no-index runA/events.jsonl runB/events.jsonl. The t field of the first differing line is the first tick where the runs visibly part. Events are births and deaths, so the real cause can be a few ticks earlier. Find the first differing tick. Build both worlds in a test, advance them one tick at a time, and compare a fingerprint of every animal after each tick: static string Fingerprint(World w) => string.Join(";", w.AllSpecies.SelectMany(s => s.Animals) .Select(x => $"{x.Id}:{x.Position.x:R},{x.Position.z:R},{x.Action}")); for (int t = 0; t < 300; t++) { a.Advance(1); b.Advance(1); Assert.AreEqual(Fingerprint(a), Fingerprint(b), $"the runs part at tick {t}"); } Find the phase. Advance both worlds to the tick before, then run that tick's phases by hand, one by one, as the tests do with w.Phases[i].Run(w.Context), and compare after each. This skips the waiting, so use a brain that answers at once, such as the random brain, and don't advance these worlds afterwards. Look for the usual causes in the code that runs there: an iteration over a Dictionary or HashSet, a draw from the wrong stream or in WaitsFor, a static field, state not reset in Initialize, a read of Time, or a result computed on another thread. Go further A tick, phase by phase: waiting, stop conditions, the tick context. Decisions and brains: the memo and the answer cache. Running and building: headless runs, batch scenarios, the player's -cache. Recording and outputs: the files of a run folder. Specification: 12 — Tick order and determinism.

guides/editor-tooling.html.title: Editor tooling | EvoSim
guides/editor-tooling.html.summary: Editor tooling The Unity editor is where you meet EvoSim. Its tools have three jobs: show the configuration (orders, prompts, food web), catch mistakes before Play, and make a running world readable (who does what, which genes spread). They all live in the EvoSim.Editor assembly, under Assets/EvoSim/Editor; the simulation never depends on them (EDIT-03). Most of them work on the configuration in Edit mode and on the running world in Play mode (EDIT-05). You find them in the inspectors of the World and its species, under Window ▸ EvoSim, in the Scene view's EvoSim overlay, and in the menus GameObject ▸ EvoSim, Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim and EvoSim. Validation One validation engine checks a world everywhere: in the inspectors, when you press Play, when the World initialises, and in the tests (EDIT-01). It is Prepare(ValidationReport): the World finds its species and modules, sets them up, and asks every module to check itself in its Validate method. Each problem becomes a ValidationMessage with: an id from the catalogue of 21 §2, such as V-04 (a species with no action) or V-30 (band edges out of order); a severity: Error stops the run from starting; Warning and Info never do; the object at fault, a module or a GameObject; a sentence that names the rule, and sometimes a fix. In the inspectors The World and Species inspectors end with a validation list, drawn by ValidationPanel. Each message is a box coloured by severity that reads V-04 Species 'prey' has no action (CORE-04). Next to it: Select selects the object at fault in the Hierarchy and highlights it. A fix button, when the check offers one, labelled with what it does: Add Rest, Rename, Move it up, Clamp, Add a text gene, Mark free… Once the fix is applied, the list is checked again at once. An empty list says Validation is green. The play-mode gate When you press Play, PlayModeGate validates every enabled World of the open scenes before Play mode starts. If one has an error, Play is cancelled and the Console shows one line per error: EvoSim: Play blocked — V-04 Error [Lab1 World/Prey]: Species 'prey' has no action (CORE-04). Click the line to select the object at fault. To use a fix button, select the World and press Validate. Warnings and information never block Play: read them in the inspector. The World inspector Select the World. Above its fields, a line gives its state: Not initialised before Play, then the run state and the tick (Running — tick 1204). While the brains answer it adds what the world waits for, such as waiting for jev: 12 queries, 1.4 s, and once the run has stopped, why. Part What it does Play, Pause, Step, Run N, Stop drive a running world (Play mode). Step runs one tick; Run N runs the number of ticks in the field next to it (100 by default) the World's fields seed, wait mode, run speed, decision period, default brain, stop conditions… (Running and building) Phases (in this order every tick) the children of the Phases object, numbered. A toggle switches a phase on or off; ▲ moves it up one place. Both work in Edit mode only and can be undone Services every world service below the World, by service name and class; (off) marks a disabled one Validation Validate in Edit mode; in Play mode Show the last report, the report of the World's initialisation The Species inspector Select a species. Below its own fields, press Show the computed tables (in Edit mode it validates the world to compute them; in Play mode they show the running world). Then you see the observation space (how many different situations the senses can describe), the signature, and these tables: Table One line per… Actions action in order, with the gene that steers it, or no gene (V-05) Senses, in situation-text order sense: its label, its tokens, and the V1 and V2 text of its first token Genes, in locus order gene: locus id, kind, number of founders, mutation operator and rate Stats and traits stat or trait, the module that declares it; for a trait its default, range and whether it has a cost Food what the species eats (method, energy), whether it is edible itself, and the threats derived from the food web Population initial size, floor, cap and its rule, and the living count in Play mode Prompt preview The Prompt preview foldout shows the exact text a brain receives, built by the same code as the Ask brains phase (PromptPreview, T-PROMPT-05): Pick a Brain among the World's brains, a Founder genome (the n-th founder sentence of each gene) and a Text style (V1 or V2). Pick one token per sense, or press Random situation. Press Build. The prompt appears with About N tokens and the brain's limit; Copy puts it on the clipboard. For JEV the preview is its whole input text. The estimate counts about one token per four characters. The Scene view overlay In Play mode, the Scene view draws over the running world. The EvoSim overlay (shown by default; the Scene view's Overlays menu hides it) has the toggles: Toggle Draws Food items a green circle on each food cell that holds an item Cover an outline on each cover cell Carcasses, Eggs a brown circle under each carcass, a yellow one under each egg Action letters the first letter of each animal's action above it, in the action's colour Show species one per species: hides or shows that species' letters Each action keeps the same colour in every window, set by its place in the species' action order. Select an animal's body to see its vision circle and a line to its target. The toggles are kept in your editor preferences. Windows Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Works in Shows Animal Inspector Play the animal whose body you click in the Scene view: age, generation, parents, stats, traits, each gene's sentence, current action (searching when nothing is in sight), busy reason, target, last situation, last probabilities as bars Ask the Brain Edit, Play the brains' answers for a genome and a situation you choose Brain Health Edit, Play each brain and mutator client: host, Test connection (reachable or V-60), tries, failures, latency in seconds; the answer cache's size and hits Ecology Monitor Play population of each species over time; births, deaths by cause, decisions, memo hits, action shares Event Log Play the run's events as they are recorded, filtered by kind, species or animal Food Web Edit, Play who eats whom as a graph, the derived threats, the food-web messages (V-20, V-22, V-24, V-25) Gene Pool Play for each locus, the share of each allele over time, the most common alleles, the lineage of one Scenario Runner Edit the scenario assets: run their seeds headless and list the results Ask the Brain The place to see what a sentence does to the brain (labs C and I). In Edit mode press Prepare the world first. Pick a species. Each text gene has a field: type a sentence, or press pro, anti or neutral to load the gene's contrast sentences. Founders puts back the first founders; Control sentences puts the World's control (random) sentences instead. Pick one token per sense: the situation text appears below. Tick one or more brains and press Ask. Each answer arrives as one line: the brain, a label, and P(action) for every action. Directed test (pro, anti) asks twice, with the chosen gene's pro sentence and then its anti sentence: compare the two lines for that gene's action. This is what the integrity check B-02 measures on every gene. Asking registers nothing in the world, so it never changes a run. Gene Pool Keep it open while the world runs: it samples the living animals every 20 ticks, so its chart starts when you open it. A text gene shows its allele shares over time, the 12 most common alleles, and the lineage of the one you click back to its founder. A number gene shows a histogram of the living animals' values. Scenario Runner Pick a scenario asset and a variant, edit the seeds and the length (-1 = the scenario's), and press Run. Each seed runs headless, like EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario (Running and building): one line per run with its ticks, events hash, model calls and run folder. Run each seed twice and compare the hashes checks that runs repeat. Close the scenario's scene first: a scene open in the editor cannot be run. Building scenes Menu What it does GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ New World a world of 48 m with the full tree: Ground, Environment (grass, thickets, carcasses, eggs), Brains (JEV, Random, Ollama points, answer cache, mutator), Recording and the eleven Phases. The random brain is the default, so it runs without a server GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ New Species with a World selected: a species with locomotion, energy, stamina, metabolism, a diet of grass, mating, litter, crossover, starvation, old age, cap, floor and staggered decisions. It has no sense and no action yet: V-04 asks for one GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Action ▸ Eat, Flee, Hide, Follow, Rest, Mate, Hunt with a species selected: the action with its text gene, under Actions GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Sense ▸ Energy, Stamina, Food, Predator, Prey, Cover, Animal, Carcass, Age the sense, under Senses; its object's name is its label GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Gene ▸ Stamina gene a number gene for maximum stamina, under Genes The Add menus copy prefabs from Assets/EvoSim/Modules. A new world has no run views, so Play mode shows little: copy the Run views object from a reference scene and add a WorldCamera to your camera, or start from a copy of Sandbox. Three menus are for course staff, when the reference itself changes: Menu What it does EvoSim ▸ Build Reference Scenes rebuilds the six reference scenes, allele pools, module prefabs and scenario assets from code (ReferenceScenes), overwriting any edit made in them EvoSim ▸ Reference ▸ Update Reference Scenes brings the saved scenes to the reference decision period and staggered decisions, without rebuilding them EvoSim ▸ Views ▸ Add Run Views to Reference Scenes adds what is missing of the run views and rebuilds the two placeholder bodies (Views and real time) Script templates In the Project window, Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ asks for a class name and writes two files: Assets/Student/<Name>.cs and its test Assets/Student/Tests/<Name>Tests.cs. Each compiles as it is. Template Derives from The script starts with Sense Sense three tokens (none, near, far), Read and Write Action AnimalAction a description line and an Act that searches Gene kind Gene a number gene that sets a trait from its founder values Stat SpeciesModule a stat declared with a start and a maximum Phase TickPhase an empty Run Brain Brain uniform probabilities Mutation operator MutationOperator a number mutation of ±1 The test derives from WorldFixture and builds a small world in code that uses your class. The first template also creates two assemblies: Student (it sees EvoSim, its HTTP brains and the samples) and Student.Tests (editor only). Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim also has Allele Pool, Scenario and Mutation Deck (a copy of the reference deck to edit). guides/environment.html.title: The environment | EvoSim
guides/environment.html.summary: The environment Everything in a world that is not an animal is part of the environment: the ground animals stand on, the food that grows on it, the cover they hide in, and entities such as carcasses and eggs. Each is a service, a component under the World's Ground and Environment objects. A world may have none, one or several of each kind (03 — Environment). This page explains the reference modules and their settings. How it fits together flowchart LR G[Ground: height, walkable, distance] --> F[FoodGrid: cells that may hold food] G --> C[CoverLayer: thickets] C -->|no food in cover| F K[Strike kills] --> CS[CarcassSystem] B[Breed phase] --> ES[EggSystem] EP[Environment phase] -->|Regrow| F EP -->|UpdateEntities| CS EP -->|UpdateEntities| ES When the World initialises, the ground comes first, since everything else is laid on it. The cover layer then builds its map of thickets. Once every module is ready (Begin), the food layer picks the cells that may hold food, outside water and cover, and places the first items. During a tick, senses and actions query the layers, the cover and the entities. The act phase removes eaten items at once, and a successful strike leaves a carcass. In the environment phase, the ninth phase of a tick, every resource layer regrows and every entity system ages its entities and removes the used-up ones. Nothing else changes the environment. The main types Type Role Ground The world rectangle: height and walkability of every point, and the world's distance function FlatGround Lab 1's ground: a flat rectangle, walkable everywhere TerrainGround A Unity Terrain: water, steep slopes and trees are not walkable ResourceLayer Edible items spread over the ground; FoodGrid is the reference ("Grass") Cover Places where animals hide from their hunters; CoverLayer is the reference ("Thickets") EntitySystem<T> Objects with a position that are not animals: CarcassSystem, EggSystem Edible Makes a species, a layer or an entity kind edible, and says how much energy it gives EnvironmentPhase Regrows the layers and updates the entities, once per tick The ground The ground answers three questions for any point: its height, whether an animal may stand there, and how far it is from another point. Distances are measured on the horizontal plane, straight line, in meters (SPACE-02), and every module measures through World.Distance. The world is a bounded rectangle with hard borders: nothing ever leaves it (SPACE-03). FlatGround is a rectangle from (0, 0) to (Width, Depth) at height 0, walkable everywhere inside. The reference sizes are 192 × 192 m (Lab1_Full), 64 m (HideVsFlee) and 48 m (Lab1_Small). TerrainGround reads a Unity Terrain on its GameObject or below it. Walkability is computed once, on a grid of Cell Size meters (1 m), from the centre of each cell: Setting Reference Effect Water Level set per scene a cell at or below this world height is water: not walkable Max Steepness 35° a steeper cell is not walkable Tree Footprint 0.5 m cells around each tree instance are not walkable (0 = trees don't block) Keep Largest Region on walkable pockets cut off from the largest region become non-walkable (SPACE-05) Heights come from the heightmap itself, not from the grid. A terrain ground also finds water: NearestWater returns a WaterHit with the water point and a walkable Shore point next to it, where a drinking animal stands. Moving on the ground Locomotions never move an animal off walkable ground (MOVE-02). The kinematic locomotion uses two helpers: SlideTo moves in a straight line. If a border, water or an obstacle is in the way, it slides along it: it tries the point clamped into the rectangle and the two one-axis moves, and keeps the one that gets farthest in the wanted direction. If none gets anywhere, it stops at the last walkable point of the line, checked every 0.25 m. SideStep frees a stuck animal: it tries up to 8 random directions, drawn from the species' actions stream, and takes the first clear one. Founders and newcomers are placed at uniformly random walkable points, drawn from the species' founders stream. Food: resource layers A resource layer holds edible items. The reference FoodGrid keeps at most one item per cell, at the cell centre (03 §1): Setting Reference Meaning Cell Size 1 m the side of a food cell Initial Fraction 0.1 share of eligible cells holding an item at the start Regrow P 0.0015 probability per empty eligible cell per tick of growing an item: about 670 ticks to regrow an eaten cell No Food In Cover on cover cells hold no food at the start and never regrow ("hungry cover", ENV-04) Near Water Bonus 2 regrowth multiplier near water (terrain only) Near Water Radius 3 m the distance to water that counts as near A cell is eligible when its centre is walkable and, with hungry cover, outside cover. Food appears uniformly at random over the eligible cells. The layer's Edible gives 25 energy points per item in the reference. An animal grazes an item when it ends its move within the act phase's Graze Reach (0.5 m) of it. Eating removes the item at once: two animals never eat the same item, and the act order decides who gets a contested one (ENV-02). Another phase can change how fast food grows: RegrowFactor multiplies the regrowth probability (1 by default). The seasons sample (Assets/EvoSim/Samples/SeasonsPhase.cs) sets it to 0.2 in winter, from a phase placed before the environment phase (The samples). Cover The reference CoverLayer makes thickets: the top Fraction of walkable cells (20 %) of a value-noise map with two octaves, 8 m and 4 m, on cells of Cell Size (1 m). The thickets come in clustered patches. They never change during a run. An animal standing in cover is hidden from the species that hunt it (ENV-11): its hunters' senses don't report it, their actions can't target it, and a strike on it fails. Its own species and the species it hunts still see it. Hiding Species limits hiding to a list of species ids (empty = every species). A world may have several covers: an animal is hidden when any of them hides it, and the hide action runs to the nearest cover point of any of them. A world without cover behaves as if no point were in cover (ENV-12). Entities: carcasses and eggs An entity is an object with a position that is not an animal (ENV-20). Each has an id, a position and a lifetime in ticks (-1 = none). Its system removes it in the environment phase once it is used up or its lifetime runs out (ENV-22). Carcasses. When a strike kills, the CarcassSystem leaves a carcass at the killed animal's position. Everything about it comes from the killed species' own Edible: Edible setting Reference (prey) Meaning Carcass Portions 2 portions, one each for animals other than the killer (0 = no carcass) Carcass Energy 30 energy points per portion Carcass Ticks 100 ticks before it rots away, eaten or not The killer never eats from its own kill, and each eater takes at most one portion. A species eats carcasses when its diet lists carcass:<species>, and finds them with the "Carcass" sense (NearestEntitySense). Its prompt then gets the carcass system's Prompt Rule: "A kill leaves a carcass that up to {portions} other predators can eat from." Eggs. Each conception lays one egg per baby in the EggSystem. Eggs have no lifetime: they wait for the hatch phase. With no incubation they hatch in the same tick. In the reference, eggs carry no Edible, so nothing eats them (Reproduction and population). Random streams Every draw comes from a named stream (RAND-02). The map uses the world seed, everything that happens during the run uses the run seed: Stream Seed Used for world/<cover name>, e.g. world/Thickets world the cover map world/<layer name>, e.g. world/Grass world the first food items <layer name>, e.g. Grass run the layer's regrowth, each tick (ENV-03) <species>/actions run side steps, strike rolls <species>/founders run where founders and newcomers appear Turn on the World's Separate World Seed and set its World Seed to keep one map while the run seed varies (RAND-04). Carcasses, eggs and the terrain ground draw no random numbers. In the editor The run views draw a flat ground with its food and cover cells, and a marker for each entity: a dark red disc per carcass, an ivory ball per egg (Views and real time). The species inspector lists what a species eats and the energy of each target. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Food Web shows who eats whom (Editor tooling). Validation reports a fraction outside [0, 1] (V-35), a terrain ground without a terrain (V-20) and diet targets without an Edible (V-24). Go further Food, cover, entities and ground: write your own layer, cover, entity kind or ground, and make anything edible. The food web: diets, threats and who hunts whom. A tick, phase by phase: where the environment phase sits. Specification: 03 — Environment, 02 — Space and time.

guides/food-web.html.title: The food web | EvoSim
guides/food-web.html.summary: The food web Who eats whom is data, not code (04). Two components decide it together: the eaten thing carries an Edible, which says how much energy it gives, and the eater's Diet lists what it eats. A meal happens only if both sides allow it (SPEC-13). From the diets the World derives each species' prey and threats, which senses and actions use to find whom to hunt and whom to flee. Any number of species can share a world, and adding one changes no code. How it works Edible. A resource layer, a species or an entity kind (eggs) becomes edible when its GameObject carries an Edible component. Without one, nothing can eat it, whatever the diets say (SPEC-10). Diet. Each species that eats has one Diet. Its entries name what it eats, each with an energy scale (SPEC-15). A species with no diet eats nothing. Resolution. When the world initializes, each diet resolves its entries by name into EdibleTargets (ARCH-08). Then the World derives the food web: a species whose diet strikes another is that species' threat, and the other is its prey (SPEC-12). Use. Senses and actions look for "threats", "prey" or "kin" through an AnimalSet. When an interaction applies, the resolver asks the eater's diet again whether this target may be eaten. Diet entries Entry Eats How Energy of one meal a layer's name, e.g. Grass the layer's food items grazed: the item is consumed the layer's Edible Energy (25 for grass) a species' id or display name, e.g. prey that species' living animals struck: killed with the hunter's kill chance the species' Edible Energy (60 for the prey) carcass:<species>, e.g. carcass:prey carcasses that species leaves scavenged: one portion at a time the species' Edible Carcass Energy (30) egg:<species> that species' eggs, while they incubate eaten whole the egg system's Edible Energy Each entry has an Energy Scale (default 1) that multiplies the energy of that food for this eater. A diet that strikes a species also declares the hunter's kill.chance trait; its default is the diet's Kill Chance (0.5). For the steps to make something edible or change a diet, see Food, cover, entities and ground. Where the Edible goes What is eaten The Edible sits on a layer's items the layer's GameObject (Environment/Grass in the reference scenes) a species' animals the species' own GameObject, next to its Species component a species' carcasses the same Edible as its animals: Carcass Portions above 0 make it leave carcasses; the world also needs a CarcassSystem a species' eggs the EggSystem's GameObject (Environment/Eggs) A disabled Edible counts as absent when the world starts (ARCH-06). What a meal gives The energy of a meal is the Edible's energy times the entry's Energy Scale. The diet's EnergyFrom can then adjust it for the eater (the reference returns it as it is), and Energy adds it, never above the maximum (ANIM-22). Every meal counts in the animal's Meals and its species' meal counter. After a kill or a carcass portion, a species with a Digestion module is busy digesting; grazing and eggs never make an animal busy. Threats, prey and kin The World builds the relations from the diets, in species order, when it initializes and again whenever a species is added during a run. They are never configured twice (SPEC-12). Set Means Used by (reference) Threats species whose diet strikes this one the prey's "Predator" sense and its flee action Prey species this one's diet strikes the predator's "Prey" sense and its hunt action Kin this species the kin senses ("Animal", "Other predator"), follow and mate Listed species named on the module, by id or display name a flee from wolves only, for example ThreatsOf(Species) and PreyOf(Species) return these lists. An animal standing in cover is hidden from its threats: their senses don't report it, their actions can't target it, and they never strike it (ENV-11). Its kin and its own prey still see it. Carcasses When a strike kills an animal whose Edible has Carcass Portions above 0, a carcass appears where it died (reference: 2 portions of 30 energy). The killer has already eaten: it may not eat from its own kill. Any other animal whose diet lists carcass:<species> may eat one portion each. The carcass is gone when its portions are eaten, or when it rots after Carcass Ticks (100); rotting happens in the environment phase. The reference hunt action runs to the nearer of the nearest prey and the nearest carcass it may eat, and a carcass wins a tie, being a sure meal. A diet that eats carcasses adds the carcass system's line to its species' prompt: "A kill leaves a carcass that up to 2 other predators can eat from." Cannibals A species may list itself in its diet (SPEC-11). It is then among its own prey and its own threats: its hunt action chases its own kind, and its flee action runs from it, like from any threat. An animal never targets itself. Species added during a run A species cloned from another during a run (SPEC-30) inherits its relations in both directions (SPEC-31): it eats what its parent species eats, and the hunters of the parent hunt it too, through its own Edible. The World rebuilds the food web when the species is added (RebuildFoodWeb()). The reference food web prey predator Edible yes: 60 per kill, carcass of 2 portions × 30, rots in 100 ticks no Diet Grass (25 per item) prey (kill chance 0.5), carcass:prey Threats (derived) predator none Prey (derived) none prey Eggs not edible not edible The main types Type Role Edible Makes a layer's items, a species' animals or an entity kind edible, with their energy Diet What a species eats; resolves its entries and answers "may I eat this?" Diet.Entry One line of a diet: a target name and an energy scale EdibleTarget One resolved entry: kind, target, its Edible, the scale AnimalSet Threats, prey, kin or listed species CarcassSystem, Carcass Carcasses: portions, eaters, rotting Settings Component Field Reference Edible Energy grass 25 per item, prey 60 per kill Edible Carcass Portions, Carcass Energy, Carcass Ticks prey 2, 30, 100 ticks Diet Eats (Target, Energy Scale) prey: Grass; predator: prey, carcass:prey; scale 1 Diet Kill Chance 0.5 Flee action, Nearest Animal sense From, Targets (and Listed) Threats In the editor Food Web window (Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Food Web): species and layers as a graph. Green edges graze, red strike, brown scavenge carcasses, yellow eat eggs. In Edit mode press Build the food web, which validates the world to resolve the diets. Below the graph: the derived threats of each species and the food-web messages. Species inspector: Show the computed tables lists what the species eats with the energy of each, its own Edible, and its derived threats. Validation reports a diet entry that names nothing (V-20), a flee, hunt or sense with nobody to look for (V-21), a species with no food (V-22), a diet target with no Edible (V-24, with a fix), and an Edible no diet lists (V-25). Go further Food, cover, entities and ground: make something edible, change a diet. Actions and movement: how grazing, strikes and scavenging happen on arrival. The environment: food layers, cover, carcasses and eggs. Specification: 04 — Species and the food web.

guides/genes-and-mutation.html.title: Genes and mutation | EvoSim
guides/genes-and-mutation.html.summary: Genes and mutation An animal's behaviour comes from its genes: short English sentences the brain reads before every decision, and sometimes numbers that set a trait such as maximum stamina. A baby inherits a mix of its parents' genes, and now and then one gene mutates: a second language model, the mutator, rewrites the sentence. Selection does the rest. This page explains how genes are stored, expressed and changed. How parents and babies meet is in Reproduction and population. Genes, loci and alleles A gene is a component under a species, a Gene. Each gene is one locus: one slot in the genome of every animal of the species. The value an animal carries in that slot is an allele. Two animals with the same sentence at the same gene carry the same allele. Gene kind Holds Expressed as TextGene a sentence, e.g. "Run from any predator you see." a line of the prompt's genes block (GENE-03) NumberGene a number, e.g. 60 a trait of the animal, e.g. stamina.max (GENE-04) A text gene placed on an action, or below it, is bound to that action and takes its name as label (GENE-05). Each reference action prefab (Eat, Flee, Rest…) carries its own text gene, so the prey's flee gene is labelled flee. A text gene under no action must have Free ticked: it appears under its own label, for a temperament or a general rule. The species collects its genes depth first in the hierarchy. That order is the locus order (Locus), the same in every genome. Each gene has a locus id <species id>.<label>, unique in the world: prey.flee, predator.hunt (GENE-11). Alleles and the registry Every allele seen in a run is registered once, in Alleles (an AlleleRegistry, GENE-10). Sentences are compared after collapsing spaces; numbers at the gene's Decimals (4 by default). Each Allele gets an id <locus id>:<n>, counted from 0 per locus: prey.flee:0, prey.flee:1… It also records where it came from (GENE-12): Field Example Origin founder, neutral, control, mutant ParentId prey.flee:2, for a mutant of that allele Operator llm#5 (instruction 5 of the deck), gauss Model, Seed gemma4:26b and the call's seed, for a sentence written by the mutator Following parent ids back from a mutant gives its lineage, down to a founder. The recorder writes every allele to alleles.jsonl (Recording and outputs). Founder pools Each gene has a founder pool, FounderPool (GENE-20). The founders at tick 0, and the newcomers that arrive below a species' floor, draw each locus independently and uniformly from it. A text gene's pool is its founder sentences, plus the neutral allele "No preference." unless Has Neutral is off (GENE-24). The reference sentences live in shared AllelePool assets, one per locus, in Assets/EvoSim/Data/AllelePools (prey_flee.asset, predator_hunt.asset…). A number gene's pool is its founder values: 45, 60 and 75 for the reference stamina gene. Pools are frozen for an experiment (GENE-21): the World registers them before anything else, so founder alleles have the same ids in every run. Founder sentences pass the same guards as mutants (GENE-22): at most 12 words, ASCII letters, digits, spaces and , . ' ’ ; : ! ? - (SentenceGuards). Genomes and expression A Genome holds one allele per locus, in locus order (GENE-06). It never changes: a baby gets a new one. Its Key hashes the species and every allele value (GENE-13); its BrainKey hashes only the genes the brain reads, and is part of the memo and cache keys (DEC-31). Express turns an allele into what acts, through an Expression. It runs at two moments: at birth, a number gene sets its trait, or multiplies the trait's default, clamped to the trait's range; when a decision's prompt is written, each gene the brain reads adds one line to the genes block (PROMPT-02). For a reference prey, the genes block looks like this: - eat: "Eat whenever food is close." - flee: "Run from any predator you see." - hide: "No preference." - follow: "Keep your distance from other animals." - rest: "Rest only when you feel safe." - mate: "Mate with any nearby adult." A number gene stays out of the prompt unless its Show In Prompt is on. Mutation flowchart LR C[Conception] --> R{Rate draw} R -->|no| K[Inherited allele] R -->|yes| O[Operator draws its choices] O -->|number| J[Job done] O -->|text| S[Mutator service] S --> M[Mutator model] --> G{Clean and guards} G -->|rejected, tries left| S G -->|5 rejected| K G -->|accepted| J J --> H{Hatching: gene check} H -->|ok| A[New allele] H -->|refused or unchanged| K Which loci. In the breed phase, after each baby's crossover, each locus mutates with the probability Rate of its operator: 0.03 per gene per baby (MUT-01). The draw comes from the species' mutation stream. Which operator. Exactly one MutationOperator applies to a locus: the first one that accepts the gene and lists it in Only These, else the first one that accepts it and lists no gene (MUT-02). The reference uses LlmMutation for text genes and GaussianMutation for number genes. Draw now. The operator draws all its random choices at conception (MUT-30) and returns a MutationJob. A Gaussian job is done at once: v′ = clamp(v + N(0, σ)) within the gene's range, σ = 5 (MUT-20). Ask the mutator. An LLM job goes to the World's MutatorService, described below. Hatch. The egg hatches once its jobs are done (MUT-32). Each new value must pass the gene's Check; it is then registered as a mutant and listed in the baby's birth event (MUT-03). A failed job, a refused value or a value equal to the parent leaves the inherited allele (MUT-04). The LLM mutator The deck is a text file of instructions, one per line; lines starting with # are ignored (MUT-10). The reference deck Assets/EvoSim/Data/Decks/mutate_v4.txt has seven, such as "Make the rule in this sentence a little weaker." and "Change when this rule applies.". For each of its 5 tries, LlmMutation draws an instruction and a seed at conception. The prompt is exactly (MUT-11): The sentence below is a rule that a wild animal follows. Make this rule say the opposite. "Run from any predator you see." Reply with the new sentence only. The mutator sees nothing else: no animal, no world, no other gene (CORE-07). Batches. The service sends all first tries of a tick as one batch at the end of the breed phase, then the redraws as later batches (MUT-31), through the World's MutatorClient. The reference client, OllamaMutatorClient, asks gemma4:26b in Ollama (http://localhost:11434) on the CPU, so the GPU stays the brain's; temperature 1.2, thinking off. Cache. Answers are stored in the AnswerCache under the model, prompt, seed and temperature (MUT-14): a repeated run gets the same mutants without a model call. Cleaning and guards (MUT-12, MutationText). The service keeps the quoted part, drops a leading "Here is …:", keeps the first sentence, adds a final period and a capital. It rejects the answer as invalid (no word, more than 12 words, the parent again, a forbidden character) or unchanged (only punctuation differs). Redraws. A rejected try is followed by the next one, with its own instruction and seed (MUT-13). After 5 rejected tries the gene stays as it was. No mutator. If the server can't be reached, the gene stays unchanged (MUT-04). With Strict on, the run also stops at the end of the tick. A real mutation: "Run from any predator you see." → "Run quickly from any predator you see." Eggs and waiting The mutator takes time, so babies wait as eggs until their genome is complete. With the reference incubation of 0 ticks, eggs hatch in the tick they are laid, and that tick waits for the mutator's answers. An Incubation of a few ticks lets the world go on while the answers arrive (MUT-33). Either way the result is the same: every choice was drawn at conception, so it never depends on when an answer comes back. The main types Type Role Gene the base class of a locus: label, kind, founder pool, expression, allowed values TextGene, NumberGene the reference gene kinds AllelePool an asset of founder and contrast sentences shared by several text genes Allele, AlleleValue one registered value with its lineage; the value itself AlleleRegistry every allele of the run, once per locus and value Genome one allele per locus, in locus order Expression what Express writes into: a trait, or a prompt line MutationOperator the base class of a mutation rule; LlmMutation, GaussianMutation MutationJob one mutation of one gene of one baby: done, failed or still running MutatorService, MutatorClient batches, cleans and caches LLM mutations; sends the prompts to a server MutationStats the run's counts: attempts, successes, model calls, rejections by reason (MUT-05) Settings Component Field Reference Meaning Text gene Pool the locus' asset shared founders; empty = the Founders list Has Neutral, Neutral, Neutral Mutates on, "No preference.", on the neutral allele and whether it may mutate (MUT-22) Free off not bound to an action Max Words 12 word limit for founders and mutants Number gene Trait, Multiply Default stamina.max, off the trait it sets; replace or multiply its default Min, Max, Founders 20, 120; 45, 60, 75 the gene's own range and founder values Show In Prompt, Decimals off, 4 whether the brain reads it; comparison precision Any operator Rate, Only These 0.03, empty probability per gene per baby; genes it is configured for LLM mutation Deck, Context Line, Tries, Max Words mutate_v4, the line above, 5, 12 Gaussian mutation Sigma 5 standard deviation, in the gene's unit Mutator service Model, Temperature, Strict, Use Cache gemma4:26b, 1.2, off, on On the World, the controls of 15 — Controls change genes for a whole run: No Mutation (C2) sets every rate to 0; Shuffled Genes (C3) makes each decision read the genes of another living animal of the species; Random Founders (C4) draws founder sentences from the World's Control Sentences and founder numbers uniformly in each gene's range. In the editor The species inspector's Genes foldout lists the genes in locus order, with their locus id, kind, founder count and the operator that applies, with its rate. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Gene Pool, in Play mode: pick a species and a locus. For a text gene it shows the allele shares over time (one colour per allele id), the 12 most common alleles with their text, origin and id, and, when you click one, its lineage back to a founder. For a number gene it shows a histogram of the living animals' values. It samples every 20 ticks while it is open. GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Gene ▸ Stamina gene adds the reference number gene with its Gaussian operator. Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Mutation Deck writes a copy of the reference deck for you to edit. Validation reports bad founders (V-40, V-42), empty pools (V-41), a missing neutral allele (V-43), a number gene's unknown trait or missing cost (V-45, V-47), a gene no operator accepts (V-48), a missing deck (V-20) or mutator (V-63). Go further Add a free gene, a number gene or a new gene kind: Genes. Write your own deck or mutation operator: Mutation. Rewrite LlmMutation from its stub: the teaching path. Use another mutator server: An HTTP brain or mutator server. The contract: 09 — Genes, alleles and genomes and 10 — Mutation.

guides/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | EvoSim
guides/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started This page takes you from opening the project to watching a run, inspecting it and finding its output files. It takes about ten minutes. What you need Unity 6000.3.9f1, installed with the Unity Hub, on Windows (the course's machines). This repository, opened as a Unity project. The EvoSim code is under Assets/EvoSim. Optional: the two model servers. Without them you can still run everything with the random brain. Server Address What it does Start it with JEV (vLLM in Docker, GPU) localhost:8000 the brain: reads genes and situations, gives a probability per action docker compose -f prototype/docker/compose.yaml up -d (5–8 minutes until healthy), after a one-time download: see Model servers Ollama with gemma4:26b (CPU) localhost:11434 the mutator: rewrites a gene sentence when it mutates ollama serve with two settings, then ollama pull gemma4:26b once: see Model servers Run level L0 (the random brain, no mutation) needs neither server. L1 needs JEV, L2 needs JEV and Ollama (see Run levels). Note The Windows player build is not in the repository: Builds/ is ignored by git. To watch runs outside the editor, build it yourself once with EvoSim ▸ Build ▸ Visual Player (see Player builds). Everything on this page works in the editor without it. Model servers (for L1 and L2) Skip this section if you only run L0. All commands run in PowerShell from the repository root. What the machine needs Docker Desktop with the WSL 2 backend and GPU support (an up-to-date NVIDIA driver on Windows; nothing to install inside WSL). An NVIDIA GPU with about 16 GB of memory: JEV in FP8 fills an RTX 5080 (14.4 GB in use). About 17 GB of free disk for the JEV weights, in your Hugging Face cache (%USERPROFILE%\.cache\huggingface). For Ollama: about 20 GB of free RAM, since gemma4:26b runs on the CPU. Python 3 from python.org, started with the py -3 launcher. Don't type bare python: on these machines it can open the Windows Store stub instead of Python. JEV: download the weights once The JEV container runs offline (HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 in prototype/docker/compose.yaml): it reads the weights from your Hugging Face cache and never downloads them. Download them once, at the revision the container is pinned to: py -3 -m pip install --user huggingface_hub py -3 -c "from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download as d; d('autotrust/JEV-9B', revision='b63f651ce8ed64481d3f5e73ecdb05f740042f01', allow_patterns=['*.json', '*.jinja', 'model-*.safetensors', 'head.safetensors', 'adapter/*', 'adapter_vllm/*'])" The download is about 17 GB. It must include the adapter_vllm/ folder: the container loads JEV's decision adapter from it. If the download stops with a 401 or 403 error, the model needs a Hugging Face token: ask the course staff. JEV: start it and check it docker compose -f prototype/docker/compose.yaml up -d docker compose -f prototype/docker/compose.yaml ps Start-up takes 5–8 minutes. Run the ps command again until the jev service shows (healthy), then check that it answers: curl.exe http://localhost:8000/v1/models The answer lists autotrust/JEV-9B and jev-decision. Finally, in Unity, open Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Brain Health and press Test connection next to JEV. If the service never becomes healthy, read its log with docker compose -f prototype/docker/compose.yaml logs jev; a "not found" or "offline" error means the weights are missing or at another revision. Stop it with docker compose -f prototype/docker/compose.yaml down. Ollama: the mutator Quit the Ollama tray app if it is running (it starts its own server with other settings), then start the server with one model loaded at a time, kept in memory for four hours: $env:OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS = "1"; $env:OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE = "4h"; ollama serve In a second window, once: ollama pull gemma4:26b. Without OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE, Ollama unloads the model after a few idle minutes, and reloading 26 B parameters from disk can take longer than the mutator's 60 s time-out: that mutation then fails and the gene is copied unchanged. Check it in Brain Health with Test connection next to the mutator. Note prototype/docker/README.md describes the servers for the Python prototype, whose mutator is a different model. For EvoSim, follow this page. 1. Open a scene The reference scenes are in Assets/EvoSim/Scenes: Scene What lives there Lab1_Small a 48 m world with prey and predators: the quickest to watch Lab1_Full the full Lab 1 ecology (164 animals at the start, up to about 340) HideVsFlee prey that can flee or hide in thickets, and the predators that hunt them ThreeSpecies three species in one food web Terrain_Locomotion a Unity Terrain with slopes, water and trees Sandbox grazers only, with the random brain: a place to try your own modules 2. Choose a brain The scenes ask JEV by default. If JEV is not running, select the World object and set Default Brain to Brains/Random, the null model that picks actions uniformly at random. Everything else works the same, and the run still repeats exactly with its seed. Without Ollama, mutations fail quietly: the gene is copied unchanged (MUT-04). Tick No Mutation on the World to switch mutation off altogether. 3. Press Play Before Play mode starts, the World's whole tree is checked. If something is wrong, the play-mode gate cancels Play and the Console shows one line per error, naming the object to fix (for example V-04 … Species 'prey' has no action). Click the line to select that object. Fix it by hand, or select the World, press Validate in its inspector and click the fix button next to the message, then press Play again. Warnings never block Play. While it runs: The panel at the top left shows the tick, the pace in ticks per second, and for each species its living animals, births, deaths and kills. It also counts mutations and model calls. Tab hides it. The ball above each animal shows its current action: green eat, yellow flee, blue hide, cyan follow, grey rest, pink mate, red hunt, white searching (nothing in sight). Camera: WASD or the arrow keys pan, the mouse wheel zooms, a right-drag or Q/E orbits, a middle-drag pans, F frames the whole ground. Click an animal to follow it and see its stats; Esc stops following. When the brain is slow, the World waits for its answers before going on (a decision is never made on old observations). The panel then says what it waits for, for example waiting for JEV: 6 queries. 4. Inspect Select the World: its state and tick, the run controls (Play, Pause, Step, Run N, Stop), its phases in order, its services, and Validate with the validation messages. Select a species and press Show the computed tables: its actions, senses, genes, stats and traits, food and population, and the Prompt preview, the exact text its animals send to the brain. Open the windows under Window ▸ EvoSim: Window Shows Animal Inspector the animal you click: stats, genes, last situation and the brain's probabilities Ecology Monitor populations over time; births, deaths by cause and action shares per species Event Log the events of the run as they happen, filtered by kind, species or animal Food Web who eats whom, and the threats each species flees Gene Pool the alleles alive in each species, how common they are, and where each came from Brain Health each brain and mutator: host, Test connection, calls, failures, latency; the answer cache Ask the Brain genes and a situation of your choice, and the answers of the brains you pick Scenario Runner the scenario assets (S00–S27): run their seeds headless and compare the hashes See Editor tooling for every inspector, window and menu. 5. Find the run's files Each run writes its files to Logs/EvoSim/runs/<run name>/: File Content events.jsonl every event, one JSON object per line: births, deaths, kills, meals, mutations… stats.csv one row of statistics every few ticks: populations, deaths by cause, means alleles.jsonl every allele (gene variant) that appeared, with its text and parent final_population.json the animals alive at the end: id, generation, species and genome (allele ids) summary.json the run's totals, why it stopped, and the events hash that identifies it run_info.json the seed, the settings and the versions needed to replay it Two runs with the same seed, the same scene and the same brain answers have the same events hash. See Recording and outputs and Determinism and replay. Next How EvoSim works: the whole loop on one page. Extending EvoSim: add your own sense, action, gene, brain or phase. The teaching path: rewrite a reference module from a stub.
