guides/overview.html.title: How EvoSim works | EvoSim
guides/overview.html.summary: How EvoSim works This page is the whole system in one read. Each section links to the guide that explains that part in depth. The idea An animal's behaviour is not coded: it is described by genes, short English sentences such as "Eat whenever you see grass." or "Run from any predator you see.". At each decision, the animal's senses describe its situation in a few words ("Food: 1-4 meters away. Predator: none within 20 meters."). A language model, the brain, reads the genes and the situation and gives a probability for each action the species can take: eat, flee, hide, follow, rest, mate, hunt. The animal draws one action from those probabilities and carries it out for a few ticks. Animals that eat well and avoid predators live longer and breed more. A baby takes each gene from one parent or the other, and sometimes a gene mutates: a second language model, the mutator, rewrites the sentence. Sentences that help animals survive spread through the population; the others die out. That is evolution, with English as the genetic code. The pieces flowchart LR W[World] --> S1[Species: prey] W --> S2[Species: predator] W --> P[Tick phases] W --> SV[Services: ground, food, cover, brains, recorder] S1 --> M[Modules: senses, actions, genes, stats, rules, mutation] S1 --> A[(Animals: plain data)] The World is a GameObject. Everything else is a component under it, so a scene is a complete experiment. (The world and its modules) A species is a GameObject under the World. Its child components are its modules: senses, actions, genes, stats, life rules and mutation operators. Add a component and the species has that feature. Animals are plain C# objects owned by their species, not GameObjects. Each has a position, stats such as energy and stamina, a genome, an age and a current action. (Animals, stats and death) Services are shared parts under the World: the ground, food layers, cover, carcasses and eggs, the brains, the mutator, the recorder. (The environment) Tick phases are components under the World's Phases object. The World runs them in hierarchy order, once per tick. (A tick, phase by phase) One tick Simulation time advances in ticks. A tick runs every phase in order: Phase What happens Sense each animal that decides this tick reads its senses: one token per sense, then its situation text Ask brains situations already answered come from the memo or the cache; the others go to the brains, one batch per brain Choose actions the World waits for the answers, then draws each deciding animal's action from its probabilities Act each action gives an intent (go there, flee from that); the locomotion moves the animal; interactions happen on arrival (graze, strike, scavenge); living costs energy Breed an animal that chose to mate and reaches a ready partner conceives a litter: one egg per baby, genes crossed over, mutations drawn and sent to the mutator Hatch eggs due this tick hatch, once their mutated genes are back Deaths killed animals die; every animal ages by one tick; death rules run (starvation, old age) Migration species above their cap lose animals chosen at random Environment food regrows, carcasses rot Floor species below their floor get newcomers Record a statistics row every 100 ticks, and the files are flushed; events are written as they happen An animal does not decide every tick. In the reference scenes it decides every 4 ticks (the World's decision period), and each species' decision schedule staggers its animals by id, so about a quarter of them decide on each tick and the brain's work is spread out. A newborn decides at once; a busy animal (digesting a kill) does not decide. Between decisions an animal keeps its action. (Decisions and brains) From senses to an action flowchart LR SE[Senses] -->|tokens| SI[Situation text] G[Genes] --> Q[Query] SI --> Q Q --> MC{Memo or cache?} MC -->|known| PB[Probabilities] MC -->|new| BR[Brain reads the prompt] --> PB PB -->|draw with temperature| AC[Action] Each sense returns one token from a fixed list, for example here, adjacent, close, medium, far or none for the nearest food. The tokens together are the animal's observation. (Senses and prompts) The genes and the situation make a query. The brain turns it into a prompt from the species' template: a header, one line per action, the rules of the world, the animal's genes, the situation text, and the question. The same genes in the same situation always get the same answer from the same brain. The memo remembers answers during a run and the answer cache on disk across runs. Only new questions reach the model. The brain returns one probability per action. JEV, a language model served on localhost:8000, is the reference brain. The random brain answers uniformly and needs no server. The animal draws its action, after the probabilities are sharpened or flattened by the sampling temperature. From an action to a movement An action never moves the animal itself. It tells an ActContext where to go (walk to that grass, run away from that predator) and what to do on arrival (graze it, strike it). The species' locomotion then moves the animal as far as its speed and stamina allow, and the interaction happens if the target is within reach. (Actions and movement, The food web) From parents to babies A mating pair produces a litter. Each baby takes each gene from one parent or the other (crossover). Each gene then mutates with a small probability (3 % per gene per birth in the reference). A mutation asks the mutator model to rewrite the sentence, for example by making it stronger, weaker or about something else. Each baby starts as an egg that carries its genes until the mutator's answers are back. In the reference the incubation is 0 ticks: the eggs hatch in the same tick, and the tick waits for the mutator if it must. Give a species an incubation of a few ticks and the world goes on while the mutator works. (Genes and mutation, Reproduction and population) Same seed, same run Every random draw comes from a named stream derived from the World's seed. As long as the brain answers the same way, which the memo and the answer cache ensure, a run repeats exactly on the same machine: in the editor, headless, or in a player build, whatever the speed and the wait mode. Each run ends with an events hash that identifies it. (Determinism and replay) What you watch and what you keep The views only display: bodies follow their animals, with a marker coloured by their action, over a ground painted with food and cover. The recorder writes every event and statistic to Logs/EvoSim/runs/. (Views and real time, Recording and outputs)

guides/recording-and-outputs.html.title: Recording and outputs | EvoSim
guides/recording-and-outputs.html.summary: Recording and outputs A run writes enough to rebuild its whole gene history afterwards: every founder, birth and death with its genome and cause, statistics over time, every allele ever seen, and what was configured. The files follow the Python prototype's formats, so its analysis tools can read Unity runs (13 — Outputs and recording). Each run also ends with an events hash, a fingerprint that tells you whether two runs were identical. How it works flowchart LR M[Phases and modules] -->|SimEvent| L[EventLog] L -->|canonical line| H[events hash] L --> R[RunRecorder] L --> W[Event Log window] RP[Record phase] -->|every 100 ticks| R RP --> LS[LiveStatistics] R --> F[(run folder)] Code that changes the world records what happened as a SimEvent: a kind, the tick, the animal's id, its species and more fields. It goes to the World's EventLog (World.Events). The event log writes the event as canonical JSON: keys sorted, numbers rounded to at most 6 decimals, separators as Python writes them (CanonicalJson). It adds that line to the running hash, then passes the event to every listener (an IEventSink): the RunRecorder, the Event Log window, tests. The record phase, last in the tick, asks the recorder for a statistics row every Stats Every ticks and lets it flush its files. It also samples the LiveStatistics for the editor's graphs. When the run stops, for any reason (tick limit, stop button, leaving Play mode, a brain failure), the recorder writes its final files. A stopped run always has complete files (RAND-20). The events hash The hash is a chain of SHA-256 digests. It starts from a hash of the run seed and the world seed, so two seeds never share a hash. Then each event's canonical line is hashed together with the previous hash (RAND-10). The hash can be read after any event: World.Events.Hash (64 hex digits) or World.Events.ShortHash (the first 16). The same scene, seeds and answer caches give the same hash, whatever the wait mode, frame rate, run speed or views (RAND-11). A different hash means something in the run changed. Compare hashes on one machine only: floating-point results may differ between machines (RAND-12). See Determinism and replay. The run folder The recorder writes each run into its own folder (OUT-01): <Output Root>/<Run Name>. By default Logs/EvoSim/runs/<world>-s<seed>-<date>-<time>, for example Logs/EvoSim/runs/Lab1_World-s1234-20261011-143005. Characters other than letters, digits, -, _ and . become _. If the folder exists already, a suffix -2, -3… is added. Paths are relative to the project folder in the editor, and to the build's folder in a player. File Written What you find there events.jsonl as events happen, flushed every 500 ticks one event per line, in tick order (Events) stats.csv a row every 100 ticks, flushed every 500 populations, means and cumulative counters per species alleles.jsonl rewritten every 5 000 ticks and at the end every allele seen: id, locus, text (or value), origin (founder, neutral, mutant), parent_id, operator, model, seed final_population.json at the end the living animals: id, gen, genome (allele ids), species summary.json at the end totals per species and for the run (Summary) run_info.json at the start, again at the end what ran: scene, seeds, settings, brains, git commit (Run information) Events Every event has kind, t (the tick) and species, and id when it is about an animal (OUT-02): Kind Fields founder genome: the animal's allele ids, in locus order immigrant genome: a newcomer added below the species' floor birth parents, gen, genome, litter (its litter's size), mutations (a list of locus, parent, child, prompt or operator, text or value); laid (the conception tick) when it hatched from an incubated egg death cause (killed, starvation, old_age, migrated, or a module's own), age, gen, food (meals eaten), offspring, and killer for a kill egg_lost id of the egg, parents, reason (eaten) species_created name, parent_species: a species added during the run For example, a death line looks like this: {"age": 412, "cause": "killed", "food": 9, "gen": 2, "id": 1873, "killer": 1702, "kind": "death", "offspring": 3, "species": "prey", "t": 5120} Allele ids read <locus>:<n>, and a locus is <species>.<gene label>: prey.eat:3 is the fourth allele of the prey's eat gene. Statistics stats.csv has one row every Stats Every ticks (100), labelled with the number of ticks done: rows t = 100, 200…. After t, each species has a block of columns prefixed with its id (prey_pop, predator_pop): Column Meaning pop living animals mean_energy, mean_stamina, mean_gen means over the living animals max_gen the highest generation alive exhausted animal-ticks that began without stamina to move births, immigrants cumulative deaths_starve, deaths_pred, deaths_age, deaths_migrated cumulative deaths by cause (deaths_pred counts kills) deaths_<cause> one more column per other cause: a death rule's, or any recorded by a module decisions, backend_queries, invalid cumulative decisions, decisions the memo could not answer, searching choices portions carcass portions eaten act_<action> cumulative decisions per action Modules add their own columns after the species' block (Recording and statistics). A column alleles (all alleles registered) follows the first species, and world modules' columns end the row. Counters are cumulative from the start of the run. If a column appears during the run (a species added, a new cause of death), the file is rewritten with the new header, and older rows get empty cells in it. Summary summary.json has, for the run: ticks, seed, world_seed, backend (the default brain), brains, mutations (tried, ok, calls, failed, rejected by reason), alleles, events (how many), events_hash and events_sha (its first 16 digits), stopped (why the run stopped), minutes, llm_calls, cache_hits, failures, mutation_calls. Under species, each species has its final population, births, newcomers, hatched eggs, deaths by cause, mean lifespan, maximum generation, decisions, brain queries, memo hit rate, brain time (backend_s), searching rate (invalid_rate), share of exhausted animal-ticks, share of each action, founders, lost eggs, failures, and for hunters kills and portions (13 §5). Run information run_info.json says what ran (CFG-03): the World's name, scene, Unity version, git commit, seed and world_seed, wait mode, act order, decision period, sampling temperature, text style, the default brain, the command line, the start time, the controls (no_mutation, shuffled…), each brain's model, the mutator's model and temperature, and settings: every serialized setting of every enabled module under the World, by path, for example "Environment/Grass/FoodGrid/regrowP": 0.0015. A scenario run adds scenario, variant and overrides. No API key or other secret is ever written: options that name a key are masked in the command line (OUT-04). Settings On the World's Recording object: Component Setting Reference Meaning RunRecorder Output Root Logs/EvoSim/runs the folder that receives one folder per run Run Name empty the run folder's name; empty = world, seed, date; {world} and {seed} are replaced Stats Every 100 ticks a statistics row every this many ticks Flush Every 500 ticks events and statistics reach the disk at least this often Alleles Every 5 000 ticks alleles.jsonl is rewritten this often Compatibility off write a two-species world as the prototype did (below) Write Files on off: no files, only the hash and the counters (tests) LiveStatistics Every 10 ticks a sample for the editor's graphs this often Capacity 2 000 samples kept per species; older ones are dropped A world without a recorder still computes its events hash. Validation warns when there is a recorder and no record phase (V-09). Compatibility mode With Compatibility on, a two-species world is written exactly as the prototype wrote it (OUT-05), so its tools (gene_report, gene_timeline, mutation_list) read it: the first species' events have no species field and its allele and locus ids no prefix (eat:3); its statistics columns have no prefix and the second species' have pred_; a kill's cause is predator; the summary puts the first species' totals at the top level and the second species' under <id>s (predators). Only the files change: the events hash is the same in both modes. Scenarios and field paths A scenario runs a scene with changed settings, without editing the scene (CFG-02, 31 — Scenarios). It is a ScenarioAsset (Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Scenario), kept in Assets/EvoSim/Scenarios: Field Meaning Title its id and title, e.g. "S07 No cover" Scene the scene, e.g. Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/Lab1_Full.unity Set overrides applied to every variant: a path and a value Variants each with a Name, its own Brain and Tier, more overrides (Set, applied after the scenario's) and GameObjects to switch off (Remove) Seeds one run per seed Ticks the run length Brain the default brain, by GameObject name or brain id; empty = the scene's Expect what the scenario should show, as notes for the reader Tier T2 (fast), T3 (regression), T4 (real models) An override names a setting by its field path, relative to the World: <GameObject path>/<Component>/<field> (FieldPath). Names are matched in any case, a species also by its id or display name, and the component is found on the GameObject or anywhere below it, so Prey/Litter/max works although the Litter sits under Prey/Life. World/<field> is the World's own setting, such as World/decisionPeriod. Values are text: 2, 0.5, true, an enum name such as Block, [8, 4] for a list of numbers. Only fields the Inspector shows can be set. The keys of run_info.json's settings are valid paths: copy one to override it. Two real examples: S20 sets Prey/CapRule/mode to Migrate in one variant and Block in the other. S07 removes Environment/Thickets, Prey/Actions/hide and Prey/Senses/Cover to run the reference world without cover. Run a scenario from Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Scenario Runner, in Edit mode with the scenario's scene closed: pick a variant, seeds and a length, and press Run. Run each seed twice and compare the hashes checks that the scenario is deterministic. In batch mode: Unity.exe -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] A scenario run's folder is named <scenario>-<variant>-s<seed>-<time>. A path or value that can't be applied stops the run before it starts, with a message naming it. Overrides skip the Inspector's limits; validation still reports values out of range (V-35). In the editor Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Event Log lists the running world's events as they are recorded, filtered by kind, species or animal. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Ecology Monitor draws each species' population over time from the LiveStatistics, with the ticks per second, and lists each species' counters: births, deaths by cause, decisions, memo hits, action shares. The run views' overlay shows the tick, the pace, and each species' population, births and deaths on screen, in the editor and in a build (Views and real time). Go further Recording and statistics: add statistics columns, causes of death, events of your own. Determinism and replay: random streams, the answer cache and resuming a run. Running and building: headless runs and the player's command line. Specification: 13 — Outputs and recording, 14 — Configuration reference, 31 — Scenarios.

guides/reproduction-and-population.html.title: Reproduction and population | EvoSim
guides/reproduction-and-population.html.summary: Reproduction and population Evolution needs births: an animal that eats well, escapes predators and finds a partner leaves babies, and its genes spread. This page follows a birth from the mate decision to the newborn, then explains the limits that keep each population in bounds: a cap above, a floor below. What happens to the genes on the way, mutation in particular, is in Genes and mutation. How a birth happens flowchart LR D[Decision: mate] --> B{Breed phase: ready partner within reach?} B -->|no| N[No litter] B -->|yes| L[Litter size; parents pay] L --> E[One egg per baby: crossover, mutations drawn] E --> H{Hatch phase: due and genome complete?} H -->|yes| A[Babies join the species] A --> M[Migration: back to the cap] M --> F[Floor: newcomers if too few] Mating An animal whose brain chose mate walks toward the nearest ready partner it sees. The breeding itself happens in the breed phase, after every animal has acted (TICK-06): The phase takes, in id order, each animal whose current action is mate, that is ready and hasn't bred in this decision period. Ready means alive, adult (age at least the Maturity trait, 150 ticks) and with at least Mate Energy (50 points) (IsReady(Animal), REPRO-01). It pairs it with the nearest ready animal of its species within Reach (1 m) that hasn't bred either; ties go to the lower id. One partner's choice is enough: the partner may be resting or eating (REPRO-02). Both are marked as having bred. Each animal breeds at most once per decision period: the mark is cleared at its next decision (REPRO-03). With Sexual off on the MatingRule, or the World's Asexual control (C7) on, a ready animal that chose mate reproduces alone and pays the whole cost (REPRO-04). Killed animals never breed (REPRO-05). Litters and their cost The Litter decides how many babies a mating makes (REPRO-10): k is drawn uniformly in [Min, Max] = [2, 4], from the species' litter stream. Each baby costs Child Energy (40 points), shared equally by the parents: with two parents, 20 each per baby. k is cut so that no parent pays more energy than it has, but never below Min. A poor parent can be left with zero energy or less, and starves at the death check. This is a choice of the contract, not an accident. Each parent then pays its share × k, its offspring counter grows by k, and it is marked as having bred (REPRO-11). With the reference values, a parent at 50 energy pays for 2 babies (40 points) and keeps 10; at 100 it can pay for 4. Crossover and eggs Each baby gets its own crossover, so siblings usually differ (GENE-32). The reference UniformCrossover takes each locus from one parent or the other with probability ½, independently, from the species' mutation stream (GENE-30). A baby of a single parent copies its genome (GENE-31). The baby's mutations are then drawn, locus by locus (MUT-30). Each baby becomes an Egg, laid at the first parent's position in the World's EggSystem (REPRO-20). An egg holds the parents, the generation (the larger parent generation + 1), the alleles after crossover, the mutations still running, the conception tick and the hatch tick: conception + the species' Incubation Ticks. Eggs are not animals: they don't sense, decide, move, eat, breed or count toward caps (REPRO-22). In the reference nothing eats them; a species can be given a taste for eggs (REPRO-23, see Reproduction and population). Hatching The hatch phase runs right after the breed phase. Eggs due at this tick hatch in conception order (REPRO-22), but only once their genome is complete: if the mutator's answers aren't in, the tick waits (MUT-32, REPRO-24). With the reference incubation of 0 ticks, babies hatch in the tick they were conceived, as in the prototype (REPRO-21). Each baby starts with the litter's Child Energy, full stamina, age 0, the heading drawn at conception, at the egg's place (REPRO-12). It has no action until its first decision, at the start of the next tick (REPRO-13). A birth event records its parents, generation, genome, litter size and mutations. Caps and migration Each species has a CapRule with a Cap and a Mode (POP-01): Mode At the cap Migrate (reference) Births go on. In the migration phase, if the species is above its cap, animals chosen uniformly at random leave the world (death cause migrated) until it is back at the cap. Animals born this tick are spared, unless too few older animals remain. Block No conception while the species is at or above its cap; a litter is cut to the places left, possibly to zero. Migration draws from the species' own migration stream and ignores genes, stats and position, so it favours no gene (POP-02). Migrate was chosen over Block because blocked births led to boom-and-bust crashes (11 §4). Floors and newcomers Each species has a FloorRule. In the floor phase, the last but one phase of the tick, while a species has fewer living animals than its Floor, a newcomer arrives (POP-03): a founder genome drawn from the founder pools, a random walkable position, the starting stats, generation 0, recorded as an immigrant event. It decides from the next tick (TICK-05). At tick 0 each species gets its Initial Population of founders the same way, recorded as founder events (POP-04). Newcomers bring founder genes back and restart that species' evolution, so a run that needs them is reported (POP-05). The aim is a world that never needs them: litters of 2 to 4 and migration at the cap made both reference species last without newcomers. The main types Type Role MatingRule who is adult and ready, the breeding reach, one or two parents Litter the litter size and the energy each baby costs Crossover, UniformCrossover how the parents' genomes mix Incubation ticks from conception to hatching Egg, EggSystem a conceived baby; the world's eggs, laid and hatched in order CapRule, FloorRule the population's upper and lower limits BreedPhase, HatchPhase the phases that conceive and hatch MigrationPhase, FloorPhase the phases that apply the cap and the floor Settings The rules sit in each species' Life group; the egg system is the World's Environment ▸ Eggs object. Component Field Reference Meaning Mating rule Mate Energy 50 points energy needed to be ready Maturity 150 ticks adult age; a trait, so a number gene could set it Reach 1 m breeding distance Sexual on two parents; off = one parent pays all Prompt Rule "Breeding needs only one of the two to choose mate…" the rule line the brain reads Litter Min, Max 2, 4 litter size range, in babies Child Energy 40 points each baby's energy, paid by the parents Incubation Ticks 0 conception to hatching Cap rule Cap prey 270, predators 68 (Lab1_Small: 40 and 6) maximum population, in animals Mode Migrate Migrate or Block Floor rule Floor prey 10, predators 3 minimum population, in animals Species Initial Population prey 136, predators 28 (Lab1_Small: 24 and 4) founders at tick 0 In the editor The species inspector's Population foldout shows the initial population, the floor, the cap and its mode, and the living count in Play mode. In Play mode, the Scene view's EvoSim overlay draws a yellow circle under each egg (the Eggs toggle). Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Event Log lists birth, immigrant, egg_lost and death events as they happen; filter by kind, species or animal, and follow one animal's descendants. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Ecology Monitor graphs the populations and counts births, founders and deaths by cause. Validation warns about a breeding species without an EggSystem (V-20), without a Litter, a crossover or an Energy module (V-26), a floor or initial population above the cap (V-32), a bad litter range (V-33), and a smallest litter that costs more than the mate energy (V-34).
