guides/running-and-building.html.title: Running and building | EvoSim
guides/running-and-building.html.summary: Running and building A world can run in four ways: in Play mode in the editor, headless from the editor, in batch mode with the editor closed, or in a Windows player build. All four give the same events hash for the same scene, seed and brain answers (see Determinism and replay). This page says when to use each and how. Way Use it to Speed Shows the world Play mode watch, inspect, debug a module as you set it yes Headless in the editor get a run's numbers quickly while the editor is open as fast as the brain allows no Batch mode CI, scenarios, replays, long checks with the editor closed as fast as the brain allows no Player build long watched runs, demos, runs on another machine as you set it yes The World's run settings These fields of the World decide how and how long a run goes. Every way of running reads them. Field What it does Reference Seed the run's seed: every random stream derives from it (RAND-02) 1234 Wait Mode Responsive: while the brain answers, Unity keeps drawing and the tick resumes later. Freeze: the main thread blocks until the answers are in. Both give the same run (SPACE-14) Responsive Run Speed PerFixedUpdate: a fixed number of ticks per physics step. Fast: as many ticks as fit in a frame budget. RealTime: a fixed number of ticks per second PerFixedUpdate Ticks Per Fixed Update, Fast Budget Ms, Real Time Ticks Per Second the number that goes with each speed 1, 10 ms, 5 Start On Play initialise and run when Play mode starts on Tick Limit, Wall Clock Minutes stop after this many ticks, or minutes of real time (0 = never) 0 Stop File stop at the next tick when this file exists empty Stop On Extinction stop when a species has no animal left off No Mutation switch mutation off (a control run) off A brain answer that takes time never changes the result: the World waits for it, whatever the speed. The speed only says how fast ticks go when nothing is waited for. Play mode Open a scene and press Play (Getting started). The run views draw the ground, the animals and the panel; see Views and real time for the camera keys. To watch at a steady pace, set Run Speed to RealTime and Real Time Ticks Per Second to 5 or 20. Run levels Three levels name the usual combinations of brain and mutation: Level Brain Mutation Servers needed L0 the random brain off none L1 the scene's brain (JEV) off JEV L2 the scene's brain (JEV) the LLM mutator JEV and Ollama EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.SetLevel(world, "L0") sets a world to a level. In batch mode, -level exists only for RealTimeRuns.FromCommandLine (below). The player has no -level argument, and it ignores an argument it doesn't know without a word: EvoSim.exe -level L0 runs the scene as it is, which is L2, calling JEV and Ollama. Give the player the equivalent arguments instead (RealTimeRuns.LevelArgs): Level Player arguments L0 -brain Random -noMutation L1 -noMutation L2 none Headless, from the editor EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns runs a scene without drawing it, in Freeze mode, and writes the run's files: // From an editor script, e.g. a menu item of your own: scene, seed, ticks, level, run name. string line = EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.Headless("HideVsFlee", 1234, 600, "L0", "my-run"); // → "HideVsFlee L0 seed 1234: 600 ticks, hash 27c52857…, brain Random, brain calls 0, …, folder C:\…\Logs\EvoSim\runs\my-run" Headless blocks the editor until the run ends. For a long run with model calls, HeadlessStart starts the same run and advances it from the editor's update loop, one tick at a time for up to 50 ms per editor update, so the editor stays usable; HeadlessStatus gives its progress, then its result line, which also goes to Logs/EvoSim/realtime-headless.txt. One stepped run goes at a time. In both cases the scene must not be open in the editor: the run opens the scene file itself, additively, and closes it without saving. To run a scenario asset the same way, use the Scenario Runner window (Editor tooling) or EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarioNamed("S03"), which returns one summary line per seed. Batch mode With the editor closed, Unity runs a static method and quits. From the repository root: $U = "C:\Program Files\Unity\Hub\Editor\6000.3.9f1\Editor\Unity.exe" & $U -batchmode -nographics -projectPath . -executeMethod EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 -seed 7 -ticks 2000 -quit Method Arguments What it does EvoSim.Batch.RunScenario -scenario S03 [-variant name] [-seed n] [-ticks n] [-responsive] runs one scenario asset (S00–S27), every seed of it unless -seed is given; one run folder per seed, Logs/EvoSim/runs/<scenario>-<variant>-s<seed>-<time>/, with run_info.json, events.jsonl, stats.csv, alleles.jsonl, final_population.json and summary.json EvoSim.Batch.RunRegression runs the EditMode tests of category T3 (pinned hashes, equivalences, scene checks); totals in Logs/EvoSim/Reports/regression-<time>.txt EvoSim.Batch.RunScenarios -tier T2\|T3\|T4 [-ticks n] runs every scenario variant of a tier, each seed twice, and checks both runs give the same hash; Logs/EvoSim/Reports/scenarios-<tier>-<time>.txt EvoSim.Batch.RunIntegrity [-checks B-02,B-03] [-scene path] [-brain JEV] [-cpu] [-judge gemma4:12b] the brain and mutator checks B-01–B-11 (32 §2); without -checks, all but B-07 and B-10. One JSON and one Markdown report per check EvoSim.Editor.RealTimeRuns.FromCommandLine -do headless\|behaviour -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -level L2 [-run NAME] -quit a headless run, or the behaviour probe (hiding, kills, food, babies); the result line is appended to Logs/EvoSim/realtime-batch.txt EvoSim.Editor.VisualPlayerBuild.BuildFromCommandLine [-scenes A,B] [-out folder] builds the Windows player (default: the six scenes, into Builds/EvoSim/<yyyy-MM-dd>) Reports go to Logs/EvoSim/Reports, run folders to Logs/EvoSim/runs. The Batch methods and BuildFromCommandLine exit Unity themselves: 0 on success, 1 when a run, a test, the build or a blocking check (B-01) failed, and 2 for RunScenario and RunIntegrity on an error such as an unknown scenario. FromCommandLine does not exit by itself: pass -quit. Its exit code is then 0 whatever happened, so read its result line. Note Batch mode cannot open a project that an open editor holds: close the editor first. Player builds The player is not in the repository: Builds/ is ignored by git, so build it yourself the first time. EvoSim ▸ Build ▸ Visual Player builds a Windows 64-bit player of the six reference scenes, HideVsFlee first, into Builds/EvoSim/<yyyy-MM-dd>/EvoSim.exe, and shows the result in a dialog. The build never edits the project's Build Settings: it passes its own scene list. It needs the Mono scripting backend for Standalone, and stops with a message rather than change Player settings. From the open editor, EvoSim.Editor.VisualPlayerBuild.BuildLater() starts the same build and writes its result to Logs/EvoSim/visual-player-build.txt. The player takes its settings from the command line. They are applied to the World before it starts: EvoSim.exe -scene HideVsFlee -seed 1234 -ticks 600 -speed 20 -capture 10 -run demo -window 1920x1080 -quitAtEnd Argument Meaning -scene NAME the scene to load (default: the first one, HideVsFlee) -seed N the run's seed -ticks N, -minutes M stop after N ticks, or M minutes of wall-clock time -speed X X ticks per second (RealTime), or fast, or fixed (PerFixedUpdate) -wait responsive\|freeze the wait mode -brain NAME the default brain, by GameObject name or brain id (-brain Random) -noMutation switch mutation off -stagger every species decides staggered (DEC-04) -capture S a screenshot every S seconds (0: start and end only, off: none) -cache FOLDER the answer cache to read and write -run NAME the run folder's name -window WxH a window of that size instead of full screen -quitAtEnd quit when the run stops, and log the events hash Run files, captures and the answer cache land next to the exe: Logs/EvoSim/… and Library/EvoSim/AnswerCache. To replay a live run without calling the model again, give the player the cache the live run wrote (-cache). To replay a player run headless in the editor, see Replay a player run in the editor.

guides/senses-and-prompts.html.title: Senses and prompts | EvoSim
guides/senses-and-prompts.html.summary: Senses and prompts A brain never sees the world. It reads a few words about it. At each decision, every sense of the animal's species turns one aspect of the world (the nearest food, the energy level) into one token from a short, fixed list. The tokens together are the animal's observation, and the species writes them as a situation text such as "Energy: low. Food: 1-4 meters away.". The species then puts that text into its prompt, with the rules of the world and the animal's genes. Discrete tokens keep the prompt short and let identical situations be answered once (06 — Senses). How it works flowchart LR S[Senses] -->|one token each| O[Observation] O -->|Write per token| T[Situation text] P[Prompt template] --> F[Full prompt] G[Genes block] --> F T --> F B[Brain's answer instruction] --> F The sense phase picks the animals that decide this tick (Decisions and brains). It casts the rays of the batched senses, then calls every sense of every deciding animal. Each sense returns an index into its token list (SENSE-01). The indices, in sense order, make an Observation (SENSE-02). Describe(Observation, TextStyle) has each sense write its token and joins the fragments with spaces: the situation text (SENSE-10). A brain that reads text fills the species' prompt template, built when the run started, with the animal's genes, the situation text and its own answer instruction (Prompt). Senses and tokens Type Role Sense reads one animal and returns one token from its fixed Tokens list BandedSense a sense of distance, in bands: "here", "adjacent" … "far", "none" BatchedSense a sense that casts rays, all in one batch per tick SenseContext what a sense may read: the state at the start of the tick, through the same queries as actions Observation one token index per sense, in sense order ObservationView an observation read by sense label, as actions do in IsRelevant The senses' depth-first order under the species is the order of the tokens in the observation and of the fragments in the situation text. Each sense has a Label ("Food", "Predator"), which starts its V1 fragment; two senses of one species can't share a label (V-17). A sense sees the world as it was at the start of the tick (SENSE-04), and never an animal hidden from it in cover nor one killed this tick (SENSE-06). The number of possible observations is the product of the token counts (SENSE-05). The species inspector shows it as Observation space. Validation warns above 100 000 (V-50), because the memo and the answer cache then rarely help. The reference senses Label Class Tokens Rule Energy LevelSense low, medium, high low below 30, high above 70 Stamina LevelSense low, medium, high prey 20 / 40, predators 10 / 20 Food NearestResourceSense here, adjacent, close, medium, far, none nearest item of a layer the diet grazes; "here" within the 0.5 m graze reach Predator NearestAnimalSense (threats) adjacent, close, medium, far, none nearest animal of a species whose diet strikes this one Prey NearestAnimalSense (prey) adjacent, close, medium, far, none nearest animal of a species this one strikes Cover NearestCoverSense here, adjacent, close, medium, far, none "here" when standing in cover Carcass NearestEntitySense adjacent, close, medium, far, none nearest carcass it may eat: portions left, not its own kill, not eaten from yet Animal, Other predator NearestAnimalSense (kin, readiness on) 4 bands × (ready, not ready), none readiness is seen within the Partner Range, 20 m Age AgeSense young, adult adult from the "maturity" trait, 150 ticks The reference prey has Energy, Stamina, Food, Predator, Cover, Animal and Age: 29 160 possible observations. The reference predator has Energy, Stamina, Prey, Carcass, Other predator and Age: 4 050. GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ Add Sense adds any of them to the selected species, from the prefabs in Assets/EvoSim/Modules/Senses. Distance bands A BandedSense turns a distance into a band (SENSE-20). Its Bands setting (Bands) holds the edges 1, 4 and 10 m and a vision of 20 m: Token Distance V1 text here (food, cover) within reach, or standing in it Food: here. adjacent ≤ 1 m Food: within 1 meter. close 1–4 m Food: 1-4 meters away. medium 4–10 m Food: 4-10 meters away. far 10–20 m Food: 10-20 meters away. none nothing within the vision Food: none within 20 meters. Vision is a trait, "vision", so a number gene can change it (SENSE-22). The sense reads each animal's own vision when it looks. The texts state the trait's default, so one token always gives one text. Band edges must be positive, increasing and below the vision (SENSE-21, V-30). Situation texts: V1 and V2 The World's Text Style chooses how every sense writes (SENSE-11). V1 is terse, V2 is first person. The reference uses V1. The same prey situation in both styles: V1: Energy: low. Stamina: high. Food: 1-4 meters away. Predator: 4-10 meters away. Cover: here. Animal: 10-20 meters away, ready to mate. Age: adult. V2: I am hungry and weak. I am rested. The nearest food is 1-4 meters away. The nearest predator is 4-10 meters away. I am in cover. The nearest other animal is 10-20 meters away. It is ready to mate. I am an adult. A text depends on the token only, never on the animal: the same observation always gives the same text (SENSE-10). The answer cache relies on it. Distances always say "meters" (SENSE-13). A level sense takes its V2 sentences from its Words field. A banded sense builds them from its Noun ("food", "other animal"). Batched raycasts A sense that needs line of sight or the terrain ahead derives from BatchedSense. It asks for its rays in RequestRays(Animal, RayBatch). The sense phase casts the rays of every deciding animal in one batch (SENSE-30), then the sense reads its results through Rays. The tokens must be the same as when rays are cast one at a time (SENSE-31). Rays never hit the views, so what an animal senses never depends on rendering (RAND-11). No reference sense casts rays; the test sense ObstacleSense does. Attachments A sense may also attach an object to the query, such as a small camera image, for a brain that reads images (SENSE-40). A query with an attachment is memoised and cached only if the sense gives a key for it (SENSE-41). The species' brain must accept attachments (V-51). No reference brain does. See A sense. How the prompt is written When the run starts, Build(Species) writes each species' prompt template (Prompt), in this order (PROMPT-01): Part Comes from Header the species' Prompt Header ("You decide what a wild animal does next in a simple world.") Actions: and one line per action, in action order each action's Description: - eat: go to the nearest visible food and eat it Rule lines every species module's WritePromptRules (search rule, locomotion, stamina, mating), then every world service's (the carcass line) Genes intro the species' Genes Intro ("This animal's instincts (its genes)…") {genes} one line per gene the brain reads, in locus order: - eat: "Eat whenever food is close." (PROMPT-02) Situation: {situation} the situation text {ask} the brain's AnswerInstruction, hard-coded in the brain because its parsing depends on it (PROMPT-07) The reference prey's prompt, for a founder in one situation, with the Ollama points brain (shortened): You decide what a wild animal does next in a simple world. Actions: - eat: go to the nearest visible food and eat it - flee: run away from the nearest predator - hide: go to the nearest cover and stay in it; predators can't see or catch an animal in cover … Animals move 1 meter per step. Predators run 2 meters per step when they hunt, but they have 30 stamina against an animal's 60, so a long chase tires them first. … This animal's instincts (its genes). They define its personality: follow them even when they seem unwise. Instincts that are meaningless have no effect. - eat: "Eat whenever food is close." - flee: "Run from any predator you see." … Situation: Energy: low. Stamina: high. Food: 1-4 meters away. Predator: 4-10 meters away. Cover: 1-4 meters away. Animal: none within 20 meters. Age: adult. Distribute 100 points across the actions according to how likely this animal is to choose each. JEV adds no instruction: it sends this text without its last line, followed by its own question and the actions as lettered options. The template's Id is a hash of its text. It is part of the answer cache's keys, so editing a header, a description or a rule line asks the model again (PROMPT-05). Placeholders Numbers in descriptions and rule lines come from the modules' settings, so the prompt never contradicts the world (PROMPT-03). The speed line above is written Animals move {walkSpeed} meter per step. Predators run {predator.Locomotion.runSpeed} meters per step…. Placeholder Reads {field} a field or property of the module writing the line: {walkSpeed} {Module.field} another module of the same species, named by its class, a base class or its GameObject: {Stamina.max} {species.Module.field} a module of another species: {predator.Stamina.max} {name} this species' display name {species.name}, {species.id} another species' display name or id {{ and }} a literal brace A field can be public or private. Numbers are written as the brain reads them ("4", "2.5"), booleans as "yes" or "no". An unknown placeholder stays in the text and validation reports it (V-53). The header and the genes intro have no writing module, so only {name} and the dotted forms work there. Frozen prompts A species can use a fixed text instead of the assembled one: set its Frozen Prompt to a text asset that contains {genes}, {situation} and {ask} (PROMPT-04). The prototype's prompts in 08 §7 are examples. Placeholders in it are still filled. A missing hole is reported (V-53). Settings Where Field Reference Effect World Text Style V1 V1 or V2 situation texts, for every species Species Prompt Header, Genes Intro see above the fixed parts of the prompt Species Frozen Prompt none replaces the assembled prompt Any sense Label empty = the sense's default the name the brain reads; must be unique in the species Banded sense Bands (Edges, Names, Vision), Noun 1, 4, 10 m; vision 20 m the bands, and the noun of V2 texts Level sense Stat, Low, High, Words energy 30 / 70 which stat, the thresholds, the V2 sentences Nearest animal sense Targets, Listed, Report Readiness, Partner Range threats; readiness off; 20 m which animals, and whether readiness is written Action Description per action its line in the prompt In the editor Select a species. In Edit mode, press Show the computed tables. The inspector lists the senses in situation-text order, with their tokens and the V1 and V2 texts of the first token. It also shows the Observation space and the Signature, which changes when a sense is added, removed, renamed or moved (V-12). Its Prompt preview builds the exact text a brain receives. Pick a Brain, a Founder genome, a Text style and one token per sense (or Random situation), then press Build. It shows the estimated token count and the brain's limit; Copy puts the text on the clipboard. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Animal Inspector shows the last situation text of the selected animal. Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Ask the Brain asks brains about a genome and a situation of your choice. Go further A sense: write your own sense, banded or batched. Decisions and brains: what happens to the observation and the prompt next. Species modules: WritePromptRules, for rule lines of your own modules. API: Sense, SenseContext, Bands, PromptWriter, PromptTemplate, SpeciesInspector. Specification: 06 — Senses and observations, 08 — Decisions, brains and prompts §7.

guides/testing.html.title: Testing | EvoSim
guides/testing.html.summary: Testing EvoSim's tests build small worlds in code, put animals exactly where a rule needs them, run a few ticks and check what happened. No test calls a language model: a scripted brain and fake mutators and servers answer instead, so every test repeats exactly with its seed. This page explains the test assemblies and the toolkit they share, EvoSim.Testing. To test a module of your own step by step, and to see what the conformance suites check, read Testing your module. The test assemblies Assembly Folder Holds Where it runs EvoSim.Tests.EditMode Assets/EvoSim/Tests/EditMode the unit tests of every system, the conformance suites, the static checks, the slow T3 tests Window ▸ General ▸ Test Runner, tab EditMode EvoSim.Tests.PlayMode Assets/EvoSim/Tests/PlayMode whole Lab 1 runs driven by FixedUpdate: run files, views, wait modes (tier T2) tab PlayMode EvoSim.Testing Assets/EvoSim/Testing the toolkit described below, and the test probes no tests of its own Student.Tests Assets/Student/Tests your tests, written by Assets ▸ Create ▸ EvoSim ▸ Script ▸ tab EditMode All four compile only when the Test Framework is present (UNITY_INCLUDE_TESTS), so none of them is ever part of a build. The EditMode folders follow the specification's chapters: Folder Covers Actions intents, interactions, act orders, locomotion and movement (07) Animals stats, traits, metabolism, busy states, age, death (05) Config tooltips and ranges of every setting, scenario overrides (14) Conformance the suites run against every module of a kind (30 §4) Core discovery, the tick loop, random streams, open hooks, static checks, the coverage gate Decisions, Http queries, brains, memo, cache, prompts; HTTP brains and mutators against fake servers (08) Environment distances, food, cover, entities, the food web (02, 03, 04) Genes, Mutation, Reproduction alleles and founders (09), mutation (10), mating, eggs and population (11) Recording, Regression run files (13); pinned hashes, soak, performance, the reference scenes (30 §6) Samples, Scenarios, Senses, Tooling the samples, the scenarios of 31, senses and situation texts (06), the editor and the exercises Every test states what it checks in its Description, with the test id and the rules it keeps: [Test, Description("T-ACT-04 (ACT-10): …")]. The coverage gate (Core/CoverageTests.cs) fails when a MUST rule of the specification is cited by no test. WorldFixture and New Derive your test class from WorldFixture and start each world with New(seed = 1234, waitMode = Freeze, name = "Test World"). It returns an empty WorldBuilder: a root with a World and its Environment, Brains and Phases objects, kept inactive until you build it. After each test the fixture destroys every world it made. Give each world of one test its own name when a test builds several. The default wait mode, Freeze, delivers late answers at once (WaitMode). Building a world Each call adds one thing and returns the builder, so the calls chain. A world has only what you add: no phase runs unless you add it, and species start with no founders. WorldBuilder call Adds Flat(width, depth) a FlatGround, x from 0 to width and z from 0 to depth, in meters Ground<T>(width, depth) a flat ground of your subclass: PondGround, RampGround, DoubleDistanceGround Food(initial, regrow, name, energy, hungryCover) a FoodGrid named "Grass" with an Edible (25 points an item); Food(0f, 0f) is empty and never regrows Cover(fraction), Carcasses() a CoverLayer "Thickets" (share 0.2), the CarcassSystem Service<T>(name, configure) any WorldService: brains, mutators and caches go under Brains, the rest under Environment DefaultBrain<T>(configure) a brain under Brains, made the World's default Phase<T>(configure) a phase after those added so far; phases run in that order (TICK-01) Species(name, s => …, id) a species, whose modules s (a SpeciesSetup) adds Configure(w => …) any World setting now: w.TextStyle, w.TickLimit, w.Asexual, w.DecisionPeriod… Get<T>(), Root, World the first component of a type built so far; the root GameObject; the World SpeciesSetup call Adds Population(n) n founders at random walkable positions when the world initialises (POP-04) Action<T>(name, configure, founders, withGene) an action under Actions with a TextGene on the same object; the name defaults to the class name without "Action", in lower case Sense<T>(configure, name) a sense under Senses; the call order is the order of the situation text (SPEC-03) Module<T>(configure, name) any other species module under Life: a stat, a rule, a locomotion, a crossover… On<T>(configure) a component on the species' own object: an Edible, a SearchRule, a Body Get<T>(), Find<T>(gameObjectName) a module added so far, to wire one module to another Every configure argument is called at once with the new component: set its fields there, or keep a reference to it. The Lab recipes Lab adds the reference parts in one call each, with the prototype's values. They are extension methods, so they chain with the builder's own calls. Call Adds PreyBody(), PredatorBody() locomotion, energy, stamina (60 / 30), metabolism, diet, mating rule, starvation, old age; the predator also digests and strikes with kill chance 0.5 PreySenses(), PredatorSenses() the 7 and 6 reference senses, in situation-text order PreyActionSet(), PredatorActionSet() the 6 and 4 actions, each with its text gene, founder pool and contrast pair LifeRules(cap, floor, incubation) litters of 2 to 4, uniform crossover, incubation, a cap and a floor LlmMutation(rate) the LLM mutation with the reference deck v4; the world then needs a mutator ReferencePhases(order) the 11 reference phases in the order of TICK-04 FakeMutation(configure) a MutatorService whose client is a FakeMutator Recorder(files), CheckInvariants() a run recorder (no files unless files is true); an InvariantPhase Ecology(size, cover, food, prey, predator, regrow) a 48 m square with grass, cover, carcasses, eggs and both species, without founders, phases or brain Lab1(prey, predators, …) the Lab 1 small world (S03): 24 prey, 4 predators, caps and floors, the phases, the fake mutator, the random brain Build or BuildUninitialized Build activates the tree and calls Initialize: discovery, validation, founders. It returns the ready World, or throws with the validation report. To test validation itself, call BuildUninitialized and validate yourself: var w = New(name: "requires").Flat(20, 20).DefaultBrain<RandomBrain>() .Species("prey", s => s.Action<RestAction>("rest").Module<KinematicLocomotion>(name: "Locomotion").Module<NeedsEnergyProbe>()) .BuildUninitialized(); var report = new ValidationReport(); Assert.IsTrue(w.Prepare(report), report.ToString()); Assert.AreEqual("Add Energy", report.Messages.Single(x => x.Id == "V-26").Fix.Label); Placing and steering animals After Build, Place sets up the exact situation a test needs. It records no event. Call Does Place.At(x, z) a point on the ground plane Place.Animal(species, point, genome, heading) an animal with each gene's first founder allele (or the given genome), its height set from the ground; the species' modules hear OnBorn Place.WithGenes(species, point, "sentence", …) an animal whose text genes hold these sentences, locus by locus Place.Food(layer, point), Place.Cover(cover, point) an item, or cover, on the cell that holds the point Place.Carcass(carcasses, species, point, killerId, portions, energy, lifetime) a carcass, as if an animal had been killed there A placed animal has chosen no action. a.Choose("eat") sets it by name, a.SetStat("energy", 90f) and a.StatOf("energy") write and read a stat by name, and a.Age = 200 makes it an adult. With only .Phase<ActPhase>() the chosen action runs every tick; with the decision phases and a brain, the brain chooses again at the next decision. Advance(n) then runs n ticks. The scripted brain ScriptedBrain answers each query in this order: FailWhen(query) returns a message: the query fails, as if the server were down (DEC-34); Vectors["species|observation key"] holds a row: that row; Policy(query) returns a row: that row; otherwise: a uniform row. ScriptedBrain.Prefer(species, "flee", epsilon) makes a row that prefers one action, and ScriptedBrain.Token(query, "Predator") reads one sense's token, so a policy can react to the situation. The brain counts Calls and Batches, keeps every query in Seen, and answers DelayCalls Advance calls late. MixesSpecies, ActionLimit, TokenLimit and TakesAttachments play the limits of real brains. The system ships no rule-based brain: this one is for tests only. Fake mutators and servers FakeMutator replaces the mutator model. By default it answers each sentence with "quickly" added before its period; set Answer = (sentence, seed, prompt) => … for another rule, FailWhen to fail, DelayCalls to answer late. It records Prompts and BatchSizes. The operators, guards and redraws stay the real ones: an answer equal to its parent is rejected and drawn again (MUT-13). FakeHttpTransport plays a server for an HTTP brain or mutator client: set it as their Transport. Jev() and OllamaPoints() answer like the two reference servers, Respond scripts any answer, FailWith returns an HTTP status, Hang never answers, DelayMs waits. Requests and MaxInFlight show what was sent. See An HTTP brain or mutator server. Checks Golden files (Golden). Golden.Check("situations.tsv", text) compares a long output with a file in Assets/EvoSim/Tests/Golden; a missing file is written from this run. See Golden files. Invariants (Invariants). Invariants.Check(w) lists every broken invariant of 30 §5 (positions, NaN, stat ranges, ids, dead animals still listed, probability rows, cap and floor, carcass portions, genomes). CheckInvariants() adds an InvariantPhase that fails the test at the first one; call it after the other phases. Statistics (Stat). Stat.Binomial(successes, trials, p) and Stat.Mean(values, expected) pass within 4 standard errors; Stat.Uniform(counts) is a χ² test. Draw from a fixed seed, so the test passes or fails the same way every run. Static checks (SourceScan). SourceScan.Find(SourceScan.Files("Runtime"), pattern) searches the code with comments removed. Core/StaticChecks.cs uses it to forbid UnityEngine.Random (T-RAND-01), Actions/ActionTests.cs to forbid actions that read genes (T-ACT-09). The probes The probes (Assets/EvoSim/Testing/Probes) stand in for a student's module; the conformance suites leave them out. Kind Probes phases CallbackPhase (runs a callback between two phases), TracePhase, BlackboardPhase, DelayedPhase (waits like a slow brain), RandomEventPhase, SnapshotPhase, ThrowingPhase, AllocationProbe, InvariantPhase actions GoToAction (walks or runs to a set point), FeedAction, ProbeAction, BatchProbeAction senses ProbeSense, ObstacleSense, AllLayersObstacleSense, CameraProbeSense, BatchProbeSense movement and ground TurningLocomotion, SlopeLimitLocomotion, BatchProbeLocomotion, PondGround, RampGround, DoubleDistanceGround, SideCover other modules SureKillDiet, TraitProbe, HookProbe, WorldHookProbe, NeedsEnergyProbe, CountingCrossover, FruitSystem, MemoryBrain, ShowProbeView A complete test Two adults next to each other, a brain that always chooses mate, one tick: the babies are born during the tick and aged by its death phase, so they end it at age 1 (ANIM-35). using System.Linq; using EvoSim; using EvoSim.Testing; using NUnit.Framework; public class BabyAgeTests : WorldFixture { [Test, Description("ANIM-35: babies born in a tick are aged by that tick's death phase")] public void BabiesAgeOnTheirBirthTick() { var w = New(name: "baby age").Ecology(40f, 0f, 0f, regrow: 0f, prey: s => s.LifeRules(40, 0)).ReferencePhases() .DefaultBrain<ScriptedBrain>(b => b.Policy = q => ScriptedBrain.Prefer(q.Species, "mate")).Build(); var prey = w.FindSpecies("prey"); foreach (var x in new[] { 10f, 10.5f }) { var a = Place.Animal(prey, Place.At(x, 10)); a.Age = 200; a.SetStat("energy", 90f); } w.Advance(1); var babies = prey.Animals.Where(a => a.Origin == "birth").ToList(); Assert.IsNotEmpty(babies); Assert.IsTrue(babies.All(b => b.Age == 1 && b.BornTick == 0)); } } Go further Testing your module: the step-by-step for your own module, the conformance suites, golden files and the slow T3 tests. The teaching path and the samples: modules to rewrite and complete extensions, each with its tests. Determinism and replay, which every test relies on, and 30 — Tests: every test id, the tiers and the regression tests.

guides/the-tick.html.title: A tick, phase by phase | EvoSim
guides/the-tick.html.summary: A tick, phase by phase Simulation time is counted in ticks, not seconds (SPACE-10). A tick runs every TickPhase of the World once, in hierarchy order (TICK-01). Unity's frame loop only decides how many ticks run per frame: what happens in a tick, and the result of a run, never depend on it. This page follows one tick, then explains how the World waits for the brain, when a run stops, and how births and deaths happen inside a tick. The reference phases The reference scenes have eleven phases under the World's Phases object (TICK-04): # Phase What it does Waits for 1 SensePhase picks who decides (living, not busy animals on their decision tick or without an action); rebuilds the spatial index; reads every sense of each deciding animal — 2 AskBrainsPhase builds each decision's query; answers it from the memo, from another animal of this tick with the same key, or from the answer cache; sends the rest, one batch per brain — 3 ChooseActionsPhase stores the answers in the memo and the cache, then draws each deciding animal's action from its species' sampling stream, after the temperature the brains 4 ActPhase in the act order, each animal's action gives an intent and maybe an interaction; the locomotion moves the animal; interactions within reach apply (graze, strike, scavenge); metabolism is paid; busy counters drop — 5 BreedPhase each ready animal that chose mate breeds with the nearest ready partner within reach: one egg per baby, crossover and mutation choices drawn now, mutation requests sent — 6 HatchPhase eggs due this tick become animals (births) the mutator, when an egg's mutations are not back 7 DeathPhase killed animals are recorded; every living animal ages by one tick; the death rules run (starvation, old age) — 8 MigrationPhase a species above its cap loses animals chosen at random (cause migrated) — 9 EnvironmentPhase food layers regrow, each with its own stream; carcasses and other entities rot, move or vanish — 10 FloorPhase a species below its floor gets newcomers — 11 RecordPhase a statistics row every 100 ticks, file flushes every 500; events are written as they happen, not here — Each phase changes only what it is responsible for, and what it changes is visible to the phases after it (TICK-02). The decisions of a tick read the state the previous tick left, after its Floor phase (TICK-05). In the reference the incubation is 0 ticks, so a baby conceived in Breed hatches in the Hatch phase of the same tick. Advance and the tick boundary Advance(maxTicks) runs ticks and returns how many it completed. Play mode calls it from FixedUpdate or Update; tests and headless runs call it directly. At the tick boundary (between two ticks) the World checks the stop conditions, then copies each animal's position to PreviousPosition, which the views interpolate from. Each phase in turn: the World asks the phase what it waits for, waits if needed, then calls its Run. An exception in a phase stops the run, with the phase's name in StopReason, and is thrown again. After the last phase Tick grows by one and the stop conditions are checked again. World.Tick counts the ticks completed. During the first tick it is 0, so the events of that tick, like the founders', have t = 0. NextPhaseIndex is the phase that runs next (0 between ticks). Waiting for the brain A phase that needs answers from a service returns them from WaitsFor as a Pending (TICK-03). The World never runs the phase before the work is done. What it does meanwhile is the World's Wait Mode (SPACE-14): flowchart LR A[Advance] --> W{phase.WaitsFor done?} W -->|yes| R[phase.Run] W -->|no, Responsive| X[return, Unity keeps drawing] --> A W -->|no, Freeze| B[block on Pending.Wait] --> R Responsive (the editor default): Advance returns at once and the tick stays at that phase. The next call asks again, and runs the phase once the answers are in. The editor keeps drawing; State is Waiting. Freeze: the main thread blocks until the answers are in; State is Blocked. Batch runs and most tests use it. Both modes give the same run and the same events hash (RAND-11): a decision is never made on old observations, and every random draw happens at the same point of the tick. WaitCount counts the waits, and WaitingFor names the phase being waited for. The World inspector's state line shows the wait, for example Waiting — tick 812 — waiting for jev: 23 queries, 1.4 s. In the reference, two phases wait: Choose actions (the brains) and Hatch (the mutator). Stop conditions A run stops cleanly at a tick boundary, with every file written (RAND-20). The conditions are fields of the World: Field Stops when Reason given Tick Limit that many ticks are done (0 = never) tick limit Wall Clock Minutes that many minutes of real time passed since Initialize (0 = never) wall-clock limit Stop File the file exists (empty = never) stop file Stop On Extinction a species has no animal left extinction of <species> RequestStop (the inspector's Stop button) also waits for the next boundary. Two stops happen inside a tick: a strict brain's failure, in Choose actions before any action is drawn, and an exception in a phase. Whatever the reason, every world module hears OnRunStopped once; the recorder closes its files there. Run speeds The Run Speed only says how many ticks run per frame. PerFixedUpdate runs Ticks Per Fixed Update ticks per physics step; Fast runs as many ticks as fit in Fast Budget Ms per frame; RealTime runs Real Time Ticks Per Second. A wait for the brain pauses all three the same way, and the run is the same at any speed (SPACE-11). The settings are in Running and building. Births and deaths during a tick Animals join the living in four places: the founders at Initialize, babies in the Hatch phase, newcomers in the Floor phase, and founders of a species added during the run. Each time, Species.Add appends the animal to Animals, puts it in the spatial index, and calls OnBorn on the species, then on each of its modules, then on each world module, in hierarchy order. A death has two steps: World.RecordDeath(a, cause) marks the animal gone, counts it, records one death event with its cause, age, generation, meals, offspring and killer (ANIM-42), then calls OnDied on the species, its modules and every world module. An animal already gone is ignored. At the end of its work, the phase calls RemoveGone on the species: the dead leave the list, which keeps its creation order. Until RemoveGone runs, a dead animal is still in Animals, marked IsGone: every loop over animals skips gone ones. A strike in the Act phase only marks its victim Killed; the animal acts no more, and the Deaths phase records it. A phase of your own can kill too: public class LightningPhase : TickPhase { [SerializeField, Range(0f, 0.01f)] float chance = 0.0005f; // per animal per tick public override void Run(TickContext t) { foreach (var s in World.AllSpecies) { var rng = t.Stream(s, "lightning"); // "<species>/lightning" foreach (var a in s.Animals) if (!a.IsGone && rng.Chance(chance)) World.RecordDeath(a, "lightning"); s.RemoveGone(); } } } The cause gets its own column in stats.csv (prey_deaths_lightning). The tick context Every phase gets the same TickContext in WaitsFor and Run. It is small on purpose: Member What it gives World the World: its species, services, queries, decisions Tick the current tick Random the World's named random streams Stream(species, purpose) a species' stream, <species id>/<purpose> (RAND-03) Stream(name) a world stream, such as act-order Everything else a phase reaches through the World: Decisions, Space, Queries, Events, and the services with World.Service<T>(). Go further The world and its modules: how the phase list is found and set up. Phases, services and world hooks: write a phase, wait for asynchronous work. Decisions and brains, Actions and movement, Reproduction and population: what the phases do in detail. Determinism and replay: why the speed and the wait mode never change a run. Specification: 12 — Tick order and determinism, 02 — Space and time.

guides/views-and-real-time.html.title: Views and real time | EvoSim
guides/views-and-real-time.html.summary: Views and real time The simulation runs on plain C# objects: animals are not GameObjects. What you see in Play mode is drawn by views that read the World after each tick and never write to it. Animal views are bodies that follow their animals. Run views are a painted ground, markers for carcasses and eggs, an on-screen panel of numbers, a camera you can steer, and screenshots. Because nothing visual feeds back into the run, a run gives the same events hash whether it is drawn or not, at any frame rate (SPACE-12, RAND-11). How it works Each frame, Unity first runs the ticks the run speed allows, then the views read the result. flowchart LR T[Ticks: FixedUpdate or Update] --> S[(Animals, food, entities)] S -->|LateUpdate| V[World places the animal views] S -->|LateUpdate| G[GroundView and EntityMarkers] S -->|Update| O[RunOverlay reads the numbers] V --> C[WorldCamera, after the views] C --> F[Frame drawn, overlay on top] F --> P[RunCapture saves a PNG] Pools. When a run starts in Play mode, the World makes one ViewPool per species that has a Body. The pools live under a Views (runtime) object under the World, which is never saved. Each pool makes Prewarm views ahead, by default as many as the species' initial population. Take and return. In its LateUpdate, the World gives a view to each new animal (Take) and takes back the view of each animal that is gone (Return). A view is reused: it holds only the animal's id (AnimalId). Placing. The World puts each view between its animal's position at the previous tick and its position now, sets its height from the ground, and turns it toward where the animal moved (or its heading when it stood still). OnShow. The World then calls OnShow on the view, which may change colours or animations. The reference view, ActionView, colours a marker above the head by the current action and darkens the body as its energy drops. Views can't change what animals sense: every view part is on layer 2, Ignore Raycast (IgnoreRaycastLayer), which every sense ray leaves out, and every collider of a view is disabled. Interpolation Ticks are discrete: an animal jumps from one position to the next. To make movement smooth, the World places each view at a fraction of the way between the two positions: InterpolationFactor, the part of the next tick already elapsed. Run speed Interpolation factor PerFixedUpdate the time since the last physics step, divided by the physics step RealTime the ticks the real-time clock owes, between 0 and 1, while running Fast 1: many ticks per frame, nothing to smooth any, while the tick waits for a brain or the mutator 1: views rest where the last tick left them Turn Interpolate Views off on the World to see the raw tick positions. The main types Type Role Body a species module: the view prefab (or a placeholder capsule), its colour and size AnimalView the component on a body's root; the World calls OnShow on it every frame ActionView the reference view: marker coloured by action, body darker when hungry ViewPool the reusable views of one species ActionColors one colour per action name, shared by views and the overlay GroundView paints a flat world's ground, cover and food EntityMarkers one small marker per carcass, egg or other entity RunOverlay the panels of numbers, drawn in the editor and in a build RunNumbers what the overlay shows, read from the World's own counters WorldCamera the camera: pan, zoom, orbit, follow an animal RunCapture, ContactSheet screenshots of the run and a sheet of thumbnails The run views The reference scenes have a Run views object at the scene root, outside the World, with GroundView, EntityMarkers, RunOverlay and RunCapture, and a WorldCamera on the main camera. EvoSim ▸ Views ▸ Add Run Views to Reference Scenes adds whatever is missing to the six reference scenes (and rebuilds the two reference bodies). In a scene of your own, add the four components to any GameObject and the camera component to the camera. Each one finds the first World of the scene when its World field is empty. Ground GroundView draws a flat ground as one quad with a texture of one pixel per cell, the finest cell of the food and cover layers. A pixel is Food colour when its cell holds a food item, Cover colour when it is in cover, Soil colour otherwise. The texture is repainted once per tick and uploaded only when a pixel changed. Show Cover and Show Food switch the layers off. A terrain ground is not painted: the terrain shows itself. Entities EntityMarkers places one marker per entity of every entity kind under the World: a dark red disc 0.8 m wide per carcass, an ivory ball per egg, a grey 0.3 m cube for any other kind. The colours are the Carcass, Egg and Other fields. Used-up entities get no marker. Action colours Bodies and the overlay's legend share these colours (ActionColors): Action Colour eat green flee yellow hide blue follow cyan rest grey mate pink hunt red searching (the action had nothing to act on, ACT-04) white no decision yet dark grey any other action name a colour made from the name's letters, the same on every run The overlay RunOverlay draws two panels with Unity's immediate-mode GUI, so they also appear in a player build. Tab hides and shows them. The text scales with the window's height (Font Size 16 at 1080 lines). The run panel, top left: Line Example Meaning tick and state Tick 412 running also paused, stopped: tick limit, or waiting for JEV: 12 queries, 1.4 s pace Ticks/s 4.9 of 5 FPS 118 ticks per second over the last second, against the target of the run speed one line per species Prey: 31 living, 40 born, 33 died, 2 eggs, gen 3 kills and eggs appear when not zero; gen is the highest generation mutations Mutations 5 ok, 1 failed of 7 new alleles, failed mutations, mutations started model calls Model calls: brain 245, mutator 5; cache 30, memo 400 calls to the models, answers from the cache and the memo Under it, the legend shows each action name of the world once, plus search, in its colour. The animal panel, top right, appears when the camera follows an animal: its species and id, age, generation, action, stats, the probabilities of its last decision, and its genes. When it dies, the panel says it is gone. All the numbers come from RunNumbers, which reads the World's counters and nothing else; a play-mode test checks them against the event log. The camera WorldCamera frames the whole world when the run starts. It reads the keys and mouse in real time, so it works while the run is paused or waits for a brain. Control Effect W A S D or the arrow keys pan (stops following) mouse wheel zoom, from 3 m to 2 000 m (not over a panel) right mouse button, held orbit left and right, tilt up and down (10° to 89°) Q, E orbit left, right middle mouse button, held drag the ground (stops following) F frame the whole world again (stops following) left click on an animal follow it Esc stop following Tab hide or show the overlay A click picks the living animal whose view is nearest on screen, within Pick Pixels (24 at 1080 lines). Views have no colliders, so picking compares screen positions, never rays. A click on an overlay panel doesn't pick: the overlay gives the camera its Covers test through Blocks. When you start following an animal, the camera comes as close as Follow Distance (15 m) and then keeps the animal in the centre. Other fields: Pitch (55°), Yaw, Pan Speed (0.8 camera distances per second), Orbit Speed (90° per second). Captures RunCapture saves what the screen shows, overlay included, as PNG files: one when the run starts, one every Every Seconds of real time (10; 0 for the start and end only), and one when the run stops. Then it makes contact_sheet.png: up to 24 thumbnails, 4 per row, evenly spread over the run, the first and the last kept (ContactSheet). Files land in Folder/run/, by default Logs/EvoSim/captures/<run>/, where run is the name of the run folder the recorder writes under Logs/EvoSim/runs/. Without a recorder it is the World's name, seed and start time. Each file is named NNN-tTTTTTT-label.png: the capture number, the tick, and start, t or end. In a player build the folder is next to the exe; -capture S sets the seconds, -capture off turns captures off (Running and building). Note Captures need drawn frames. In batch mode with -nographics nothing is captured. In the editor, keep the Game view visible: a capture that gets no frame for 5 s is given up and counted in Skipped. Watching in real time The run speed decides how many ticks run per frame; the World's run settings are in Running and building. To watch, use RealTime with Real Time Ticks Per Second at 5 or 20. When a tick needs answers from a model, it stops at the phase that needs them until every answer is in (SPACE-13). waiting for JEV: 12 queries, 1.4 s means that the Choose actions phase waits for 12 queries sent to the brain named JEV, for 1.4 s so far. waiting for the mutator: 2 eggs means the Hatch phase waits for the mutated genes of 2 eggs that are due to hatch. In the Responsive wait mode, Unity keeps drawing meanwhile: the views rest, the camera and the overlay still work. In Freeze mode the main thread blocks, so the window doesn't redraw until the answers arrive. Either way the run is the same (SPACE-14). So the pace you see is the slower of the target and the models. In the reference test of HideVsFlee with JEV and the mutator live, the overlay showed about 0.55 ticks per second for a target of 5; the same run replayed from the answer cache kept the target. After a wait the real-time clock doesn't catch up in a burst: it owes at most a tenth of a second of ticks (or one tick). Settings Where Field What it does Reference World Show Views draw the animals on World Interpolate Views place views between tick positions on World Views Outside Play Mode also make views outside Play mode (tests leave it off) off Body Prefab, Color, Size, Prewarm the view prefab or capsule colour, size in meters, views made ahead prey 0.6 m, predator 0.9 m ActionView Hungry Brightness brightness of the body at zero energy 0.35 RunOverlay Font Size, Visible text size at 1080 lines; panels shown 16, on RunCapture Every Seconds, Folder, Contact Sheet capture period, folder, make the sheet 10, Logs/EvoSim/captures, on In the editor During Play mode the views are under World ▸ Views (runtime). Select one in the Hierarchy or the Scene view, and Window ▸ EvoSim ▸ Animal Inspector shows its animal. See Editor tooling for the other windows. Go further Views: your own AnimalView, a body prefab, markers for your entities, a panel of your own. Determinism and replay: why the hash doesn't depend on rendering. Specification: 02 — Space and time (SPACE-12 to SPACE-14).

guides/world-and-modules.html.title: The world and its modules | EvoSim
guides/world-and-modules.html.summary: The world and its modules A simulation is one GameObject with a World component, and everything under it. Each feature is a component, a module: a sense, an action, a food layer, a brain, a tick phase. To add a feature you add a component; to switch it off you disable it. The World finds its modules, sets them up in a fixed order, checks the configuration, and then runs ticks. This page explains how the World reads its tree and what it calls, when. The tree of a reference scene Assets/EvoSim/Scenes/HideVsFlee.unity, as EvoSim ▸ Build Reference Scenes makes it (the other Lab 1 scenes differ only in sizes and numbers): Lab1 World World ├── Ground FlatGround, 64 × 64 m ├── Environment │ ├── Grass FoodGrid, Edible (grazed, 25 points per item) │ ├── Thickets CoverLayer (30 % of the ground) │ ├── Carcasses CarcassSystem │ └── Eggs EggSystem ├── Brains JEV (JevBrain, the default brain), Random, Ollama points, │ Answer cache, Mutator (MutatorService), Mutator client ├── Recording RunRecorder, LiveStatistics ├── Phases Sense, Ask brains, Choose actions, Act, Breed, Hatch, │ Deaths, Migration, Environment, Floor, Record (one phase each) ├── Prey Species (40 founders), SearchRule, Edible (struck), Body │ ├── Locomotion KinematicLocomotion │ ├── Stats Energy, Stamina, Metabolism │ ├── Senses Energy, Stamina, Food, Predator, Cover, Animal, Age │ ├── Actions eat, flee, hide, follow, rest, mate (each with its TextGene) │ ├── Food Diet (Grass) │ ├── Life MatingRule, Litter, UniformCrossover, Incubation, Starvation, │ │ OldAge, CapRule, FloorRule, DecisionSchedule │ └── Mutation LlmMutation └── Predator the same groups: hunt, follow, rest, mate; Digestion; Diet (prey, carcass:prey) The camera, the light and the Run views object sit beside the World, not under it: they only display (Views and real time). GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ New World makes the same World tree with the random brain as default, and GameObject ▸ EvoSim ▸ New Species adds a species to it. Who owns a module The World reads its tree with three rules (ARCH-05, ARCH-06): A module belongs to the nearest owner above it. A SpeciesModule belongs to the nearest Species above it (or on the same GameObject). A species inside another species is an error (V-01). A species module with no species above it is an error too (V-02). Disabled means absent. A disabled component, or one on an inactive GameObject, is not part of the world. Disabling an action also removes the text gene on it or under it, from the genome, the prompt and the signature. Order matters only within a kind. Groups such as Senses or Life are only folders. The modules of one kind are ordered depth first in the hierarchy: the n-th action found is action n (its place in the probabilities and the prompt), the n-th sense gives the n-th fragment of the situation text, the n-th gene is locus n. A text gene steers the nearest enabled action on its GameObject or above it. A text gene under no action is treated as free, with a warning (V-06) unless it is marked free. World modules: phases and services A WorldModule sits under the World and outside every species (one under a species is ignored, V-15). There are two kinds: Kind Base class What it is Found by Phase TickPhase one step of every tick the World runs every phase in hierarchy order Service WorldService something phases and modules use: the ground, food layers, cover, brains, the recorder type: World.Service<T>(); type and name: World.Service<FoodGrid>("Grass") A service's name is its GameObject's name (ServiceName). Modules find services by type or name when they initialise, never through a scene reference: that is what lets one prefab serve several scenes (ARCH-08). Initialisation, step by step Initialize sets up a run. It is called by Play mode when Start On Play is on, by Play, or by a test. Modules never set themselves up in Awake or Start, whose order Unity does not guarantee: the World calls them, always in this order (ARCH-04). The step numbers are those of 20 §4, which the API comments use too. Step What happens — Reset: tick 0; new random streams and a new event log from the seed 0 a World inside another World is an error (V-16) 1 species: every enabled species under the World, in hierarchy order 2 world modules: every enabled phase and service, in hierarchy order; the phase list is the tick's order (TICK-01) 3 services: each service's Initialize, the ground first, then the others in hierarchy order 4–5 species modules: each species collects the modules it owns, binds each text gene to its action, and builds its action, gene and sense orders; ids and display names must be unique (V-07) 6 every species module's Declare (stats and traits), then every species module's Initialize (look-ups), then every phase's Initialize; the founder alleles are registered 7 the food web is derived from the diets; each species is signed (SPEC-03) and its prompt template built 8 validation: the core checks, then every module's Validate; an error stops here, Initialize returns false and keeps the messages in LastReport 9 views: a pool of views per species that has a Body — Begin: every world module's Begin, in hierarchy order, for initial content such as the first food items 10 founders: each species' Initial Population, at random walkable positions, genomes drawn from the founder pools (POP-04) The reset and steps 0 to 8 are Prepare, which creates no animal. The editor validates with it, so Declare, Initialize and Validate also run in Edit mode. They must not change the scene: put anything that creates content in Begin. The lifecycle hooks Hook On Called Initialize services step 3, before the species' modules exist Declare species modules step 6, before any species module initialises Initialize species modules, then phases step 6, after every Declare WritePromptRules species modules, services step 7, while each species' prompt is built Validate every module step 8; also by the Validate button, the play-mode gate, and when a species is added during the run Begin world modules once, after validation passed, before the founders; never in Edit mode OnBorn the species, its modules, then every world module each animal that joins the living, founders included OnDied the species, its modules, then every world module each death, once it is recorded OnSpeciesAdded world modules when AddSpecies adds a species during the run OnRunStopped world modules once, when the run stops, whatever the reason Within each line, modules are called in hierarchy order. The extension pages explain each hook from the module's side: Species modules and Phases, services and world hooks. Validation and the play-mode gate One validation engine runs everywhere (EDIT-01): the Validate button of the World and Species inspectors, the play-mode gate, Initialize, and the tests. Each message has a validator id (V-01 to V-62, listed in 21 §2), a severity, the object at fault, and often a fix button. Severity Effect Error blocks Play and the run Warning the run starts; something is probably not what you meant Information worth knowing When you press Play, the gate (PlayModeGate) validates every enabled World of the open scenes. An error cancels Play and logs EvoSim: Play blocked — V-xx …; clicking the line selects the object at fault. The inspectors' validation lists and fix buttons are described in Editor tooling. Run controls Once initialised, the World advances as its run controls say. In Play mode the World inspector shows them as buttons (Play, Pause, Step, Run N, Stop). Method What it does Play initialises if needed, then runs Pause, Resume stops advancing, goes on again; a tick that waits for the brain stays where it is Step runs one tick, then pauses RunFor runs that many ticks, then pauses RequestStop ends the run at the next tick boundary (the inspector's Stop) Stop ends the run now; for a tick boundary, or inside a tick before anything changed A stopped run is over: its files are complete, and a new run needs Initialize again. Leaving Play mode, or disabling the World, stops the run too. State says where the run is: Idle, Running, Paused, Stepping, Waiting or Blocked (a tick waits for answers), Stopped. Tests and batch runs skip the controls and call Advance directly (A tick, phase by phase). The main types Type Role World the root: finds, sets up, validates and runs everything below it Species a kind of animal; owns its modules and its living animals SpeciesModule the base of every module under a species WorldModule the base of phases and services TickPhase, WorldService the two kinds of world module Ownership the ownership rules above, as functions ValidationReport, ValidationMessage, ValidationFix the messages of a validation pass Settings The World's run settings (seed, wait mode, speed, stop conditions) are listed in Running and building. The others: Field What it does Reference Separate World Seed, World Seed give the map (terrain, cover, initial food) its own seed (RAND-04) off Decision Period ticks between two decisions of an animal (DEC-01) 4 Sampling Temperature sharpens (below 1) or flattens (above 1) the brain's probabilities before the draw (DEC-20) 1 Memo Capacity most answers the decision memo keeps (DEC-30); 0 = no limit 262 144 Text Style situation texts terse (V1) or in the first person (V2) (SENSE-11) V1 Default Brain the brain of species that name none (DEC-13) JEV Shuffled Genes, Random Founders, No Mutation, Asexual the experimental controls C3, C4, C2, C7 (15 §1) off Show Views, Interpolate Views, Views Outside Play Mode what the views do; they never change a run on, on, off Go further A tick, phase by phase: what happens once the run starts. Species modules and Phases, services and world hooks: writing your own modules. Editor tooling: the World and Species inspectors. index.html.title: Evolving animals in Unity | EvoSim
index.html.summary: EvoSim: evolving animals in Unity Animals whose behaviour is written in English. Each gene is a short sentence, such as "Run from any predator you see." At every decision, a language model reads an animal's genes together with what it senses, and gives a probability for each action it could take. Animals eat, flee, hide, hunt and mate. Their babies inherit a mix of their parents' sentences, and now and then a sentence mutates. Over generations, the sentences that keep animals alive spread. The HideVsFlee scene at tick 34. Light green cells are grass and dark green cells are thickets where prey can hide. The ball above each animal shows its current action: green eat, yellow flee, blue hide, red hunt, and so on. The panel counts living animals, births, deaths and model calls. Where to start You want to… Read open a scene and watch it run Getting started understand the whole loop in one page How EvoSim works learn one part in depth the guides: the world, a tick, senses, brains, actions, genes, mutation… add a sense, an action, a gene, a brain, a phase… Extending EvoSim, then the page for your kind of module rewrite a reference module as an exercise The teaching path look up a class or a method the API reference, grouped by folder know exactly what must hold (rule SENSE-01, DEC-30…) the specification Three ideas to keep in mind The scene is the configuration. A world is a tree of GameObjects. Every feature (a sense, an action, a gene, a tick phase, a brain) is a component in that tree. Add a component and its feature is in. Disable it and the feature is gone. No code changes needed. Animals are data. An animal is a plain C# object, not a GameObject. Phases process all animals in batches, and the visible bodies only display them. A seed replays a run exactly. Every random draw comes from a named stream seeded by the World. The same seed and the same answers from the brain give the same run, event for event. Your modules must keep this: see Determinism and replay. About this site The API reference is generated from the documentation comments in the code (///). The specification is the contract the code implements (Docs/Interface in the repository). Each rule id in the text, such as SENSE-01, links to its rule. To document your own code the same way, see Documenting your code.

spec/01-concepts-and-glossary.html.title: 01 — Concepts and glossary | EvoSim
spec/01-concepts-and-glossary.html.summary: 01 — Concepts and glossary 1. The loop in one picture ┌────────────────────────── one tick ──────────────────────────┐ genes ──┐ │ │ (text, │ │ senses ──► observation ──► brain ──► probabilities ──► draw │ numbers)│ │ (discrete) (+ situation (batched, over the an │ │ │ text) cached) species' action │ │ │ actions │ │ │ action ──► intent ──► locomotion ──► interactions │ │ │ (repeated every tick until the next decision) │ │ │ │ │ │ metabolism ─► deaths ─► mating ─► (mutation) ─► births │ │ │ environment: food regrows, carcasses rot, ... │ │ └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ └──── number genes set traits at birth (e.g. stamina) ───────────────── Nobody programs which behaviour is good. Animals that eat, escape and mate leave more children, and their genes spread. There is no fitness function. Genes are readable: most of them are short English sentences ("Rest when you are tired."). A brain (an LLM in the reference) turns the sentences and the animal's situation into probabilities over its actions. Ordinary code does everything physical: moving, eating, striking, breeding. The brain only chooses among actions. Mutation is blind: it changes a gene at random (an LLM making a small edit to a sentence, or a numeric rule changing a number) without knowing what helps. Selection decides what stays. 2. Core rules CORE-01 (MUST) No fitness function exists anywhere. Survival and reproduction follow only from the world rules and the animals' behaviour. CORE-02 (MUST) Every behaviour-relevant feature (a sense, an action, a gene, a stat, a resource, a population rule, a mutation operator, a brain, a tick phase, a locomotion) is a module behind a documented interface. Adding, removing or replacing one needs no change to core code. CORE-03 (MUST) No species, action, sense or gene name is special in core code. The prey/predator ecology of the prototype is a configuration of reference modules. CORE-04 (MUST) The system runs with any number of species (≥ 1), actions per species (≥ 1), genes (≥ 0) and senses (≥ 0). Limits imposed by a module (e.g. at most 16 options for the JEV brain) are checked before the run. CORE-05 (MUST) Per-animal state lives in the animal's record. Modules hold settings and logic; they never keep hidden per-animal state of their own (a module needing per-animal data declares a stat or a trait, 05). CORE-06 (MUST) The brain never moves an animal or changes the world. It returns probabilities over the actions of the animal's species; everything else is done by actions, the locomotion and the tick phases. CORE-07 (MUST) Mutation is blind: a mutation operator sees the gene it changes (and, for text genes, at most one fixed context line), never the animal, its fitness, the world or the other genes. CORE-08 (SHOULD) Configuration errors are found before the first tick (validation in the editor and at start), not in the middle of a run. CORE-09 (MUST) A run is reproducible from its configuration, its seed and its answer caches (12). 3. Glossary Term Meaning World The root of a simulation: space, environment, species, tick phases, services, random streams. One world per run; several worlds may exist side by side (tests). Tick One simulation step. All rules are written per tick. Unity time only drives the visuals. Phase One step of a tick (decide, act, breed, …). A world holds an ordered list of phases (12). Run Ticks from 0 to a stop condition, with a seed, writing outputs (13). Species A kind of animal: its genes, senses, actions, stats, diet, reproduction, mutation and population rules. Animal One individual: position, heading, stats, genome, traits, current action, counters. Data, not a GameObject. Kin Other animals of the same species. Edible A component that makes the thing it sits on edible (a resource layer's items, a species' animals, carcasses, eggs…): how it is eaten (graze, strike, scavenge) and how much energy it holds. Without it, nothing can eat that thing. Food web, diet Who eats what. A species' diet component lists the edible things it eats (resource layers, species, carcasses, …), optionally scaling their energy. Threat A species that has the animal's species in its diet. Derived from the food web. Resource layer Something edible spread over the ground, e.g. food items on a grid of cells that regrow. Entity A world object with a position that is not an animal: a carcass, an egg, a water hole. May move. Carcass What a kill leaves: portions that other hunters may eat, rotting after a while. Cover Places where an animal is hidden from the species that hunt it. Stat A per-animal number that changes during life: energy, stamina, age, thirst. Trait A per-animal number fixed at birth, with a default from the species' settings, that number genes can set: maximum stamina, speed, vision. Metabolism The rules that charge and refill stats each tick. Busy A state in which an animal neither decides nor moves for a number of ticks (e.g. digesting a meal). Gene, locus A slot of the genome with a fixed meaning, e.g. "the eat gene". Identified by a locus id. Text gene A gene whose value is a sentence, read by the brain through the prompt. Number gene A gene whose value is a number, expressed into a trait. Allele One value a gene can take (a sentence or a number), with an id and a lineage. Genome One allele per locus of the animal's species, in the species' locus order. Expression Turning a genome into what acts at run time: sentences into the prompt, numbers into traits. Founder pool The alleles from which the first animals and newcomers are drawn, per locus, including a neutral allele ("No preference."). Contrast alleles A "pro" and an "anti" sentence per locus, used only in tests of the brain. Control alleles Meaningless or irrelevant sentences, used in controls and tests. Crossover Building a child's genome from its parents', locus by locus. Mutation operator A rule that changes one allele: an LLM instruction deck for sentences, a numeric rule for numbers. Mutator The service that runs LLM mutations (a small model, batched). Guard, redraw A check on a mutated sentence; a rejected answer is drawn again with a new instruction and seed. Mating, litter Two ready animals in contact produce a litter of several babies, each with its own crossover and mutations. Egg, incubation A conceived baby waiting to hatch. Incubation gives the mutator time to answer. Generation The larger parent generation + 1; founders are generation 0. Cap, migration The maximum population of a species. Above it, random older animals leave the world ("migrated"). Floor, newcomer The minimum population. Below it, newcomers with founder genomes are added. Sense A module that reads the world for one animal and returns a discrete token (e.g. food "2-4 m away"). Observation The tuple of tokens of all the species' senses for one animal at one decision. Band A distance range with a name: adjacent, close, medium, far, none. Situation text The observation written as text for the brain. Action A behaviour the brain can choose (eat, flee, hide, hunt, …). It chooses a target, produces an intent (a direction, walk or run, how far at most) and may trigger an interaction. Search What an action does when it has nothing to act on in sight: a random walk. Counted as an invalid choice. Locomotion The species' module that turns an intent into movement over the ground: kinematic straight lines in the reference; terrain, NavMesh or physics subclasses later. Interaction A contact effect: graze, strike, eat a carcass portion, enter cover. Act order The order in which animals act within a tick (species in turn, all mixed, or simultaneous). Decision period Ticks between two decisions (4 in the reference). Brain A module that maps a batch of queries to probability rows over actions. Query What the brain receives for one animal: species, brain-visible genes, observation, situation text. Sampling temperature τ applied to the brain's probabilities before drawing: p^(1/τ), renormalised. Memo Within a run, the answer for each (species, brain, brain-visible genome, observation) is computed once. Answer cache A persistent store of brain and mutator answers, so a repeated run replays without model calls. Prompt The full text sent to an LLM brain: rules, actions, genes, situation, answer instruction. Gate A pass/fail test of a brain or of evolution, fixed in advance (15). Control A run setting that removes one ingredient (mutation, gene expression, meaningful founders) to compare against. Event, events hash One logged fact (birth, death, …); a running hash of all events identifies a run exactly.

spec/02-space-and-time.html.title: 02 — Space and time | EvoSim
spec/02-space-and-time.html.summary: 02 — Space and time The prototype lives on a grid of cells with 8-neighbour moves. The Unity system does not: positions are continuous and change through direction and speed vectors, on a flat plane or a Unity Terrain. Grids may still exist inside modules (a food layer stored per cell, a spatial index), but never constrain where an animal stands or how it moves. 1. Space SPACE-01 (MUST) An animal's position is a continuous point. Movement changes it by a velocity (direction × speed) over a tick, in a straight line in the reference. The speed belongs to the species (its locomotion component, 07 §2). Nothing snaps positions to cells. SPACE-02 (MUST) Distances are measured on the horizontal plane (x, z), Euclidean, through one world-level distance function that every module uses. A module MAY replace the function (e.g. path length on a NavMesh); no module computes distances its own way. SPACE-03 (MUST) The world is a bounded rectangle with hard borders. No animal or entity ever leaves it; there is no wrap-around. SPACE-04 (MUST) A ground module answers two questions for any point: its height, and whether it is walkable. No animal ever stands on a non-walkable point (water, too steep, an obstacle, outside the NavMesh). SPACE-05 (SHOULD) All walkable ground is connected, so every animal can in principle reach every walkable point. A generator that produces isolated pockets either removes them (makes them non-walkable) or retries. SPACE-06 (MUST) An animal's height follows the ground under it. Height does not count in distances (reference); slope MAY count in movement costs. Ground modules Module Walkable Height Use Flat ground (reference, Lab 1) everywhere inside the rectangle 0 the evolution lab Terrain above the water level, steepness below a maximum, outside obstacle footprints (trees, rocks) the terrain's heightmap terrain and foliage labs NavMesh on the NavMesh baked from the terrain the NavMesh surface terrain labs, path finding around obstacles Reference (Python). Lab 1 is flat and fully walkable. A terrain preview exists: a value-noise heightmap (three octaves) whose lowest 15 % becomes water and highest 10 % mountain (both impassable); only the largest connected walkable region is kept, and the generator retries (up to 50 times) until it covers at least 60 % of the world. An option splits the world into k × k areas with one-meter ridges, each with a gap of a few meters (tried against population crashes, made them worse, off). 2. Spatial queries SPACE-07 (MUST) "The nearest X within r of an animal" returns, among the candidates that pass the query's filter, the one at the smallest world distance, or nothing if none is within r. The animal itself is never a candidate. SPACE-08 (MUST) Ties are broken deterministically (by a fixed key such as the animal id, or by a named random stream), never by the iteration order of an unordered collection. SPACE-09 (SHOULD) Queries within one phase see one consistent state: either the state at the start of the phase, or the state after each animal's move if the act order is sequential (07 §6). 3. Time SPACE-10 (MUST) Simulation time is the tick count, an integer starting at 0. Every duration (age, digestion, rot, incubation, decision period, stats interval) is in ticks. SPACE-11 (MUST) A run's result does not depend on frame rate, Time.deltaTime, Time.fixedDeltaTime, or how many ticks run per frame. Speeds are in meters per tick. SPACE-12 (MUST) Visuals (meshes, animation, interpolation between two tick states) read the simulation and never write to it. 4. Waiting for the brain: lockstep A batch of LLM decisions takes seconds (JEV-9B: about 2.8 s per tick for about 330 animals; Ollama gemma4:12b: about 4 decisions per second). The owner's choice: the simulation waits, so that a decision is never made on old observations. SPACE-13 (MUST) A tick that needs answers from a service (decisions from a brain, mutated genes from the mutator) does not continue past the phase that needs them until they are all in. A decision always uses the observation made in its own tick. SPACE-14 (SHOULD) Two wait modes, with identical results (the same events hash): Mode What happens while waiting Where Freeze The main thread blocks until the answers arrive. Unity freezes. batch mode, tests, simplest code Responsive The tick stops at the phase that needs the answers. Unity keeps rendering and the editor stays usable; the tick resumes at that phase when the answers are in. the editor (default) SPACE-15 (MAY) A real-time mode in which answers are applied when they arrive (on observations that are by then old) is outside the contract: it is not reproducible. If built, it is labelled as such and never used for measurements. Not planned for now (owner decision); the reference is lockstep. Run controls Control Effect Pause / resume stops between ticks (or inside one, while waiting) Step one tick, then pause Run N N ticks, then pause Fast as many ticks per frame as fit in a time budget (e.g. 10 ms) Real time k ticks per second, for watching Stop condition a tick count, a wall-clock limit, a stop file or button, extinction of a species Reference. One tick ≈ one step of one meter at walking speed. Without a model in the loop (its keyword brain) the prototype took about 17 ms per tick for about 330 animals in the 192 × 192 world (Python); a C# implementation should be well below that, the brain's own time excluded.

spec/03-environment.html.title: 03 — Environment | EvoSim
spec/03-environment.html.summary: 03 — Environment Everything in the world that is not an animal: what grows on the ground (resource layers), where animals can hide (cover), and objects with a position (entities such as carcasses and eggs). Each is a replaceable module; a world may have none, one or several of each kind. 1. Resource layers A resource layer holds edible items spread over the ground, for example grass. The diet of a species says which layers it grazes and how much energy an item gives (04). ENV-01 (MUST) A resource layer answers: the nearest item within a radius of a point (position and distance), whether an item is within reach of a point, and how many items it holds. It can remove (consume) one item. ENV-02 (MUST) Consuming an item removes it at once: two animals can never eat the same item. When two animals reach for one item in the same tick, the act order decides who gets it (07 §6). ENV-03 (MUST) A layer that changes over time (regrowth) changes only in its own phase, once per tick, with its own random stream. ENV-04 (SHOULD) A layer may forbid items in some places (water, cover, steep ground) and may vary its growth rate by place (near water, by biome). Reference: the food layer of Lab 1.
